    FAILED = "FAILED"
    WARNING = "WARNING"


@dataclass
class ExpectationResult:
    """Data class to store expectation results"""
    expectation_type: str
    column: Optional[str]
    success: bool
    observed_value: Any
    expected_value: Any
    message: str
    timestamp: str


class GreatExpectationsPattern:
    """
    Implementation of Great Expectations-like pattern for PySpark
    Provides declarative expectations for data quality validation
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
        self.results: List[ExpectationResult] = []
        self.df: Optional[DataFrame] = None
        
    def load_data(self, df: DataFrame) -> 'GreatExpectationsPattern':
        """Load DataFrame for validation"""
        self.df = df
        return self
    
    def expect_column_values_to_not_be_null(
        self, 
        column: str, 
        threshold: float = 1.0
    ) -> 'GreatExpectationsPattern':
        """
        Expect column values to not be null
        
        Args:
            column: Column name to check
            threshold: Minimum proportion of non-null values (0.0 to 1.0)
        """
        if self.df is None:
            raise ValueError("DataFrame not loaded. Call load_data() first.")
        
        total_count = self.df.count()
        null_count = self.df.filter(
            col(column).isNull() | isnan(col(column))
        ).count()
        
        non_null_proportion = (total_count - null_count) / total_count if total_count > 0 else 0
        success = non_null_proportion >= threshold
        
        result = ExpectationResult(
            expectation_type="expect_column_values_to_not_be_null",
            column=column,
            success=success,
            observed_value=non_null_proportion,
            expected_value=threshold,
            message=f"Column '{column}' has {non_null_proportion:.2%} non-null values "
                   f"(expected >= {threshold:.2%})",
            timestamp=datetime.now().isoformat()
        )
        
        self.results.append(result)
        return self
    
    def expect_column_values_to_be_between(
        self, 
        column: str, 
        min_value: float, 
        max_value: float,
        threshold: float = 1.0
    ) -> 'GreatExpectationsPattern':
        """
        Expect column values to be between min and max
        
        Args:
            column: Column name to check
            min_value: Minimum acceptable value
            max_value: Maximum acceptable value
            threshold: Minimum proportion of values in range
        """
        if self.df is None:
            raise ValueError("DataFrame not loaded. Call load_data() first.")
        
        total_count = self.df.count()
        in_range_count = self.df.filter(
            (col(column) >= min_value) & (col(column) <= max_value)
        ).count()
        
        in_range_proportion = in_range_count / total_count if total_count > 0 else 0
        success = in_range_proportion >= threshold
        
        result = ExpectationResult(
            expectation_type="expect_column_values_to_be_between",
            column=column,
            success=success,
            observed_value=in_range_proportion,
            expected_value=threshold,
            message=f"Column '{column}' has {in_range_proportion:.2%} values between "
                   f"{min_value} and {max_value} (expected >= {threshold:.2%})",
            timestamp=datetime.now().isoformat()
        )
        
        self.results.append(result)
        return self
    
    def expect_column_values_to_be_in_set(
        self, 
        column: str, 
        value_set: List[Any],
        threshold: float = 1.0
    ) -> 'GreatExpectationsPattern':
        """
        Expect column values to be in a specified set
        
        Args:
            column: Column name to check
            value_set: List of acceptable values
            threshold: Minimum proportion of values in set
        """
        if self.df is None:
            raise ValueError("DataFrame not loaded. Call load_data() first.")
        
        total_count = self.df.count()
        in_set_count = self.df.filter(col(column).isin(value_set)).count()
        
        in_set_proportion = in_set_count / total_count if total_count > 0 else 0
        success = in_set_proportion >= threshold
        
        result = ExpectationResult(
            expectation_type="expect_column_values_to_be_in_set",
            column=column,
            success=success,
            observed_value=in_set_proportion,
            expected_value=threshold,
            message=f"Column '{column}' has {in_set_proportion:.2%} values in set "
                   f"{value_set} (expected >= {threshold:.2%})",
            timestamp=datetime.now().isoformat()
        )
        
        self.results.append(result)
        return self
    
    def expect_column_values_to_be_unique(
        self, 
        column: str,
        threshold: float = 1.0
    ) -> 'GreatExpectationsPattern':
        """
        Expect column values to be unique
        
        Args:
            column: Column name to check
            threshold: Minimum proportion of unique values
        """
        if self.df is None:
            raise ValueError("DataFrame not loaded. Call load_data() first.")
        
        total_count = self.df.count()
        unique_count = self.df.select(column).distinct().count()
        
        uniqueness_proportion = unique_count / total_count if total_count > 0 else 0
        success = uniqueness_proportion >= threshold
        
        result = ExpectationResult(
            expectation_type="expect_column_values_to_be_unique",
            column=column,
            success=success,
            observed_value=uniqueness_proportion,
            expected_value=threshold,
            message=f"Column '{column}' has {uniqueness_proportion:.2%} unique values "
                   f"(expected >= {threshold:.2%})",
            timestamp=datetime.now().isoformat()
        )
        
        self.results.append(result)
        return self
    
    def expect_table_row_count_to_be_between(
        self, 
        min_value: int, 
        max_value: int
    ) -> 'GreatExpectationsPattern':
        """
        Expect table row count to be between min and max
        
        Args:
            min_value: Minimum acceptable row count
            max_value: Maximum acceptable row count
        """
        if self.df is None:
            raise ValueError("DataFrame not loaded. Call load_data() first.")
        
        row_count = self.df.count()
        success = min_value <= row_count <= max_value
        
        result = ExpectationResult(
            expectation_type="expect_table_row_count_to_be_between",
            column=None,
            success=success,
            observed_value=row_count,
            expected_value=(min_value, max_value),
            message=f"Table has {row_count} rows (expected between {min_value} and {max_value})",
            timestamp=datetime.now().isoformat()
        )
        
        self.results.append(result)
        return self
    
    def get_validation_results(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Get validation results as dictionary"""
        success_count = sum(1 for r in self.results if r.success)
        total_count = len(self.results)
        
        return {
            "run_id": datetime.now().isoformat(),
            "success": all(r.success for r in self.results),
            "statistics": {
                "evaluated_expectations": total_count,
                "successful_expectations": success_count,
                "unsuccessful_expectations": total_count - success_count,
                "success_percent": (success_count / total_count * 100) if total_count > 0 else 0
            },
            "results": [asdict(r) for r in self.results]
        }
    
    def save_validation_results(self, output_path: str):
        """Save validation results to JSON file"""
        results = self.get_validation_results()
        with open(output_path, 'w') as f:
            json.dump(results, f, indent=2)


# Example Usage
def example_great_expectations():
    """Example usage of Great Expectations Pattern"""
    spark = SparkSession.builder \
        .appName("GreatExpectationsPattern") \
        .getOrCreate()
    
    # Create sample data
    data = [
        (1, "John", 25, "USA"),
        (2, "Jane", 30, "UK"),
        (3, "Bob", 35, "USA"),
        (4, "Alice", None, "Canada"),
        (5, "Charlie", 40, "UK")
    ]
    df = spark.createDataFrame(data, ["id", "name", "age", "country"])
    
    # Initialize Great Expectations Pattern
    ge = GreatExpectationsPattern(spark)
    
    # Run expectations
    ge.load_data(df) \
        .expect_column_values_to_not_be_null("id", threshold=1.0) \
        .expect_column_values_to_not_be_null("age", threshold=0.8) \
        .expect_column_values_to_be_between("age", 0, 100, threshold=0.8) \
        .expect_column_values_to_be_in_set("country", ["USA", "UK", "Canada"]) \
        .expect_column_values_to_be_unique("id") \
        .expect_table_row_count_to_be_between(1, 10)
    
    # Get results
    results = ge.get_validation_results()
    print(json.dumps(results, indent=2))
    
    spark.stop()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    example_great_expectations()

## 2. Deequ Pattern

```python
"""
Deequ Pattern for PySpark
Amazon's Deequ-inspired data quality framework with metrics and constraints
"""

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession, DataFrame
from pyspark.sql.functions import col, count, sum as spark_sum, avg, stddev, min as spark_min, max as spark_max
from typing import Dict, List, Any, Callable, Optional
from dataclasses import dataclass, asdict
from datetime import datetime
import json


@dataclass
class Metric:
    """Data class for storing metrics"""
    name: str
    entity: str
    instance: str
    value: float
    timestamp: str


@dataclass
class Constraint:
    """Data class for storing constraints"""
    constraint_name: str
    constraint_type: str
    level: str  # Error or Warning
    message: str
    status: str  # Success or Failure
    timestamp: str


class DeequPattern:
    """
    Implementation of Deequ-like pattern for PySpark
    Provides metric computation and constraint verification
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
        self.metrics: List[Metric] = []
        self.constraints: List[Constraint] = []
        self.df: Optional[DataFrame] = None
        
    def load_data(self, df: DataFrame) -> 'DeequPattern':
        """Load DataFrame for analysis"""
        self.df = df
        return self
    
    # Metric Analyzers
    
    def analyze_size(self) -> 'DeequPattern':
        """Analyze dataset size"""
        if self.df is None:
            raise ValueError("DataFrame not loaded")
        
        size = self.df.count()
        metric = Metric(
            name="Size",
            entity="Dataset",
            instance="*",
            value=float(size),
            timestamp=datetime.now().isoformat()
        )
        self.metrics.append(metric)
        return self
    
    def analyze_completeness(self, column: str) -> 'DeequPattern':
        """Analyze column completeness (non-null ratio)"""
        if self.df is None:
            raise ValueError("DataFrame not loaded")
        
        total = self.df.count()
        non_null = self.df.filter(col(column).isNotNull()).count()
        completeness = non_null / total if total > 0 else 0
        
        metric = Metric(
            name="Completeness",
            entity="Column",
            instance=column,
            value=completeness,
            timestamp=datetime.now().isoformat()
        )
        self.metrics.append(metric)
        return self
    
    def analyze_uniqueness(self, column: str) -> 'DeequPattern':
        """Analyze column uniqueness"""
        if self.df is None:
            raise ValueError("DataFrame not loaded")
        
        total = self.df.count()
        unique = self.df.select(column).distinct().count()
        uniqueness = unique / total if total > 0 else 0
        
        metric = Metric(
            name="Uniqueness",
            entity="Column",
            instance=column,
            value=uniqueness,
            timestamp=datetime.now().isoformat()
        )
        self.metrics.append(metric)
        return self
    
    def analyze_mean(self, column: str) -> 'DeequPattern':
        """Analyze column mean"""
        if self.df is None:
            raise ValueError("DataFrame not loaded")
        
        mean_value = self.df.select(avg(col(column))).collect()[0][0]
        mean_value = float(mean_value) if mean_value is not None else 0.0
        
        metric = Metric(
            name="Mean",
            entity="Column",
            instance=column,
            value=mean_value,
            timestamp=datetime.now().isoformat()
        )
        self.metrics.append(metric)
        return self
    
    def analyze_min_max(self, column: str) -> 'DeequPattern':
        """Analyze column min and max"""
        if self.df is None:
            raise ValueError("DataFrame not loaded")
        
        result = self.df.select(
            spark_min(col(column)).alias("min"),
            spark_max(col(column)).alias("max")
        ).collect()[0]
        
        min_metric = Metric(
            name="Minimum",
            entity="Column",
            instance=column,
            value=float(result["min"]) if result["min"] is not None else 0.0,
            timestamp=datetime.now().isoformat()
        )
        max_metric = Metric(
            name="Maximum",
            entity="Column",
            instance=column,
            value=float(result["max"]) if result["max"] is not None else 0.0,
            
```python
            timestamp=datetime.now().isoformat()
        )
        
        self.metrics.append(min_metric)
        self.metrics.append(max_metric)
        return self
    
    def analyze_standard_deviation(self, column: str) -> 'DeequPattern':
        """Analyze column standard deviation"""
        if self.df is None:
            raise ValueError("DataFrame not loaded")
        
        std_value = self.df.select(stddev(col(column))).collect()[0][0]
        std_value = float(std_value) if std_value is not None else 0.0
        
        metric = Metric(
            name="StandardDeviation",
            entity="Column",
            instance=column,
            value=std_value,
            timestamp=datetime.now().isoformat()
        )
        self.metrics.append(metric)
        return self
    
    def analyze_distinctness(self, column: str) -> 'DeequPattern':
        """Analyze number of distinct values"""
        if self.df is None:
            raise ValueError("DataFrame not loaded")
        
        distinct_count = self.df.select(column).distinct().count()
        
        metric = Metric(
            name="Distinctness",
            entity="Column",
            instance=column,
            value=float(distinct_count),
            timestamp=datetime.now().isoformat()
        )
        self.metrics.append(metric)
        return self
    
    # Constraint Verifiers
    
    def has_size(self, assertion: Callable[[int], bool], hint: str = "") -> 'DeequPattern':
        """Verify dataset size constraint"""
        if self.df is None:
            raise ValueError("DataFrame not loaded")
        
        size = self.df.count()
        success = assertion(size)
        
        constraint = Constraint(
            constraint_name="SizeConstraint",
            constraint_type="Size",
            level="Error",
            message=f"Dataset size is {size}. {hint}",
            status="Success" if success else "Failure",
            timestamp=datetime.now().isoformat()
        )
        self.constraints.append(constraint)
        return self
    
    def has_completeness(
        self, 
        column: str, 
        assertion: Callable[[float], bool],
        hint: str = ""
    ) -> 'DeequPattern':
        """Verify completeness constraint"""
        if self.df is None:
            raise ValueError("DataFrame not loaded")
        
        total = self.df.count()
        non_null = self.df.filter(col(column).isNotNull()).count()
        completeness = non_null / total if total > 0 else 0
        success = assertion(completeness)
        
        constraint = Constraint(
            constraint_name=f"CompletenessConstraint({column})",
            constraint_type="Completeness",
            level="Error",
            message=f"Column '{column}' completeness is {completeness:.2%}. {hint}",
            status="Success" if success else "Failure",
            timestamp=datetime.now().isoformat()
        )
        self.constraints.append(constraint)
        return self
    
    def has_uniqueness(
        self, 
        column: str, 
        assertion: Callable[[float], bool],
        hint: str = ""
    ) -> 'DeequPattern':
        """Verify uniqueness constraint"""
        if self.df is None:
            raise ValueError("DataFrame not loaded")
        
        total = self.df.count()
        unique = self.df.select(column).distinct().count()
        uniqueness = unique / total if total > 0 else 0
        success = assertion(uniqueness)
        
        constraint = Constraint(
            constraint_name=f"UniquenessConstraint({column})",
            constraint_type="Uniqueness",
            level="Error",
            message=f"Column '{column}' uniqueness is {uniqueness:.2%}. {hint}",
            status="Success" if success else "Failure",
            timestamp=datetime.now().isoformat()
        )
        self.constraints.append(constraint)
        return self
    
    def is_contained_in(
        self, 
        column: str, 
        allowed_values: List[Any],
        assertion: Callable[[float], bool],
        hint: str = ""
    ) -> 'DeequPattern':
        """Verify values are contained in allowed set"""
        if self.df is None:
            raise ValueError("DataFrame not loaded")
        
        total = self.df.count()
        contained = self.df.filter(col(column).isin(allowed_values)).count()
        containment_ratio = contained / total if total > 0 else 0
        success = assertion(containment_ratio)
        
        constraint = Constraint(
            constraint_name=f"ContainmentConstraint({column})",
            constraint_type="Containment",
            level="Error",
            message=f"Column '{column}' has {containment_ratio:.2%} values in allowed set. {hint}",
            status="Success" if success else "Failure",
            timestamp=datetime.now().isoformat()
        )
        self.constraints.append(constraint)
        return self
    
    def is_non_negative(
        self, 
        column: str,
        assertion: Callable[[float], bool],
        hint: str = ""
    ) -> 'DeequPattern':
        """Verify column has non-negative values"""
        if self.df is None:
            raise ValueError("DataFrame not loaded")
        
        total = self.df.count()
        non_negative = self.df.filter(col(column) >= 0).count()
        ratio = non_negative / total if total > 0 else 0
        success = assertion(ratio)
        
        constraint = Constraint(
            constraint_name=f"NonNegativeConstraint({column})",
            constraint_type="NonNegative",
            level="Error",
            message=f"Column '{column}' has {ratio:.2%} non-negative values. {hint}",
            status="Success" if success else "Failure",
            timestamp=datetime.now().isoformat()
        )
        self.constraints.append(constraint)
        return self
    
    def get_analysis_results(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Get complete analysis results"""
        constraint_success = sum(1 for c in self.constraints if c.status == "Success")
        constraint_total = len(self.constraints)
        
        return {
            "analysis_id": datetime.now().isoformat(),
            "metrics": [asdict(m) for m in self.metrics],
            "constraints": {
                "total": constraint_total,
                "successful": constraint_success,
                "failed": constraint_total - constraint_success,
                "details": [asdict(c) for c in self.constraints]
            },
            "overall_status": "Success" if all(c.status == "Success" for c in self.constraints) else "Failure"
        }
    
    def save_results(self, output_path: str):
        """Save analysis results to JSON file"""
        results = self.get_analysis_results()
        with open(output_path, 'w') as f:
            json.dump(results, f, indent=2)


# Example Usage
def example_deequ():
    """Example usage of Deequ Pattern"""
    spark = SparkSession.builder \
        .appName("DeequPattern") \
        .getOrCreate()
    
    # Create sample data
    data = [
        (1, "Product A", 100, "Electronics"),
        (2, "Product B", 200, "Electronics"),
        (3, "Product C", 150, "Clothing"),
        (4, "Product D", 300, "Electronics"),
        (5, "Product E", 250, "Clothing")
    ]
    df = spark.createDataFrame(data, ["id", "name", "price", "category"])
    
    # Initialize Deequ Pattern
    deequ = DeequPattern(spark)
    
    # Run analysis and verification
    deequ.load_data(df) \
        .analyze_size() \
        .analyze_completeness("id") \
        .analyze_completeness("price") \
        .analyze_uniqueness("id") \
        .analyze_mean("price") \
        .analyze_min_max("price") \
        .analyze_standard_deviation("price") \
        .analyze_distinctness("category") \
        .has_size(lambda x: x >= 5, "Expected at least 5 rows") \
        .has_completeness("id", lambda x: x == 1.0, "ID must be complete") \
        .has_uniqueness("id", lambda x: x == 1.0, "ID must be unique") \
        .is_contained_in("category", ["Electronics", "Clothing"], lambda x: x == 1.0) \
        .is_non_negative("price", lambda x: x == 1.0, "Price must be non-negative")
    
    # Get and print results
    results = deequ.get_analysis_results()
    print(json.dumps(results, indent=2))
    
    spark.stop()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    example_deequ()

## 3. Custom Validation Framework Pattern

```python
"""
Custom Validation Framework Pattern for PySpark
Flexible, extensible validation framework with custom rules
"""

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession, DataFrame
from pyspark.sql.functions import col, count, when, lit
from typing import Dict, List, Any, Callable, Optional, Tuple
from dataclasses import dataclass, asdict, field
from datetime import datetime
from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
import json


@dataclass
class ValidationRule:
    """Base class for validation rules"""
    rule_id: str
    rule_name: str
    description: str
    severity: str  # CRITICAL, ERROR, WARNING, INFO
    category: str  # COMPLETENESS, ACCURACY, CONSISTENCY, etc.


@dataclass
class ValidationResult:
    """Result of a validation rule execution"""
    rule_id: str
    rule_name: str
    severity: str
    category: str
    passed: bool
    records_checked: int
    records_failed: int
    failure_rate: float
    details: Dict[str, Any]
    timestamp: str
    error_message: Optional[str] = None


class BaseValidator(ABC):
    """Abstract base class for validators"""
    
    def __init__(self, rule: ValidationRule):
        self.rule = rule
    
    @abstractmethod
    def validate(self, df: DataFrame) -> ValidationResult:
        """Execute validation logic"""
        pass


class CompletenessValidator(BaseValidator):
    """Validator for checking data completeness"""
    
    def __init__(
        self, 
        rule_id: str,
        column: str, 
        threshold: float = 1.0,
        severity: str = "ERROR"
    ):
        rule = ValidationRule(
            rule_id=rule_id,
            rule_name=f"Completeness Check: {column}",
            description=f"Check if {column} has at least {threshold*100}% non-null values",
            severity=severity,
            category="COMPLETENESS"
        )
        super().__init__(rule)
        self.column = column
        self.threshold = threshold
    
    def validate(self, df: DataFrame) -> ValidationResult:
        """Execute completeness validation"""
        total_records = df.count()
        null_records = df.filter(col(self.column).isNull()).count()
        non_null_records = total_records - null_records
        
        completeness_rate = non_null_records / total_records if total_records > 0 else 0
        passed = completeness_rate >= self.threshold
        
        return ValidationResult(
            rule_id=self.rule.rule_id,
            rule_name=self.rule.rule_name,
            severity=self.rule.severity,
            category=self.rule.category,
            passed=passed,
            records_checked=total_records,
            records_failed=null_records,
            failure_rate=null_records / total_records if total_records > 0 else 0,
            details={
                "column": self.column,
                "completeness_rate": completeness_rate,
                "threshold": self.threshold,
                "null_count": null_records
            },
            timestamp=datetime.now().isoformat()
        )


class UniquenessValidator(BaseValidator):
    """Validator for checking data uniqueness"""
    
    def __init__(
        self, 
        rule_id: str,
        columns: List[str], 
        threshold: float = 1.0,
        severity: str = "ERROR"
    ):
        rule = ValidationRule(
            rule_id=rule_id,
            rule_name=f"Uniqueness Check: {', '.join(columns)}",
            description=f"Check if {', '.join(columns)} has at least {threshold*100}% unique values",
            severity=severity,
            category="UNIQUENESS"
        )
        super().__init__(rule)
        self.columns = columns
        self.threshold = threshold
    
    def validate(self, df: DataFrame) -> ValidationResult:
        """Execute uniqueness validation"""
        total_records = df.count()
        unique_records = df.select(self.columns).distinct().count()
        duplicate_records = total_records - unique_records
        
        uniqueness_rate = unique_records / total_records if total_records > 0 else 0
        passed = uniqueness_rate >= self.threshold
        
        return ValidationResult(
            rule_id=self.rule.rule_id,
            rule_name=self.rule.rule_name,
            severity=self.rule.severity,
            category=self.rule.category,
            passed=passed,
            records_checked=total_records,
            records_failed=duplicate_records,
            failure_rate=duplicate_records / total_records if total_records > 0 else 0,
            details={
                "columns": self.columns,
                "uniqueness_rate": uniqueness_rate,
                "threshold": self.threshold,
                "duplicate_count": duplicate_records
            },
            timestamp=datetime.now().isoformat()
        )


class RangeValidator(BaseValidator):
    """Validator for checking value ranges"""
    
    def __init__(
        self, 
        rule_id: str,
        column: str,
        min_value: Optional[float] = None,
        max_value: Optional[float] = None,
        threshold: float = 1.0,
        severity: str = "ERROR"
    ):
        rule = ValidationRule(
            rule_id=rule_id,
            rule_name=f"Range Check: {column}",
            description=f"Check if {column} values are within range [{min_value}, {max_value}]",
            severity=severity,
            category="ACCURACY"
        )
        super().__init__(rule)
        self.column = column
        self.min_value = min_value
        self.max_value = max_value
        self.threshold = threshold
    
    def validate(self, df: DataFrame) -> ValidationResult:
        """Execute range validation"""
        total_records = df.count()
        
        # Build filter condition
        condition = lit(True)
        if self.min_value is not None:
            condition = condition & (col(self.column) >= self.min_value)
        if self.max_value is not None:
            condition = condition & (col(self.column) <= self.max_value)
        
        valid_records = df.filter(condition).count()
        invalid_records = total_records - valid_records
        
        validity_rate = valid_records / total_records if total_records > 0 else 0
        passed = validity_rate >= self.threshold
        
        return ValidationResult(
            rule_id=self.rule.rule_id,
            rule

class CustomFunctionValidator(BaseValidator):
    """Validator using custom validation function"""
    
    def __init__(
        self, 
        rule_id: str,
        rule_name: str,
        validation_func: Callable[[DataFrame], Tuple[int, int]],
        description: str = "",
        threshold: float = 1.0,
        severity: str = "ERROR",
        category: str = "CUSTOM"
    ):
        rule = ValidationRule(
            rule_id=rule_id,
            rule_name=rule_name,
            description=description,
            severity=severity,
            category=category
        )
        super().__init__(rule)
        self.validation_func = validation_func
        self.threshold = threshold
    
    def validate(self, df: DataFrame) -> ValidationResult:
        """Execute custom validation"""
        try:
            valid_count, total_count = self.validation_func(df)
            invalid_count = total_count - valid_count
            
            validity_rate = valid_count / total_count if total_count > 0 else 0
            passed = validity_rate >= self.threshold
            
            return ValidationResult(
                rule_id=self.rule.rule_id,
                rule_name=self.rule.rule_name,
                severity=self.rule.severity,
                category=self.rule.category,
                passed=passed,
                records_checked=total_count,
                records_failed=invalid_count,
                failure_rate=invalid_count / total_count if total_count > 0 else 0,
                details={
                    "validity_rate": validity_rate,
                    "threshold": self.threshold
                },
                timestamp=datetime.now().isoformat()
            )
        except Exception as e:
            return ValidationResult(
                rule_id=self.rule.rule_id,
                rule_name=self.rule.rule_name,
                severity=self.rule.severity,
                category=self.rule.category,
                passed=False,
                records_checked=0,
                records_failed=0,
                failure_rate=1.0,
                details={},
                timestamp=datetime.now().isoformat(),
                error_message=str(e)
            )


class ReferentialIntegrityValidator(BaseValidator):
    """Validator for checking referential integrity"""
    
    def __init__(
        self, 
        rule_id: str,
        source_column: str,
        reference_df: DataFrame,
        reference_column: str,
        threshold: float = 1.0,
        severity: str = "ERROR"
    ):
        rule = ValidationRule(
            rule_id=rule_id,
            rule_name=f"Referential Integrity: {source_column}",
            description=f"Check if all {source_column} values exist in reference table",
            severity=severity,
            category="CONSISTENCY"
        )
        super().__init__(rule)
        self.source_column = source_column
        self.reference_df = reference_df
        self.reference_column = reference_column
        self.threshold = threshold
    
    def validate(self, df: DataFrame) -> ValidationResult:
        """Execute referential integrity validation"""
        total_records = df.count()
        
        # Get valid references
        reference_values = self.reference_df.select(self.reference_column).distinct()
        
        # Check how many records have valid references
        valid_records = df.join(
            reference_values,
            df[self.source_column] == reference_values[self.reference_column],
            "inner"
        ).count()
        
        invalid_records = total_records - valid_records
        validity_rate = valid_records / total_records if total_records > 0 else 0
        passed = validity_rate >= self.threshold
        
        return ValidationResult(
            rule_id=self.rule.rule_id,
            rule_name=self.rule.rule_name,
            severity=self.rule.severity,
            category=self.rule.category,
            passed=passed,
            records_checked=total_records,
            records_failed=invalid_records,
            failure_rate=invalid_records / total_records if total_records > 0 else 0,
            details={
                "source_column": self.source_column,
                "reference_column": self.reference_column,
                "validity_rate": validity_rate,
                "threshold": self.threshold,
                "orphaned_records": invalid_records
            },
            timestamp=datetime.now().isoformat()
        )


class CustomValidationFramework:
    """
    Custom Validation Framework for PySpark
    Manages and executes multiple validators
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession, framework_name: str = "CustomDQFramework"):
        self.spark = spark
        self.framework_name = framework_name
        self.validators: List[BaseValidator] = []
        self.results: List[ValidationResult] = []
        
    def add_validator(self, validator: BaseValidator) -> 'CustomValidationFramework':
        """Add a validator to the framework"""
        self.validators.append(validator)
        return self
    
    def add_completeness_check(
        self, 
        rule_id: str, 
        column: str, 
        threshold: float = 1.0,
        severity: str = "ERROR"
    ) -> 'CustomValidationFramework':
        """Add completeness validator"""
        validator = CompletenessValidator(rule_id, column, threshold, severity)
        return self.add_validator(validator)
    
    def add_uniqueness_check(
        self, 
        rule_id: str, 
        columns: List[str], 
        threshold: float = 1.0,
        severity: str = "ERROR"
    ) -> 'CustomValidationFramework':
        """Add uniqueness validator"""
        validator = UniquenessValidator(rule_id, columns, threshold, severity)
        return self.add_validator(validator)
    
    def add_range_check(
        self, 
        rule_id: str, 
        column: str,
        min_value: Optional[float] = None,
        max_value: Optional[float] = None,
        threshold: float = 1.0,
        severity: str = "ERROR"
    ) -> 'CustomValidationFramework':
        """Add range validator"""
        validator = RangeValidator(rule_id, column, min_value, max_value, threshold, severity)
        return self.add_validator(validator)
    
    def add_custom_check(
        self, 
        rule_id: str,
        rule_name: str,
        validation_func: Callable[[DataFrame], Tuple[int, int]],
        description: str = "",
        threshold: float = 1.0,
        severity: str = "ERROR",
        category: str = "CUSTOM"
    ) -> 'CustomValidationFramework':
        """Add custom validator"""
        validator = CustomFunctionValidator(
            rule_id, rule_name, validation_func, description, threshold, severity, category
        )
        return self.add_validator(validator)
    
    def add_referential_integrity_check(
        self, 
        rule_id: str,
        source_column: str,
        reference_df: DataFrame,
        reference_column: str,
        threshold: float = 1.0,
        severity: str = "ERROR"
    ) -> 'CustomValidationFramework':
        """Add referential integrity validator"""
        validator = ReferentialIntegrityValidator(
            rule_id, source_column, reference_df, reference_column, threshold, severity
        )
        return self.add_validator(validator)
    
    def run_validations(self, df: DataFrame) -> 'CustomValidationFramework':
        """Execute all validators"""
        self.results = []
        for validator in self.validators:
            try:
                result = validator.validate(df)
                self.results.append(result)
            except Exception as e:
                # Create error result
                error_result = ValidationResult(
                    rule_id=validator.rule.rule_id,
                    rule_name=validator.rule.rule_name,
                    severity=validator.rule.severity,
                    category=validator.rule.category,
                    passed=False,
                    records_checked=0,
                    records_failed=0,
                    failure_rate=1.0,
                    details={},
                    timestamp=datetime.now().isoformat(),
                    error_message=f"Validation execution failed: {str(e)}"
                )
                self.results.append(error_result)
        
        return self
    
    def get_summary(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Get validation summary"""
        total_validations = len(self.results)
        passed_validations = sum(1 for r in self.results if r.passed)
        failed_validations = total_validations - passed_validations
        
        # Group by severity
        severity_summary = {}
        for result in self.results:
            severity = result.severity
            if severity not in severity_summary:
                severity_summary[severity] = {"total": 0, "passed": 0, "failed": 0}
            severity_summary[severity]["total"] += 1
            if result.passed:
                severity_summary[severity]["passed"] += 1
            else:
                severity_summary[severity]["failed"] += 1
        
        # Group by category
        category_summary = {}
        for result in self.results:
            category = result.category
            if category not in category_summary:
                category_summary[category] = {"total": 0, "passed": 0, "failed": 0}
            category_summary[category]["total"] += 1
            if result.passed:
                category_summary[category]["passed"] += 1
            else:
                category_summary[category]["failed"] += 1
        
        return {
            "framework": self.framework_name,
            "execution_time": datetime.now().isoformat(),
            "overall_status": "PASSED" if failed_validations == 0 else "FAILED",
            "summary": {
                "total_validations": total_validations,
                "passed": passed_validations,
                "failed": failed_validations,
                "success_rate": (passed_validations / total_validations * 100) if total_validations > 0 else 0
            },
            "severity_breakdown": severity_summary,
            "category_breakdown": category_summary,
            "detailed_results": [asdict(r) for r in self.results]
        }
    
    def get_failed_validations(self) -> List[ValidationResult]:
        """Get only failed validations"""
        return [r for r in self.results if not r.passed]
    
    def save_results(self, output_path: str):
        """Save validation results to JSON file"""
        summary = self.get_summary()
        with open(output_path, 'w') as f:
            json.dump(summary, f, indent=2)
    
    def print_summary(self):
        """Print validation summary to console"""
        summary = self.get_summary()
        print(f"\n{'='*80}")
        print(f"Validation Framework: {self.framework_name}")
        print(f"{'='*80}")
        print(f"Overall Status: {summary['overall_status']}")
        print(f"Total Validations: {summary['summary']['total_validations']}")
        print(f"Passed: {summary['summary']['passed']}")
        print(f"Failed: {summary['summary']['failed']}")
        print(f"Success Rate: {summary['summary']['success_rate']:.2f}%")
        print(f"{'='*80}\n")
        
        if summary['summary']['failed'] > 0:
            print("Failed Validations:")
            for result in self.get_failed_validations():
                print(f"  - [{result.severity}] {result.rule_name}")
                print(f"    Failure Rate: {result.failure_rate:.2%}")
                print(f"    Details: {result.details}")
                if result.error_message:
                    print(f"    Error: {result.error_message}")
                print()


# Example Usage
def example_custom_validation():
    """Example usage of Custom Validation Framework"""
    spark = SparkSession.builder \
        .appName("CustomValidationFramework") \
        .getOrCreate()
    
    # Create sample data
    data = [
        (1, "John", 25, "USA", 1001),
        (2, "Jane", 30, "UK", 1002),
        (3, "Bob", None, "USA", 1001),
        (4, "Alice", 35, "Canada", 1003),
        (5, "Charlie", 40, "UK", 9999)  # Invalid country_code
    ]
    df = spark.createDataFrame(data, ["id", "name", "age", "country", "country_code"])
    
    # Create reference data
    ref_data = [
        (1001, "USA"),
        (1002, "UK"),
        (1003, "Canada")
    ]
    ref_df = spark.createDataFrame(ref_data, ["code", "country_name"])
    
    # Custom validation function
    def validate_name_format(df: DataFrame) -> Tuple[int, int]:
        """Custom validator: check if names start with capital letter"""
        total = df.count()
        valid = df.filter(col("name").rlike("^[A-Z]")).count()
        return valid, total
    
    # Initialize framework
    framework = CustomValidationFramework(spark, "ProductionDQFramework")
    
    # Add validators
    framework \
        .add_completeness_check("CHK001", "id", threshold=1.0, severity="CRITICAL") \
        .add_completeness_check("CHK002", "age", threshold=0.8, severity="WARNING") \
        .add_uniqueness_check("CHK003", ["id"], threshold=1.0, severity="CRITICAL") \
        .add_range_check("CHK004", "age", min_value=0, max_value=120, threshold=0.9, severity="ERROR") \
        .add_custom_check(
            "CHK005", 
            "Name Format Check",
            validate_name_format,
            "Names should start with capital letter",
            threshold=1.0,
            severity="WARNING"
        ) \
        .add_referential_integrity_check(
            "CHK006",
            "country_code",
            ref_df,
            "code",
            threshold=1.0,
            severity="ERROR"
        )
    
    # Run validations
    framework.run_validations(df)
    
    # Print summary
    framework.print_summary()
    
    # Get detailed results
    summary = framework.get_summary()
    print(json.dumps(summary, indent=2))
    
    spark.stop()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    example_custom_validation()

## 4. Multi-Framework Pattern

```python
"""
Multi-Framework Pattern for PySpark
Combines multiple data quality frameworks for comprehensive validation
"""

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession, DataFrame
```python
from pyspark.sql.functions import col, count, when
from typing import Dict, List, Any, Optional
from dataclasses import dataclass, asdict
from datetime import datetime
from enum import Enum
import json


class FrameworkType(Enum):
    """Enumeration for framework types"""
    GREAT_EXPECTATIONS = "GREAT_EXPECTATIONS"
    DEEQU = "DEEQU"
    CUSTOM = "CUSTOM"


@dataclass
class FrameworkResult:
    """Result from a single framework execution"""
    framework_type: str
    framework_name: str
    execution_time: str
    status: str
    total_checks: int
    passed_checks: int
    failed_checks: int
    success_rate: float
    details: Dict[str, Any]
    execution_duration_ms: float


class MultiFrameworkPattern:
    """
    Multi-Framework Pattern for PySpark
    Orchestrates multiple data quality frameworks and aggregates results
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession, orchestrator_name: str = "MultiFrameworkDQ"):
        self.spark = spark
        self.orchestrator_name = orchestrator_name
        self.framework_results: List[FrameworkResult] = []
        self.df: Optional[DataFrame] = None
        
    def load_data(self, df: DataFrame) -> 'MultiFrameworkPattern':
        """Load DataFrame for validation"""
        self.df = df
        return self
    
    def run_great_expectations_checks(
        self, 
        expectations_config: Dict[str, Any]
    ) -> 'MultiFrameworkPattern':
        """
        Run Great Expectations style checks
        
        Args:
            expectations_config: Configuration for expectations
        """
        if self.df is None:
            raise ValueError("DataFrame not loaded")
        
        start_time = datetime.now()
        
        # Initialize Great Expectations pattern
        ge = GreatExpectationsPattern(self.spark)
        ge.load_data(self.df)
        
        # Apply expectations from config
        total_checks = 0
        for expectation in expectations_config.get("expectations", []):
            exp_type = expectation.get("type")
            
            if exp_type == "column_not_null":
                ge.expect_column_values_to_not_be_null(
                    expectation["column"],
                    expectation.get("threshold", 1.0)
                )
                total_checks += 1
                
            elif exp_type == "column_between":
                ge.expect_column_values_to_be_between(
                    expectation["column"],
                    expectation["min_value"],
                    expectation["max_value"],
                    expectation.get("threshold", 1.0)
                )
                total_checks += 1
                
            elif exp_type == "column_in_set":
                ge.expect_column_values_to_be_in_set(
                    expectation["column"],
                    expectation["value_set"],
                    expectation.get("threshold", 1.0)
                )
                total_checks += 1
                
            elif exp_type == "column_unique":
                ge.expect_column_values_to_be_unique(
                    expectation["column"],
                    expectation.get("threshold", 1.0)
                )
                total_checks += 1
        
        # Get results
        ge_results = ge.get_validation_results()
        passed_checks = ge_results["statistics"]["successful_expectations"]
        failed_checks = ge_results["statistics"]["unsuccessful_expectations"]
        
        end_time = datetime.now()
        duration_ms = (end_time - start_time).total_seconds() * 1000
        
        # Store framework result
        framework_result = FrameworkResult(
            framework_type=FrameworkType.GREAT_EXPECTATIONS.value,
            framework_name="Great Expectations",
            execution_time=end_time.isoformat(),
            status="SUCCESS" if ge_results["success"] else "FAILED",
            total_checks=total_checks,
            passed_checks=passed_checks,
            failed_checks=failed_checks,
            success_rate=ge_results["statistics"]["success_percent"],
            details=ge_results,
            execution_duration_ms=duration_ms
        )
        
        self.framework_results.append(framework_result)
        return self
    
    def run_deequ_checks(
        self, 
        deequ_config: Dict[str, Any]
    ) -> 'MultiFrameworkPattern':
        """
        Run Deequ style checks
        
        Args:
            deequ_config: Configuration for Deequ checks
        """
        if self.df is None:
            raise ValueError("DataFrame not loaded")
        
        start_time = datetime.now()
        
        # Initialize Deequ pattern
        deequ = DeequPattern(self.spark)
        deequ.load_data(self.df)
        
        # Apply analyzers
        for analyzer in deequ_config.get("analyzers", []):
            analyzer_type = analyzer.get("type")
            
            if analyzer_type == "size":
                deequ.analyze_size()
            elif analyzer_type == "completeness":
                deequ.analyze_completeness(analyzer["column"])
            elif analyzer_type == "uniqueness":
                deequ.analyze_uniqueness(analyzer["column"])
            elif analyzer_type == "mean":
                deequ.analyze_mean(analyzer["column"])
            elif analyzer_type == "min_max":
                deequ.analyze_min_max(analyzer["column"])
        
        # Apply constraints
        total_checks = 0
        for constraint in deequ_config.get("constraints", []):
            constraint_type = constraint.get("type")
            
            if constraint_type == "size":
                deequ.has_size(
                    lambda x: eval(constraint["assertion"].replace("x", str(x))),
                    constraint.get("hint", "")
                )
                total_checks += 1
                
            elif constraint_type == "completeness":
                deequ.has_completeness(
                    constraint["column"],
                    lambda x: x >= constraint["threshold"],
                    constraint.get("hint", "")
                )
                total_checks += 1
                
            elif constraint_type == "uniqueness":
                deequ.has_uniqueness(
                    constraint["column"],
                    lambda x: x >= constraint["threshold"],
                    constraint.get("hint", "")
                )
                total_checks += 1
        
        # Get results
        deequ_results = deequ.get_analysis_results()
        passed_checks = deequ_results["constraints"]["successful"]
        failed_checks = deequ_results["constraints"]["failed"]
        success_rate = (passed_checks / total_checks * 100) if total_checks > 0 else 0
        
        end_time = datetime.now()
        duration_ms = (end_time - start_time).total_seconds() * 1000
        
        # Store framework result
        framework_result = FrameworkResult(
            framework_type=FrameworkType.DEEQU.value,
            framework_name="Deequ",
            execution_time=end_time.isoformat(),
            status="SUCCESS" if deequ_results["overall_status"] == "Success" else "FAILED",
            total_checks=total_checks,
            passed_checks=passed_checks,
            failed_checks=failed_checks,
            success_rate=success_rate,
            details=deequ_results,
            execution_duration_ms=duration_ms
        )
        
        self.framework_results.append(framework_result)
        return self
    
    def run_custom_checks(
        self, 
        custom_config: Dict[str, Any]
    ) -> 'MultiFrameworkPattern':
        """
        Run custom validation checks
        
        Args:
            custom_config: Configuration for custom checks
        """
        if self.df is None:
            raise ValueError("DataFrame not loaded")
        
        start_time = datetime.now()
        
        # Initialize custom framework
        custom_fw = CustomValidationFramework(self.spark, custom_config.get("name", "Custom"))
        
        # Apply validators
        for validator_config in custom_config.get("validators", []):
            validator_type = validator_config.get("type")
            
            if validator_type == "completeness":
                custom_fw.add_completeness_check(
                    validator_config["rule_id"],
                    validator_config["column"],
                    validator_config.get("threshold", 1.0),
                    validator_config.get("severity", "ERROR")
                )
                
            elif validator_type == "uniqueness":
                custom_fw.add_uniqueness_check(
                    validator_config["rule_id"],
                    validator_config["columns"],
                    validator_config.get("threshold", 1.0),
                    validator_config.get("severity", "ERROR")
                )
                
            elif validator_type == "range":
                custom_fw.add_range_check(
                    validator_config["rule_id"],
                    validator_config["column"],
                    validator_config.get("min_value"),
                    validator_config.get("max_value"),
                    validator_config.get("threshold", 1.0),
                    validator_config.get("severity", "ERROR")
                )
        
        # Run validations
        custom_fw.run_validations(self.df)
        
        # Get results
        custom_results = custom_fw.get_summary()
        
        end_time = datetime.now()
        duration_ms = (end_time - start_time).total_seconds() * 1000
        
        # Store framework result
        framework_result = FrameworkResult(
            framework_type=FrameworkType.CUSTOM.value,
            framework_name=custom_config.get("name", "Custom"),
            execution_time=end_time.isoformat(),
            status=custom_results["overall_status"],
            total_checks=custom_results["summary"]["total_validations"],
            passed_checks=custom_results["summary"]["passed"],
            failed_checks=custom_results["summary"]["failed"],
            success_rate=custom_results["summary"]["success_rate"],
            details=custom_results,
            execution_duration_ms=duration_ms
        )
        
        self.framework_results.append(framework_result)
        return self
    
    def get_consolidated_results(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Get consolidated results from all frameworks"""
        total_checks = sum(r.total_checks for r in self.framework_results)
        total_passed = sum(r.passed_checks for r in self.framework_results)
        total_failed = sum(r.failed_checks for r in self.framework_results)
        
        overall_success_rate = (total_passed / total_checks * 100) if total_checks > 0 else 0
        overall_status = "SUCCESS" if total_failed == 0 else "FAILED"
        
        # Framework breakdown
        framework_breakdown = {}
        for result in self.framework_results:
            framework_breakdown[result.framework_name] = {
                "status": result.status,
                "total_checks": result.total_checks,
                "passed_checks": result.passed_checks,
                "failed_checks": result.failed_checks,
                "success_rate": result.success_rate,
                "execution_duration_ms": result.execution_duration_ms
            }
        
        return {
            "orchestrator": self.orchestrator_name,
            "execution_time": datetime.now().isoformat(),
            "overall_status": overall_status,
            "consolidated_summary": {
                "total_frameworks": len(self.framework_results),
                "total_checks": total_checks,
                "passed_checks": total_passed,
                "failed_checks": total_failed,
                "overall_success_rate": overall_success_rate
            },
            "framework_breakdown": framework_breakdown,
            "detailed_results": [asdict(r) for r in self.framework_results]
        }
    
    def save_consolidated_results(self, output_path: str):
        """Save consolidated results to JSON file"""
        results = self.get_consolidated_results()
        with open(output_path, 'w') as f:
            json.dump(results, f, indent=2)
    
    def print_consolidated_summary(self):
        """Print consolidated summary to console"""
        results = self.get_consolidated_results()
        
        print(f"\n{'='*80}")
        print(f"Multi-Framework Data Quality Orchestrator: {self.orchestrator_name}")
        print(f"{'='*80}")
        print(f"Overall Status: {results['overall_status']}")
        print(f"Total Frameworks: {results['consolidated_summary']['total_frameworks']}")
        print(f"Total Checks: {results['consolidated_summary']['total_checks']}")
        print(f"Passed: {results['consolidated_summary']['passed_checks']}")
        print(f"Failed: {results['consolidated_summary']['failed_checks']}")
        print(f"Overall Success Rate: {results['consolidated_summary']['overall_success_rate']:.2f}%")
        print(f"{'='*80}\n")
        
        print("Framework Breakdown:")
        for fw_name, fw_details in results['framework_breakdown'].items():
            print(f"\n  {fw_name}:")
            print(f"    Status: {fw_details['status']}")
            print(f"    Checks: {fw_details['total_checks']}")
            print(f"    Success Rate: {fw_details['success_rate']:.2f}%")
            print(f"    Duration: {fw_details['execution_duration_ms']:.2f}ms")

## 5. Pluggable Framework Pattern

```python
"""
Pluggable Framework Pattern for PySpark
Extensible architecture allowing dynamic plugin registration and execution
"""

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession, DataFrame
from pyspark.sql.functions import col
from typing import Dict, List, Any, Optional, Type
from dataclasses import dataclass, asdict
from datetime import datetime
from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
import json
import importlib
import inspect


@dataclass
class PluginMetadata:
    """Metadata for a plugin"""
    plugin_id: str
    plugin_name: str
    plugin_version: str
    plugin_type: str
    description: str
    author: str
    dependencies: List[str]


@dataclass
class PluginExecutionResult:
    """Result of plugin execution"""
    plugin_id: str
    plugin_name: str
    execution_time: str
    status: str
    execution_duration_ms: float
    results: Dict[str, Any]
    errors: Optional[List[str]] = None


class DataQualityPlugin(ABC):
    """
    Abstract base class for all data quality plugins
    All plugins must inherit from this class
    """
    
    def __init__(self):
        self.metadata = self.get_metadata()
    
    @abstractmethod
    def get_metadata(self) -> PluginMetadata:
        """Return plugin metadata"""
        pass
    
    @abstractmethod
    def validate(self, df: DataFrame, config: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Execute plugin validation logic
        
        Args:
            df: DataFrame to validate
            config: Plugin-specific configuration
            
        Returns:
            Dictionary containing validation results
        """
        pass
    
    @abstractmethod
    def get_default_config(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Return default configuration for the plugin"""
        pass


class SchemaValidationPlugin(DataQualityPlugin):
    """Plugin for validating DataFrame schema"""
    
    def get_metadata(self) -> PluginMetadata:
        return PluginMetadata(
            plugin_id="schema_validator_v1",
            plugin_name="Schema Validation Plugin",
            plugin_version="1.0.0",
            plugin_type="SCHEMA",
            description="Validates DataFrame schema against expected schema",
            author="DQ Team",
            dependencies=[]
        )
    
    def get_default_config(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "expected_columns": [],
            "expected_types": {},
            "allow_extra_columns": False,
            "case_sensitive": True
        }
    
    def validate(self, df: DataFrame, config: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Validate DataFrame schema"""
        expected_columns = config.get("expected_columns", [])
        expected_types = config.get("expected_types", {})
        allow_extra = config.get("allow_extra_columns", False)
        case_sensitive = config.get("case_sensitive", True)
        
        actual_columns = df.columns
        actual_schema = {field.name: str(field.dataType) for field in df.schema.fields}
        
        # Check for missing columns
        missing_columns = []
        for col_name in expected_columns:
            if case_sensitive:
                if col_name not in actual_columns:
                    missing_columns.append(col_name)
            else:
                if col_name.lower() not in [c.lower() for c in actual_columns]:
                    missing_columns.append(col_name)
        
        # Check for extra columns
        extra_columns = []
        if not allow_extra:
            for col_name in actual_columns:
                if case_sensitive:
                    if col_name not in expected_columns:
                        extra_columns.append(col_name)
                else:
                    if col_name.lower() not in [c.lower() for c in expected_columns]:
                        extra_columns.append(col_name)
        
        # Check data types
        type_mismatches = []
        for col_name, expected_type in expected_types.items():
            if col_name in actual_schema:
                if expected_type not in actual_schema[col_name]:
                    type_mismatches.append({
                        "column": col_name,
                        "expected": expected_type,
                        "actual": actual_schema[col_name]
                    })
        
        passed = len(missing_columns) == 0 and len(extra_columns) == 0 and len(type_mismatches) == 0
        
        return {
            "passed": passed,
            "missing_columns": missing_columns,
            "extra_columns": extra_columns,
            "type_mismatches": type_mismatches,
            "actual_schema": actual_schema
        }


class DataProfilingPlugin(DataQualityPlugin):
    """Plugin for profiling DataFrame data"""
    
    def get_metadata(self) -> PluginMetadata:
        return PluginMetadata(
            plugin_id="data_profiler_v1",
            plugin_name="Data Profiling Plugin",
            plugin_version="1.0.0",
            plugin_type="PROFILING",
            description="Generates statistical profile of DataFrame",
            author="DQ Team",
            dependencies=[]
        )
    
    def get_default_config(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "columns_to_profile": [],
            "include_percentiles": True,
            "percentiles": [0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.95, 0.99]
        }
    
    def validate(self, df: DataFrame, config: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Profile DataFrame data"""
        columns_to_profile = config.get("columns_to_profile", df.columns)
        include_percentiles = config.get("include_percentiles", True)
        
        profile = {
            "row_count": df.count(),
            "column_count": len(df.columns),
            "column_profiles": {}
        }
        
        for col_name in columns_to_profile:
            if col_name not in df.columns:
                continue
            
            col_type = dict(df.dtypes)[col_name]
            col_profile = {
                "data_type": col_type,
                "null_count": df.filter(col(col_name).isNull()).count(),
                "distinct_count": df.select(col_name).distinct().count()
            }
            
            # Add numeric statistics for numeric columns
            if col_type in ['int', 'bigint', 'double', 'float', 'decimal']:
                stats = df.select(col_name).summary().collect()
                stats_dict = {row['summary']: row[col_name] for row in stats}
                col_profile.update({
                    "min": stats_dict.get('min'),
                    "max": stats_dict.get('max'),
                    "mean": stats_dict.get('mean'),
                    "stddev": stats_dict.get('stddev')
                })
                
                if include_percentiles:
                    percentiles = config.get("percentiles", [0.25, 0.5, 0.75])
                    approx_quantiles = df.stat.approxQuantile(col_name, percentiles, 0.01)
                    col_profile["percentiles"] = {
                        f"p{int(p*100)}": q for p, q in zip(percentiles, approx_quantiles)
                    }
            
            profile["column_profiles"][col_name] = col_profile
        
        return {
            "passed": True,
            "profile": profile
        }


class BusinessRulesPlugin(DataQualityPlugin):
    """Plugin for validating business rules"""
    
    def get_metadata(self) -> PluginMetadata:
        return PluginMetadata(
            plugin_id="business_rules_v1",
            plugin_name="Business Rules Plugin",
            plugin_version="1.0.0",
            plugin_type="BUSINESS_RULES",
            description="Validates custom business rules",
            author="DQ Team",
            dependencies=[]
        )
    
    def get_default_config(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "rules": []
        }
    
    def validate(self, df: DataFrame, config: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Validate business rules"""
        rules = config.get("rules", [])
        rule_results = []
        
        for rule in rules:
            rule_id = rule.get("rule_id")
            rule_name = rule.get("rule_name")
            rule_expression = rule.get("expression")
            threshold = rule.get("threshold", 1.0)
            
            try:
                # Evaluate rule expression
                total_count = df.count()
                valid_count = df.filter(rule_expression).count()
                invalid_count = total_count - valid_count
                
                validity_rate = valid_count / total_count if total_count > 0 else 0
                passed = validity_rate >= threshold
                
                rule_results.append({
                    "rule_id": rule_id,
                    "rule_name": rule_name,
                    "passed": passed,
                    "total_records": total_count,
                    "valid_records": valid_count,
                    "invalid_records": invalid_count,
                    "validity_rate": validity_rate,
                    "threshold": threshold
                })
            except Exception as e:
                rule_results.append({
                    "rule_id": rule_id,
                    "rule_name": rule_name,
                    "passed": False,
                    "error": str(e)
                })
        
        overall_passed = all(r.get("passed", False) for r in rule_results)
        
        return {
            "passed": overall_passed,
            "rule_results": rule_results
        }


class AnomalyDetectionPlugin(DataQualityPlugin):
    """Plugin for detecting anomalies in data"""
    
    def get_metadata(self) -> PluginMetadata:
        return PluginMetadata(
            plugin_id="anomaly_detector_v1",
            plugin_name="Anomaly Detection Plugin",
            plugin_version="1.0.0",
            plugin_type="ANOMALY_DETECTION",
            description="Detects anomalies using statistical methods",
            author="DQ Team",
            dependencies=[]
        )
    
    def get_default_config(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "columns": [],
            "method": "zscore",  # zscore or iqr
            "threshold": 3.0
        }
    
    def validate(self, df: DataFrame, config: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Detect anomalies in data"""
        columns = config.get("columns", [])
        method = config.get("method", "zscore")
        threshold = config.get("threshold", 3.0)
        
        anomaly_results = {}
        
        for col_name in columns:
            if col_name not in df.columns:
                continue
            
            col_type = dict(df.dtypes)[col_name]
            if col_type not in ['int', 'bigint', 'double', 'float', 'decimal']:
                continue
            
            if method == "zscore":
                # Z-score method
                stats = df.select(col_name).summary().collect()
                stats_dict = {row['summary']: float(row[col_name]) for row in stats}
                mean = stats_dict.get('mean', 0)
                stddev = stats_dict.get('stddev', 1)
                
                if stddev > 0:
                    anomaly_count = df.filter(
                        (col(col_name) < mean - threshold * stddev) |
                        (col(col_name) > mean + threshold * stddev)
                    ).count()
                else:
                    anomaly_count = 0
                
                anomaly_results[col_name] = {
                    "method": "zscore",
                    "anomaly_count": anomaly_count,
                    "mean": mean,
                    "stddev": stddev,
                    "threshold": threshold
                }
                
            elif method == "iqr":
                # IQR method
                quantiles = df.stat.approxQuantile(col_name, [0.25, 0.75], 0.01)
                q1, q3 = quantiles[0], quantiles[1]
                iqr = q3 - q1
                
                lower_bound = q1 - threshold * iqr
                upper_bound = q3 + threshold * iqr
                
                anomaly_count = df.filter(
                    (col(col_name) < lower_bound) |
                    (col(col_name) > upper_bound)
                ).count()
                
                anomaly_results[col_name] = {
                    "method": "iqr",
                    "anomaly_count": anomaly_count,
                    "q1": q1,
                    "q3": q3,
                    "iqr": iqr,
                    "lower_bound": lower_bound,
                    "upper_bound": upper_bound
                }
        
        total_anomalies = sum(r["anomaly_count"] for r in anomaly_results.values())
        
        return {
            "passed": total_anomalies == 0,
            "total_anomalies": total_anomalies,
            "anomaly_results": anomaly_results
        }
