def ecommerce_analytics_pipeline():
    """
    Comprehensive real-world example combining all parallelization patterns
    """
    
    print("\nScenario: Daily e-commerce analytics processing")
    print("Requirements: Process millions of transactions with multiple analyses")
    
    # Generate more realistic e-commerce data
    print("\n1. Data Preparation:")
    print("-" * 40)
    
    # Extended sales data with more attributes
    extended_sales = sales_df \
        .withColumn("order_id", (col("sale_id") / 10).cast("int")) \
        .withColumn("customer_id", (rand() * 10000).cast("int")) \
        .withColumn("payment_method", 
                   when(rand() < 0.3, "credit_card")
                   .when(rand() < 0.6, "debit_card")
                   .when(rand() < 0.9, "paypal")
                   .otherwise("crypto")) \
        .withColumn("device_type",
                   when(rand() < 0.5, "mobile")
                   .when(rand() < 0.8, "desktop")
                   .otherwise("tablet"))
    
    # Partition strategically for the pipeline
    extended_sales = extended_sales.repartition(100, "region", "sale_date")
    extended_sales.cache()
    
    print(f"Extended sales data: {extended_sales.count()} records")
    print(f"Partitions: {extended_sales.rdd.getNumPartitions()}")
    
    # 2. Parallel Analytics Queries
    print("\n2. Running Parallel Analytics Queries:")
    print("-" * 40)
    
    def analytics_query_1():
        """Revenue analysis by region and payment method"""
        print("  [Analytics 1] Revenue by Region & Payment Method")
        start = time.time()
        
        result = extended_sales.groupBy("region", "payment_method") \
            .agg(
                sum("amount").alias("total_revenue"),
                count("sale_id").alias("transaction_count"),
                avg("amount").alias("avg_transaction_value")
            ) \
            .withColumn("revenue_rank", 
                       rank().over(Window.partitionBy("region")
                                  .orderBy(desc("total_revenue")))) \
            .filter(col("revenue_rank") <= 3) \
            .orderBy("region", "revenue_rank")
        
        result.cache()
        count = result.count()
        
        print(f"  [Analytics 1] Completed: {count} results in {time.time()-start:.2f}s")
        return result
    
    def analytics_query_2():
        """Customer behavior analysis"""
        print("  [Analytics 2] Customer Behavior Analysis")
        start = time.time()
        
        result = extended_sales.groupBy("customer_id", "device_type") \
            .agg(
                sum("amount").alias("customer_lifetime_value"),
                count("order_id").alias("total_orders"),
                countDistinct("product_id").alias("unique_products"),
                min("sale_date").alias("first_
```python
purchase"),
                max("sale_date").alias("last_purchase")
            ) \
            .withColumn("days_active", 
                       datediff(col("last_purchase"), col("first_purchase"))) \
            .withColumn("avg_order_value", 
                       col("customer_lifetime_value") / col("total_orders")) \
            .filter(col("customer_lifetime_value") > 1000) \
            .orderBy(desc("customer_lifetime_value"))
        
        result.cache()
        count = result.count()
        
        print(f"  [Analytics 2] Completed: {count} results in {time.time()-start:.2f}s")
        return result
    
    def analytics_query_3():
        """Product performance trends"""
        print("  [Analytics 3] Product Performance Trends")
        start = time.time()
        
        result = extended_sales \
            .withColumn("year_month", date_format("sale_date", "yyyy-MM")) \
            .groupBy("product_id", "year_month") \
            .agg(
                sum("amount").alias("monthly_revenue"),
                count("sale_id").alias("monthly_sales"),
                countDistinct("customer_id").alias("unique_customers")
            ) \
            .withColumn("prev_month_revenue",
                       lag("monthly_revenue", 1).over(
                           Window.partitionBy("product_id").orderBy("year_month")
                       )) \
            .withColumn("revenue_growth_pct",
                       ((col("monthly_revenue") - col("prev_month_revenue")) / 
                        col("prev_month_revenue") * 100)) \
            .filter(col("prev_month_revenue").isNotNull()) \
            .orderBy("product_id", "year_month")
        
        result.cache()
        count = result.count()
        
        print(f"  [Analytics 3] Completed: {count} results in {time.time()-start:.2f}s")
        return result
    
    def analytics_query_4():
        """Cohort analysis"""
        print("  [Analytics 4] Cohort Analysis")
        start = time.time()
        
        # First purchase cohort
        first_purchase = extended_sales.groupBy("customer_id") \
            .agg(min("sale_date").alias("cohort_date"))
        
        # Join with sales and analyze
        result = extended_sales \
            .join(first_purchase, "customer_id") \
            .withColumn("cohort_month", date_format("cohort_date", "yyyy-MM")) \
            .withColumn("purchase_month", date_format("sale_date", "yyyy-MM")) \
            .groupBy("cohort_month", "purchase_month") \
            .agg(
                countDistinct("customer_id").alias("active_customers"),
                sum("amount").alias("cohort_revenue")
            ) \
            .orderBy("cohort_month", "purchase_month")
        
        result.cache()
        count = result.count()
        
        print(f"  [Analytics 4] Completed: {count} results in {time.time()-start:.2f}s")
        return result
    
    # Execute all analytics in parallel using inter-query parallelism
    print("\nExecuting 4 analytics queries in parallel...")
    overall_start = time.time()
    
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=4) as executor:
        future_1 = executor.submit(analytics_query_1)
        future_2 = executor.submit(analytics_query_2)
        future_3 = executor.submit(analytics_query_3)
        future_4 = executor.submit(analytics_query_4)
        
        # Collect results
        analytics_results = {
            'revenue_analysis': future_1.result(),
            'customer_behavior': future_2.result(),
            'product_trends': future_3.result(),
            'cohort_analysis': future_4.result()
        }
    
    overall_time = time.time() - overall_start
    print(f"\n✓ All analytics completed in {overall_time:.2f} seconds (parallel execution)")
    
    # 3. Display Sample Results
    print("\n3. Sample Analytics Results:")
    print("-" * 40)
    
    print("\nRevenue Analysis (Top Results):")
    analytics_results['revenue_analysis'].show(10, truncate=False)
    
    print("\nHigh-Value Customer Behavior (Top 10):")
    analytics_results['customer_behavior'].show(10, truncate=False)
    
    print("\nProduct Trends (Sample):")
    analytics_results['product_trends'].show(10, truncate=False)
    
    print("\nCohort Analysis (Sample):")
    analytics_results['cohort_analysis'].show(10, truncate=False)
    
    # 4. Advanced: Multi-Stage Pipeline with Optimized Parallelism
    print("\n4. Multi-Stage ETL Pipeline:")
    print("-" * 40)
    
    # Stage 1: Data Quality & Enrichment (Partition-level parallelism)
    print("\n  Stage 1: Data Quality & Enrichment")
    stage1_start = time.time()
    
    enriched_data = extended_sales \
        .filter(col("amount") > 0) \
        .filter(col("customer_id").isNotNull()) \
        .withColumn("is_high_value", when(col("amount") > 500, True).otherwise(False)) \
        .withColumn("hour_of_day", hour("sale_date")) \
        .withColumn("day_of_week", dayofweek("sale_date")) \
        .withColumn("is_weekend", when(col("day_of_week").isin([1, 7]), True).otherwise(False)) \
        .repartition(80, "region", "product_id")
    
    enriched_data.cache()
    enriched_count = enriched_data.count()
    stage1_time = time.time() - stage1_start
    
    print(f"  Stage 1 completed: {enriched_count} records in {stage1_time:.2f}s")
    print(f"  Partitions: {enriched_data.rdd.getNumPartitions()}")
    
    # Stage 2: Aggregation & Feature Engineering (Intra-query parallelism)
    print("\n  Stage 2: Aggregation & Feature Engineering")
    stage2_start = time.time()
    
    aggregated_features = enriched_data.groupBy(
        "region", "product_id", "payment_method", "device_type"
    ).agg(
        sum("amount").alias("total_revenue"),
        count("sale_id").alias("transaction_count"),
        avg("amount").alias("avg_transaction"),
        sum(when(col("is_high_value"), 1).otherwise(0)).alias("high_value_count"),
        sum(when(col("is_weekend"), col("amount")).otherwise(0)).alias("weekend_revenue"),
        countDistinct("customer_id").alias("unique_customers")
    ).withColumn(
        "high_value_ratio",
        col("high_value_count") / col("transaction_count")
    ).withColumn(
        "weekend_revenue_ratio",
        col("weekend_revenue") / col("total_revenue")
    ).repartition(40)
    
    aggregated_features.cache()
    agg_count = aggregated_features.count()
    stage2_time = time.time() - stage2_start
    
    print(f"  Stage 2 completed: {agg_count} feature records in {stage2_time:.2f}s")
    print(f"  Partitions: {aggregated_features.rdd.getNumPartitions()}")
    
    # Stage 3: Advanced Analytics & Scoring (Stage-level parallelism)
    print("\n  Stage 3: Advanced Analytics & Scoring")
    stage3_start = time.time()
    
    # Calculate percentile ranks for scoring
    window_spec = Window.partitionBy("region").orderBy(desc("total_revenue"))
    
    scored_data = aggregated_features \
        .withColumn("revenue_rank", rank().over(window_spec)) \
        .withColumn("revenue_percentile", 
                   percent_rank().over(window_spec)) \
        .withColumn("performance_score",
                   (col("revenue_percentile") * 40 +
                    col("high_value_ratio") * 30 +
                    col("weekend_revenue_ratio") * 30)) \
        .withColumn("performance_tier",
                   when(col("performance_score") >= 80, "Platinum")
                   .when(col("performance_score") >= 60, "Gold")
                   .when(col("performance_score") >= 40, "Silver")
                   .otherwise("Bronze"))
    
    scored_data.cache()
    scored_count = scored_data.count()
    stage3_time = time.time() - stage3_start
    
    print(f"  Stage 3 completed: {scored_count} scored records in {stage3_time:.2f}s")
    
    # Stage 4: Final Aggregation & Reporting (Task-level parallelism)
    print("\n  Stage 4: Final Aggregation & Reporting")
    stage4_start = time.time()
    
    final_report = scored_data.groupBy("region", "performance_tier") \
        .agg(
            sum("total_revenue").alias("tier_revenue"),
            sum("transaction_count").alias("tier_transactions"),
            avg("performance_score").alias("avg_score"),
            count("*").alias("segment_count")
        ) \
        .withColumn("tier_order",
                   when(col("performance_tier") == "Platinum", 1)
                   .when(col("performance_tier") == "Gold", 2)
                   .when(col("performance_tier") == "Silver", 3)
                   .otherwise(4)) \
        .orderBy("region", "tier_order") \
        .coalesce(10)  # Reduce partitions for final output
    
    final_report.cache()
    final_count = final_report.count()
    stage4_time = time.time() - stage4_start
    
    print(f"  Stage 4 completed: {final_count} report records in {stage4_time:.2f}s")
    print(f"  Final partitions: {final_report.rdd.getNumPartitions()}")
    
    # Pipeline Summary
    print("\n5. ETL Pipeline Summary:")
    print("-" * 40)
    
    total_pipeline_time = stage1_time + stage2_time + stage3_time + stage4_time
    
    pipeline_summary = {
        'Stage 1 (Quality & Enrichment)': f"{stage1_time:.2f}s",
        'Stage 2 (Aggregation)': f"{stage2_time:.2f}s",
        'Stage 3 (Scoring)': f"{stage3_time:.2f}s",
        'Stage 4 (Reporting)': f"{stage4_time:.2f}s",
        'Total Pipeline Time': f"{total_pipeline_time:.2f}s",
        'Records Processed': enriched_count,
        'Final Report Records': final_count,
        'Data Reduction': f"{(1 - final_count/enriched_count) * 100:.1f}%"
    }
    
    for key, value in pipeline_summary.items():
        print(f"  {key}: {value}")
    
    # Display final report
    print("\n6. Final Performance Report by Region & Tier:")
    print("-" * 40)
    final_report.show(20, truncate=False)
    
    # Optimization recommendations
    print("\n7. Pipeline Optimization Analysis:")
    print("-" * 40)
    
    print("\n  Parallelization Strategies Applied:")
    print("  ✓ Inter-Query: 4 analytics queries executed in parallel")
    print("  ✓ Intra-Query: Complex transformations distributed across partitions")
    print("  ✓ Partition-Level: Strategic repartitioning at each stage")
    print("  ✓ Task-Level: Optimized partition count for task distribution")
    print("  ✓ Stage-Level: Multi-stage pipeline with cached intermediate results")
    
    print("\n  Performance Optimizations:")
    print("  ✓ Caching: Intermediate results cached to avoid recomputation")
    print("  ✓ Partition Management: Reduced partitions progressively (100→80→40→10)")
    print("  ✓ Filter Pushdown: Early filtering to reduce data volume")
    print("  ✓ Column Pruning: Only necessary columns carried through pipeline")
    
    return {
        'analytics_results': analytics_results,
        'pipeline_results': {
            'enriched': enriched_data,
            'aggregated': aggregated_features,
            'scored': scored_data,
            'final_report': final_report
        },
        'metrics': pipeline_summary
    }

# Execute the comprehensive e-commerce analytics pipeline
ecommerce_results = ecommerce_analytics_pipeline()

def troubleshooting_guide():
    """
    Common parallelization issues and solutions
    """
    
    issues = {
        "1. Out of Memory Errors": {
            "symptoms": [
                "java.lang.OutOfMemoryError",
                "Container killed by YARN",
                "Executor lost"

            "causes": [
                "Too few partitions (large partition size)",

                "Insufficient executor memory"
            ],
            "solutions": [
                "Increase number of partitions: df.repartition(N)",
                "Increase executor memory: spark.executor.memory",
                "Use salting for skewed keys",
                "Enable dynamic allocation: spark.dynamicAllocation.enabled"
            ],

from pyspark.sql.functions import rand, concat, lit

def complete_optimized_pipeline():
    """
    Final demonstration combining all parallelization patterns
    with best practices applied
    """
    
    print("\nExecuting fully optimized multi-pattern pipeline...")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    pipeline_start = time.time()
    
    # ========================================================================
    # PHASE 1: DATA INGESTION & PREPARATION (Partition-Level Parallelism)
    # ========================================================================
    print("\n[PHASE 1] Data Ingestion & Preparation")
    phase1_start = time.time()
    
    # Optimal initial partitioning
    data_size = sales_df.count()
    optimal_partitions = max(int(data_size / 50000), 20)
    
    prepared_data = sales_df \
        .repartition(optimal_partitions, "region", "product_id") \
        .filter(col("amount") > 0) \
        .withColumn("transaction_date", to_date("sale_date")) \
        .withColumn("year", year("sale_date")) \
        .withColumn("quarter", quarter("sale_date")) \
        .withColumn("month", month("sale_date"))
    
    # Cache for reuse
    prepared_data.cache()
    prepared_count = prepared_data.count()
    
    phase1_time = time.time() - phase1_start
    print(f"  ✓ Prepared {prepared_count:,} records in {phase1_time:.2f}s")
    print(f"  ✓ Partitions: {prepared_data.rdd.getNumPartitions()}")
    
    # ========================================================================
    # PHASE 2: PARALLEL ANALYTICS (Inter-Query Parallelism)
    # ========================================================================
    print("\n[PHASE 2] Parallel Analytics Execution")
    phase2_start = time.time()
    
    def regional_analysis():
        """Regional performance analysis"""
        return prepared_data.groupBy("region", "year", "quarter") \
            .agg(
                sum("amount").alias("total_revenue"),
                count("sale_id").alias("transactions"),
                countDistinct("product_id").alias("unique_products"),
                avg("amount").alias("avg_transaction")
            ).cache()
    
    def product_analysis():
        """Product performance analysis"""
        return prepared_data.groupBy("product_id", "year", "month") \
            .agg(
                sum("amount").alias("monthly_revenue"),
                count("sale_id").alias("monthly_sales")
            ).cache()
    
    def temporal_analysis():
        """Time-based trend analysis"""
        return prepared_data.groupBy("transaction_date") \
            .agg(
                sum("amount").alias("daily_revenue"),
                count("sale_id").alias("daily_transactions")
            ).cache()
    
    # Execute analytics in parallel
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=3) as executor:
        regional_future = executor.submit(regional_analysis)
        product_future = executor.submit(product_analysis)
        temporal_future = executor.submit(temporal_analysis)
        
        regional_df = regional_future.result()
        product_df = product_future.result()
        temporal_df = temporal_future.result()
    
    phase2_time = time.time() - phase2_start
    print(f"  ✓ Completed 3 parallel analytics in {phase2_time:.2f}s")
    print(f"  ✓ Regional results: {regional_df.count():,} rows")
    print(f"  ✓ Product results: {product_df.count():,} rows")
    print(f"  ✓ Temporal results: {temporal_df.count():,} rows")
    
    # ========================================================================
    # PHASE 3: ADVANCED AGGREGATION (Intra-Query Parallelism)
    # ========================================================================
    print("\n[PHASE 3] Advanced Aggregation Pipeline")
    phase3_start = time.time()
    
    # Complex aggregation with window functions
    window_spec = Window.partitionBy("region", "year").orderBy(desc("total_revenue"))
    
    advanced_metrics = regional_df \
        .withColumn("quarter_rank", rank().over(window_spec)) \
        .withColumn("revenue_percentile", percent_rank().over(window_spec)) \
        .withColumn("running_total", 
                   sum("total_revenue").over(
                       window_spec.rowsBetween(Window.unboundedPreceding, 0)
                   )) \
        .filter(col("quarter_rank") <= 4)
    
    advanced_metrics.cache()
    advanced_count = advanced_metrics.count()
    
    phase3_time = time.time() - phase3_start
    print(f"  ✓ Generated {advanced_count:,} advanced metrics in {phase3_time:.2f}s")
    
    # ========================================================================
    # PHASE 4: ENRICHMENT WITH JOINS (Stage-Level Parallelism)
    # ========================================================================
    print("\n[PHASE 4] Data Enrichment with Optimized Joins")
    phase4_start = time.time()
    
    # Prepare customer dimension with broadcast
    customer_dim = customer_df.select("region", "segment").distinct()
    
    # Broadcast join for small dimension
    enriched_metrics = advanced_metrics.join(
        broadcast(customer_dim),
        on="region",
        how="left"
    )
    
    # Repartition for next aggregation
    enriched_metrics = enriched_metrics.repartition(30, "segment", "year")
    enriched_metrics.cache()
    enriched_count = enriched_metrics.count()
    
    phase4_time = time.time() - phase4_start
    print(f"  ✓ Enriched {enriched_count:,} records in {phase4_time:.2f}s")
    print(f"  ✓ Used broadcast join to avoid shuffle")
    
    # ========================================================================
    # PHASE 5: FINAL AGGREGATION (Task-Level Parallelism)
    # ========================================================================
    print("\n[PHASE 5] Final Aggregation & Scoring")
    phase5_start = time.time()
    
    final_summary = enriched_metrics.groupBy("segment", "year") \
        .agg(
            sum("total_revenue").alias("segment_revenue"),
            sum("transactions").alias("segment_transactions"),
            avg("avg_transaction").alias("segment_avg_transaction"),
            count("region").alias("active_regions")
        ) \
        .withColumn("performance_index",
                   (col("segment_revenue") / 1000000) * 
                   (col("segment_transactions") / 10000)) \
        .withColumn("tier",
                   when(col("performance_index") >= 100, "Elite")
                   .when(col("performance_index") >= 50, "Premium")
                   .when(col("performance_index") >= 25, "Standard")
                   .otherwise("Basic")) \
        .orderBy(desc("segment_revenue"))
    
    # Coalesce for final output
    final_summary = final_summary.coalesce(5)
    final_summary.cache()
    final_count = final_summary.count()
    
    phase5_time = time.time() - phase5_start
    print(f"  ✓ Generated {final_count:,} final summary records in {phase5_time:.2f}s")
    print(f"  ✓ Coalesced to {final_summary.rdd.getNumPartitions()} partitions for output")
    
    # ========================================================================
    # PHASE 6: OUTPUT & PERSISTENCE
    # ========================================================================
    print("\n[PHASE 6] Output & Persistence")
    phase6_start = time.time()
    
    # Write optimized output
    output_path = "/tmp/optimized_pipeline_output"
    
    final_summary.write \
        .mode("overwrite") \
        .option("compression", "snappy") \
        .partitionBy("year") \
        .parquet(output_path)
    
    phase6_time = time.time() - phase6_start
    print(f"  ✓ Written output in {phase6_time:.2f}s")
    print(f"  ✓ Output location: {output_path}")
    
    # ========================================================================
    # PIPELINE SUMMARY
    # ========================================================================
    total_pipeline_time = time.time() - pipeline_start
    
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("PIPELINE EXECUTION SUMMARY")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    summary_data = [
        ("Phase 1: Data Preparation", phase1_time, prepared_count, "Partition-Level"),
        ("Phase 2: Parallel Analytics", phase2_time, 
         regional_df.count() + product_df.count() + temporal_df.count(), "Inter-Query"),
        ("Phase 3: Advanced Aggregation", phase3_time, advanced_count, "Intra-Query"),
        ("Phase 4: Data Enrichment", phase4_time, enriched_count, "Stage-Level"),
        ("Phase 5: Final Aggregation", phase5_time, final_count, "Task-Level"),
        ("Phase 6: Output", phase6_time, final_count, "I/O Optimized")
    ]
    
    print(f"\n{'Phase':<30} {'Time (s)':<12} {'Records':<15} {'Pattern'}")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    for phase, exec_time, records, pattern in summary_data:
        print(f"{phase:<30} {exec_time:<12.2f} {records:<15,} {pattern}")
    
    print("-" * 80)
    print(f"{'TOTAL PIPELINE TIME':<30} {total_pipeline_time:<12.2f}")
    print(f"{'Data Reduction Ratio':<30} {prepared_count/final_count:<12.1f}x")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Display final results
    print("\nFINAL RESULTS (Top 10 Segments):")
    print("-" * 80)
    final_summary.show(10, truncate=False)
    
    # Cleanup
    prepared_data.unpersist()
    regional_df.unpersist()
    product_df.unpersist()
    temporal_df.unpersist()
    advanced_metrics.unpersist()
    enriched_metrics.unpersist()
    final_summary.unpersist()
    
    print("\n✓ Pipeline completed successfully!")
    print("✓ All cached data unpersisted")
    
    return {
        'execution_time': total_pipeline_time,
        'final_results': final_summary,
        'phase_metrics': summary_data
    }

# Execute the complete optimized pipeline
final_results = complete_optimized_pipeline()

# ============================================================================
# CLEANUP AND FINAL NOTES
# ============================================================================
print("\n\n" + "=" * 80)
print("CLEANUP AND FINAL NOTES")
print("=" * 80)

# Unpersist all cached DataFrames
sales_df.unpersist()
customer_df.unpersist()

print("\n✓ All resources cleaned up")
print("\nKey Takeaways:")
print("-" * 80)
print("""
1. Choose the right parallelization pattern for your use case

This comprehensive PySpark program demonstrates all 5 query parallelization patterns with:

1. **Inter-Query Parallelism**: Multiple independent queries executed concurrently using ThreadPoolExecutor
2. **Intra-Query Parallelism**: Complex queries with parallel transformations
```python
3. **Partition-Level Parallelism**: Strategic data partitioning using repartition, coalesce, and custom partitioners
4. **Task-Level Parallelism**: Fine-grained control over task execution with partition analysis and optimization
5. **Stage-Level Parallelism**: Multi-stage pipelines with optimized parallelism at each stage

    # Check parallelism
    try:
        shuffle_partitions = int(spark_session.conf.get('spark.sql.shuffle.partitions', '200'))
        if shuffle_partitions == 200:
            recommendations.append("💡 Consider adjusting spark.sql.shuffle.partitions based on data size")

    if recommendations:
        for rec in recommendations:
            print(f"  {rec}")
    else:
        print("  ✓ Configuration looks good!")
    
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)

def print_pattern_comparison_matrix():
    """

COMMON PITFALLS & SOLUTIONS
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

❌ PITFALL: Too many small partitions
✓ SOLUTION: Use coalesce() to reduce partitions

❌ PITFALL: Data skew in joins/aggregations
✓ SOLUTION: Use salting or enable AQE skew join

❌ PITFALL: Unnecessary shuffles
✓ SOLUTION: Partition by join/group keys, use broadcast

❌ PITFALL: Out of memory errors
✓ SOLUTION: Increase partitions, executor memory, or use disk

❌ PITFALL: Caching everything
✓ SOLUTION: Only cache frequently reused DataFrames

❌ PITFALL: Using collect() on large data
✓ SOLUTION: Use take(), show(), or write to storage

❌ PITFALL: Too few partitions for large data
✓ SOLUTION: Repartition to 2-4x number of cores

SALTING TECHNIQUE FOR SKEWED DATA
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

from pyspark.sql.functions import rand, concat, lit, split

# Add salt to skewed key
salted_df = df.withColumn(
    "salted_key",
    concat(col("skewed_key"), lit("_"), (rand() * 10).cast("int"))
)

# Aggregate with salt
salted_agg = salted_df.groupBy("salted_key") \\
    .agg(sum("value").alias("sum_val"))

# Remove salt and final aggregation
final_result = salted_agg \\
    .withColumn("original_key", split(col("salted_key"), "_")[0]) \\
    .groupBy("original_key") \\
    .agg(sum("sum_val").alias("final_sum"))

    # Business logic for partitioning
    if key in high_priority_keys:
        return hash(key) % 10  # More partitions for priority
    else:
        return 10 + (hash(key) % 40)  # Fewer for others

import time

def benchmark_query(df, query_func, name, iterations=3):
    """Benchmark a query with multiple iterations"""
    times = []
    
    for i in range(iterations):
        start = time.time()
        result = query_func(df)
        count = result.count()  # Force execution
        elapsed = time.time() - start
        times.append(elapsed)
        print(f"  Iteration {i+1}: {elapsed:.2f}s ({count:,} rows)")
    
    avg_time = sum(times) / len(times)
    print(f"  {name} - Average: {avg_time:.2f}s")
    return avg_time

# Usage
def query1(df):
    return df.groupBy("region").agg(sum("amount"))

benchmark_query(df, query1, "Regional Aggregation")

DATA SKEW DETECTION
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def detect_skew(df, column, threshold=2.0):
    """Detect data skew in a column"""
    
    # Get distribution
    dist = df.groupBy(column).count() \\
        .agg(
            avg("count").alias("avg_count"),
            stddev("count").alias("stddev_count"),
            max("count").alias("max_count")
        ).collect()[0]
    
    # Calculate coefficient of variation
    cv = dist["stddev_count"] / dist["avg_count"]
    skew_factor = dist["max_count"] / dist["avg_count"]
    
    print(f"Skew Analysis for '{column}':")
    print(f"  Average: {dist['avg_count']:.0f}")
    print(f"  Max: {dist['max_count']:.0f}")
    print(f"  Skew Factor: {skew_factor:.2f}x")
    print(f"  CV: {cv:.2f}")
    
    if skew_factor > threshold:
        print(f"  ⚠️  SKEWED! Consider salting or AQE skew join")
    else:
        print(f"  ✓ Distribution is reasonable")
    
    return skew_factor

# Usage
detect_skew(df, "region", threshold=2.0)

OPTIMAL PARTITION CALCULATOR
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def calculate_optimal_partitions(
    df,
    target_partition_size_mb=128,
    min_partitions=None,
    max_partitions=None
):
    """Calculate optimal number of partitions"""
    
    # Estimate data size (approximate)
    sample_size = df.limit(1000).count()
    if sample_size == 0:
        return spark.sparkContext.defaultParallelism
    
    # Rough estimate of total size
    total_rows = df.count()
    avg_row_size = 1024  # Assume 1KB per row (adjust as needed)
    estimated_size_mb = (total_rows * avg_row_size) / (1024 * 1024)
    
    # Calculate partitions
    optimal = int(estimated_size_mb / target_partition_size_mb)
    
    # Apply constraints
    cores = int(spark.conf.get("spark.default.parallelism", "1"))
    optimal = max(optimal, cores * 2)  # At least 2x cores
    
    if min_partitions:
        optimal = max(optimal, min_partitions)
    if max_partitions:
        optimal = min(optimal, max_partitions)
    
    print(f"Partition Calculation:")
    print(f"  Estimated Data Size: {estimated_size_mb:.2f} MB")
    print(f"  Target Partition Size: {target_partition_size_mb} MB")
    print(f"  Recommended Partitions: {optimal}")
    print(f"  Available Cores: {cores}")
    
    return optimal

# Usage
optimal_partitions = calculate_optimal_partitions(df)
df_optimized = df.repartition(optimal_partitions)

EXAMPLE 1: HANDLING SKEWED DATA WITH SALTING
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

from pyspark.sql.functions import rand, concat, lit, split, col

def handle_skewed_join(skewed_df, normal_df, join_key, salt_factor=10):
    \"\"\"
    Handle skewed join using salting technique
    
    Args:
        skewed_df: DataFrame with skewed distribution
        normal_df: DataFrame to join with
        join_key: Column name to join on
        salt_factor: Number of salt values (default: 10)
    \"\"\"
    
```python
    # Step 1: Add salt to skewed DataFrame
    skewed_salted = skewed_df.withColumn(
        "salt",
        (rand() * salt_factor).cast("int")
    ).withColumn(
        "salted_key",
        concat(col(join_key), lit("_"), col("salt"))
    )
    
    # Step 2: Explode normal DataFrame with all salt values
    from pyspark.sql.functions import explode, array, lit as lit_val
    
    salt_array = array([lit_val(i) for i in range(salt_factor)])
    normal_exploded = normal_df.withColumn("salt", explode(salt_array)) \
        .withColumn(
            "salted_key",
            concat(col(join_key), lit("_"), col("salt"))
        )
    
    # Step 3: Join on salted key
    result = skewed_salted.join(normal_exploded, "salted_key") \
        .drop("salt", "salted_key")
    
    return result

# Usage

    skewed_sales_df,
    customer_df,

EXAMPLE 2: DYNAMIC PARTITION OPTIMIZATION
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def optimize_partitions_dynamically(df, target_partition_size_mb=128):
    \"\"\"
    Dynamically optimize DataFrame partitions based on data size
    
    Args:
        df: Input DataFrame
        target_partition_size_mb: Target size per partition in MB
    \"\"\"
    from pyspark.sql import DataFrame
    
    # Estimate data size
    sample_count = df.limit(10000).count()
    if sample_count == 0:
        return df
    
    # Get approximate row size by sampling
    sample_df = df.limit(1000)
    sample_size_bytes = sample_df.rdd.map(
        lambda row: len(str(row))
    ).sum()
    avg_row_size = sample_size_bytes / sample_count if sample_count > 0 else 1000
    
    # Calculate total size and optimal partitions
    total_rows = df.count()
    total_size_mb = (total_rows * avg_row_size) / (1024 * 1024)
    optimal_partitions = max(
        int(total_size_mb / target_partition_size_mb),
        1
    )
    
    # Get current partitions
    current_partitions = df.rdd.getNumPartitions()
    
    print(f"Partition Optimization:")
    print(f"  Estimated size: {total_size_mb:.2f} MB")
    print(f"  Current partitions: {current_partitions}")
    print(f"  Optimal partitions: {optimal_partitions}")
    
    # Repartition or coalesce as needed
    if optimal_partitions > current_partitions * 1.5:
        print(f"  Action: Repartitioning to {optimal_partitions}")
        return df.repartition(optimal_partitions)
    elif optimal_partitions < current_partitions * 0.5:
        print(f"  Action: Coalescing to {optimal_partitions}")
        return df.coalesce(optimal_partitions)
    else:
        print(f"  Action: No change needed")
        return df

# Usage
optimized_df = optimize_partitions_dynamically(df, target_partition_size_mb=128)

class CacheManager:
    \"\"\"Manage DataFrame caching with automatic cleanup\"\"\"
    
    def __init__(self, spark_session):
        self.spark = spark_session
        self.cached_dfs = {}
        self.access_count = {}
    
    def cache(self, df, name, storage_level=None):
        \"\"\"Cache a DataFrame with tracking\"\"\"
        from pyspark import StorageLevel
        
        if storage_level:
            df.persist(storage_level)
        else:
            df.cache()
        
        self.cached_dfs[name] = df
        self.access_count[name] = 0
        
        print(f"✓ Cached '{name}' with {df.rdd.getNumPartitions()} partitions")
        return df
    
    def get(self, name):
        \"\"\"Get cached DataFrame and track access\"\"\"
        if name in self.cached_dfs:
            self.access_count[name] += 1
            return self.cached_dfs[name]
        return None
    
    def unpersist(self, name):
        \"\"\"Unpersist a specific DataFrame\"\"\"
        if name in self.cached_dfs:
            self.cached_dfs[name].unpersist()
            del self.cached_dfs[name]
            print(f"✓ Unpersisted '{name}'")
    
    def cleanup_unused(self, min_access_count=2):
        \"\"\"Clean up DataFrames accessed fewer than threshold times\"\"\"
        to_remove = [
            name for name, count in self.access_count.items()
            if count < min_access_count
        ]
        
        for name in to_remove:
            self.unpersist(name)
    
    def cleanup_all(self):
        \"\"\"Unpersist all cached DataFrames\"\"\"
        for name in list(self.cached_dfs.keys()):
            self.unpersist(name)
    
    def report(self):
        \"\"\"Print cache status report\"\"\"
        print("\nCache Status Report:")
        print("-" * 60)
        for name, df in self.cached_dfs.items():
            access = self.access_count.get(name, 0)
            partitions = df.rdd.getNumPartitions()
            print(f"  {name:<20} Accesses: {access:<5} Partitions: {partitions}")
        print("-" * 60)

# Usage
cache_mgr = CacheManager(spark)

# Cache important DataFrames
sales_cached = cache_mgr.cache(sales_df, "sales")
customer_cached = cache_mgr.cache(customer_df, "customers")

# Use cached data
result1 = cache_mgr.get("sales").groupBy("region").count()
result2 = cache_mgr.get("sales").groupBy("product").count()

# Report and cleanup
cache_mgr.report()
cache_mgr.cleanup_unused(min_access_count=2)
cache_mgr.cleanup_all()

EXAMPLE 4: PARALLEL DATA QUALITY CHECKS
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor, as_completed
from pyspark.sql.functions import col, isnan, isnull, when, count

def parallel_data_quality_checks(df):
    \"\"\"Run multiple data quality checks in parallel\"\"\"
    
    def check_nulls(df):
        \"\"\"Check for null values in all columns\"\"\"
        print("  [Check 1] Checking for null values...")
        null_counts = df.select([
            count(when(col(c).isNull(), c)).alias(c)
            for c in df.columns
        ]).collect()[0].asDict()
        
        return {
            "check": "null_values",
            "results": {k: v for k, v in null_counts.items() if v > 0}
        }
    
    def check_duplicates(df):
        \"\"\"Check for duplicate rows\"\"\"
        print("  [Check 2] Checking for duplicates...")
        total_count = df.count()
        distinct_count = df.distinct().count()
        duplicates = total_count - distinct_count
        
        return {
            "check": "duplicates",
            "results": {
                "total_rows": total_count,
                "distinct_rows": distinct_count,
                "duplicate_count": duplicates
            }
        }
    
    def check_data_types(df):
        \"\"\"Validate data types\"\"\"
        print("  [Check 3] Checking data types...")
        schema_info = {
            field.name: str(field.dataType)
            for field in df.schema.fields
        }
        
        return {
            "check": "data_types",
            "results": schema_info
        }
    
    def check_value_ranges(df):
        \"\"\"Check value ranges for numeric columns\"\"\"
        print("  [Check 4] Checking value ranges...")
        numeric_cols = [
            field.name for field in df.schema.fields
            if str(field.dataType) in ['IntegerType', 'LongType', 'DoubleType', 'FloatType']
        ]
        
        if not numeric_cols:
            return {"check": "value_ranges", "results": {}}
        
        stats = df.select(numeric_cols).summary("min", "max", "mean").collect()
        
        results = {}
        for col_name in numeric_cols:
            results[col_name] = {
                "min": stats[0][col_name],
                "max": stats[1][col_name],
                "mean": stats[2][col_name]
            }
        
        return {
            "check": "value_ranges",
            "results": results
        }
    
    # Execute all checks in parallel
    print("\nRunning parallel data quality checks...")
    start_time = time.time()
    
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=4) as executor:
        futures = {
            executor.submit(check_nulls, df): "nulls",
            executor.submit(check_duplicates, df): "duplicates",
            executor.submit(check_data_types, df): "types",
            executor.submit(check_value_ranges, df): "ranges"
        }
        
        results = {}
        for future in as_completed(futures):
            check_name = futures[future]
            try:
                result = future.result()
                results[check_name] = result
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"  Error in {check_name}: {str(e)}")
    
    elapsed = time.time() - start_time
    print(f"\n✓ All quality checks completed in {elapsed:.2f}s")
    
    # Print summary
    print("\nData Quality Summary:")
    print("-" * 60)
    for check_name, result in results.items():
        print(f"\n{result['check'].upper()}:")
        if isinstance(result['results'], dict):
            for key, value in result['results'].items():
                print(f"  {key}: {value}")
    
    return results

# Usage
quality_results = parallel_data_quality_checks(sales_df)

EXAMPLE 5: INCREMENTAL PROCESSING WITH CHECKPOINTING
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

class IncrementalProcessor:
    \"\"\"Process data incrementally with checkpointing\"\"\"
    
    def __init__(self, spark, checkpoint_dir):
        self.spark = spark
        self.checkpoint_dir = checkpoint_dir
        spark.sparkContext.setCheckpointDir(checkpoint_dir)
    
    def process_incremental(self, df, partition_col, batch_size=100000):
        \"\"\"
        Process large DataFrame in batches with checkpointing
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            partition_col: Column to partition processing by
            batch_size: Records per batch
        \"\"\"
        from pyspark.sql.functions import monotonically_increasing_id
        
        # Add row number for batching
        df_with_id = df.withColumn("row_id", monotonically_increasing_id())
        
        # Determine number of batches
        total_rows = df_with_id.count()
        num_batches = (total_rows // batch_size) + 1
        
        print(f"Processing {total_rows:,} rows in {num_batches} batches")
        
        results = []
        
        for batch_num in range(num_batches):
            start_id = batch_num * batch_size
            end_id = start_id + batch_size
            
            print(f"\nProcessing batch {batch_num + 1}/{num_batches}...")
            
            # Process batch
            batch_df = df_with_id.filter(
                (col("row_id") >= start_id) & (col("row_id") < end_id)
            )
            
            # Your processing logic here
            processed_batch = batch_df.groupBy(partition_col).agg(
                count("*").alias("count"),
                sum("amount").alias("total")
            )
            
            # Checkpoint every 10 batches to truncate lineage
            if batch_num % 10 == 0:
                processed_batch = processed_batch.checkpoint()
                print(f"  Checkpointed at batch {batch_num + 1}")
            
            results.append(processed_batch)
        
        # Union all batches
        final_result = results[0]
        for batch_result in results[1:]:
            final_result = final_result.union(batch_result)
        
        # Final aggregation
        final_result = final_result.groupBy(partition_col).agg(
            sum("count").alias("total_count"),
            sum("total").alias("total_amount")
        )
        
        return final_result

# Usage
processor = IncrementalProcessor(spark, "/tmp/checkpoints")
result = processor.process_incremental(
    large_df,
    partition_col="region",
    batch_size=100000
)

from functools import wraps

def adaptive_repartition(partition_key=None, target_size_mb=128):
    \"\"\"
    Decorator to automatically repartition DataFrame before processing
    \"\"\"
    def decorator(func):
        @wraps(func)
        def wrapper(df, *args, **kwargs):
            # Calculate optimal partitions
            row_count = df.count()
            if row_count == 0:
                return func(df, *args, **kwargs)
            
            # Estimate size (rough approximation)
            avg_row_size = 1024  # 1KB assumption
            total_size_mb = (row_count * avg_row_size) / (1024 * 1024)
            optimal_partitions = max(int(total_size_mb / target_size_mb), 1)
            
            current_partitions = df.rdd.getNumPartitions()
            
            # Repartition if needed
            if abs(optimal_partitions - current_partitions) / current_partitions > 0.3:
                print(f"Adaptive repartition: {current_partitions} → {optimal_partitions}")
                if partition_key:
                    df = df.repartition(optimal_partitions, partition_key)
                else:
                    df = df.repartition(optimal_partitions)
            
            # Execute function
            return func(df, *args, **kwargs)
        
        
```python
        return wrapper
    return decorator

EXAMPLE 7: PARTITION SKEW ANALYZER AND REBALANCER
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

class PartitionAnalyzer:
    \"\"\"Analyze and rebalance skewed partitions\"\"\"
    
    @staticmethod
    def analyze_skew(df, threshold=2.0):
        \"\"\"
        Analyze partition skew and provide recommendations
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            threshold: Skew threshold (max/avg ratio)
        
        Returns:
            Dictionary with analysis results
        \"\"\"
        # Get partition sizes
        partition_sizes = df.rdd.mapPartitionsWithIndex(
            lambda idx, it: [(idx, sum(1 for _ in it))]
        ).collect()
        
        if not partition_sizes:
            return {"skewed": False, "message": "No data"}
        
        sizes = [size for _, size in partition_sizes]
        total_records = sum(sizes)
        num_partitions = len(sizes)
        avg_size = total_records / num_partitions
        max_size = max(sizes)
        min_size = min(sizes)
        
        skew_factor = max_size / avg_size if avg_size > 0 else 0
        
        # Identify skewed partitions
        skewed_partitions = [
            (idx, size, size/avg_size)
            for idx, size in partition_sizes
            if size > avg_size * threshold
        ]
        
        analysis = {
            "total_records": total_records,
            "num_partitions": num_partitions,
            "avg_size": avg_size,
            "min_size": min_size,
            "max_size": max_size,
            "skew_factor": skew_factor,
            "skewed": skew_factor > threshold,
            "skewed_partitions": skewed_partitions
        }
        
        # Print report
        print("\nPartition Skew Analysis:")
        print("-" * 60)
        print(f"  Total Records: {total_records:,}")
        print(f"  Partitions: {num_partitions}")
        print(f"  Average Size: {avg_size:,.0f}")
        print(f"  Min Size: {min_size:,}")
        print(f"  Max Size: {max_size:,}")
        print(f"  Skew Factor: {skew_factor:.2f}x")
        
        if skewed_partitions:
            print(f"\n  ⚠️  {len(skewed_partitions)} skewed partitions detected:")
            for idx, size, factor in skewed_partitions[:5]:
                print(f"    Partition {idx}: {size:,} records ({factor:.2f}x avg)")
        else:
            print("\n  ✓ No significant skew detected")
        
        return analysis
    
    @staticmethod
    def rebalance(df, target_partitions=None):
        \"\"\"
        Rebalance DataFrame to eliminate skew
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            target_partitions: Target number of partitions (auto if None)
        \"\"\"
        analysis = PartitionAnalyzer.analyze_skew(df)
        
        if not analysis["skewed"]:
            print("\n✓ No rebalancing needed")
            return df
        
        # Calculate target partitions if not specified
        if target_partitions is None:
            target_partitions = analysis["num_partitions"]
        
        print(f"\nRebalancing to {target_partitions} partitions...")
        
        # Use repartition to evenly distribute
        rebalanced = df.repartition(target_partitions)
        
        # Verify rebalancing
        print("\nAfter rebalancing:")
        PartitionAnalyzer.analyze_skew(rebalanced)
        
        return rebalanced

# Usage
analyzer = PartitionAnalyzer()

# Analyze current skew
analysis = analyzer.analyze_skew(sales_df)

# Rebalance if skewed
if analysis["skewed"]:
    balanced_df = analyzer.rebalance(sales_df, target_partitions=100)
else:
    balanced_df = sales_df

EXAMPLE 8: MULTI-LEVEL CACHING STRATEGY
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

from pyspark import StorageLevel

class MultiLevelCache:
    \"\"\"Implement multi-level caching strategy\"\"\"
    
    def __init__(self, spark):
        self.spark = spark
        self.hot_cache = {}    # Frequently accessed - MEMORY_ONLY
        self.warm_cache = {}   # Moderately accessed - MEMORY_AND_DISK
        self.cold_cache = {}   # Rarely accessed - DISK_ONLY
        self.access_count = {}
    
    def cache(self, df, name):
        \"\"\"Cache DataFrame with automatic tier assignment\"\"\"
        # Start in warm cache
        cached_df = df.persist(StorageLevel.MEMORY_AND_DISK)
        self.warm_cache[name] = cached_df
        self.access_count[name] = 0
        
        print(f"✓ Cached '{name}' in WARM tier")
        return cached_df
    
    def get(self, name):
        \"\"\"Get cached DataFrame and update tier if needed\"\"\"
        # Check all tiers
        if name in self.hot_cache:
            df = self.hot_cache[name]
            tier = "HOT"
        elif name in self.warm_cache:
            df = self.warm_cache[name]
            tier = "WARM"
        elif name in self.cold_cache:
            df = self.cold_cache[name]
            tier = "COLD"
        else:
            return None
        
        # Update access count
        self.access_count[name] = self.access_count.get(name, 0) + 1
        
        # Promote to hot tier if frequently accessed
        if self.access_count[name] > 5 and tier != "HOT":
            self._promote_to_hot(name, df)
        
        return df
    
    def _promote_to_hot(self, name, df):
        \"\"\"Promote DataFrame to hot tier\"\"\"
        # Remove from current tier
        if name in self.warm_cache:
            del self.warm_cache[name]
        elif name in self.cold_cache:
            del self.cold_cache[name]
        
        # Unpersist and re-cache in memory
        df.unpersist()
        hot_df = df.persist(StorageLevel.MEMORY_ONLY)
        self.hot_cache[name] = hot_df
        
        print(f"↑ Promoted '{name}' to HOT tier")
    
    def _demote_to_cold(self, name):
        \"\"\"Demote DataFrame to cold tier\"\"\"
        if name in self.warm_cache:
            df = self.warm_cache[name]
            del self.warm_cache[name]
            
            df.unpersist()
            cold_df = df.persist(StorageLevel.DISK_ONLY)
            self.cold_cache[name] = cold_df
            
            print(f"↓ Demoted '{name}' to COLD tier")
    
    def optimize_tiers(self):
        \"\"\"Optimize cache tiers based on access patterns\"\"\"
        print("\nOptimizing cache tiers...")
        
        # Demote warm cache items with low access
        for name in list(self.warm_cache.keys()):
            if self.access_count.get(name, 0) < 2:
                self._demote_to_cold(name)
    
    def report(self):
        \"\"\"Print cache tier report\"\"\"
        print("\nMulti-Level Cache Report:")
        print("-" * 60)
        
        print(f"\nHOT Tier (MEMORY_ONLY): {len(self.hot_cache)} items")
        for name in self.hot_cache.keys():
            print(f"  {name}: {self.access_count.get(name, 0)} accesses")
        
        print(f"\nWARM Tier (MEMORY_AND_DISK): {len(self.warm_cache)} items")
        for name in self.warm_cache.keys():
            print(f"  {name}: {self.access_count.get(name, 0)} accesses")
        
        print(f"\nCOLD Tier (DISK_ONLY): {len(self.cold_cache)} items")
        for name in self.cold_cache.keys():
            print(f"  {name}: {self.access_count.get(name, 0)} accesses")
        
        print("-" * 60)
    
    def cleanup_all(self):
        \"\"\"Cleanup all cached DataFrames\"\"\"
        for cache_dict in [self.hot_cache, self.warm_cache, self.cold_cache]:
            for df in cache_dict.values():
                df.unpersist()
        
        self.hot_cache.clear()
        self.warm_cache.clear()
        self.cold_cache.clear()
        print("\n✓ All cache tiers cleared")

# Usage
cache = MultiLevelCache(spark)

# Cache DataFrames
sales_cached = cache.cache(sales_df, "sales")
customer_cached = cache.cache(customer_df, "customers")

# Access multiple times (will be promoted to hot tier)
for i in range(6):
    df = cache.get("sales")
    result = df.count()

# Optimize tiers based on access patterns
cache.optimize_tiers()

# View report
cache.report()

# Cleanup
cache.cleanup_all()

class OptimizedWriter:
    \"\"\"Write DataFrames with optimized partitioning\"\"\"
    
    @staticmethod
    def write_optimized(df, output_path, partition_cols=None, 
                       file_format="parquet", mode="overwrite",
                       target_file_size_mb=128):
        \"\"\"
        Write DataFrame with optimized file sizes
        
        Args:
            df: DataFrame to write
            output_path: Output path
            partition_cols: Columns to partition by
            file_format: Output format (parquet, orc, csv, etc.)
            mode: Write mode
            target_file_size_mb: Target file size in MB
        \"\"\"
        print(f"\nOptimized Write Configuration:")
        print("-" * 60)
        
        # Calculate optimal partitions for writing
        total_rows = df.count()
        avg_row_size = 1024  # Estimate 1KB per row
        total_size_mb = (total_rows * avg_row_size) / (1024 * 1024)
        
        optimal_files = max(int(total_size_mb / target_file_size_mb), 1)
        
        print(f"  Total rows: {total_rows:,}")
        print(f"  Estimated size: {total_size_mb:.2f} MB")
        print(f"  Target file size: {target_file_size_mb} MB")
        print(f"  Optimal files: {optimal_files}")
        
        # Coalesce to optimal number of partitions
        optimized_df = df.coalesce(optimal_files)
        
        # Configure write options
        writer = optimized_df.write.mode(mode)
        
        # Set format-specific options
        if file_format == "parquet":
            writer = writer \
                .option("compression", "snappy") \
                .option("parquet.block.size", 134217728)  # 128MB
        elif file_format == "orc":
            writer = writer \
                .option("compression", "snappy") \
                .option("orc.stripe.size", 67108864)  # 64MB
        
        # Add max records per file
        writer = writer.option("maxRecordsPerFile", 
                              int(target_file_size_mb * 1024 * 1024 / avg_row_size))
        
        # Write with or without partitioning
        if partition_cols:
            print(f"  Partitioning by: {', '.join(partition_cols)}")
            writer.partitionBy(*partition_cols).format(file_format).save(output_path)
        else:
            writer.format(file_format).save(output_path)
        
        print(f"\n✓ Data written to {output_path}")
        
        # Verify output
        written_df = spark.read.format(file_format).load(output_path)
        written_count = written_df.count()
        
        print(f"✓ Verification: {written_count:,} rows written")
        
        return written_df

# Usage
writer = OptimizedWriter()

# Write with optimization
result = writer.write_optimized(
    df=sales_df,
    output_path="/tmp/optimized_sales",
    partition_cols=["year", "month"],
    file_format="parquet",
    target_file_size_mb=128
)

import time
from datetime import datetime

class PerformanceProfiler:
    \"\"\"Profile PySpark operations comprehensively\"\"\"
    
    def __init__(self, spark):
        self.spark = spark
        self.profiles = []
    
    def profile(self, name):
        \"\"\"Decorator to profile a function\"\"\"
        def decorator(func):
            @wraps(func)
            def wrapper(*args, **kwargs):
                print(f"\n{'='*60}")
                print(f"Profiling: {name}")
                print(f"{'='*60}")
                
                # Get initial metrics
                start_time = time.time()
                start_timestamp = datetime.now()
                
                # Execute function
                result = func(*args, **kwargs)
                
                # Force evaluation if result is DataFrame
                if hasattr(result, 'count'):
                    result_count = result.count()
                    result_partitions = result.rdd.getNumPartitions()
                else:
                    result_count = None
                    result_partitions = None
                
                # Calculate metrics
                end_time = time.time()
                execution_time = end_time - start_time
                
                # Store profile
                profile = {
                    'name': name,
                    'timestamp': start_timestamp,
                    'execution_time': execution_time,
                    'result_count': result_count,
                    'result_partitions': result_partitions
                }
                
                self.profiles.append(profile)

"""
Technical Metadata Pattern captures structural and technical information about data assets
including schema, data types, formats, storage details, and physical characteristics.
"""

class TechnicalMetadataPattern:
    """
    Manages technical metadata for data assets including schema, storage, and format information.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark_session):
        self.spark = spark_session
        
    def create_technical_metadata_schema(self):
        """Define schema for technical metadata catalog"""
        return StructType([
            StructField("asset_id", StringType(), False),
            StructField("asset_name", StringType(), False),
            StructField("asset_type", StringType(), False),  # table, view, file, stream
            StructField("database_name", StringType(), True),
            StructField("schema_name", StringType(), True),
            StructField("columns", ArrayType(StructType([
                StructField("column_name", StringType(), False),
                StructField("data_type", StringType(), False),
                StructField("is_nullable", BooleanType(), False),
                StructField("is_primary_key", BooleanType(), False),
                StructField("is_foreign_key", BooleanType(), False),
                StructField("precision", IntegerType(), True),
                StructField("scale", IntegerType(), True),
                StructField("max_length", IntegerType(), True)
            ])), False),
            StructField("storage_format", StringType(), False),  # parquet, delta, csv, json
            StructField("compression_type", StringType(), True),
            StructField("partition_columns", ArrayType(StringType()), True),
            StructField("storage_location", StringType(), False),
            StructField("file_size_bytes", LongType(), True),
            StructField("row_count", LongType(), True),
            StructField("created_timestamp", TimestampType(), False),
            StructField("last_modified_timestamp", TimestampType(), False),
            StructField("checksum", StringType(), True),
            StructField("encoding", StringType(), True),
            StructField("delimiter", StringType(), True),
            StructField("header_present", BooleanType(), True),
            StructField("statistics", MapType(StringType(), StringType()), True)
        ])
    
    def extract_technical_metadata(self, df, asset_name, storage_location):
        """
        Extract technical metadata from a DataFrame
        
        Args:
            df: Source DataFrame
            asset_name: Name of the data asset
            storage_location: Physical storage path
            
        Returns:
            DataFrame with technical metadata
        """
        # Extract column metadata
        columns_metadata = []
        for field in df.schema.fields:
            col_meta = {
                "column_name": field.name,
                "data_type": str(field.dataType),
                "is_nullable": field.nullable,
                "is_primary_key": False,  # Would need additional logic to determine
                "is_foreign_key": False,
                "precision": None,
                "scale": None,
                "max_length": None
            }
            columns_metadata.append(col_meta)
        
        # Calculate statistics
        row_count = df.count()
        
        # Create metadata record
        metadata = [{
            "asset_id": hashlib.md5(asset_name.encode()).hexdigest(),
            "asset_name": asset_name,
            "asset_type": "table",
            "database_name": "default",
            "schema_name": "public",
            "columns": columns_metadata,
            "storage_format": "parquet",
            "compression_type": "snappy",
            "partition_columns": [],
            "storage_location": storage_location,
            "file_size_bytes": None,
            "row_count": row_count,
            "created_timestamp": datetime.now(),
            "last_modified_timestamp": datetime.now(),
            "checksum": None,
            "encoding": "UTF-8",
            "delimiter": None,
            "header_present": True,
            "statistics": {
                "row_count": str(row_count),
                "column_count": str(len(df.columns))
            }
        }]
        
        return self.spark.createDataFrame(metadata, self.create_technical_metadata_schema())
    
    def profile_data_quality(self, df):
        """
        Profile data quality metrics as part of technical metadata
        
        Returns:
            Dictionary with quality metrics
        """
        quality_metrics = {}
        
        for col_name in df.columns:
            col_metrics = {
                "null_count": df.filter(col(col_name).isNull()).count(),
                "distinct_count": df.select(col_name).distinct().count(),
                "null_percentage": (df.filter(col(col_name).isNull()).count() / df.count()) * 100
            }
            quality_metrics[col_name] = col_metrics
        
        return quality_metrics

    def calculate_data_quality_metrics(self, df, quality_rules):
        """
        Calculate comprehensive data quality metrics
        
        Args:
            df: DataFrame to assess
            quality_rules: Dictionary of quality rules to apply
            
        Returns:
            Dictionary with quality scores
        """
        total_records = df.count()
        
        # Completeness: Percentage of non-null values
        completeness_scores = []
        for col_name in df.columns:
            non_null_count = df.filter(col(col_name).isNotNull()).count()
            completeness_scores.append(non_null_count / total_records)
        completeness_score = sum(completeness_scores) / len(completeness_scores) * 100
        
        # Validity: Records meeting validation rules
        validity_score = 100.0  # Default
        if quality_rules.get("validity_checks"):
            valid_records = df
            for rule in quality_rules["validity_checks"]:
                valid_records = valid_records.filter(expr(rule))
            validity_score = (valid_records.count() / total_records) * 100
        
        # Overall quality score
        overall_score = (completeness_score + validity_score) / 2
        
        return {
            "completeness_score": completeness_score,
            "accuracy_score": 95.0,  # Would need business rules to calculate
            "consistency_score": 98.0,  # Would need cross-system validation
            "timeliness_score": 100.0,  # Based on SLA compliance
            "validity_score": validity_score,
            "overall_quality_score": overall_score
        }

    def add_rating(self, asset_id, asset_name, user_id, user_name, rating, review_text=None):
        """
        Add a user rating for a data asset
        
        Args:
            asset_id: Unique asset identifier
            asset_name: Name of the asset
            user_id: ID of the user providing rating
            user_name: Name of the user
            rating: Rating value (1-5)
            review_text: Optional review text
        """
        rating_entry = {
            "user_id": user_id,
            "user_name": user_name,
            "rating": rating,
            "rating_date": datetime.now(),
            "review_text": review_text
        }
        
        return rating_entry
    
    def add_comment(self, asset_id, user_id, user_name, comment_text, parent_comment_id=None):
        """
        Add a user comment to a data asset
        """
        comment_id = hashlib.md5(f"{asset_id}{user_id}{datetime.now()}".encode()).hexdigest()
        
        comment_entry = {
            "comment_id": comment_id,
            "user_id": user_id,
            "user_name": user_name,
            "comment_text": comment_text,
            "comment_date": datetime.now(),
            "parent_comment_id": parent_comment_id,
            "likes_count": 0,
            "is_edited": False,
            "edited_date": None
        }
        
        return comment_entry
    
    def track_usage(self, asset_id, user_id, user_name, action_type):
        """
        Track user interactions with data assets
        
        Args:
            asset_id: Asset identifier
            user_id: User identifier
            user_name: User name
            action_type: Type of action (view, download, query)
        """
        usage_event = {
            "asset_id": asset_id,
            "user_id": user_id,
            "user_name": user_name,
            "action_type": action_type,
            "action_timestamp": datetime.now()
        }
        
        return usage_event
    
    def calculate_popularity_score(self, ratings_count, views_count, favorites_count, comments_count):
        """
        Calculate popularity score based on user engagement metrics
        
        Returns:
            Popularity score (0-100)
        """
        # Weighted scoring algorithm
        weights = {
            "ratings": 0.3,
            "views": 0.2,
            "favorites": 0.35,
            "comments": 0.15
        }
        
        # Normalize values (assuming max values for normalization)
        max_ratings = 100
        max_views = 10000
        max_favorites = 500
        max_comments = 200
        
        normalized_ratings = min(ratings_count / max_ratings, 1.0)
        normalized_views = min(views_count / max_views, 1.0)
        normalized_favorites = min(favorites_count / max_favorites, 1.0)
        normalized_comments = min(comments_count / max_comments, 1.0)
        
        popularity_score = (
            normalized_ratings * weights["ratings"] +
            normalized_views * weights["views"] +
            normalized_favorites * weights["favorites"] +
            normalized_comments * weights["comments"]
        ) * 100
        
        return round(popularity_score, 2)
    
    def create_social_metadata_summary(self, asset_id, asset_name, social_data):
        """
        Create a comprehensive social metadata record
        
        Args:
            asset_id: Asset identifier
            asset_name: Asset name
            social_data: Dictionary containing all social metadata
        """
        # Calculate average rating
        ratings = social_data.get("user_ratings", [])
        avg_rating = sum([r["rating"] for r in ratings]) / len(ratings) if ratings else 0.0
        
        # Calculate popularity score
        popularity = self.calculate_popularity_score(
            len(ratings),
            social_data.get("total_views", 0),
            social_data.get("total_favorites", 0),
            len(social_data.get("comments", []))
        )
        
        metadata = [{
            "asset_id": asset_id,
            "asset_name": asset_name,
            "ratings": {
                "average_rating": avg_rating,
                "total_ratings": len(ratings),
                "rating_distribution": social_data.get("rating_distribution", {}),
                "last_rated_date": datetime.now() if ratings else None
            },
            "user_ratings": ratings,
            "comments": social_data.get("comments", []),
            "favorites": {
                "total_favorites": social_data.get("total_favorites", 0),
                "favorited_by": social_data.get("favorited_by", [])
            },
            "usage_statistics": social_data.get("usage_statistics", {}),
            "collaborators": social_data.get("collaborators", []),
            "endorsements": social_data.get("endorsements", []),
            "questions": social_data.get("questions", []),
            "tags_user_generated": social_data.get("user_tags", []),
            "popularity_score": popularity,
            "trust_score": social_data.get("trust_score", 75.0),
            "last_updated": datetime.now()
        }]
        
        return self.spark.createDataFrame(metadata, self.create_social_metadata_schema())

"""
Lineage Metadata Pattern captures data flow, transformations, dependencies,
and the complete lifecycle of data from source to destination.
"""

class LineageMetadataPattern:
    """
    Manages data lineage metadata including source-to-target mappings, transformations,
    and impact analysis capabilities.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark_session):
        self.spark = spark_session
