# ============================================================================
# PATTERN 1: SAFE CAST PATTERN
# Description: Validates data before casting, returns null for invalid values
# Use Case: When you want to preserve data integrity and identify invalid data
# ============================================================================

def safe_cast_pattern():
    """
    Safe Cast Pattern: Validates data before casting to prevent errors.
    Returns NULL for values that cannot be safely cast.
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("PATTERN 1: SAFE CAST PATTERN")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Create sample data with mixed valid/invalid values
    data = [
        ("1", "100", "123.45", "2024-01-15", "true"),
        ("2", "abc", "456.78", "2024-02-20", "false"),
        ("3", "200", "invalid", "invalid_date", "yes"),
        ("4", None, "789.12", "2024-03-25", None),
        ("5", "300", "999.99", "2024-04-30", "1"),
        ("6", "99999999999999999999", "1.23", "2024-05-15", "0")
    ]
    
    df = spark.createDataFrame(
        data, 
        ["id", "int_value", "decimal_value", "date_value", "bool_value"]
    )
    
    print("\nOriginal Data:")
    df.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Safe cast implementation with validation
    safe_cast_df = df.select(
        col("id"),
        col("int_value"),
        col("decimal_value"),
        col("date_value"),
        col("bool_value"),
        
        # Safe Integer Cast - validates numeric pattern
        when(
            col("int_value").rlike("^-?\\d+$") &  # Check if pure integer
            (col("int_value").cast(LongType()).between(-2147483648, 2147483647)),
            col("int_value").cast(IntegerType())
        ).otherwise(lit(None)).alias("safe_int"),
        
        # Safe Decimal Cast - validates decimal pattern
        when(
            col("decimal_value").rlike("^-?\\d+\\.?\\d*$"),  # Check decimal pattern
            col("decimal_value").cast(DecimalType(10, 2))
        ).otherwise(lit(None)).alias("safe_decimal"),
        
        # Safe Date Cast - try to parse date
        when(
            col("date_value").rlike("^\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}$"),  # Basic date format check
            to_date(col("date_value"), "yyyy-MM-dd")
        ).otherwise(lit(None)).alias("safe_date"),
        
        # Safe Boolean Cast - accepts multiple formats
        when(
            col("bool_value").isin("true", "false", "1", "0", "yes", "no"),
            when(col("bool_value").isin("true", "1", "yes"), lit(True))
            .otherwise(lit(False))
        ).otherwise(lit(None)).alias("safe_boolean"),
        
        # Validation flags
        when(
            col("int_value").rlike("^-?\\d+$") &
            (col("int_value").cast(LongType()).between(-2147483648, 2147483647)),
            lit("VALID")
        ).otherwise(lit("INVALID")).alias("int_validation_status")
    )
    
    print("\nSafe Cast Results:")
    safe_cast_df.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Show validation summary
    print("\nValidation Summary:")
    safe_cast_df.groupBy("int_validation_status").count().show()
    
    return safe_cast_df


# ============================================================================
# PATTERN 2: UNSAFE CAST PATTERN
# Description: Direct casting without validation, may lose data or fail
# Use Case: When you're certain about data quality or performance is critical
# ============================================================================

def unsafe_cast_pattern():
    """
    Unsafe Cast Pattern: Direct casting without validation.
    May result in NULL values or data loss without warning.
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("PATTERN 2: UNSAFE CAST PATTERN")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    data = [
        ("1", "100", "123.456789", "2024-01-15 10:30:00"),
        ("2", "200.5", "456.789012", "2024-02-20 14:45:00"),  # Will truncate
        ("3", "abc", "invalid", "invalid"),  # Will become NULL
        ("4", "99999999999", "999.999999", "2024-03-25 08:15:00"),  # May overflow
    ]
    
    df = spark.createDataFrame(
        data,
        ["id", "numeric_str", "precise_decimal", "timestamp_str"]
    )
    
    print("\nOriginal Data:")
    df.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Unsafe direct casts
    unsafe_cast_df = df.select(
        col("id"),
        
        # Direct cast - truncates decimal, returns NULL for invalid
        col("numeric_str").cast(IntegerType()).alias("unsafe_int"),
        
        # Direct cast - may lose precision
        col("precise_decimal").cast(FloatType()).alias("unsafe_float"),
        
        # Direct cast with limited precision
        col("precise_decimal").cast(DecimalType(5, 2)).alias("unsafe_decimal_truncated"),
        
        # Direct timestamp cast - NULL for invalid format
        col("timestamp_str").cast(TimestampType()).alias("unsafe_timestamp"),
        
        # Show original for comparison
        col("numeric_str").alias("original_numeric"),
        col("precise_decimal").alias("original_decimal")
    )
    
    print("\nUnsafe Cast Results (Note data loss and NULLs):")
    unsafe_cast_df.show(truncate=False)
    
    print("\n⚠️  WARNING: Unsafe casting can lead to:")
    print("   - Silent data loss (precision truncation)")
    print("   - NULL values without clear indication of failure")
    print("   - Overflow errors in some cases")
    
    return unsafe_cast_df


# ============================================================================
# PATTERN 3: TRY-CAST PATTERN (REFINED)
# Description: Attempts cast and provides detailed error information
# Use Case: Data quality monitoring and error tracking
# ============================================================================

def try_cast_pattern():
    """
    Try-Cast Pattern: Attempts casting and captures detailed error information.
    Provides error codes, messages, and original values for failed casts.
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("PATTERN 3: TRY-CAST PATTERN (REFINED)")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    data = [
        ("1", "100", "123.45", "2024-01-15", "45.67"),
        ("2", "abc", "456.78", "2024-02-20", "89.12"),
        ("3", "200", "xyz", "invalid", "34.56"),
        ("4", "", "789.12", "2024-03-25", ""),
        ("5", "300", "999.99", "2024-04-30", "12.34"),
        ("6", "999999999999", "1.23", "2024-13-45", "56.78")  # Invalid month/day
    ]
    
    df = spark.createDataFrame(
        data,
        ["id", "int_str", "dec_str", "date_str", "float_str"]
    )
    
    print("\nOriginal Data:")
    df.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Try-Cast with detailed error tracking
    try_cast_df = df.select(
        col("id"),
        col("int_str"),
        col("dec_str"),
        col("date_str"),
        col("float_str"),
        
        # Try-Cast Integer with error details
        when(
            col("int_str").isNull() | (trim(col("int_str")) == ""),
            lit(None)
        ).when(
            col("int_str").rlike("^-?\\d+$") &
            (col("int_str").cast(LongType()).between(-2147483648, 2147483647)),
            col("int_str").cast(IntegerType())
        ).otherwise(lit(None)).alias("casted_int"),
        
        # Error code for integer cast
        when(
            col("int_str").isNull() | (trim(col("int_str")) == ""),
            lit("ERR_NULL_OR_EMPTY")
        ).when(
            ~col("int_str").rlike("^-?\\d+$"),
            lit("ERR_INVALID_FORMAT")
        ).when(
            ~(col("int_str").cast(LongType()).between(-2147483648, 2147483647)),
            lit("ERR_OVERFLOW")
        ).otherwise(lit("SUCCESS")).alias("int_cast_status"),
        
        # Try-Cast Decimal with validation
        when(
            col("dec_str").rlike("^-?\\d+\\.?\\d*$"),
            col("dec_str").cast(DecimalType(10, 2))
        ).otherwise(lit(None)).alias("casted_decimal"),
        
        when(
            col("dec_str").isNull() | (trim(col("dec_str")) == ""),
            lit("ERR_NULL_OR_EMPTY")
        ).when(
            ~col("dec_str").rlike("^-?\\d+\\.?\\d*$"),
            lit("ERR_INVALID_FORMAT")
        ).otherwise(lit("SUCCESS")).alias("decimal_cast_status"),
        
        # Try-Cast Date with validation
        when(
            col("date_str").rlike("^\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}$"),
            to_date(col("date_str"), "yyyy-MM-dd")
        ).otherwise(lit(None)).alias("casted_date"),
        
        when(
            col("date_str").isNull() | (trim(col("date_str")) == ""),
            lit("ERR_NULL_OR_EMPTY")
        ).when(
            ~col("date_str").rlike("^\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}$"),
            lit("ERR_INVALID_FORMAT")
        ).when(
            to_date(col("date_str"), "yyyy-MM-dd").isNull(),
            lit("ERR_INVALID_DATE")
        ).otherwise(lit("SUCCESS")).alias("date_cast_status"),
        
        # Try-Cast Float
        when(
            col("float_str").rlike("^-?\\d+\\.?\\d*$"),
            col("float_str").cast(FloatType())
        ).otherwise(lit(None)).alias("casted_float"),
        
        when(
            col("float_str").isNull() | (trim(col("float_str")) == ""),
            lit("ERR_NULL_OR_EMPTY")
        ).when(
            ~col("float_str").rlike("^-?\\d+\\.?\\d*$"),
            lit("ERR_INVALID_FORMAT")
        ).otherwise(lit("SUCCESS")).alias("float_cast_status")
    )
    
    print("\nTry-Cast Results with Error Tracking:")
    try_cast_df.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Error summary
    print("\nError Summary by Type:")
    
    print("\nInteger Cast Errors:")
    try_cast_df.groupBy("int_cast_status").count().orderBy("count", ascending=False).show()
    
    print("Decimal Cast Errors:")
    try_cast_df.groupBy("decimal_cast_status").count().orderBy("count", ascending=False).show()
    
    print("Date Cast Errors:")
    try_cast_df.groupBy("date_cast_status").count().orderBy("count", ascending=False).show()
    
    # Failed records detail
    print("\nDetailed Failed Records:")
    failed_df = try_cast_df.filter(
        (col("int_cast_status") != "SUCCESS") |
        (col("decimal_cast_status") != "SUCCESS") |
        (col("date_cast_status") != "SUCCESS") |
        (col("float_cast_status") != "SUCCESS")
    )
    failed_df.show(truncate=False)
    
    return try_cast_df


# ============================================================================
# PATTERN 4: FORMAT-PRESERVING CAST PATTERN
# Description: Casts data while maintaining original format/representation
# Use Case: When display format must be preserved (e.g., leading zeros)
# ============================================================================

def format_preserving_cast_pattern():
    """
    Format-Preserving Cast Pattern: Maintains original string format 
    while providing typed values for computation.
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("PATTERN 4: FORMAT-PRESERVING CAST PATTERN")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    data = [
        ("1", "00123", "0045.50", "01/15/2024", "001234567890"),
        ("2", "00456", "0123.00", "02/20/2024", "009876543210"),
        ("3", "00789", "0999.99", "03/25/2024", "005551234567"),
        ("4", "01000", "1234.56", "12/31/2024", "001112223333"),
    ]
    
    df = spark.createDataFrame(
        data,
        ["id", "padded_int", "padded_decimal", "formatted_date", "account_number"]
    )
    
    print("\nOriginal Data (with formatting):")
    df.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Format-preserving casts
    format_preserving_df = df.select(
        col("id"),
        
        # Preserve original format
        col("padded_int").alias("original_int_format"),
        col("padded_decimal").alias("original_decimal_format"),
        col("formatted_date").alias("original_date_format"),
        col("account_number").alias("original_account_format"),
        
        # Typed values for computation
        col("padded_int").cast(IntegerType()).alias("computed_int"),
        col("padded_decimal").cast(DecimalType(10, 2)).alias("computed_decimal"),
        to_date(col("formatted_date"), "MM/dd/yyyy").alias("compute
d_date"),
        col("account_number").cast(LongType()).alias("computed_account"),
        
        # Demonstrate computation on typed values
        (col("padded_int").cast(IntegerType()) * 2).alias("doubled_value"),
        (col("padded_decimal").cast(DecimalType(10, 2)) * 1.1).alias("increased_by_10_percent"),
        
        # Reconstruct format after computation
        when(
            col("padded_int").cast(IntegerType()).isNotNull(),
            # Pad back to original length (5 digits)
            lpad((col("padded_int").cast(IntegerType()) * 2).cast(StringType()), 5, "0")
        ).alias("doubled_value_formatted"),
        
        # Format decimal back to original pattern (4 digits before, 2 after)
        when(
            col("padded_decimal").cast(DecimalType(10, 2)).isNotNull(),
            concat(
                lpad(
                    substring(
                        (col("padded_decimal").cast(DecimalType(10, 2)) * 1.1).cast(StringType()),
                        1,
                        length((col("padded_decimal").cast(DecimalType(10, 2)) * 1.1).cast(StringType())) - 3
                    ),
                    4,
                    "0"
                ),
                lit("."),
                substring(
                    (col("padded_decimal").cast(DecimalType(10, 2)) * 1.1).cast(StringType()),
                    -2,
                    2
                )
            )
        ).alias("increased_value_formatted")
    )
    
    print("\nFormat-Preserving Cast Results:")
    format_preserving_df.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Create a cleaner example with proper formatting functions
    print("\nCleaner Format Preservation Example:")
    
    from pyspark.sql.functions import lpad, concat, format_number
    
    clean_format_df = df.select(
        col("id"),
        col("padded_int").alias("original"),
        col("padded_int").cast(IntegerType()).alias("typed_value"),
        
        # Apply business logic on typed value
        (col("padded_int").cast(IntegerType()) + 100).alias("after_calculation"),
        
        # Restore format
        lpad(
            (col("padded_int").cast(IntegerType()) + 100).cast(StringType()),
            5,
            "0"
        ).alias("formatted_result"),
        
        # Account number formatting
        col("account_number").alias("original_account"),
        lpad(
            col("account_number").cast(LongType()).cast(StringType()),
            12,
            "0"
        ).alias("preserved_account_format")
    )
    
    clean_format_df.show(truncate=False)
    
    return format_preserving_df


# ============================================================================
# PATTERN 5: LOSSY CAST PATTERN
# Description: Intentional data loss during casting (e.g., precision reduction)
# Use Case: Data aggregation, storage optimization, privacy masking
# ============================================================================

def lossy_cast_pattern():
    """
    Lossy Cast Pattern: Intentionally loses precision or detail during casting.
    Used for aggregation, storage optimization, or data anonymization.
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("PATTERN 5: LOSSY CAST PATTERN")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    data = [
        ("1", "123.456789", "1234567890.123456", "2024-01-15 14:30:45.123", "192.168.1.100", "42.5"),
        ("2", "456.789012", "9876543210.987654", "2024-02-20 09:15:30.456", "10.0.0.255", "37.8"),
        ("3", "789.123456", "5555555555.555555", "2024-03-25 18:45:15.789", "172.16.0.1", "51.2"),
        ("4", "999.999999", "1111111111.111111", "2024-04-30 23:59:59.999", "8.8.8.8", "28.9"),
    ]
    
    df = spark.createDataFrame(
        data,
        ["id", "precise_decimal", "large_number", "precise_timestamp", "ip_address", "temperature"]
    )
    
    print("\nOriginal High-Precision Data:")
    df.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Various lossy cast scenarios
    lossy_cast_df = df.select(
        col("id"),
        
        # Original values
        col("precise_decimal").alias("original_decimal"),
        col("large_number").alias("original_large_num"),
        col("precise_timestamp").alias("original_timestamp"),
        col("ip_address").alias("original_ip"),
        col("temperature").alias("original_temp"),
        
        # LOSSY: Decimal precision reduction
        col("precise_decimal").cast(DecimalType(5, 2)).alias("lossy_decimal_5_2"),
        col("precise_decimal").cast(FloatType()).alias("lossy_float"),
        col("precise_decimal").cast(IntegerType()).alias("lossy_int_truncate"),
        
        # LOSSY: Large number to smaller type (potential overflow)
        col("large_number").cast(IntegerType()).alias("lossy_to_int_overflow"),
        col("large_number").cast(FloatType()).alias("lossy_to_float"),
        
        # LOSSY: Timestamp to date (loses time component)
        to_date(col("precise_timestamp")).alias("lossy_date_only"),
        
        # LOSSY: Timestamp to hour (loses minutes/seconds)
        date_trunc("hour", col("precise_timestamp")).alias("lossy_hour_only"),
        
        # LOSSY: IP address masking (privacy)
        concat(
            substring_index(col("ip_address"), ".", 3),
            lit(".xxx")
        ).alias("lossy_masked_ip"),
        
        # LOSSY: Temperature rounding
        spark_round(col("temperature").cast(DoubleType()), 0).alias("lossy_temp_rounded"),
        
        # LOSSY: Bucketing/Binning
        when(col("temperature").cast(DoubleType()) < 30, lit("Cold"))
        .when(col("temperature").cast(DoubleType()) < 40, lit("Moderate"))
        .when(col("temperature").cast(DoubleType()) < 50, lit("Warm"))
        .otherwise(lit("Hot")).alias("lossy_temp_category")
    )
    
    print("\nLossy Cast Results (Intentional Data Loss):")
    lossy_cast_df.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Demonstrate precision loss
    print("\nPrecision Loss Analysis:")
    precision_loss_df = df.select(
        col("id"),
        col("precise_decimal"),
        col("precise_decimal").cast(DecimalType(5, 2)).alias("reduced_precision"),
        (
            col("precise_decimal").cast(DoubleType()) - 
            col("precise_decimal").cast(DecimalType(5, 2)).cast(DoubleType())
        ).alias("precision_lost")
    )
    precision_loss_df.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Storage optimization example
    print("\nStorage Optimization Comparison:")
    print("Original: DecimalType(18, 6) - High precision, more storage")
    print("Optimized: DecimalType(5, 2) - Lower precision, less storage")
    print("Trade-off: ~60% storage reduction with acceptable precision loss")
    
    return lossy_cast_df


# ============================================================================
# PATTERN 6: LOSSLESS CAST PATTERN
# Description: Guarantees no data loss during type conversion
# Use Case: Critical financial data, scientific measurements, audit trails
# ============================================================================

def lossless_cast_pattern():
    """
    Lossless Cast Pattern: Ensures complete data preservation during casting.
    Validates that no information is lost in the conversion process.
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("PATTERN 6: LOSSLESS CAST PATTERN")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    data = [
        ("1", "123", "123.45", "2024-01-15", "true", "100"),
        ("2", "456", "456.78", "2024-02-20", "false", "200"),
        ("3", "789", "789.12", "2024-03-25", "true", "300"),
        ("4", "999", "999.99", "2024-04-30", "false", "400"),
        ("5", "111", "111.11", "2024-05-15", "true", "500"),
    ]
    
    df = spark.createDataFrame(
        data,
        ["id", "int_str", "decimal_str", "date_str", "bool_str", "numeric_str"]
    )
    
    print("\nOriginal Data:")
    df.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Lossless casting with validation
    lossless_cast_df = df.select(
        col("id"),
        col("int_str"),
        col("decimal_str"),
        col("date_str"),
        col("bool_str"),
        col("numeric_str"),
        
        # LOSSLESS: String to Integer (with validation)
        col("int_str").cast(IntegerType()).alias("casted_int"),
        
        # Verify lossless: Cast back to string and compare
        (col("int_str").cast(IntegerType()).cast(StringType()) == col("int_str"))
        .alias("int_lossless_verified"),
        
        # LOSSLESS: String to Decimal with sufficient precision
        col("decimal_str").cast(DecimalType(10, 2)).alias("casted_decimal"),
        
        # Verify lossless: Cast back and compare
        (
            col("decimal_str").cast(DecimalType(10, 2)).cast(StringType()) == 
            col("decimal_str")
        ).alias("decimal_lossless_verified"),
        
        # LOSSLESS: String to Date
        to_date(col("date_str"), "yyyy-MM-dd").alias("casted_date"),
        
        # Verify lossless: Format back and compare
        (
            date_format(to_date(col("date_str"), "yyyy-MM-dd"), "yyyy-MM-dd") == 
            col("date_str")
        ).alias("date_lossless_verified"),
        
        # LOSSLESS: String to Boolean
        when(col("bool_str") == "true", lit(True))
        .when(col("bool_str") == "false", lit(False))
        .alias("casted_boolean"),
        
        # Verify lossless
        (
            when(
                when(col("bool_str") == "true", lit(True))
                .when(col("bool_str") == "false", lit(False)) == True,
                lit("true")
            ).otherwise(lit("false")) == col("bool_str")
        ).alias("boolean_lossless_verified"),
        
        # LOSSLESS: Numeric widening (Int -> Long -> Decimal)
        col("numeric_str").cast(IntegerType()).alias("as_int"),
        col("numeric_str").cast(LongType()).alias("as_long"),
        col("numeric_str").cast(DecimalType(20, 2)).alias("as_decimal"),
        
        # Verify all conversions are equal
        (
            (col("numeric_str").cast(IntegerType()) == col("numeric_str").cast(LongType())) &
            (col("numeric_str").cast(LongType()) == col("numeric_str").cast(DecimalType(20, 2)))
        ).alias("widening_lossless_verified")
    )
    
    print("\nLossless Cast Results with Verification:")
    lossless_cast_df.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Verification summary
    print("\nLossless Verification Summary:")
    verification_df = lossless_cast_df.select(
        col("id"),
        col("int_lossless_verified"),
        col("decimal_lossless_verified"),
        col("date_lossless_verified"),
        col("boolean_lossless_verified"),
        col("widening_lossless_verified")
    )
    verification_df.show()
    
    # Check if all conversions are lossless
    all_lossless = lossless_cast_df.filter(
        col("int_lossless_verified") &
        col("decimal_lossless_verified") &
        col("date_lossless_verified") &
        col("boolean_lossless_verified") &
        col("widening_lossless_verified")
    ).count()
    
    total_records = lossless_cast_df.count()
    
    print(f"\n✓ Lossless Conversion Success Rate: {all_lossless}/{total_records} " +
          f"({100 * all_lossless / total_records:.1f}%)")
    
    # Advanced lossless pattern: Type widening hierarchy
    print("\n" + "-" * 80)
    print("Type Widening Hierarchy (Always Lossless):")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    widening_data = [
        ("1", 100, 100, 100.0, 100.00),
        ("2", 200, 200, 200.0, 200.00),
    ]
    
    widening_schema = StructType([
        StructField("id", StringType(), True),
        StructField("byte_val", IntegerType(), True),
        StructField("int_val", IntegerType(), True),
        StructField("long_val", DoubleType(), True),
        StructField("decimal_val", DecimalType(10, 2), True)
    ])
    
    widening_df = spark.createDataFrame(widening_data, widening_schema)
    
    widening_result = widening_df.select(
        col("id"),
        col("byte_val"),
        
        # Widening conversions (always lossless)
        col("byte_val").cast(IntegerType()).alias("byte_to_int"),
        col("int_val").cast(LongType()).alias("int_to_long"),
        col("int_val").cast(DoubleType()).alias("int_to_double"),
        col("long_val").cast(DecimalType(20, 2)).alias("long_to_decimal"),
        
        # Verify equality after widening
        (col("byte_val") == col("byte_val").cast(IntegerType())).alias("byte_to_int_equal"),
        (col("int_val") == col("int_val").cast(LongType())).alias("int_to_long_equal"),
        (col("int_val") == col("int_val").cast(DoubleType())).alias("int_to_double_equal")
    )
    
    print("\nType Widening Examples:")
    widening_result.show()
    
    print("\nLossless Type Widening Hierarchy:")
    print("  Byte → Short → Int → Long → Decimal")
    print("  Float → Double → Decimal (with sufficient precision)")
    print("  Date → Timestamp")
    
    return lossless_cast_df


# ============================================================================
# COMPREHENSIVE COMPARISON AND BEST PRACTICES
# ============================================================================

def comprehensive_
comparison():
    """
    Comprehensive comparison of all casting patterns with recommendations.
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("COMPREHENSIVE COMPARISON OF CASTING PATTERNS")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Create comprehensive test dataset
    data = [
        ("1", "100", "123.456", "2024-01-15", "true", "valid"),
        ("2", "abc", "456.789", "2024-02-20", "false", "invalid_int"),
        ("3", "200", "xyz", "invalid_date", "yes", "invalid_decimal"),
        ("4", None, "789.123", "2024-03-25", None, "null_values"),
        ("5", "99999999999", "999.999999", "2024-04-30", "1", "overflow"),
        ("6", "300", "111.11", "2024-05-15", "0", "valid"),
    ]
    
    df = spark.createDataFrame(
        data,
        ["id", "int_value", "decimal_value", "date_value", "bool_value", "scenario"]
    )
    
    print("\nTest Dataset:")
    df.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Apply all patterns
    comparison_df = df.select(
        col("id"),
        col("scenario"),
        col("int_value").alias("original_int"),
        col("decimal_value").alias("original_decimal"),
        
        # Pattern 1: Safe Cast
        when(
            col("int_value").rlike("^-?\\d+$") &
            (col("int_value").cast(LongType()).between(-2147483648, 2147483647)),
            col("int_value").cast(IntegerType())
        ).otherwise(lit(None)).alias("safe_cast_int"),
        
        # Pattern 2: Unsafe Cast
        col("int_value").cast(IntegerType()).alias("unsafe_cast_int"),
        
        # Pattern 3: Try-Cast with status
        when(
            col("int_value").rlike("^-?\\d+$") &
            (col("int_value").cast(LongType()).between(-2147483648, 2147483647)),
            col("int_value").cast(IntegerType())
        ).otherwise(lit(None)).alias("try_cast_int"),
        
        when(
            col("int_value").isNull(),
            lit("NULL_INPUT")
        ).when(
            ~col("int_value").rlike("^-?\\d+$"),
            lit("INVALID_FORMAT")
        ).when(
            ~(col("int_value").cast(LongType()).between(-2147483648, 2147483647)),
            lit("OVERFLOW")
        ).otherwise(lit("SUCCESS")).alias("try_cast_status"),
        
        # Pattern 5: Lossy Cast (decimal precision reduction)
        col("decimal_value").cast(DecimalType(10, 6)).alias("original_precision"),
        col("decimal_value").cast(DecimalType(5, 2)).alias("lossy_cast_decimal"),
        
        # Pattern 6: Lossless Cast (with verification)
        col("decimal_value").cast(DecimalType(10, 3)).alias("lossless_cast_decimal"),
        (
            col("decimal_value").cast(DecimalType(10, 3)).cast(StringType()) ==
            col("decimal_value")
        ).alias("lossless_verified")
    )
    
    print("\nPattern Comparison Results:")
    comparison_df.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Performance comparison
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("PERFORMANCE CHARACTERISTICS")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    performance_summary = """
    Pattern                  | Performance | Safety | Use Case
    -------------------------|-------------|--------|---------------------------
    Safe Cast                | Medium      | High   | Production data pipelines
    Unsafe Cast              | Fastest     | Low    | Trusted data sources
    Try-Cast                 | Slow        | High   | Data quality monitoring
    Format-Preserving Cast   | Slow        | Medium | Display/reporting
    Lossy Cast               | Fast        | Medium | Aggregation/optimization
    Lossless Cast            | Medium      | Highest| Financial/critical data
    """
    
    print(performance_summary)
    
    # Best practices summary
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("BEST PRACTICES AND RECOMMENDATIONS")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    best_practices = """
    1. SAFE CAST PATTERN
       ✓ Use for: Production ETL pipelines
       ✓ When: Data quality is uncertain
       ✓ Benefit: Prevents pipeline failures
       ✗ Avoid: High-performance scenarios
    
    2. UNSAFE CAST PATTERN
       ✓ Use for: Performance-critical operations
       ✓ When: Data quality is guaranteed
       ✗ Avoid: Untrusted data sources
       ✗ Risk: Silent data loss
    
    3. TRY-CAST PATTERN
       ✓ Use for: Data quality auditing
       ✓ When: Need detailed error tracking
       ✓ Benefit: Comprehensive error reporting
       ✗ Avoid: Real-time processing (overhead)
    
    4. FORMAT-PRESERVING CAST PATTERN
       ✓ Use for: User-facing applications
       ✓ When: Display format matters (IDs, codes)
       ✓ Example: Account numbers, postal codes
       ✗ Avoid: Pure computation scenarios
    
    5. LOSSY CAST PATTERN
       ✓ Use for: Data aggregation
       ✓ When: Storage optimization needed
       ✓ Example: Rounding, bucketing, masking
       ✗ Avoid: Reversible operations required
    
    6. LOSSLESS CAST PATTERN
       ✓ Use for: Financial transactions
       ✓ When: Precision is critical
       ✓ Benefit: Audit trail integrity
       ✗ Avoid: When precision isn't critical
    """
    
    print(best_practices)
    
    return comparison_df


# ============================================================================
# ADVANCED PATTERN: COMPOSITE CASTING WITH FALLBACK
# ============================================================================

def composite_casting_pattern():
    """
    Advanced pattern combining multiple casting strategies with fallback logic.
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("ADVANCED: COMPOSITE CASTING WITH FALLBACK")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    data = [
        ("1", "100", "USD", "123.45"),
        ("2", "200.5", "EUR", "456.78"),  # Has decimal
        ("3", "three hundred", "GBP", "789.12"),  # Text number
        ("4", "400", "JPY", "invalid"),  # Invalid amount
        ("5", "", "CAD", "999.99"),  # Empty quantity
    ]
    
    df = spark.createDataFrame(
        data,
        ["id", "quantity", "currency", "amount"]
    )
    
    print("\nOriginal Data:")
    df.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Composite casting with multiple fallback strategies
    composite_df = df.select(
        col("id"),
        col("quantity"),
        col("amount"),
        
        # Strategy 1: Try direct integer cast
        col("quantity").cast(IntegerType()).alias("strategy_1_direct_int"),
        
        # Strategy 2: Try float cast, then round to int
        spark_round(col("quantity").cast(FloatType()), 0).cast(IntegerType())
        .alias("strategy_2_float_round"),
        
        # Strategy 3: Try to extract numbers from text
        regexp_extract(col("quantity"), r'(\d+)', 1).cast(IntegerType())
        .alias("strategy_3_extract_number"),
        
        # Composite result with fallback chain
        coalesce(
            # Try Strategy 1: Direct cast
            col("quantity").cast(IntegerType()),
            # Try Strategy 2: Float round
            spark_round(col("quantity").cast(FloatType()), 0).cast(IntegerType()),
            # Try Strategy 3: Extract number
            regexp_extract(col("quantity"), r'(\d+)', 1).cast(IntegerType()),
            # Fallback: Default value
            lit(0)
        ).alias("final_quantity"),
        
        # Track which strategy succeeded
        when(
            col("quantity").cast(IntegerType()).isNotNull(),
            lit("DIRECT_CAST")
        ).when(
            spark_round(col("quantity").cast(FloatType()), 0).cast(IntegerType()).isNotNull(),
            lit("FLOAT_ROUND")
        ).when(
            regexp_extract(col("quantity"), r'(\d+)', 1).cast(IntegerType()).isNotNull(),
            lit("REGEX_EXTRACT")
        ).otherwise(
            lit("DEFAULT_VALUE")
        ).alias("strategy_used"),
        
        # Amount casting with validation
        when(
            col("amount").rlike("^\\d+\\.\\d{2}$"),
            col("amount").cast(DecimalType(10, 2))
        ).otherwise(lit(None)).alias("validated_amount"),
        
        # Calculate total with proper types
        (
            coalesce(
                col("quantity").cast(IntegerType()),
                spark_round(col("quantity").cast(FloatType()), 0).cast(IntegerType()),
                regexp_extract(col("quantity"), r'(\d+)', 1).cast(IntegerType()),
                lit(0)
            ) *
            coalesce(
                when(
                    col("amount").rlike("^\\d+\\.\\d{2}$"),
                    col("amount").cast(DecimalType(10, 2))
                ),
                lit(0)
            )
        ).alias("total_value")
    )
    
    print("\nComposite Casting Results:")
    composite_df.show(truncate=False)
    
    print("\nStrategy Usage Summary:")
    composite_df.groupBy("strategy_used").count().show()
    
    return composite_df


# ============================================================================
# REAL-WORLD EXAMPLE: DATA MIGRATION SCENARIO
# ============================================================================

def data_migration_example():
    """
    Real-world example: Migrating data from legacy system with mixed formats.
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("REAL-WORLD EXAMPLE: DATA MIGRATION")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Simulating legacy data with inconsistent formats
    legacy_data = [
        ("1", "John Doe", "1985-06-15", "35000.00", "2020-01-15 09:00:00", "Active", "001"),
        ("2", "Jane Smith", "15/07/1990", "42000", "2019-03-20 14:30:00", "1", "002"),
        ("3", "Bob Johnson", "1988-12-01", "38,500.50", "20/05/2021 10:15:00", "true", "3"),
        ("4", "Alice Brown", "invalid", "45000.00", "2018-11-10 16:45:00", "Active", "0004"),
        ("5", "Charlie Wilson", "1992-03-25", "N/A", "2022-02-28 08:00:00", "0", "5"),
    ]
    
    legacy_df = spark.createDataFrame(
        legacy_data,
        ["emp_id", "name", "birth_date", "salary", "hire_date", "is_active", "dept_code"]
    )
    
    print("\nLegacy Data (Mixed Formats):")
    legacy_df.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Migration with comprehensive casting
    migrated_df = legacy_df.select(
        # Employee ID: Format-preserving cast
        col("emp_id").cast(IntegerType()).alias("employee_id"),
        lpad(col("emp_id"), 10, "0").alias("employee_id_formatted"),
        
        col("name"),
        
        # Birth Date: Try-cast with multiple formats
        coalesce(
            to_date(col("birth_date"), "yyyy-MM-dd"),
            to_date(col("birth_date"), "dd/MM/yyyy"),
            to_date(col("birth_date"), "MM/dd/yyyy")
        ).alias("birth_date_standardized"),
        
        # Track which format was used
        when(
            to_date(col("birth_date"), "yyyy-MM-dd").isNotNull(),
            lit("ISO_FORMAT")
        ).when(
            to_date(col("birth_date"), "dd/MM/yyyy").isNotNull(),
            lit("EU_FORMAT")
        ).when(
            to_date(col("birth_date"), "MM/dd/yyyy").isNotNull(),
            lit("US_FORMAT")
        ).otherwise(
            lit("INVALID")
        ).alias("birth_date_format"),
        
        # Salary: Safe cast with cleaning
        when(
            regexp_replace(col("salary"), "[^0-9.]", "").rlike("^\\d+\\.?\\d*$"),
            regexp_replace(col("salary"), "[^0-9.]", "").cast(DecimalType(10, 2))
        ).otherwise(lit(None)).alias("salary_cleaned"),
        
        # Hire Date: Lossless timestamp cast
        coalesce(
            to_timestamp(col("hire_date"), "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss"),
            to_timestamp(col("hire_date"), "dd/MM/yyyy HH:mm:ss")
        ).alias("hire_timestamp"),
        
        # Active Status: Safe boolean cast with multiple formats
        when(
            col("is_active").isin("Active", "true", "1", "yes"),
            lit(True)
        ).when(
            col("is_active").isin("Inactive", "false", "0", "no"),
            lit(False)
        ).otherwise(lit(None)).alias("is_active_boolean"),
        
        # Department Code: Format-preserving with validation
        col("dept_code").alias("original_dept_code"),
        lpad(col("dept_code"), 4, "0").alias("dept_code_standardized"),
        
        # Data Quality Flags
        when(
            coalesce(
                to_date(col("birth_date"), "yyyy-MM-dd"),
                to_date(col("birth_date"), "dd/MM/yyyy"),
                to_date(col("birth_date"), "MM/dd/yyyy")
            ).isNull(),
            lit("INVALID_DATE")
        ).when(
            regexp_replace(col("salary"), "[^0-9.]", "").cast(DecimalType(10, 2)).isNull(),
            lit("INVALID_SALARY")
        ).otherwise(
            lit("VALID")
        ).alias("data_quality_status")
    )
    
    print("\nMigrated Data (Standardized):")
    migrated_df.show(truncate=False)
    
    print("\nData Quality Summary:")
    migrated_df.groupBy("data_quality_status").count().show()
    
    print("\nDate Format Distribution:")
    migrated_df.groupBy("birth_date_format").count().show()
    
    # Calculate migration success rate
    total_records = migrated_df.count()
    valid_records = migrated_df.filter(col("data_quality_status") == "VALID").count()
    
    print(f"\nMigration Success Rate: {valid_records}/{total_records} " +
          f"({100 * valid_records / total_records:.1f}%)")
    
    return migrated_df

# ============================================================================
# PATTERN-SPECIFIC ERROR HANDLING AND RECOVERY
# ============================================================================

def error_handling_and_recovery():
    """
    Demonstrates error handling and recovery strategies for casting operations.
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("ERROR HANDLING AND RECOVERY STRATEGIES")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Create data with various error scenarios
    error_data = [
        ("1", "100", "123.45", "2024-01-15", "valid_record"),
        ("2", "abc", "456.78", "2024-02-20", "invalid_integer"),
        ("3", "200", "xyz", "2024-03-25", "invalid_decimal"),
        ("4", "300", "789.12", "invalid", "invalid_date"),
        ("5", None, None, None, "all_nulls"),
        ("6", "999999999999999", "123.45", "2024-04-30", "integer_overflow"),
        ("7", "400", "999999999.99", "2024-05-15", "decimal_overflow"),
        ("8", "", "", "", "empty_strings"),
    ]
    
    error_df = spark.createDataFrame(
        error_data,
        ["id", "int_value", "decimal_value", "date_value", "error_scenario"]
    )
    
    print("\nData with Various Error Scenarios:")
    error_df.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Comprehensive error handling with recovery
    error_handled_df = error_df.select(
        col("id"),
        col("error_scenario"),
        col("int_value"),
        col("decimal_value"),
        col("date_value"),
        
        # INTEGER CASTING WITH ERROR RECOVERY
        # Attempt 1: Direct cast
        col("int_value").cast(IntegerType()).alias("int_attempt_1"),
        
        # Attempt 2: Trim and cast
        trim(col("int_value")).cast(IntegerType()).alias("int_attempt_2"),
        
        # Attempt 3: Extract digits only
        regexp_replace(col("int_value"), "[^0-9-]", "").cast(IntegerType())
        .alias("int_attempt_3"),
        
        # Final with fallback to default
        coalesce(
            col("int_value").cast(IntegerType()),
            trim(col("int_value")).cast(IntegerType()),
            regexp_replace(col("int_value"), "[^0-9-]", "").cast(IntegerType()),
            lit(-1)  # Sentinel value indicating error
        ).alias("int_final_with_recovery"),
        
        # DECIMAL CASTING WITH ERROR RECOVERY
        # Clean and cast decimal
        when(
            regexp_replace(trim(col("decimal_value")), "[^0-9.-]", "")
            .rlike("^-?\\d+\\.?\\d*$"),
            regexp_replace(trim(col("decimal_value")), "[^0-9.-]", "")
            .cast(DecimalType(15, 2))
        ).otherwise(lit(None)).alias("decimal_cleaned"),
        
        # Fallback to zero for calculations
        coalesce(
            when(
                regexp_replace(trim(col("decimal_value")), "[^0-9.-]", "")
                .rlike("^-?\\d+\\.?\\d*$"),
                regexp_replace(trim(col("decimal_value")), "[^0-9.-]", "")
                .cast(DecimalType(15, 2))
            ),
            lit(0.00).cast(DecimalType(15, 2))
        ).alias("decimal_with_zero_fallback"),
        
        # DATE CASTING WITH MULTIPLE FORMAT ATTEMPTS
        coalesce(
            to_date(col("date_value"), "yyyy-MM-dd"),
            to_date(col("date_value"), "dd/MM/yyyy"),
            to_date(col("date_value"), "MM/dd/yyyy"),
            to_date(col("date_value"), "yyyy/MM/dd"),
            lit("1900-01-01").cast(DateType())  # Default date for errors
        ).alias("date_with_fallback"),
        
        # ERROR CLASSIFICATION
        when(
            col("int_value").isNull() | (trim(col("int_value")) == ""),
            lit("NULL_OR_EMPTY")
        ).when(
            ~col("int_value").rlike("^-?\\d+$"),
            lit("NON_NUMERIC")
        ).when(
            col("int_value").cast(LongType()) > 2147483647,
            lit("OVERFLOW")
        ).when(
            col("int_value").cast(LongType()) < -2147483648,
            lit("UNDERFLOW")
        ).otherwise(
            lit("SUCCESS")
        ).alias("int_error_type"),
        
        # RECOVERY ACTION TAKEN
        when(
            col("int_value").cast(IntegerType()).isNotNull(),
            lit("NO_RECOVERY_NEEDED")
        ).when(
            trim(col("int_value")).cast(IntegerType()).isNotNull(),
            lit("TRIMMED")
        ).when(
            regexp_replace(col("int_value"), "[^0-9-]", "").cast(IntegerType()).isNotNull(),
            lit("CLEANED")
        ).otherwise(
            lit("DEFAULT_VALUE_USED")
        ).alias("recovery_action")
    )
    
    print("\nError Handling Results:")
    error_handled_df.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Error type distribution
    print("\nError Type Distribution:")
    error_handled_df.groupBy("int_error_type").count().orderBy("count", ascending=False).show()
    
    print("\nRecovery Action Distribution:")
    error_handled_df.groupBy("recovery_action").count().orderBy("count", ascending=False).show()
    
    # Create error report
    print("\n" + "-" * 80)
    print("DETAILED ERROR REPORT")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    error_report = error_handled_df.filter(
        col("int_error_type") != "SUCCESS"
    ).select(
        col("id"),
        col("error_scenario"),
        col("int_value").alias("original_value"),
        col("int_error_type"),
        col("recovery_action"),
        col("int_final_with_recovery").alias("recovered_value")
    )
    
    error_report.show(truncate=False)
    
    return error_handled_df


# ============================================================================
# PERFORMANCE OPTIMIZATION PATTERNS
# ============================================================================

def performance_optimization_patterns():
    """
    Demonstrates performance optimization techniques for casting operations.
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("PERFORMANCE OPTIMIZATION PATTERNS")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Create larger dataset for performance testing
    from pyspark.sql.functions import expr, monotonically_increasing_id
    
    # Generate sample data
    perf_data = [(str(i), str(i * 10), str(i * 1.5), f"2024-01-{(i % 28) + 1:02d}") 
                 for i in range(1, 101)]
    
    perf_df = spark.createDataFrame(
        perf_data,
        ["id", "value1", "value2", "date_value"]
    )
    
    print(f"\nTest Dataset Size: {perf_df.count()} records")
    perf_df.show(5)
    
    # OPTIMIZATION 1: Batch Validation Before Casting
    print("\n" + "-" * 80)
    print("OPTIMIZATION 1: Pre-Validation Filter")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    # Pre-filter valid records for faster processing
    valid_records = perf_df.filter(
        col("value1").rlike("^\\d+$") &
        col("value2").rlike("^\\d+\\.?\\d*$") &
        col("date_value").rlike("^\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}$")
    )
    
    invalid_records = perf_df.filter(
        ~(col("value1").rlike("^\\d+$") &
          col("value2").rlike("^\\d+\\.?\\d*$") &
          col("date_value").rlike("^\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}$"))
    )
    
    # Cast only valid records (faster)
    optimized_valid = valid_records.select(
        col("id"),
        col("value1").cast(IntegerType()).alias("int_value"),
        col("value2").cast(DoubleType()).alias("double_value"),
        to_date(col("date_value"), "yyyy-MM-dd").alias("date_value"),
        lit("VALID").alias("status")
    )
    
    # Handle invalid records separately
    optimized_invalid = invalid_records.select(
        col("id"),
        lit(None).cast(IntegerType()).alias("int_value"),
        lit(None).cast(DoubleType()).alias("double_value"),
        lit(None).cast(DateType()).alias("date_value"),
        lit("INVALID").alias("status")
    )
    
    # Union results
    optimized_result = optimized_valid.union(optimized_invalid)
    
    print(f"Valid Records: {optimized_valid.count()}")
    print(f"Invalid Records: {optimized_invalid.count()}")
    
    # OPTIMIZATION 2: Cache Intermediate Results
    print("\n" + "-" * 80)
    print("OPTIMIZATION 2: Caching Strategy")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    # Cache validated data for multiple operations
    validated_df = perf_df.select(
        col("id"),
        col("value1"),
        col("value1").rlike("^\\d+$").alias("is_valid_int"),
        col("value2"),
        col("value2").rlike("^\\d+\\.?\\d*$").alias("is_valid_decimal")
    ).cache()
    
    print("Cached validation results for reuse")
    
    # Use cached validation multiple times
    int_casts = validated_df.filter(col("is_valid_int")).select(
        col("id"),
        col("value1").cast(IntegerType()).alias("casted_value")
    )
    
    decimal_casts = validated_df.filter(col("is_valid_decimal")).select(
        col("id"),
        col("value2").cast(DecimalType(10, 2)).alias("casted_value")
    )
    
    print(f"Integer casts: {int_casts.count()}")
    print(f"Decimal casts: {decimal_casts.count()}")
    
    # Unpersist when done
    validated_df.unpersist()
    
    # OPTIMIZATION 3: Lazy Evaluation with Coalesce
    print("\n" + "-" * 80)
    print("OPTIMIZATION 3: Lazy Evaluation Pattern")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    # Use coalesce to short-circuit evaluation
    lazy_eval_df = perf_df.select(
        col("id"),
        # Only evaluates subsequent casts if previous ones fail
        coalesce(
            col("value1").cast(IntegerType()),
            lit(0)
        ).alias("optimized_int")
    )
    
    print("Using coalesce for short-circuit evaluation")
    lazy_eval_df.show(5)
    
    # OPTIMIZATION 4: Partition-wise Processing
    print("\n" + "-" * 80)
    print("OPTIMIZATION 4: Partition-wise Processing")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    # Repartition for parallel processing
    partitioned_df = perf_df.repartition(4)
    
    print(f"Original partitions: {perf_df.rdd.getNumPartitions()}")
    print(f"Optimized partitions: {partitioned_df.rdd.getNumPartitions()}")
    
    # Process in parallel
    parallel_result = partitioned_df.select(
        col("id"),
        col("value1").cast(IntegerType()).alias("int_value"),
        col("value2").cast(DoubleType()).alias("double_value")
    )
    
    print("Parallel processing enabled")
    
    return optimized_result


# ============================================================================
# UNIT TESTING FRAMEWORK FOR CASTING PATTERNS
# ============================================================================

def casting_unit_tests():
    """
    Unit tests for validating casting pattern implementations.
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("UNIT TESTING FRAMEWORK FOR CASTING PATTERNS")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    test_results = []
    
    # TEST 1: Safe Cast Null Handling
    print("\nTEST 1: Safe Cast Null Handling")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    test1_data = [("1", None), ("2", "100"), ("3", "")]
    test1_df = spark.createDataFrame(test1_data, ["id", "value"])
    
    test1_result = test1_df.select(
        col("id"),
        when(
            col("value").isNotNull() & (trim(col("value")) != "") & col("value").rlike("^\\d+$"),
            col("value").cast(IntegerType())
        ).otherwise(lit(None)).alias("safe_cast")
    )
    
    null_count = test1_result.filter(col("safe_cast").isNull()).count()
    expected_nulls = 2  # Record 1 and 3
    
    test1_pass = (null_count == expected_nulls)
    test_results.append(("Safe Cast Null Handling", test1_pass))
    
    print(f"Expected nulls: {expected_nulls}, Actual nulls: {null_count}")
    print(f"Result: {'✓ PASS' if test1_pass else '✗ FAIL'}")
    
    # TEST 2: Lossless Cast Verification
    print("\nTEST 2: Lossless Cast Verification")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    test2_data = [("1", "123"), ("2", "456"), ("3", "789")]
    test2_df = spark.createDataFrame(test2_data, ["id", "value"])
    
    test2_result = test2_df.select(
        col("id"),
        col("value"),
        col("value").cast(IntegerType()).alias("casted"),
        (col("value").cast(IntegerType()).cast(StringType()) == col("value")).alias("is_lossless")
    )
    
    all_lossless = test2_result.filter(col("is_lossless") == False).count() == 0
    test_results.append(("Lossless Cast Verification", all_lossless))
    
    print(f"All conversions lossless: {all_lossless}")
    print(f"Result: {'✓ PASS' if all_lossless else '✗ FAIL'}")
    
    # TEST 3: Overflow Detection
    print("\nTEST 3: Overflow Detection")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    test3_data = [
        ("1", "2147483647"),  # Max int
        ("2", "2147483648"),  # Overflow
        ("3", "-2147483648"), # Min int
        ("4", "-2147483649")  # Underflow
    ]
    test3_df = spark.createDataFrame(test3_
data, ["id", "value"])
    
    test3_result = test3_df.select(
        col("id"),
        col("value"),
        when(
            col("value").rlike("^-?\\d+$") &
            (col("value").cast(LongType()).between(-2147483648, 2147483647)),
            col("value").cast(IntegerType())
        ).otherwise(lit(None)).alias("safe_int"),
        when(
            col("value").cast(LongType()) > 2147483647,
            lit("OVERFLOW")
        ).when(
            col("value").cast(LongType()) < -2147483648,
            lit("UNDERFLOW")
        ).otherwise(lit("OK")).alias("overflow_status")
    )
    
    overflow_detected = test3_result.filter(
        col("overflow_status").isin("OVERFLOW", "UNDERFLOW")
    ).count()
    
    test3_pass = (overflow_detected == 2)  # Records 2 and 4
    test_results.append(("Overflow Detection", test3_pass))
    
    print(f"Expected overflow cases: 2, Detected: {overflow_detected}")
    print(f"Result: {'✓ PASS' if test3_pass else '✗ FAIL'}")
    test3_result.show(truncate=False)
    
    # TEST 4: Format Preservation
    print("\nTEST 4: Format Preservation")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    test4_data = [("1", "00123"), ("2", "00456"), ("3", "00789")]
    test4_df = spark.createDataFrame(test4_data, ["id", "padded_value"])
    
    test4_result = test4_df.select(
        col("id"),
        col("padded_value").alias("original"),
        col("padded_value").cast(IntegerType()).alias("computed"),
        lpad(col("padded_value").cast(IntegerType()).cast(StringType()), 5, "0")
        .alias("reformatted"),
        (col("padded_value") == 
         lpad(col("padded_value").cast(IntegerType()).cast(StringType()), 5, "0"))
        .alias("format_preserved")
    )
    
    all_preserved = test4_result.filter(col("format_preserved") == False).count() == 0
    test_results.append(("Format Preservation", all_preserved))
    
    print(f"All formats preserved: {all_preserved}")
    print(f"Result: {'✓ PASS' if all_preserved else '✗ FAIL'}")
    test4_result.show(truncate=False)
    
    # TEST 5: Try-Cast Error Classification
    print("\nTEST 5: Try-Cast Error Classification")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    test5_data = [
        ("1", "100", "VALID"),
        ("2", "abc", "INVALID_FORMAT"),
        ("3", None, "NULL_INPUT"),
        ("4", "", "EMPTY_INPUT"),
        ("5", "999999999999", "OVERFLOW")
    ]
    test5_df = spark.createDataFrame(test5_data, ["id", "value", "expected_error"])
    
    test5_result = test5_df.select(
        col("id"),
        col("value"),
        col("expected_error"),
        when(
            col("value").isNull(),
            lit("NULL_INPUT")
        ).when(
            trim(col("value")) == "",
            lit("EMPTY_INPUT")
        ).when(
            ~col("value").rlike("^-?\\d+$"),
            lit("INVALID_FORMAT")
        ).when(
            ~(col("value").cast(LongType()).between(-2147483648, 2147483647)),
            lit("OVERFLOW")
        ).otherwise(
            lit("VALID")
        ).alias("actual_error"),
        when(
            col("expected_error") == 
            when(
                col("value").isNull(),
                lit("NULL_INPUT")
            ).when(
                trim(col("value")) == "",
                lit("EMPTY_INPUT")
            ).when(
                ~col("value").rlike("^-?\\d+$"),
                lit("INVALID_FORMAT")
            ).when(
                ~(col("value").cast(LongType()).between(-2147483648, 2147483647)),
                lit("OVERFLOW")
            ).otherwise(
                lit("VALID")
            ),
            lit(True)
        ).otherwise(lit(False)).alias("classification_correct")
    )
    
    all_correct = test5_result.filter(col("classification_correct") == False).count() == 0
    test_results.append(("Error Classification", all_correct))
    
    print(f"All errors correctly classified: {all_correct}")
    print(f"Result: {'✓ PASS' if all_correct else '✗ FAIL'}")
    test5_result.show(truncate=False)
    
    # TEST 6: Lossy vs Lossless Comparison
    print("\nTEST 6: Lossy vs Lossless Comparison")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    test6_data = [("1", "123.456789"), ("2", "456.789012"), ("3", "789.123456")]
    test6_df = spark.createDataFrame(test6_data, ["id", "precise_value"])
    
    test6_result = test6_df.select(
        col("id"),
        col("precise_value"),
        col("precise_value").cast(DecimalType(10, 6)).alias("lossless"),
        col("precise_value").cast(DecimalType(5, 2)).alias("lossy"),
        (
            col("precise_value").cast(DecimalType(10, 6)) !=
            col("precise_value").cast(DecimalType(5, 2)).cast(DecimalType(10, 6))
        ).alias("precision_lost")
    )
    
    precision_loss_detected = test6_result.filter(col("precision_lost") == True).count()
    test6_pass = (precision_loss_detected == 3)  # All should lose precision
    test_results.append(("Lossy Detection", test6_pass))
    
    print(f"Expected precision loss: 3, Detected: {precision_loss_detected}")
    print(f"Result: {'✓ PASS' if test6_pass else '✗ FAIL'}")
    test6_result.show(truncate=False)
    
    # FINAL TEST SUMMARY
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("UNIT TEST SUMMARY")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    total_tests = len(test_results)
    passed_tests = sum(1 for _, passed in test_results if passed)
    
    print(f"\nTotal Tests: {total_tests}")
    print(f"Passed: {passed_tests}")
    print(f"Failed: {total_tests - passed_tests}")
    print(f"Success Rate: {100 * passed_tests / total_tests:.1f}%\n")
    
    for test_name, passed in test_results:
        status = "✓ PASS" if passed else "✗ FAIL"
        print(f"{status}: {test_name}")
    
    return test_results

        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("EXECUTION COMPLETE - SUMMARY OF PATTERNS")

        summary = """
        ✓ Pattern 1: Safe Cast Pattern
          - Validates before casting
          - Returns NULL for invalid data
          - Best for production pipelines
        
        ✓ Pattern 2: Unsafe Cast Pattern
          - Direct casting without validation
          - Fastest performance
          - Use only with trusted data

def create_casting_validator():
    """
    Creates a reusable validator for common casting scenarios.
    """
    from pyspark.sql.functions import udf
    from pyspark.sql.types import BooleanType
    
    # UDF for complex validation
    @udf(BooleanType())
    def is_valid_integer(value):
        if value is None:
            return False
        try:
            int_val = int(value)
            return -2147483648 <= int_val <= 2147483647
        except:
            return False
    
    return is_valid_integer


def generate_casting_report(df, column_name, target_type):
    """
    Generates a detailed casting report for a specific column.
    """
    print(f"\nCasting Report for: {column_name} → {target_type}")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    total_records = df.count()
    null_records = df.filter(col(column_name).isNull()).count()
    
    # Attempt cast
    casted_df = df.withColumn(
        f"{column_name}_casted",
        col(column_name).cast(target_type)
    )
    
    successful_casts = casted_df.filter(
        col(f"{column_name}_casted").isNotNull()
    ).count()
    
    failed_casts = total_records - successful_casts - null_records
    
    print(f"Total Records: {total_records}")
    print(f"Null Records: {null_records}")
    print(f"Successful Casts: {successful_casts}")
    print(f"Failed Casts: {failed_casts}")
    print(f"Success Rate: {100 * successful_casts / (total_records - null_records):.2f}%")
    
    # Show sample failures
    if failed_casts > 0:
        print("\nSample Failed Casts:")
        casted_df.filter(
            col(column_name).isNotNull() &
            col(f"{column_name}_casted").isNull()
        ).select(column_name).show(5, truncate=False)

# PATTERN 1: Side-by-Side Comparison Pattern

"""
Purpose: Compare two query plans side-by-side to identify structural differences
Use Case: Understanding how query rewrites or optimizations change execution plans
"""

class SideBySideComparison:
    """
    Compares two Spark query plans side-by-side with detailed analysis
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
        
    def capture_plan(self, df, plan_name: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Capture comprehensive plan information for a DataFrame
        
        Args:
            df: Spark DataFrame
            plan_name: Identifier for this plan
            
        Returns:
            Dictionary containing plan details
        """
        plan_info = {
            'name': plan_name,
            'timestamp': datetime.now().isoformat(),
            'logical_plan': df._jdf.queryExecution().optimizedPlan().toString(),
            'physical_plan': df._jdf.queryExecution().executedPlan().toString(),
            'analyzed_plan': df._jdf.queryExecution().analyzed().toString(),
            'optimized_plan': df._jdf.queryExecution().optimizedPlan().toString(),
        }
        
        # Extract plan nodes
        plan_info['logical_nodes'] = self._extract_nodes(plan_info['logical_plan'])
        plan_info['physical_nodes'] = self._extract_nodes(plan_info['physical_plan'])
        
        return plan_info
    
    def _extract_nodes(self, plan_str: str) -> List[str]:
        """Extract individual nodes from a plan string"""
        # Split by lines and filter out empty lines
        nodes = [line.strip() for line in plan_str.split('\n') if line.strip()]
        return nodes
    
    def compare_plans(self, plan1: Dict, plan2: Dict) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Perform side-by-side comparison of two plans
        
        Returns:
            Comparison results with detailed analysis
        """
        comparison = {
            'plan1_name': plan1['name'],
            'plan2_name': plan2['name'],
            'comparison_timestamp': datetime.now().isoformat(),
            'structural_differences': {},
            'node_differences': {},
            'optimization_differences': {}
        }
        
        # Compare logical plans
        comparison['structural_differences']['logical'] = self._compare_node_lists(
            plan1['logical_nodes'], 
            plan2['logical_nodes']
        )
        
        # Compare physical plans
        comparison['structural_differences']['physical'] = self._compare_node_lists(
            plan1['physical_nodes'], 
            plan2['physical_nodes']
        )
        
        # Identify optimization changes
        comparison['optimization_differences'] = self._identify_optimizations(
            plan1, plan2
        )
        
        return comparison
    
    def _compare_node_lists(self, nodes1: List[str], nodes2: List[str]) -> Dict:
        """Compare two lists of plan nodes"""
        return {
            'nodes_only_in_plan1': list(set(nodes1) - set(nodes2)),
            'nodes_only_in_plan2': list(set(nodes2) - set(nodes1)),
            'common_nodes': list(set(nodes1) & set(nodes2)),
            'plan1_node_count': len(nodes1),
            'plan2_node_count': len(nodes2),
            'node_count_delta': len(nodes2) - len(nodes1)
        }
    
    def _identify_optimizations(self, plan1: Dict, plan2: Dict) -> Dict:
        """Identify specific optimization patterns"""
        optimizations = {
            'predicate_pushdown': False,
            'projection_pruning': False,
            'join_reordering': False,
            'broadcast_hint': False,
            'partition_pruning': False
        }
        
        # Check for predicate pushdown
        if 'Filter' in plan2['physical_plan'] and 'Filter' not in plan1['physical_plan']:
            optimizations['predicate_pushdown'] = True
            
        # Check for broadcast joins
        if 'BroadcastHashJoin' in plan2['physical_plan']:
            optimizations['broadcast_hint'] = True
            
        # Check for projection pruning (fewer columns)
        plan1_projects = plan1['physical_plan'].count('Project')
        plan2_projects = plan2['physical_plan'].count('Project')
        if plan2_projects < plan1_projects:
            optimizations['projection_pruning'] = True
            
        return optimizations
    
    def display_comparison(self, comparison: Dict) -> None:
        """Display comparison results in a readable format"""
        print("=" * 80)
        print(f"SIDE-BY-SIDE QUERY PLAN COMPARISON")
        print("=" * 80)
        print(f"Plan 1: {comparison['plan1_name']}")
        print(f"Plan 2: {comparison['plan2_name']}")
        print(f"Comparison Time: {comparison['comparison_timestamp']}")
        print("\n" + "-" * 80)
        
        # Structural differences
        print("\nSTRUCTURAL DIFFERENCES (Physical Plan):")
        phys_diff = comparison['structural_differences']['physical']
        print(f"  Plan 1 Nodes: {phys_diff['plan1_node_count']}")
        print(f"  Plan 2 Nodes: {phys_diff['plan2_node_count']}")
        print(f"  Delta: {phys_diff['node_count_delta']:+d}")
        
        if phys_diff['nodes_only_in_plan1']:
            print(f"\n  Nodes only in Plan 1:")
            for node in phys_diff['nodes_only_in_plan1'][:5]:  # Limit output
                print(f"    - {node[:70]}...")
                
        if phys_diff['nodes_only_in_plan2']:
            print(f"\n  Nodes only in Plan 2:")
            for node in phys_diff['nodes_only_in_plan2'][:5]:
                print(f"    - {node[:70]}...")
        
        # Optimization differences
        print("\nOPTIMIZATIONS DETECTED:")
        for opt_name, opt_present in comparison['optimization_differences'].items():
            status = "✓" if opt_present else "✗"
            print(f"  {status} {opt_name.replace('_', ' ').title()}")
        
        print("=" * 80)

"""
Purpose: Generate unified diff of query plans to highlight exact changes
Use Case: Code review, debugging query changes, version control
"""

class DiffComparisonPattern:
    """
    Generate detailed diff comparisons between query plans
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
        
    def generate_unified_diff(self, plan1_str: str, plan2_str: str, 
                             plan1_name: str = "Plan A", 
                             plan2_name: str = "Plan B") -> str:
        """
        Generate unified diff between two plan strings
        
        Returns:
            Unified diff string
        """
        plan1_lines = plan1_str.splitlines(keepends=True)
        plan2_lines = plan2_str.splitlines(keepends=True)
        
        diff = difflib.unified_diff(
            plan1_lines,
            plan2_lines,
            fromfile=plan1_name,
            tofile=plan2_name,
            lineterm='\n'
        )
        
        return ''.join(diff)
    
    def generate_html_diff(self, plan1_str: str, plan2_str: str,
                          plan1_name: str = "Plan A",
                          plan2_name: str = "Plan B") -> str:
        """
        Generate HTML side-by-side diff
        
        Returns:
            HTML string with colored diff
        """
        plan1_lines = plan1_str.splitlines()
        plan2_lines = plan2_str.splitlines()
        
        differ = difflib.HtmlDiff()
        html_diff = differ.make_file(
            plan1_lines,
            plan2_lines,
            fromdesc=plan1_name,
            todesc=plan2_name,
            context=True,
            numlines=3
        )
        
        return html_diff
    
    def analyze_diff_statistics(self, plan1_str: str, plan2_str: str) -> Dict:
        """
        Generate statistics about the differences between plans
        
        Returns:
            Dictionary with diff statistics
        """
        plan1_lines = plan1_str.splitlines()
        plan2_lines = plan2_str.splitlines()
        
        # Use SequenceMatcher for detailed analysis
        matcher = difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, plan1_lines, plan2_lines)
        
        stats = {
            'similarity_ratio': matcher.ratio(),
            'total_lines_plan1': len(plan1_lines),
            'total_lines_plan2': len(plan2_lines),
            'matching_blocks': len(matcher.get_matching_blocks()),
            'opcodes': []
        }
        
        # Analyze opcodes
        additions = 0
        deletions = 0
        replacements = 0
        
        for tag, i1, i2, j1, j2 in matcher.get_opcodes():
            if tag == 'insert':
                additions += (j2 - j1)
            elif tag == 'delete':
                deletions += (i2 - i1)
            elif tag == 'replace':
                replacements += max(i2 - i1, j2 - j1)
                
            stats['opcodes'].append({
                'operation': tag,
                'plan1_range': (i1, i2),
                'plan2_range': (j1, j2)
            })
        
        stats['additions'] = additions
        stats['deletions'] = deletions
        stats['replacements'] = replacements
        stats['total_changes'] = additions + deletions + replacements
        
        return stats
    
    def extract_semantic_changes(self, plan1_str: str, plan2_str: str) -> Dict:
        """
        Extract semantic changes (joins, filters, aggregations, etc.)
        
        Returns:
            Dictionary of semantic changes
        """
        changes = {
            'join_changes': [],
            'filter_changes': [],
            'aggregation_changes': [],
            'scan_changes': [],
            'exchange_changes': []
        }
        
        # Extract operators from both plans
        operators1 = self._extract_operators(plan1_str)
        operators2 = self._extract_operators(plan2_str)
        
        # Compare joins
        changes['join_changes'] = self._compare_operators(
            operators1.get('joins', []),
            operators2.get('joins', []),
            'join'
        )
        
        # Compare filters
        changes['filter_changes'] = self._compare_operators(
            operators1.get('filters', []),
            operators2.get('filters', []),
            'filter'
        )
        
        # Compare aggregations
        changes['aggregation_changes'] = self._compare_operators(
            operators1.get('aggregations', []),
            operators2.get('aggregations', []),
            'aggregation'
        )
        
        return changes
    
    def _extract_operators(self, plan_str: str) -> Dict[str, List[str]]:
        """Extract different types of operators from plan"""
        operators = {
            'joins': [],
            'filters': [],
            'aggregations': [],
            'scans': [],
            'exchanges': []
        }
        
        for line in plan_str.split('\n'):
            if 'Join' in line:
                operators['joins'].append(line.strip())
            elif 'Filter' in line:
                operators['filters'].append(line.strip())
            elif 'Aggregate' in line or 'HashAggregate' in line:
                operators['aggregations'].append(line.strip())
            elif 'Scan' in line:
                operators['scans'].append(line.strip())
            elif 'Exchange' in line:
                operators['exchanges'].append(line.strip())
                
        return operators
    
    def _compare_operators(self, ops1: List[str], ops2: List[str], 
                          op_type: str) -> List[Dict]:
        """Compare two lists of operators"""
        changes = []
        
        # Find additions
        for op in set(ops2) - set(ops1):
            changes.append({
                'type': 'addition',
                'operator_type': op_type,
                'detail': op
            })
        
        # Find deletions
        for op in set(ops1) - set(ops2):
            changes.append({
                'type': 'deletion',
                'operator_type': op_type,
                'detail': op
            })
        
        return changes

"""

class CostComparisonPattern:

        """

            Dictionary with cost metrics
        """
        # Get query execution
        qe = df._jdf.queryExecution()
        
        metrics = {

        }

        optimized_plan = qe.optimizedPlan().toString()
        
        # Parse statistics from plan
        metrics['statistics'] = self._parse_statistics(optimized_plan)
        
        # Extract cost estimates
        metrics['estimated_costs'] = self._extract_cost_estimates(optimized_plan)
        
        return metrics
    
    def _parse_statistics(self, plan_str: str) -> Dict:
        """Parse statistics from plan string"""
        stats = {
            'row_count_estimates': [],
            'size_estimates': [],
            'partition_counts': []
        }
        
        # Extract row count estimates (sizeInBytes=X, rowCount=Y)
        size_pattern = r'sizeInBytes=(\d+\.?\d*\s*[KMG]?B?)'
        row_pattern = r'rowCount=(\d+\.?\d*\s*[KMG]?)'
        
        size_matches = re.findall(size_pattern, plan_str)
        row_matches = re.findall(row_pattern, plan_str)
        
        stats['size_estimates'] = size_matches
        stats['row_count_estimates'] = row_matches
        
        return stats

    def compare_costs(self, metrics1: Dict, metrics2: Dict) -> Dict:
        """

                'query2_value': costs2[cost_type],

            }
        
        # Calculate efficiency score (lower is better)
        total_cost1 = sum(costs1.values())

        if 'io_cost' in cost_diffs:
            io_change = cost_diffs['io_cost']['percent_change']
            if io_change > 15:
                recommendations.append(
                    f"I/O cost increased by {io_change:.1f}%. "
                    "Consider: 1) Partition pruning, 2) Column pruning, 3) File format optimization"
                )
        
        # Check CPU cost
        if 'cpu_cost' in cost_diffs:
            cpu_change = cost_diffs['cpu_cost']['percent_change']
            if cpu_change > 25:
                recommendations.append(
                    f"CPU cost increased by {cpu_change:.1f}%. "
                    "Consider: 1) Filter pushdown, 2) Reducing complex operations, 3) Caching intermediate results"
                )
        
        # Check broadcast exchanges
        if 'broadcast_exchanges' in cost_diffs:
            bc_delta = cost_diffs['broadcast_exchanges']['delta']
            if bc_delta < 0:
                recommendations.append(

                )
