# ADVANCED MONITORING AND ALERTING SYSTEM
# ============================================================================

class ReplicationAlertSystem:
    """
    Advanced alerting system for replication issues
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession, alert_thresholds: Dict[str, any]):
        """
        Initialize alert system
        
        Args:
            spark: SparkSession instance
            alert_thresholds: Dictionary of alert thresholds
        """
        self.spark = spark
        self.thresholds = alert_thresholds
        self.alerts = []
    
    def check_replication_health(self, master_path: str, 
                                replica_paths: List[str]) -> List[Dict]:
        """
        Check replication health and generate alerts
        
        Args:
            master_path: Master data path
            replica_paths: List of replica paths
            
        Returns:
            List of alerts
        """
        print("\n" + "="*60)
        print("REPLICATION HEALTH CHECK - Generating Alerts")
        print("="*60 + "\n")
        
        alerts = []
        
        try:
            master_df = self.spark.read.parquet(master_path)
            master_count = master_df.count()
            master_timestamp = master_df.select(max("write_timestamp")).collect()[0][0]
            
            print(f"Master Status:")
            print(f"  Path: {master_path}")
            print(f"  Records: {master_count}")
            print(f"  Last Update: {master_timestamp}")
            
            for replica_path in replica_paths:
                print(f"\nChecking replica: {replica_path}")
                
                try:
                    replica_df = self.spark.read.parquet(replica_path)
                    replica_count = replica_df.count()
                    replica_timestamp = replica_df.select(
                        max("slave_sync_timestamp")
                    ).collect()[0][0]
                    
                    # Check 1: Record count difference
                    count_diff = abs(master_count - replica_count)
                    count_diff_pct = (count_diff / master_count * 100) if master_count > 0 else 0
                    
                    if count_diff_pct > self.thresholds.get("max_count_diff_pct", 5):
                        alert = {
                            "severity": "HIGH",
                            "type": "COUNT_MISMATCH",
                            "replica": replica_path,
                            "message": f"Record count differs by {count_diff_pct:.2f}%",
                            "details": {
                                "master_count": master_count,
                                "replica_count": replica_count,
                                "difference": count_diff
                            }
                        }
                        alerts.append(alert)
                        print(f"  ⚠ ALERT: {alert['message']}")
                    
                    # Check 2: Replication lag
                    if master_timestamp and replica_timestamp:
                        lag_seconds = (master_timestamp - replica_timestamp).total_seconds()
                        
                        if lag_seconds > self.thresholds.get("max_lag_seconds", 300):
                            alert = {
                                "severity": "MEDIUM",
                                "type": "REPLICATION_LAG",
                                "replica": replica_path,
                                "message": f"Replication lag is {lag_seconds:.0f} seconds",
                                "details": {
                                    "lag_seconds": lag_seconds,
                                    "threshold": self.thresholds.get("max_lag_seconds", 300)
                                }
                            }
                            alerts.append(alert)
                            print(f"  ⚠ ALERT: {alert['message']}")
                    
                    # Check 3: Data freshness
                    current_time = datetime.now()
                    if replica_timestamp:
                        age_seconds = (current_time - replica_timestamp).total_seconds()
                        
                        if age_seconds > self.thresholds.get("max_age_seconds", 3600):
                            alert = {
                                "severity": "LOW",
                                "type": "STALE_DATA",
                                "replica": replica_path,
                                "message": f"Data is {age_seconds/3600:.1f} hours old",
                                "details": {
                                    "age_seconds": age_seconds,
                                    "last_update": replica_timestamp.isoformat()
                                }
                            }
                            alerts.append(alert)
                            print(f"  ⚠ ALERT: {alert['message']}")
                    
                    if not any(a["replica"] == replica_path for a in alerts):
                        print(f"  ✓ Replica healthy")
                    
                except Exception as e:
                    alert = {
                        "severity": "CRITICAL",
                        "type": "REPLICA_UNAVAILABLE",
                        "replica": replica_path,
                        "message": f"Replica unavailable: {str(e)}",
                        "details": {"error": str(e)}
                    }
                    alerts.append(alert)
                    print(f"  ✗ CRITICAL: {alert['message']}")
        
        except Exception as e:
            alert = {
                "severity": "CRITICAL",
                "type": "MASTER_UNAVAILABLE",
                "replica": "N/A",
                "message": f"Master unavailable: {str(e)}",
                "details": {"error": str(e)}
            }
            alerts.append(alert)
            print(f"✗ CRITICAL: Master unavailable - {str(e)}")
        
        # Summary
        print(f"\n{'='*60}")
        print(f"Health Check Summary:")
        print(f"  Total Alerts: {len(alerts)}")
        
        severity_counts = {}
        for alert in alerts:
            severity = alert["severity"]
            severity_counts[severity] = severity_counts.get(severity, 0) + 1
        
        for severity, count in severity_counts.items():
            print(f"  {severity}: {count}")
        
        print(f"{'='*60}\n")
        
        self.alerts.extend(alerts)
        return alerts
    
    def send_alerts(self, alerts: List[Dict], notification_method: str = "console"):
        """
        Send alerts via specified notification method
        
        Args:
            alerts: List of alerts to send
            notification_method: Method to use (console, email, slack, etc.)
        """
        print("\n" + "="*60)
        print(f"SENDING ALERTS via {notification_method.upper()}")
        print("="*60 + "\n")
        
        if not alerts:
            print("No alerts to send")
            return
        
        # Sort by severity
        severity_order = {"CRITICAL": 0, "HIGH": 1, "MEDIUM": 2, "LOW": 3}
        sorted_alerts = sorted(alerts, key=lambda x: severity_order.get(x["severity"], 4))
        
        for alert in sorted_alerts:
            self._format_alert(alert, notification_method)
    
    def _format_alert(self, alert: Dict, method: str):
        """Format and display/send alert"""
        
        severity_icons = {
            "CRITICAL": "🔴",
            "HIGH": "🟠",
            "MEDIUM": "🟡",
            "LOW": "🟢"
        }
        
        icon = severity_icons.get(alert["severity"], "⚪")
        
        print(f"{icon} [{alert['severity']}] {alert['type']}")
        print(f"   Replica: {alert['replica']}")
        print(f"   Message: {alert['message']}")
        
        if alert.get("details"):
            print(f"   Details: {json.dumps(alert['details'], indent=6)}")
        
        print()

# DATA QUALITY VALIDATION FOR REPLICAS
# ============================================================================

class ReplicationDataQuality:
    """
    Validate data quality across replicas
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
    
    def validate_schema_consistency(self, paths: List[str]) -> bool:
        """
        Validate that all replicas have consistent schemas
        
        Args:
            paths: List of replica paths
            
        Returns:
            True if schemas are consistent
        """
        print("\n" + "="*60)
        print("SCHEMA CONSISTENCY VALIDATION")
        print("="*60 + "\n")
        
        schemas = {}
        
        for path in paths:
            try:
                df = self.spark.read.parquet(path)
                schemas[path] = df.schema
                print(f"✓ Schema loaded from: {path}")
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"✗ Failed to load schema from {path}: {str(e)}")
                return False
        
        # Compare all schemas
        reference_schema = list(schemas.values())[0]
        
        all_consistent = True
        for path, schema in schemas.items():
            if schema != reference_schema:
                print(f"\n✗ Schema mismatch detected in: {path}")
                print(f"   Expected: {reference_schema}")
                print(f"   Found: {schema}")
                all_consistent = False
        
        if all_consistent:
            print(f"\n✓ All {len(schemas)} replicas have consistent schemas")
        
        print(f"{'='*60}\n")
        return all_consistent
    
    def validate_data_integrity(self, source_path: str, 
                               replica_path: str,
                               sample_size: int = 1000) -> Dict[str, any]:
        """
        Validate data integrity between source and replica
        
        Args:
            source_path: Source data path
            replica_path: Replica data path
            sample_size: Number of records to sample
            
        Returns:
            Validation results
        """
        print("\n" + "="*60)
        print("DATA INTEGRITY VALIDATION")
        print("="*60)
        print(f"Source: {source_path}")
        print(f"Replica: {replica_path}")
        print(f"Sample Size: {sample_size}\n")
        
        result = {
            "schema_match": False,
            "count_match": False,
            "checksum_match": False,
            "sample_match": False,
            "issues": []
        }
        
        try:
            source_df = self.spark.read.parquet(source_path)
            replica_df = self.spark.read.parquet(replica_path)
            
            # 1. Schema validation
            if source_df.schema == replica_df.schema:
                result["schema_match"] = True
                print("✓ Schemas match")
            else:
                result["issues"].append("Schema mismatch")
                print("✗ Schemas do not match")
            
            # 2. Count validation
            source_count = source_df.count()
            replica_count = replica_df.count()
            
            if source_count == replica_count:
                result["count_match"] = True
                print(f"✓ Record counts match ({source_count} records)")
            else:
                result["issues"].append(f"Count mismatch: {source_count} vs {replica_count}")
                print(f"✗ Record counts differ: {source_count} vs {replica_count}")
            
            # 3. Checksum validation (on sample)
            print(f"\nValidating checksums on {sample_size} records...")
            
            # Create checksums for comparison
            source_sample = source_df.limit(sample_size) \
                .withColumn("row_checksum", 
                           sha2(concat_ws("|", *source_df.columns), 256))
            
            replica_sample = replica_df.limit(sample_size) \
                .withColumn("row_checksum", 
                           sha2(concat_ws("|", *replica_df.columns), 256))
            
            source_checksums = set([row.row_checksum for row in source_sample.collect()])
            replica_checksums = set([row.row_checksum for row in replica_sample.collect()])
            
            matching_checksums = len(source_checksums.intersection(replica_checksums))
            match_percentage = (matching_checksums / len(source_checksums) * 100) if source_checksums else 0
            
            if match_percentage >= 99:
                result["checksum_match"] = True
                print(f"✓ Checksums match ({match_percentage:.2f}%)")
            else:
                result["issues"].append(f"Checksum mismatch: {match_percentage:.2f}% match")
                print(f"✗ Checksums differ ({match_percentage:.2f}% match)")
            
            # 4. Sample data validation
            if source_df.limit(10).collect() == replica_df.limit(10).collect():
                result["sample_match"] = True
                print("✓ Sample data matches")
            else:
                result["issues"].append("Sample data mismatch")
                print("✗ Sample data differs")
            
        except Exception as e:
            result["issues"].append(f"Validation error: {str(e)}")
            print(f"✗ Validation failed: {str(e)}")
        
        # Summary
        print(f"\n{'='*60}")
        print("Validation Summary:")
        print(f"  Schema Match: {'✓' if result['schema_match'] else '✗'}")
        print(f"  Count Match: {'✓' if result['count_match'] else '✗'}")
        print(f"  Checksum Match: {'✓' if result['checksum_match'] else '✗'}")
        print(f"  Sample Match: {'✓' if result['sample_match'] else '✗'}")
        
        if result["issues"]:
            print(f"\n  Issues Found: {len(result['issues'])}")
            for issue in result["issues"]:
                print(f"    - {issue}")
        else:
            print(f"\n  ✓ No issues found - data integrity verified")
        
        print(f"{'='*60}\n")
        
        return result

# AUTOMATED RECOVERY SYSTEM
# ============================================================================

class AutomatedRecoverySystem:
    """
    Automated recovery for failed replications
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession, max_retries: int = 3):
        """
        Initialize automated recovery system
        
        Args:
            spark: SparkSession instance
            max_retries: Maximum number of retry attempts
        """
        self.spark = spark
        self.max_retries = max_retries
        self.recovery_log = []
    
    def recover_failed_replica(self, source_path: str, 
                               failed_replica_path: str,
                               retry_delay: int = 5) -> bool:
        """
        Attempt to recover a failed replica
        
        Args:
            source_path: Source data path
            failed_replica_path: Path of failed replica
            retry_delay: Delay between retries (seconds)
            
        Returns:
            True if recovery successful
        """
        print("\n" + "="*60)
        print("AUTOMATED RECOVERY - Starting")
        print("="*60)
        print(f"Source: {source_path}")
        print(f"Failed Replica: {failed_replica_path}")
        print(f"Max Retries: {self.max_retries}\n")
```python
        
        for attempt in range(1, self.max_retries + 1):
            print(f"[Attempt {attempt}/{self.max_retries}] Attempting recovery...")
            
            try:
                # Read source data
                source_df = self.spark.read.parquet(source_path)
                source_count = source_df.count()
                
                print(f"  Source data loaded: {source_count} records")
                
                # Add recovery metadata
                recovery_df = source_df.withColumn("recovery_attempt", lit(attempt)) \
                                      .withColumn("recovery_timestamp", current_timestamp()) \
                                      .withColumn("recovered", lit(True))
                
                # Attempt to write to failed replica
                recovery_df.write \
                    .mode("overwrite") \
                    .option("compression", "snappy") \
                    .parquet(failed_replica_path)
                
                # Verify recovery
                recovered_df = self.spark.read.parquet(failed_replica_path)
                recovered_count = recovered_df.count()
                
                if recovered_count == source_count:
                    print(f"  ✓ Recovery successful!")
                    print(f"  Verified {recovered_count} records")
                    
                    # Log successful recovery
                    self._log_recovery(failed_replica_path, attempt, "SUCCESS", source_count)
                    
                    print(f"\n{'='*60}")
                    print(f"✓ Replica recovered successfully on attempt {attempt}")
                    print(f"{'='*60}\n")
                    
                    return True
                else:
                    print(f"  ✗ Verification failed: {recovered_count} vs {source_count} records")
                    raise Exception("Record count mismatch after recovery")
                
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"  ✗ Attempt {attempt} failed: {str(e)}")
                
                self._log_recovery(failed_replica_path, attempt, "FAILED", 0, str(e))
                
                if attempt < self.max_retries:
                    print(f"  Waiting {retry_delay} seconds before retry...")
                    time.sleep(retry_delay)
                    retry_delay *= 2  # Exponential backoff
        
        print(f"\n{'='*60}")
        print(f"✗ Recovery failed after {self.max_retries} attempts")
        print(f"{'='*60}\n")
        
        return False
    
    def auto_failover(self, master_path: str, slave_paths: List[str],
                     new_master_index: int = 0) -> Dict[str, any]:
        """
        Perform automatic failover from master to slave
        
        Args:
            master_path: Current master path
            slave_paths: List of slave paths
            new_master_index: Index of slave to promote
            
        Returns:
            Failover result
        """
        print("\n" + "="*60)
        print("AUTOMATED FAILOVER - Starting")
        print("="*60)
        print(f"Current Master: {master_path}")
        print(f"Promoting Slave {new_master_index + 1}: {slave_paths[new_master_index]}\n")
        
        result = {
            "success": False,
            "old_master": master_path,
            "new_master": None,
            "backup_path": None,
            "timestamp": datetime.now().isoformat()
        }
        
        try:
            # Step 1: Verify slave is healthy
            print("[Step 1] Verifying slave health...")
            slave_path = slave_paths[new_master_index]
            slave_df = self.spark.read.parquet(slave_path)
            slave_count = slave_df.count()
            
            print(f"  ✓ Slave is healthy ({slave_count} records)")
            
            # Step 2: Backup current master (if accessible)
            print("\n[Step 2] Backing up current master...")
            backup_path = f"{master_path}_backup_{int(time.time())}"
            
            try:
                master_df = self.spark.read.parquet(master_path)
                master_df.write.mode("overwrite").parquet(backup_path)
                result["backup_path"] = backup_path
                print(f"  ✓ Master backed up to: {backup_path}")
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"  ⚠ Master backup failed (may be unavailable): {str(e)}")
            
            # Step 3: Promote slave to master
            print("\n[Step 3] Promoting slave to master...")
            
            promoted_df = slave_df.withColumn("is_master", lit(True)) \
                                 .withColumn("promoted_at", current_timestamp()) \
                                 .withColumn("failover_reason", lit("auto_failover"))
            
            promoted_df.write \
                .mode("overwrite") \
                .parquet(master_path)
            
            print(f"  ✓ Slave promoted to master")
            
            # Step 4: Verify new master
            print("\n[Step 4] Verifying new master...")
            new_master_df = self.spark.read.parquet(master_path)
            new_master_count = new_master_df.count()
            
            if new_master_count == slave_count:
                print(f"  ✓ New master verified ({new_master_count} records)")
                result["success"] = True
                result["new_master"] = master_path
            else:
                raise Exception(f"Verification failed: {new_master_count} vs {slave_count}")
            
            # Step 5: Update slave list
            print("\n[Step 5] Updating slave configuration...")
            remaining_slaves = [s for i, s in enumerate(slave_paths) if i != new_master_index]
            print(f"  ✓ Remaining slaves: {len(remaining_slaves)}")
            
            print(f"\n{'='*60}")
            print("✓ Automated failover completed successfully")
            print(f"  New Master: {master_path}")
            print(f"  Backup: {backup_path}")
            print(f"{'='*60}\n")
            
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"\n✗ Failover failed: {str(e)}")
            result["error"] = str(e)
            
            # Attempt rollback if backup exists
            if result["backup_path"]:
                print("\nAttempting rollback...")
                try:
                    backup_df = self.spark.read.parquet(result["backup_path"])
                    backup_df.write.mode("overwrite").parquet(master_path)
                    print("  ✓ Rollback successful")
                except Exception as rollback_error:
                    print(f"  ✗ Rollback failed: {str(rollback_error)}")
        
        self._log_recovery(master_path, 1, "FAILOVER", 0, 
                          "SUCCESS" if result["success"] else "FAILED")
        
        return result
    
    def _log_recovery(self, path: str, attempt: int, status: str, 
                     count: int, error: str = None):
        """Log recovery event"""
        log_entry = {
            "timestamp": datetime.now().isoformat(),
            "path": path,
            "attempt": attempt,
            "status": status,
            "record_count": count,
            "error": error
        }
        self.recovery_log.append(log_entry)

class ReplicationOptimizer:
    """
    Optimize replication performance
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
    
    def optimize_partition_strategy(self, df: DataFrame, 
                                    target_partition_size_mb: int = 128) -> DataFrame:
        """
        Optimize DataFrame partitioning for replication
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            target_partition_size_mb: Target partition size in MB
            
        Returns:
            Optimized DataFrame
        """
        print("\n" + "="*60)
        print("PARTITION OPTIMIZATION")
        print("="*60 + "\n")
        
        # Calculate current statistics
        current_partitions = df.rdd.getNumPartitions()
        
        # Estimate data size (rough approximation)
        sample_size = min(1000, df.count())
        if sample_size > 0:
            sample_df = df.limit(sample_size)
            # Rough estimation based on sample
            estimated_total_mb = sample_size * 0.001  # Placeholder estimation
        else:
            estimated_total_mb = 100
        
        # Calculate optimal partitions
        optimal_partitions = max(1, int(estimated_total_mb / target_partition_size_mb))
        
        print(f"Current Configuration:")
        print(f"  Partitions: {current_partitions}")
        print(f"  Estimated Size: {estimated_total_mb:.2f} MB")
        
        print(f"\nOptimized Configuration:")
        print(f"  Target Partition Size: {target_partition_size_mb} MB")
        print(f"  Recommended Partitions: {optimal_partitions}")
        
        if optimal_partitions != current_partitions:
            print(f"\n  Repartitioning from {current_partitions} to {optimal_partitions}...")
            optimized_df = df.repartition(optimal_partitions)
            print(f"  ✓ Repartitioning complete")
        else:
            print(f"\n  ✓ Current partitioning is optimal")
            optimized_df = df
        
        print(f"{'='*60}\n")
        
        return optimized_df
    
    def add_compression(self, df: DataFrame, output_path: str,
                       compression_type: str = "snappy") -> Dict[str, any]:
        """
        Write DataFrame with optimal compression
        
        Args:
            df: DataFrame to write
            output_path: Output path
            compression_type: Compression codec (snappy, gzip, lz4, zstd)
            
        Returns:
            Compression statistics
        """
        print("\n" + "="*60)
        print(f"COMPRESSION OPTIMIZATION - {compression_type.upper()}")
        print("="*60 + "\n")
        
        result = {
            "compression_type": compression_type,
            "output_path": output_path,
            "write_time": None
        }
        
        start_time = time.time()
        
        try:
            df.write \
                .mode("overwrite") \
                .option("compression", compression_type) \
                .parquet(output_path)
            
            result["write_time"] = time.time() - start_time
            
            # Read back to verify
            compressed_df = self.spark.read.parquet(output_path)
            result["record_count"] = compressed_df.count()
            
            print(f"✓ Data written with {compression_type} compression")
            print(f"  Records: {result['record_count']}")
            print(f"  Write Time: {result['write_time']:.2f}s")
            print(f"  Output: {output_path}")
            
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"✗ Compression failed: {str(e)}")
            result["error"] = str(e)
        
        print(f"{'='*60}\n")
        
        return result
    
    def benchmark_compression_methods(self, df: DataFrame, 
                                     base_path: str) -> DataFrame:
        """
        Benchmark different compression methods
        
        Args:
            df: Test DataFrame
            base_path: Base path for test outputs
            
        Returns:
            DataFrame with benchmark results
        """
        print("\n" + "="*60)
        print("COMPRESSION BENCHMARK")
        print("="*60 + "\n")
        
        compression_methods = ["none", "snappy", "gzip", "lz4"]
        results = []
        
        for method in compression_methods:
            print(f"Testing {method}...")
            
            output_path = f"{base_path}/compression_test_{method}"
            
            try:
                start_time = time.time()
                
                df.write \
                    .mode("overwrite") \
                    .option("compression", method) \
                    .parquet(output_path)
                
                write_time = time.time() - start_time
                
                # Read back
                read_start = time.time()
                test_df = self.spark.read.parquet(output_path)
                count = test_df.count()
                read_time = time.time() - read_start
                
                # Get size (rough estimate)
                import os
                size_mb = 0
                if os.path.exists(output_path):
                    for root, dirs, files in os.walk(output_path):
                        size_mb += sum(os.path.getsize(os.path.join(root, f)) 
                                     for f in files) / (1024 * 1024)
                
                results.append({
                    "compression": method,
                    "write_time_sec": round(write_time, 2),
                    "read_time_sec": round(read_time, 2),
                    "size_mb": round(size_mb, 2),
                    "records": count
                })
                
                print(f"  Write: {write_time:.2f}s, Read: {read_time:.2f}s, Size: {size_mb:.2f}MB")
                
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"  ✗ Failed: {str(e)}")
                results.append({
                    "compression": method,
                    "write_time_sec": None,
                    "read_time_sec": None,
                    "size_mb": None,
                    "records": 0
                })
        
        # Create results DataFrame
        schema = StructType([
            StructField("compression", StringType(), False),
            StructField("write_time_sec", DoubleType(), True),
            StructField("read_time_sec", DoubleType(), True),
            StructField("size_mb", DoubleType(), True),
            StructField("records", IntegerType(), True)
        ])
        
        results_df = self.spark.createDataFrame(results, schema)
        
        print(f"\n{'='*60}")
        print("Compression Benchmark Results:")
        results_df.show(truncate=False)
        print(f"{'='*60}\n")
        
        return results_df

class ReplicationScheduler:
    """
    Schedule and manage periodic replication tasks
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
        self.scheduled_tasks = []
    
    def schedule_replication(self, task_name: str, pattern: any,
                            schedule_type: str, interval_seconds: int,
                            source_df: DataFrame, target_paths: List[str]):
        """
        Schedule a replication task
        
        Args:
            task_name: Name of the task
            pattern: Replication pattern instance
            schedule_type: Type of schedule (interval, cron, etc.)
            interval_seconds: Interval in seconds
            source_df: Source DataFrame
            target_paths: Target paths
        """
        task = {
            "name": task_name,
            "pattern": pattern,
            "schedule_
```python
            "schedule_type": schedule_type,
            "interval_seconds": interval_seconds,
            "source_df": source_df,
            "target_paths": target_paths,
            "last_run": None,
            "next_run": datetime.now(),
            "run_count": 0,
            "status": "SCHEDULED"
        }
        
        self.scheduled_tasks.append(task)
        
        print(f"\n✓ Scheduled replication task: {task_name}")
        print(f"  Schedule Type: {schedule_type}")
        print(f"  Interval: {interval_seconds} seconds")
        print(f"  Next Run: {task['next_run']}")
    
    def run_scheduled_tasks(self, max_runs: int = None):
        """
        Run scheduled replication tasks
        
        Args:
            max_runs: Maximum number of runs (None for infinite)
        """
        print("\n" + "="*60)
        print("REPLICATION SCHEDULER - Starting")
        print("="*60)
        print(f"Scheduled Tasks: {len(self.scheduled_tasks)}")
        print(f"Max Runs: {max_runs if max_runs else 'Infinite'}\n")
        
        run_count = 0
        
        try:
            while True:
                current_time = datetime.now()
                
                for task in self.scheduled_tasks:
                    if task["status"] != "ACTIVE":
                        continue
                    
                    if current_time >= task["next_run"]:
                        print(f"\n[{current_time.strftime('%H:%M:%S')}] Running task: {task['name']}")
                        
                        try:
                            # Execute replication based on pattern type
                            if isinstance(task["pattern"], SynchronousReplicationPattern):
                                task["pattern"].replicate_data(
                                    task["source_df"],
                                    task["target_paths"]
                                )
                            elif isinstance(task["pattern"], AsynchronousReplicationPattern):
                                task["pattern"].replicate_data(
                                    task["source_df"],
                                    task["target_paths"][0],
                                    task["target_paths"][1:]
                                )
                            # Add other pattern types as needed
                            
                            task["last_run"] = current_time
                            task["run_count"] += 1
                            task["next_run"] = current_time + timedelta(seconds=task["interval_seconds"])
                            
                            print(f"  ✓ Task completed (Run #{task['run_count']})")
                            print(f"  Next run: {task['next_run'].strftime('%H:%M:%S')}")
                            
                        except Exception as e:
                            print(f"  ✗ Task failed: {str(e)}")
                            task["status"] = "FAILED"
                
                run_count += 1
                
                if max_runs and run_count >= max_runs:
                    print(f"\n{'='*60}")
                    print(f"Reached maximum runs ({max_runs})")
                    break
                
                # Sleep for a short interval
                time.sleep(5)
                
        except KeyboardInterrupt:
            print(f"\n{'='*60}")
            print("Scheduler stopped by user")
        
        print(f"{'='*60}\n")
    
    def get_task_status(self) -> DataFrame:
        """Get status of all scheduled tasks"""
        
        if not self.scheduled_tasks:
            print("No scheduled tasks")
            return None
        
        status_data = []
        for task in self.scheduled_tasks:
            status_data.append({
                "task_name": task["name"],
                "status": task["status"],
                "run_count": task["run_count"],
                "last_run": task["last_run"].isoformat() if task["last_run"] else None,
                "next_run": task["next_run"].isoformat() if task["next_run"] else None
            })
        
        schema = StructType([
            StructField("task_name", StringType(), False),
            StructField("status", StringType(), False),
            StructField("run_count", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("last_run", StringType(), True),
            StructField("next_run", StringType(), True)
        ])
        
        status_df = self.spark.createDataFrame(status_data, schema)
        
        print("\n" + "="*60)
        print("SCHEDULED TASKS STATUS")
        print("="*60 + "\n")
        
        status_df.show(truncate=False)
        
        return status_df

# REPLICATION METRICS COLLECTOR
# ============================================================================

class ReplicationMetricsCollector:
    """
    Collect and analyze replication metrics
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
        self.metrics_history = []
    
    def collect_metrics(self, pattern_name: str, result: Dict[str, any]):
        """
        Collect metrics from a replication operation
        
        Args:
            pattern_name: Name of the replication pattern
            result: Result dictionary from replication
        """
        metric = {
            "timestamp": datetime.now().isoformat(),
            "pattern": pattern_name,
            "status": result.get("status", "UNKNOWN"),
            "duration_seconds": result.get("total_time", result.get("write_time", 0)),
            "record_count": result.get("record_count", 0),
            "replica_count": len(result.get("replica_status", {})) if "replica_status" in result else 0
        }
        
        self.metrics_history.append(metric)
    
    def generate_metrics_report(self) -> DataFrame:
        """
        Generate comprehensive metrics report
        
        Returns:
            DataFrame with metrics analysis
        """
        print("\n" + "="*60)
        print("REPLICATION METRICS REPORT")
        print("="*60 + "\n")
        
        if not self.metrics_history:
            print("No metrics collected yet")
            return None
        
        schema = StructType([
            StructField("timestamp", StringType(), False),
            StructField("pattern", StringType(), False),
            StructField("status", StringType(), False),
            StructField("duration_seconds", DoubleType(), True),
            StructField("record_count", IntegerType(), True),
            StructField("replica_count", IntegerType(), True)
        ])
        
        metrics_df = self.spark.createDataFrame(self.metrics_history, schema)
        
        # Calculate summary statistics
        print("Overall Statistics:")
        metrics_df.groupBy("pattern") \
            .agg(
                count("*").alias("operations"),
                avg("duration_seconds").alias("avg_duration"),
                sum("record_count").alias("total_records")
            ) \
            .show(truncate=False)
        
        print("\nSuccess Rate by Pattern:")
        metrics_df.groupBy("pattern", "status") \
            .count() \
            .show(truncate=False)
        
        return metrics_df
    
    def export_metrics(self, output_path: str, format: str = "parquet"):
        """
        Export metrics to file
        
        Args:
            output_path: Output file path
            format: Output format (parquet, csv, json)
        """
        if not self.metrics_history:
            print("No metrics to export")
            return
        
        metrics_df = self.generate_metrics_report()
        
        print(f"\nExporting metrics to: {output_path}")
        
        try:
            if format == "parquet":
                metrics_df.write.mode("overwrite").parquet(output_path)
            elif format == "csv":
                metrics_df.write.mode("overwrite") \
                    .option("header", "true") \
                    .csv(output_path)
            elif format == "json":
                metrics_df.write.mode("overwrite").json(output_path)
            else:
                raise ValueError(f"Unsupported format: {format}")
            
            print(f"✓ Metrics exported successfully")
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"✗ Export failed: {str(e)}")

        data_quality = ReplicationDataQuality(spark)
        metrics_collector = ReplicationMetricsCollector(spark)
        
        print("✓ All components initialized")
        
        # Step 3: Optimize data
        print("\n[STEP 3] Optimizing data for replication...")
        optimized_df = optimizer.optimize_partition_strategy(df, target_partition_size_mb=128)
        
        # Step 4: Execute master-slave replication
        print("\n[STEP 4] Executing master-slave replication...")
        write_result = master_slave.write_to_master(optimized_df)
        metrics_collector.collect_metrics("master-slave-write", write_result)
        
        replication_result = master_slave.replicate_to_slaves()
        metrics_collector.collect_metrics("master-slave-replicate", replication_result)
        
        # Step 5: Validate data quality
        print("\n[STEP 5] Validating data quality...")
        schema_valid = data_quality.validate_schema_consistency([
            f"{base_path}/master",
            f"{base_path}/slave_1",
            f"{base_path}/slave_2"
        ])
        
        integrity_result = data_quality.validate_data_integrity(
            f"{base_path}/master",
            f"{base_path}/slave_1",
            sample_size=1000
        )
        
        # Step 6: Health monitoring
        print("\n[STEP 6] Running health checks...")
        alerts = alert_system.check_replication_health(
            f"{base_path}/master",
            [f"{base_path}/slave_1", f"{base_path}/slave_2", f"{base_path}/slave_3"]
        )
        
        if alerts:
            alert_system.send_alerts(alerts, "console")
        
        # Step 7: Test failover scenario
        print("\n[STEP 7] Testing automated failover...")
        failover_result = recovery_system.auto_failover(
            f"{base_path}/master",
            [f"{base_path}/slave_1", f"{base_path}/slave_2", f"{base_path}/slave_3"],
            new_master_index=0
        )
        
        # Step 8: Generate reports
        print("\n[STEP 8] Generating comprehensive reports...")
        
        metrics_report = metrics_collector.generate_metrics_report()
        
        # Export metrics
        metrics_collector.export_metrics(f"{base_path}/metrics", format="parquet")
        
        # Step 9: Compression benchmark
        print("\n[STEP 9] Running compression benchmark...")
        compression_results = optimizer.benchmark_compression_methods(
            df.limit(10000),
            f"{base_path}/compression_test"
        )
        
        # Final Summary
        print("\n" + "="*80)
        print(" PRODUCTION SETUP COMPLETED SUCCESSFULLY")
        print("="*80 + "\n")
        
        print("Summary:")
        print(f"  ✓ Dataset: {df.count()} records")
        print(f"  ✓ Master-Slave replication: Complete")
        print(f"  ✓ Data quality validation: {'Passed' if schema_valid else 'Failed'}")
        print(f"  ✓ Health checks: {len(alerts)} alerts generated")
        print(f"  ✓ Failover test: {'Success' if failover_result['success'] else 'Failed'}")
        print(f"  ✓ Metrics collected and exported")
        print(f"  ✓ Compression benchmark: Complete")
        
        print(f"\nData Location: {base_path}")

        traceback.print_exc()

class ReplicationCLI:
    """
    Interactive command-line interface for replication management
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
        self.patterns = {}
        self.current_pattern = None
    
    def run(self):
        """Run interactive CLI"""
        
        print("""
        ╔════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
```python
        ╔════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
        ║                                                                    ║
        ║          REPLICATION MANAGEMENT CLI - Interactive Mode             ║
        ║                                                                    ║
        ╚════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
        
        Available Commands:
        -------------------
        1. create    - Create a new replication pattern
        2. replicate - Execute replication
        3. monitor   - Check replication health
        4. validate  - Validate data consistency
        5. failover  - Perform failover
        6. metrics   - View metrics
        7. help      - Show this help
        8. exit      - Exit CLI
        
        """)
        
        while True:
            try:
                command = input("\nreplication> ").strip().lower()
                
                if command == "exit" or command == "quit":
                    print("Exiting CLI...")
                    break
                elif command == "help":
                    self._show_help()
                elif command == "create":
                    self._create_pattern()
                elif command == "replicate":
                    self._execute_replication()
                elif command == "monitor":
                    self._monitor_health()
                elif command == "validate":
                    self._validate_data()
                elif command == "failover":
                    self._perform_failover()
                elif command == "metrics":
                    self._show_metrics()
                elif command == "list":
                    self._list_patterns()
                elif command == "":
                    continue
                else:
                    print(f"Unknown command: {command}. Type 'help' for available commands.")
            
            except KeyboardInterrupt:
                print("\n\nUse 'exit' to quit.")
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"Error: {str(e)}")
    
    def _show_help(self):
        """Show detailed help"""
        help_text = """
        
        DETAILED COMMAND HELP
        =====================
        
        create
        ------
        Create a new replication pattern instance.
        Options: synchronous, asynchronous, semi-synchronous, multi-master, master-slave
        
        Example:
          replication> create
          Select pattern type: master-slave
        
        replicate
        ---------
        Execute replication using the current pattern.
        
        Example:
          replication> replicate
        
        monitor
        -------
        Check health of all replicas and generate alerts.
        
        Example:
          replication> monitor
        
        validate
        --------
        Validate data consistency between master and replicas.
        
        Example:
          replication> validate
        
        failover
        --------
        Perform automated failover from master to slave.
        
        Example:
          replication> failover
        
        metrics
        -------
        Display replication metrics and statistics.
        
        Example:
          replication> metrics
        
        list
        ----
        List all created replication patterns.
        
        Example:
          replication> list
        
        """
        print(help_text)
    
    def _create_pattern(self):
        """Create a new replication pattern"""
        print("\nAvailable patterns:")
        print("1. Synchronous")
        print("2. Asynchronous")
        print("3. Semi-Synchronous")
        print("4. Multi-Master")
        print("5. Master-Slave")
        
        choice = input("\nSelect pattern (1-5): ").strip()
        
        pattern_name = input("Enter pattern name: ").strip()
        
        if choice == "1":
            replica_count = int(input("Number of replicas: "))
            pattern = SynchronousReplicationPattern(self.spark, replica_count)
        elif choice == "2":
            lag = int(input("Replication lag (seconds): "))
            pattern = AsynchronousReplicationPattern(self.spark, lag)
        elif choice == "3":
            min_replicas = int(input("Minimum replicas: "))
            total_replicas = int(input("Total replicas: "))
            pattern = SemiSynchronousReplicationPattern(self.spark, min_replicas, total_replicas)
        elif choice == "4":
            masters = input("Master nodes (comma-separated): ").split(",")
            pattern = MultiMasterReplicationPattern(self.spark, [m.strip() for m in masters])
        elif choice == "5":
            master_path = input("Master path: ").strip()
            slave_count = int(input("Number of slaves: "))
            slave_paths = [f"{master_path}_slave_{i}" for i in range(1, slave_count + 1)]
            pattern = MasterSlaveReplicationPattern(self.spark, master_path, slave_paths)
        else:
            print("Invalid choice")
            return
        
        self.patterns[pattern_name] = pattern
        self.current_pattern = pattern_name
        
        print(f"\n✓ Pattern '{pattern_name}' created and set as current")
    
    def _execute_replication(self):
        """Execute replication"""
        if not self.current_pattern:
            print("No pattern selected. Use 'create' first.")
            return
        
        print(f"\nExecuting replication with pattern: {self.current_pattern}")
        print("(Simulated - integrate with actual data sources)")
    
    def _monitor_health(self):
        """Monitor replication health"""
        print("\nMonitoring replication health...")
        print("(Simulated - integrate with actual monitoring)")
    
    def _validate_data(self):
        """Validate data consistency"""
        print("\nValidating data consistency...")
        print("(Simulated - integrate with actual validation)")
    
    def _perform_failover(self):
        """Perform failover"""
        print("\nPerforming automated failover...")
        print("(Simulated - integrate with actual failover)")
    
    def _show_metrics(self):
        """Show metrics"""
        print("\nReplication Metrics:")
        print("(Simulated - integrate with actual metrics)")
    
    def _list_patterns(self):
        """List all patterns"""
        if not self.patterns:
            print("\nNo patterns created yet.")
            return
        
        print("\nCreated Patterns:")
        for name, pattern in self.patterns.items():
            current = " (current)" if name == self.current_pattern else ""
            print(f"  - {name}: {type(pattern).__name__}{current}")

"""
PySpark Stream Event Ordering Patterns
======================================
This module demonstrates 5 different patterns for ordering streaming events:
1. Timestamp Ordering Pattern
2. Sequence Number Ordering Pattern
3. Causal Ordering Pattern
4. Total Ordering Pattern
5. Partial Ordering Pattern
"""

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import *
from pyspark.sql.types import *
from pyspark.sql.window import Window
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
import time

# Initialize Spark Session with Structured Streaming
spark = SparkSession.builder \
    .appName("StreamEventOrderingPatterns") \
    .config("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "4") \
    .config("spark.sql.streaming.checkpointLocation", "/tmp/checkpoint") \
    .getOrCreate()

spark.sparkContext.setLogLevel("WARN")

print("=" * 80)
print("PySpark Stream Event Ordering Patterns")
print("=" * 80)


# =============================================================================
# 1. TIMESTAMP ORDERING PATTERN
# =============================================================================
# Orders events based on event timestamps with watermarking for late arrivals
# =============================================================================

def timestamp_ordering_pattern():
    """
    Timestamp Ordering Pattern: Orders events based on event-time timestamps.
    Handles late arrivals using watermarking.
    
    Use Case: Log aggregation, time-series analysis, event correlation
    """
    print("\n1. TIMESTAMP ORDERING PATTERN")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    # Define schema for incoming events
    event_schema = StructType([
        StructField("event_id", StringType(), False),
        StructField("user_id", StringType(), False),
        StructField("event_type", StringType(), False),
        StructField("event_timestamp", TimestampType(), False),
        StructField("processing_timestamp", TimestampType(), False),
        StructField("value", DoubleType(), True)
    ])
    
    # Simulated streaming source (replace with actual streaming source)
    # Example sources: Kafka, socket, file stream, etc.
    sample_data = [
        ("evt_001", "user_1", "click", datetime(2024, 1, 1, 10, 0, 0), datetime(2024, 1, 1, 10, 0, 5), 100.0),
        ("evt_002", "user_1", "view", datetime(2024, 1, 1, 10, 0, 2), datetime(2024, 1, 1, 10, 0, 6), 50.0),
        ("evt_003", "user_2", "click", datetime(2024, 1, 1, 10, 0, 1), datetime(2024, 1, 1, 10, 0, 7), 75.0),
        ("evt_004", "user_1", "purchase", datetime(2024, 1, 1, 10, 0, 5), datetime(2024, 1, 1, 10, 0, 8), 200.0),
        # Late arrival event
        ("evt_005", "user_2", "view", datetime(2024, 1, 1, 9, 59, 58), datetime(2024, 1, 1, 10, 0, 9), 30.0),
    ]
    
    df = spark.createDataFrame(sample_data, schema=event_schema)
    
    # Apply timestamp ordering with watermarking
    ordered_df = df \
        .withWatermark("event_timestamp", "1 minute") \
        .orderBy("event_timestamp") \
        .withColumn("event_delay_seconds", 
                   unix_timestamp("processing_timestamp") - unix_timestamp("event_timestamp"))
    
    # Window-based aggregation with timestamp ordering
    windowed_aggregation = ordered_df \
        .groupBy(
            window("event_timestamp", "30 seconds", "10 seconds"),
            "user_id"
        ) \
        .agg(
            count("*").alias("event_count"),
            sum("value").alias("total_value"),
            collect_list(struct("event_id", "event_type", "event_timestamp")).alias("events")
        ) \
        .orderBy("window")
    
    print("Timestamp Ordered Events:")
    ordered_df.show(truncate=False)
    
    print("\nWindowed Aggregation (30s window, 10s slide):")
    windowed_aggregation.show(truncate=False)
    
    return ordered_df


# =============================================================================
# 2. SEQUENCE NUMBER ORDERING PATTERN
# =============================================================================
# Orders events based on monotonically increasing sequence numbers
# Detects gaps and duplicates in the sequence
# =============================================================================

def sequence_number_ordering_pattern():
    """
    Sequence Number Ordering Pattern: Orders events by sequence numbers.
    Detects missing sequences, duplicates, and out-of-order events.
    
    Use Case: Message queue processing, transaction ordering, database replication
    """
    print("\n2. SEQUENCE NUMBER ORDERING PATTERN")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    # Schema with sequence numbers
    sequence_schema = StructType([
        StructField("event_id", StringType(), False),
        StructField("sequence_number", LongType(), False),
        StructField("partition_key", StringType(), False),
        StructField("payload", StringType(), True),
        StructField("timestamp", TimestampType(), False)
    ])
    
    # Sample data with out-of-order and duplicate sequences
    sample_data = [
        ("evt_001", 1, "partition_A", "data_1", datetime(2024, 1, 1, 10, 0, 0)),
        ("evt_002", 3, "partition_A", "data_3", datetime(2024, 1, 1, 10, 0, 2)),  # Gap: missing seq 2
        ("evt_003", 2, "partition_A", "data_2", datetime(2024, 1, 1, 10, 0, 3)),  # Out of order
        ("evt_004", 4, "partition_A", "data_4", datetime(2024, 1, 1, 10, 0, 4)),
        ("evt_005", 4, "partition_A", "data_4_dup", datetime(2024, 1, 1, 10, 0, 5)),  # Duplicate
        ("evt_006", 1, "partition_B", "data_1", datetime(2024, 1, 1, 10, 0, 0)),
        ("evt_007", 2, "partition_B", "data_2", datetime(2024, 1, 1, 10, 0, 1)),
    ]
    
    df = spark.createDataFrame(sample_data, schema=sequence_schema)
    
    # Order by partition and sequence number
    ordered_df = df.orderBy("partition_key", "sequence_number")
    
    # Detect gaps, duplicates, and out-of-order events
    window_spec = Window.partitionBy("partition_key").orderBy("sequence_number")
    
    analyzed_df = ordered_df \
        .withColumn("prev_sequence", lag("sequence_number", 1).over(window_spec)) \
        .withColumn("next_sequence", lead("sequence_number", 1).over(window_spec)) \
        .withColumn("is_duplicate", 
                   when(col("sequence_number") == col("prev_sequence"), True).otherwise(False)) \
        .withColumn("has_gap_before",
                   when((col("prev_sequence").isNotNull()) & 
                        (col("sequence_number") - col("prev_sequence") > 1), True).otherwise(False)) \
        .withColumn("gap_size",
                   when(col("has_gap_before"), col("sequence_number") - col("prev_sequence") - 1).otherwise(0))
    
    # Identify missing sequences per partition
    missing_sequences = analyzed_df \
        .filter(col("has_gap_before") == True) \
        .select(
            "partition_key",
            "sequence_number",
            "prev_sequence",
            "gap_size"
        )
    
    print("Sequence Ordered Events with Analysis:")
    analyzed_df.select(
        "partition_key", "sequence_number", "event_id", 
        "is_duplicate", "has_gap_before", "gap_size"
    ).show(truncate=False)
    
    print("\nDetected Gaps in Sequences:")
    missing_sequences.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Deduplicated and ordered stream
    deduplicated_df = analyzed_df \
        .filter(col("is_duplicate") == False) \
        .orderBy("partition_key", "sequence_number")
    
    print("\nDeduplicated Ordered Stream:")
    deduplicated_df.select("partition_key", "sequence_number", "event_id", "payload").show(truncate=False)
    
    return analyzed_df


# =============================================================================
# 3. CAUSAL ORDERING PATTERN
# =============================================================================
# Orders events based on causal relationships (happens-before)
# Implements vector clock-based ordering
# =============================================================================

def causal_ordering_pattern():
    """
    Causal Ordering Pattern: Orders events based on causal relationships.
    Uses vector clocks to determine happens-before relationships.
    
    Use Case: Distributed systems, collaborative editing, conflict resolution
    """
    print("\n3. CAUSAL ORDERING PATTERN")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    # Schema with vector clocks
    causal_schema = StructType([
        StructField("event_id", StringType(), False),
        StructField("node_id", StringType(), False),
        StructField("vector_clock", MapType(StringType(), IntegerType()), False),
        StructField("parent_event_id", StringType(), True),
        StructField("operation", StringType(), False),
        StructField("timestamp", TimestampType(), False)
    ])
    
    # Sample data with causal dependencies
    # Vector clock format: {node_id: logical_clock}
    sample_data = [
        ("evt_1", "node_A", {"node_A": 1, "node_B": 0, "node_C": 0}, None, "write_x", datetime(2024, 1, 1, 10, 0, 0)),
        ("evt_2", "node_B", {"node_A": 1, "node_B": 1, "node_C": 0}, "evt_1", "read_x", datetime(2024, 1, 1, 10, 0, 1)),
        ("evt_3", "node_C", {"node_A": 0, "node_B": 0, "node_C": 1}, None, "write_y", datetime(2024, 1, 1, 10, 0, 2)),
        ("evt_4", "node_A", {"node_A": 2, "node_B": 1, "node_C": 0}, "evt_2", "write_z", datetime(2024, 1, 1, 10, 0, 3)),
        ("evt_5", "node_B", {"node_A": 2, "node_B": 2, "node_C": 1}, "evt_4", "read_z", datetime(2024, 1, 1, 10, 0, 4)),
    ]
    
    df = spark.createDataFrame(sample_data, schema=causal_schema)
    
    # UDF to compare vector clocks (happens-before relationship)
    def happens_before(vc1, vc2):
        """
        Returns True if vc1 happens-before vc2
        vc1 < vc2 iff: for all nodes, vc1[node] <= vc2[node] AND exists node where vc1[node] < vc2[node]
        """
        if vc1 is None or vc2 is None:
            return False
        
        all_less_or_equal = True
        at_least_one_less = False
        
        all_nodes = set(vc1.keys()) | set(vc2.keys())
        for node in all_nodes:
            v1 = vc1.get(node, 0)
            v2 = vc2.get(node, 0)
            
            if v1 > v2:
                all_less_or_equal = False
                break
            if v1 < v2:
                at_least_one_less = True
        
        return all_less_or_equal and at_least_one_less
    
    # Register UDF
    happens_before_udf = udf(happens_before, BooleanType())
    
    # Calculate causal order score (sum of vector clock values)
    df_with_score = df.withColumn(
        "causal_order_score",
        expr("aggregate(map_values(vector_clock), 0, (acc, x) -> acc + x)")
    )
    
    # Create causally ordered view
    causally_ordered = df_with_score.orderBy("causal_order_score", "timestamp")
    
    # Detect concurrent events (neither happens-before the other)
    cross_df = df.alias("e1").crossJoin(df.alias("e2"))
    
    concurrent_events = cross_df \
        .filter(col("e1.event_id") < col("e2.event_id")) \
        .withColumn("e1_before_e2", happens_before_udf(col("e1.vector_clock"), col("e2.vector_clock"))) \
        .withColumn("e2_before_e1", happens_before_udf(col("e2.vector_clock"), col("e1.vector_clock"))) \
        .filter((col("e1_before_e2") == False) & (col("e2_before_e1") == False)) \
        .select(
            col("e1.event_id").alias("event_1"),
            col("e2.event_id").alias("event_2"),
            col("e1.node_id").alias("node_1"),
            col("e2.node_id").alias("node_2")
        )
    
    print("Causally Ordered Events:")
    causally_ordered.select(
        "event_id", "node_id", "vector_clock", "parent_event_id", 
        "operation", "causal_order_score"
    ).show(truncate=False)
    
    print("\nConcurrent Events (no causal relationship):")
    concurrent_events.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Build causal dependency graph
    print("\nCausal Dependency Chain:")
    causally_ordered.select("event_id", "parent_event_id", "operation", "node_id").show(truncate=False)
    
    return causally_ordered


# =============================================================================
# 4. TOTAL ORDERING PATTERN
# =============================================================================
# Ensures a single global order across all events
# Uses a combination of timestamp and tie-breaker
# =============================================================================

def total_ordering_pattern():
    """
    Total Ordering Pattern: Establishes a single global order for all events.
    Uses timestamp + unique ID as tie-breaker for deterministic ordering.
    
    Use Case: Audit logs, financial transactions, state machine replication
    """
    print("\n4. TOTAL ORDERING PATTERN")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    # Schema for total ordering
    total_order_schema = StructType([
        StructField("event_id", StringType(), False),
        StructField("source_id", StringType(), False),
```python
        StructField("event_timestamp", TimestampType(), False),
        StructField("transaction_id", StringType(), False),
        StructField("operation", StringType(), False),
        StructField("amount", DoubleType(), True)
    ])
    
    # Sample data with potential timestamp collisions
    sample_data = [
        ("evt_001", "source_A", datetime(2024, 1, 1, 10, 0, 0, 100000), "txn_001", "debit", 100.0),
        ("evt_002", "source_B", datetime(2024, 1, 1, 10, 0, 0, 100000), "txn_002", "credit", 50.0),  # Same timestamp
        ("evt_003", "source_C", datetime(2024, 1, 1, 10, 0, 0, 100000), "txn_003", "debit", 75.0),   # Same timestamp
        ("evt_004", "source_A", datetime(2024, 1, 1, 10, 0, 1, 0), "txn_004", "credit", 200.0),
        ("evt_005", "source_B", datetime(2024, 1, 1, 10, 0, 0, 500000), "txn_005", "debit", 30.0),
        ("evt_006", "source_C", datetime(2024, 1, 1, 10, 0, 2, 0), "txn_006", "credit", 150.0),
    ]
    
    df = spark.createDataFrame(sample_data, schema=total_order_schema)
    
    # Create total ordering using timestamp + event_id as tie-breaker
    # This ensures deterministic ordering even for events with identical timestamps
    totally_ordered = df \
        .withColumn("timestamp_nanos", 
                   unix_timestamp("event_timestamp") * 1000000000 + 
                   date_format("event_timestamp", "SSSSSS").cast("long") * 1000) \
        .withColumn("total_order_key", 
                   concat(
                       lpad(col("timestamp_nanos").cast("string"), 20, "0"),
                       lit("_"),
                       col("event_id")
                   )) \
        .orderBy("total_order_key")
    
    # Add global sequence number
    window_spec = Window.orderBy("total_order_key")
    
    totally_ordered = totally_ordered \
        .withColumn("global_sequence", row_number().over(window_spec)) \
        .withColumn("prev_event_id", lag("event_id", 1).over(window_spec)) \
        .withColumn("next_event_id", lead("event_id", 1).over(window_spec))
    
    # Calculate running balance (demonstrates total order importance for financial transactions)
    balance_window = Window.orderBy("global_sequence").rowsBetween(Window.unboundedPreceding, Window.currentRow)
    
    totally_ordered = totally_ordered \
        .withColumn("amount_signed", 
                   when(col("operation") == "credit", col("amount"))
                   .otherwise(-col("amount"))) \
        .withColumn("running_balance", sum("amount_signed").over(balance_window))
    
    print("Totally Ordered Events with Global Sequence:")
    totally_ordered.select(
        "global_sequence", "event_id", "source_id", "event_timestamp", 
        "operation", "amount", "running_balance"
    ).show(truncate=False)
    
    # Verify ordering properties
    print("\nOrdering Verification:")
    print(f"Total events: {totally_ordered.count()}")
    print(f"Unique global sequences: {totally_ordered.select('global_sequence').distinct().count()}")
    print(f"Events with same timestamp: {df.groupBy('event_timestamp').count().filter('count > 1').count()}")
    
    # Show tie-breaking for same timestamp
    same_timestamp_events = totally_ordered \
        .filter(col("event_timestamp") == datetime(2024, 1, 1, 10, 0, 0, 100000)) \
        .select("global_sequence", "event_id", "source_id", "total_order_key")
    
    print("\nTie-breaking for events with identical timestamps:")
    same_timestamp_events.show(truncate=False)
    
    return totally_ordered


# =============================================================================
# 5. PARTIAL ORDERING PATTERN
# =============================================================================
# Orders events within partitions while allowing parallelism across partitions
# Maintains order guarantees only within logical groups
# =============================================================================

def partial_ordering_pattern():
    """
    Partial Ordering Pattern: Maintains order within partitions/groups only.
    Allows parallel processing across independent partitions.
    
    Use Case: User session processing, per-device event streams, multi-tenant systems
    """
    print("\n5. PARTIAL ORDERING PATTERN")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    # Schema for partial ordering
    partial_order_schema = StructType([
        StructField("event_id", StringType(), False),
        StructField("partition_key", StringType(), False),  # e.g., user_id, device_id
        StructField("sub_partition", StringType(), True),   # Optional secondary grouping
        StructField("event_timestamp", TimestampType(), False),
        StructField("sequence_in_partition", LongType(), False),
        StructField("event_type", StringType(), False),
        StructField("data", StringType(), True)
    ])
    
    # Sample data representing multiple independent streams
    sample_data = [
        # User A events (must be ordered within this partition)
        ("evt_001", "user_A", "session_1", datetime(2024, 1, 1, 10, 0, 0), 1, "login", "data_1"),
        ("evt_002", "user_A", "session_1", datetime(2024, 1, 1, 10, 0, 5), 2, "click", "data_2"),
        ("evt_003", "user_A", "session_1", datetime(2024, 1, 1, 10, 0, 10), 3, "purchase", "data_3"),
        
        # User B events (independent from User A, can be processed in parallel)
        ("evt_004", "user_B", "session_1", datetime(2024, 1, 1, 10, 0, 1), 1, "login", "data_4"),
        ("evt_005", "user_B", "session_1", datetime(2024, 1, 1, 10, 0, 3), 2, "view", "data_5"),
        ("evt_006", "user_B", "session_2", datetime(2024, 1, 1, 10, 1, 0), 1, "login", "data_6"),
        
        # User C events (another independent partition)
        ("evt_007", "user_C", "session_1", datetime(2024, 1, 1, 10, 0, 2), 1, "login", "data_7"),
        ("evt_008", "user_C", "session_1", datetime(2024, 1, 1, 10, 0, 8), 2, "click", "data_8"),
        
        # Out of order event for User A (should be reordered within partition)
        ("evt_009", "user_A", "session_1", datetime(2024, 1, 1, 10, 0, 7), 4, "view", "data_9"),
    ]
    
    df = spark.createDataFrame(sample_data, schema=partial_order_schema)
    
    # Define window for partial ordering within each partition
    partition_window = Window.partitionBy("partition_key", "sub_partition") \
                              .orderBy("sequence_in_partition")
    
    # Apply partial ordering
    partially_ordered = df \
        .withColumn("partition_sequence", row_number().over(partition_window)) \
        .withColumn("prev_event_in_partition", lag("event_id", 1).over(partition_window)) \
        .withColumn("next_event_in_partition", lead("event_id", 1).over(partition_window)) \
        .withColumn("time_since_prev_event",
                   when(col("prev_event_in_partition").isNotNull(),
                        unix_timestamp("event_timestamp") - 
                        unix_timestamp(lag("event_timestamp", 1).over(partition_window)))
                   .otherwise(None))
    
    # Detect out-of-order events within partitions
    partially_ordered = partially_ordered \
        .withColumn("is_out_of_order",
                   when((col("prev_event_in_partition").isNotNull()) &
                        (col("event_timestamp") < lag("event_timestamp", 1).over(partition_window)),
                        True).otherwise(False))
    
    print("Partially Ordered Events (ordered within partitions):")
    partially_ordered.select(
        "partition_key", "sub_partition", "partition_sequence", "event_id",
        "event_timestamp", "event_type", "is_out_of_order"
    ).orderBy("partition_key", "sub_partition", "partition_sequence").show(truncate=False)
    
    # Aggregate statistics per partition
    partition_stats = partially_ordered \
        .groupBy("partition_key", "sub_partition") \
        .agg(
            count("*").alias("event_count"),
            min("event_timestamp").alias("first_event_time"),
            max("event_timestamp").alias("last_event_time"),
            sum(when(col("is_out_of_order"), 1).otherwise(0)).alias("out_of_order_count"),
            collect_list("event_type").alias("event_sequence")
        )
    
    print("\nPartition-level Statistics:")
    partition_stats.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Demonstrate parallel processing capability
    # Each partition can be processed independently
    print("\nDemonstrating Parallel Processing by Partition:")
    
    def process_partition_events(partition_iter):
        """
        Process events within a partition independently.
        This function can be executed in parallel across partitions.
        """
        events = list(partition_iter)
        partition_key = events[0]['partition_key'] if events else 'unknown'
        
        # Simulate partition-specific processing
        processed_events = []
        state = {"event_count": 0, "partition_key": partition_key}
        
        for event in sorted(events, key=lambda x: x['sequence_in_partition']):
            state["event_count"] += 1
            processed_event = {
                "partition_key": event['partition_key'],
                "event_id": event['event_id'],
                "processed_sequence": state["event_count"],
                "event_type": event['event_type']
            }
            processed_events.append(processed_event)
        
        return iter(processed_events)
    
    # Apply partition-wise processing
    processed_schema = StructType([
        StructField("partition_key", StringType(), False),
        StructField("event_id", StringType(), False),
        StructField("processed_sequence", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("event_type", StringType(), False)
    ])
    
    processed_partitions = partially_ordered \
        .repartition("partition_key", "sub_partition") \
        .rdd \
        .mapPartitions(process_partition_events) \
        .toDF(processed_schema)
    
    print("\nProcessed Events (partition-wise processing):")
    processed_partitions.orderBy("partition_key", "processed_sequence").show(truncate=False)
    
    # Session-based ordering (combining partial ordering with session windows)
    session_window = Window.partitionBy("partition_key", "sub_partition") \
                           .orderBy("event_timestamp") \
                           .rangeBetween(-30, 0)  # 30 second session window
    
    session_ordered = partially_ordered \
        .withColumn("events_in_session", count("*").over(session_window)) \
        .withColumn("session_duration", 
                   max("event_timestamp").over(session_window).cast("long") - 
                   min("event_timestamp").over(session_window).cast("long"))
    
    print("\nSession-based Partial Ordering (30s session window):")
    session_ordered.select(
        "partition_key", "sub_partition", "event_id", "event_timestamp",
        "events_in_session", "session_duration"
    ).orderBy("partition_key", "event_timestamp").show(truncate=False)
    
    return partially_ordered


# =============================================================================
# COMPREHENSIVE COMPARISON AND TESTING
# =============================================================================

def compare_ordering_patterns():
    """
    Compares all ordering patterns and demonstrates when to use each.
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("ORDERING PATTERNS COMPARISON")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    comparison_data = [
        ("Timestamp Ordering", "Event-time based", "Time-series analysis, logs", "Late arrivals", "Watermarking"),
        ("Sequence Number", "Monotonic sequence", "Message queues, DB replication", "Gaps, duplicates", "Gap detection"),
        ("Causal Ordering", "Happens-before", "Distributed systems", "Concurrent events", "Vector clocks"),
        ("Total Ordering", "Global single order", "Financial transactions", "Scalability", "Deterministic tie-breaking"),
        ("Partial Ordering", "Per-partition order", "User sessions, multi-tenant", "Cross-partition order", "Parallel processing")
    ]
    
    comparison_schema = StructType([
        StructField("pattern", StringType(), False),
        StructField("ordering_basis", StringType(), False),
        StructField("use_cases", StringType(), False),
        StructField("challenges", StringType(), False),
        StructField("solution", StringType(), False)
    ])
    
    comparison_df = spark.createDataFrame(comparison_data, schema=comparison_schema)
    
    print("\nPattern Comparison:")
    comparison_df.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Performance characteristics
    print("\nPerformance Characteristics:")
    print("-" * 80)
    print("1. Timestamp Ordering: O(n log n) - Good for bounded disorder")
    print("2. Sequence Number: O(n) - Excellent for ordered sources")
    print("3. Causal Ordering: O(n²) worst case - Complex dependency resolution")
    print("4. Total Ordering: O(n log n) - Single bottleneck, limited scalability")
    print("5. Partial Ordering: O(n/p log(n/p)) - Best scalability with p partitions")

    # Create a streaming DataFrame using rate source
    streaming_df = spark.readStream \
        .format("rate") \
        .option("rowsPerSecond", 5) \
        .option("numPartitions", 2) \
        .load()
    
    # Add event processing
    processed_stream = streaming_df \
        .withColumn("event_id", concat(lit("evt_"), col("value").cast("string"))) \
        .withColumn("partition_key", expr("value % 3").cast("string")) \
```python
        .withColumn("event_timestamp", col("timestamp")) \
        .withColumn("processing_timestamp", current_timestamp()) \
        .withWatermark("event_timestamp", "10 seconds") \
        .select(
            "event_id",
            "partition_key",
            "event_timestamp",
            "processing_timestamp",
            "value"
        )
    
    # Apply windowed aggregation with timestamp ordering
    windowed_stream = processed_stream \
        .groupBy(

            "max_value",
            "avg_value"
        )
    
    print("\nStreaming Query Configuration:")
