def advanced_pagination_examples():
    """
    Demonstrate advanced pagination scenarios
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("ADVANCED PAGINATION EXAMPLES")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Create sample data
    df = create_sample_data()
    
    # ========================================================================
    # Example 1: Bi-directional pagination
    # ========================================================================
    print("\n[Example 1] Bi-directional Pagination")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    cursor_pager = CursorBasedPagination(df, page_size=10)
    
    # Navigate forward
    print("\nNavigating forward:")
    page = cursor_pager.get_page()
    print(f"Page 1 - First ID: {page['data'].first()['id']}")
    
    page = cursor_pager.get_page(cursor=page['next_cursor'])
    print(f"Page 2 - First ID: {page['data'].first()['id']}")
    
    # Navigate backward
    print("\nNavigating backward:")
    page = cursor_pager.get_page(cursor=page['previous_cursor'], direction="previous")
    print(f"Back to Page 1 - First ID: {page['data'].first()['id']}")
    
    # ========================================================================
    # Example 2: Infinite scroll pagination
    # ========================================================================
    print("\n[Example 2] Infinite Scroll Pattern")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    def infinite_scroll_generator(df, page_size=20):
        """
        Generator function for infinite scroll
        Yields pages until no more data
        """
        keyset_pager = KeysetPagination(df, page_size=page_size)
        last_key = None
        page_num = 1
        
        while True:
            result = keyset_pager.get_page(last_key=last_key)
            
            if result['data'] is None or result['page_size'] == 0:
                break
            
            yield {
                'page_number': page_num,
                'data': result['data'],
                'count': result['page_size']
            }
            
            if not result['has_next']:
                break
            
            last_key = result['next_key']
            page_num += 1
    
    print("\nSimulating infinite scroll (first 3 pages):")
    for i, page in enumerate(infinite_scroll_generator(df, page_size=15)):
        print(f"Scroll page {page['page_number']}: {page['count']} records")
        if i >= 2:  # Show first 3 pages only
            break
    
    # ========================================================================
    # Example 3: Search results pagination with ranking
    # ========================================================================
    print("\n[Example 3] Search Results with Ranking")
    print("-" * 80)

    # Create multi-column keyset pagination (score desc, id asc)

    result = search_pager.get_page_with_composite_key(
        sort_columns=[("relevance_score", "desc"), ("id", "asc")]
    )
    
    print("\nSearch results (sorted by relevance):")
    result['data'].select("id", "order_number", "relevance_score").show(10)
    
    # ========================================================================
    # Example 4: Real-time feed pagination
    # ========================================================================
    print("\n[Example 4] Real-time Feed Pagination")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    time_pager = TimeBasedPagination(df, page_size=15)
    
    # Get most recent items (like a social media feed)
    print("\nMost recent items (newest first):")
    recent = time_pager.get_page(direction="backward")
    recent['data'].select("id", "order_number", "created_at").show(5)
    
    # Simulate "load more" - get older items
    if recent['next_timestamp']:
        print("\nLoading older items...")
        older = time_pager.get_page(
            last_timestamp=recent['next_timestamp'],
            last_id=recent['next_id'],
            direction="backward"
        )
        older['data'].select("id", "order_number", "created_at").show(5)
    
    # ========================================================================
    # Example 5: Partitioned pagination
    # ========================================================================
    print("\n[Example 5] Partitioned Pagination (by user)")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    # Paginate within a specific user's data
    user_id = "user_10"
    user_df = df.filter(col("user_id") == user_id)
    
    user_pager = OffsetBasedPagination(user_df, page_size=5)
    
    print(f"\nPaginating orders for {user_id}:")
    print(f"Total orders: {user_pager.total_records}")
    print(f"Total pages: {user_pager.total_pages}")
    
    user_page = user_pager.get_page(1)
    user_page['data'].select("id", "user_id", "order_number", "amount").show()
    
    # ========================================================================
    # Example 6: Cached pagination results
    # ========================================================================
    print("\n[Example 6] Cached Pagination for Performance")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    # Cache the dataframe for faster pagination
    cached_df = df.cache()
    
    cached_pager = KeysetPagination(cached_df, page_size=20)
    
    print("\nFetching multiple pages with cached data:")
    last_key = None
    for i in range(3):
        result = cached_pager.get_page(last_key=last_key)
        print(f"Page {i+1}: {result['page_size']} records")
        last_key = result['next_key']
    
    cached_df.unpersist()

class PaginationBestPractices:
    """
    Collection of best practices and utilities for pagination
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def validate_page_size(page_size, min_size=1, max_size=1000):
        """
        Validate and sanitize page size
        
        Args:
            page_size: Requested page size
            min_size: Minimum allowed size
            max_size: Maximum allowed size
            
        Returns:
            Validated page size
        """
        if page_size < min_size:
            return min_size
        if page_size > max_size:
            return max_size
        return page_size
    
    @staticmethod
    def create_pagination_metadata(current_page, total_records, page_size):
        """
        Create standardized pagination metadata
        
        Args:
            current_page: Current page number
            total_records: Total number of records
            page_size: Records per page
            
        Returns:
            Dictionary with pagination metadata
        """
        total_pages = (total_records + page_size - 1) // page_size
        
        return {
            "current_page": current_page,
            "page_size": page_size,
            "total_records": total_records,
            "total_pages": total_pages,
            "has_previous": current_page > 1,
            "has_next": current_page < total_pages,
            "previous_page": current_page - 1 if current_page > 1 else None,
            "next_page": current_page + 1 if current_page < total_pages else None
        }
    
    @staticmethod
    def optimize_dataframe_for_pagination(df, partition_column=None, num_partitions=None):
        """
        Optimize DataFrame for pagination operations
        
        Args:
            df: Source DataFrame
            partition_column: Column to partition by
            num_partitions: Number of partitions
            
        Returns:
            Optimized DataFrame
        """
        if partition_column:
            # Repartition by specific column
            optimized_df = df.repartition(num_partitions or 10, partition_column)
        elif num_partitions:
            # Just repartition
            optimized_df = df.repartition(num_partitions)
        else:
            # Coalesce if too many partitions
            current_partitions = df.rdd.getNumPartitions()
            if current_partitions > 200:
                optimized_df = df.coalesce(200)
            else:
                optimized_df = df
        
        return optimized_df
    
    @staticmethod
    def create_stable_sort_key(df, primary_key="id"):
        """
        Add a stable sort key to ensure consistent pagination
        
        Args:
            df: Source DataFrame
            primary_key: Primary key column
            
        Returns:
            DataFrame with stable sort key
        """
        # Add row number as tie-breaker if needed
        if primary_key not in df.columns:
            df = df.withColumn("_sort_key", monotonically_increasing_id())
        else:
            df = df.withColumn("_sort_key", col(primary_key))
        
        return df

# REST API STYLE PAGINATION RESPONSES
# ============================================================================

class PaginationResponseFormatter:
    """
    Format pagination results in common API response styles
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def format_offset_response(page_data, page, page_size, total):
        """
        Format response in offset/limit style (common REST API pattern)
        
        Returns:
            Dictionary formatted as REST API response
        """
        return {
            "data": page_data.toJSON().collect() if page_data else [],
            "pagination": {
                "page": page,
                "page_size": page_size,
                "total_records": total,
                "total_pages": (total + page_size - 1) // page_size
            },
            "links": {
                "self": f"/api/resource?page={page}&page_size={page_size}",
                "first": f"/api/resource?page=1&page_size={page_size}",
                "last": f"/api/resource?page={(total + page_size - 1) // page_size}&page_size={page_size}",
                "next": f"/api/resource?page={page + 1
```python
                "next": f"/api/resource?page={page + 1}&page_size={page_size}" if page < (total + page_size - 1) // page_size else None,
                "prev": f"/api/resource?page={page - 1}&page_size={page_size}" if page > 1 else None
            }
        }
    
    @staticmethod
    def format_cursor_response(page_data, next_cursor, prev_cursor, page_size):
        """
        Format response in cursor style (GraphQL/modern API pattern)
        
        Returns:
            Dictionary formatted as cursor-based response
        """
        edges = []
        if page_data:
            for row in page_data.collect():
                edges.append({
                    "cursor": base64.b64encode(str(row['id']).encode()).decode(),
                    "node": row.asDict()
                })
        
        return {
            "edges": edges,
            "pageInfo": {
                "hasNextPage": next_cursor is not None,
                "hasPreviousPage": prev_cursor is not None,
                "startCursor": edges[0]["cursor"] if edges else None,
                "endCursor": edges[-1]["cursor"] if edges else None
            },
            "totalCount": page_size
        }
    
    @staticmethod
    def format_hateoas_response(page_data, page, page_size, total, base_url="/api/resource"):
        """
        Format response with HATEOAS (Hypermedia) links
        
        Returns:
            Dictionary with hypermedia controls
        """
        total_pages = (total + page_size - 1) // page_size
        
        links = [
            {"rel": "self", "href": f"{base_url}?page={page}&page_size={page_size}"},
            {"rel": "first", "href": f"{base_url}?page=1&page_size={page_size}"},
            {"rel": "last", "href": f"{base_url}?page={total_pages}&page_size={page_size}"}
        ]
        
        if page > 1:
            links.append({
                "rel": "prev",
                "href": f"{base_url}?page={page - 1}&page_size={page_size}"
            })
        
        if page < total_pages:
            links.append({
                "rel": "next",
                "href": f"{base_url}?page={page + 1}&page_size={page_size}"
            })
        
        return {
            "_embedded": {
                "items": page_data.toJSON().collect() if page_data else []
            },
            "_links": {link["rel"]: {"href": link["href"]} for link in links},
            "page": {
                "size": page_size,
                "totalElements": total,
                "totalPages": total_pages,
                "number": page
            }
        }

class AdvancedPaginationEngine:
    """
    Complete pagination engine with filtering, sorting, and search
    """
    
    def __init__(self, df):
        """
        Initialize advanced pagination engine
        
        Args:
            df: Source DataFrame
        """
        self.df = df
    
    def paginate(self, 
                 page=1, 
                 page_size=10, 
                 filters=None, 
                 sort_by=None, 
                 search=None,
                 pagination_type="offset"):
        """
        Universal pagination method with filtering and sorting
        
        Args:
            page: Page number (for offset-based)
            page_size: Records per page
            filters: Dictionary of filter conditions
            sort_by: List of tuples [(column, direction), ...]
            search: Dictionary for search {column: search_term}
            pagination_type: Type of pagination to use
            
        Returns:
            Paginated results with metadata
        """
        # Start with base dataframe
        working_df = self.df
        
        # Apply search if provided
        if search:
            search_conditions = []
            for column, term in search.items():
                if column in working_df.columns:
                    search_conditions.append(
                        col(column).like(f"%{term}%")
                    )
            
            if search_conditions:
                from functools import reduce
                search_filter = reduce(lambda a, b: a | b, search_conditions)
                working_df = working_df.filter(search_filter)
        
        # Apply filters if provided
        if filters:
            for column, condition in filters.items():
                if isinstance(condition, dict):
                    for operator, value in condition.items():
                        if operator == "eq":
                            working_df = working_df.filter(col(column) == value)
                        elif operator == "ne":
                            working_df = working_df.filter(col(column) != value)
                        elif operator == "gt":
                            working_df = working_df.filter(col(column) > value)
                        elif operator == "gte":
                            working_df = working_df.filter(col(column) >= value)
                        elif operator == "lt":
                            working_df = working_df.filter(col(column) < value)
                        elif operator == "lte":
                            working_df = working_df.filter(col(column) <= value)
                        elif operator == "in":
                            working_df = working_df.filter(col(column).isin(value))
                        elif operator == "not_in":
                            working_df = working_df.filter(~col(column).isin(value))
                        elif operator == "contains":
                            working_df = working_df.filter(col(column).contains(value))
                        elif operator == "startswith":
                            working_df = working_df.filter(col(column).startswith(value))
                        elif operator == "endswith":
                            working_df = working_df.filter(col(column).endswith(value))
                elif isinstance(condition, list):
                    # IN clause
                    working_df = working_df.filter(col(column).isin(condition))
                else:
                    # Simple equality
                    working_df = working_df.filter(col(column) == condition)
        
        # Apply sorting if provided
        if sort_by:
            sort_expressions = []
            for column, direction in sort_by:
                if direction.lower() == "asc":
                    sort_expressions.append(col(column).asc())
                else:
                    sort_expressions.append(col(column).desc())
            working_df = working_df.orderBy(*sort_expressions)
        else:
            # Default sort by id
            if "id" in working_df.columns:
                working_df = working_df.orderBy("id")
        
        # Get total count after filtering
        total_count = working_df.count()
        
        # Apply pagination based on type
        if pagination_type == "offset":
            pager = OffsetBasedPagination(working_df, page_size)
            result = pager.get_page(page)
        elif pagination_type == "cursor":
            pager = CursorBasedPagination(working_df, page_size)
            result = pager.get_page()
        elif pagination_type == "keyset":
            pager = KeysetPagination(working_df, page_size)
            result = pager.get_page()
        elif pagination_type == "token":
            sort_columns = [col_name for col_name, _ in sort_by] if sort_by else ["id"]
            pager = TokenBasedPagination(working_df, page_size, sort_columns)
            result = pager.get_page()
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown pagination type: {pagination_type}")
        
        # Add total count to result
        result['total_count'] = total_count
        result['filtered'] = filters is not None or search is not None
        
        return result

class PaginationPerformanceMonitor:
    """
    Monitor and analyze pagination performance
    """
    
    def __init__(self):
        self.metrics = []
    
    def measure(self, pagination_type, operation, df_size):
        """
        Measure pagination operation performance
        
        Args:
            pagination_type: Type of pagination
            operation: Operation being performed
            df_size: Size of dataset
            
        Returns:
            Decorator function
        """
        def decorator(func):
            def wrapper(*args, **kwargs):
                import time
                start_time = time.time()
                start_memory = 0  # In production, use memory_profiler
                
                result = func(*args, **kwargs)
                
                end_time = time.time()
                execution_time = end_time - start_time
                
                self.metrics.append({
                    "pagination_type": pagination_type,
                    "operation": operation,
                    "df_size": df_size,
                    "execution_time": execution_time,
                    "timestamp": datetime.now()
                })
                
                return result
            return wrapper
        return decorator
    
    def get_report(self):
        """
        Generate performance report
        
        Returns:
            Performance metrics summary
        """
        if not self.metrics:
            return "No metrics collected"
        
        report = "\n" + "=" * 80 + "\n"
        report += "PAGINATION PERFORMANCE REPORT\n"
        report += "=" * 80 + "\n"
        
        # Group by pagination type
        by_type = {}
        for metric in self.metrics:
            ptype = metric["pagination_type"]
            if ptype not in by_type:
                by_type[ptype] = []
            by_type[ptype].append(metric["execution_time"])
        
        for ptype, times in by_type.items():
            avg_time = sum(times) / len(times)
            min_time = min(times)
            max_time = max(times)
            
            report += f"\n{ptype.upper()} Pagination:\n"
            report += f"  Operations: {len(times)}\n"
            report += f"  Avg Time: {avg_time:.4f}s\n"
            report += f"  Min Time: {min_time:.4f}s\n"
            report += f"  Max Time: {max_time:.4f}s\n"
        
        return report

class ProductionPaginationUtils:
    """
    Production-ready utility functions for pagination
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def create_pagination_config(config_dict=None):
        """
        Create pagination configuration with defaults
        
        Args:
            config_dict: Custom configuration overrides
            
        Returns:
            Configuration dictionary
        """
        default_config = {
            "default_page_size": 20,
            "min_page_size": 1,
            "max_page_size": 100,
            "default_pagination_type": "keyset",
            "enable_caching": True,
            "cache_ttl_seconds": 300,
            "enable_metrics": True,
            "allow_arbitrary_sort": False,
            "allowed_sort_columns": ["id", "created_at", "updated_at"],
            "enable_search": True,
            "search_columns": ["order_number", "user_id"],
            "enable_filtering": True,
            "max_filter_conditions": 10
        }
        
        if config_dict:
            default_config.update(config_dict)
        
        return default_config
    
    @staticmethod
    def sanitize_pagination_params(params, config):
        """
        Sanitize and validate pagination parameters
        
        Args:
            params: Raw pagination parameters
            config: Pagination configuration
            
        Returns:
            Sanitized parameters
        """
        sanitized = {}
        
        # Sanitize page number
        page = params.get("page", 1)
        try:
            page = max(1, int(page))
        except (ValueError, TypeError):
            page = 1
        sanitized["page"] = page
        
        # Sanitize page size
        page_size = params.get("page_size", config["default_page_size"])
        try:
            page_size = int(page_size)
            page_size = max(config["min_page_size"], 
                          min(page_size, config["max_page_size"]))
        except (ValueError, TypeError):
            page_size = config["default_page_size"]
        sanitized["page_size"] = page_size
        
        # Sanitize sort parameters
        sort_by = params.get("sort_by", [])
        if sort_by and config.get("allow_arbitrary_sort", False):
            sanitized_sort = []
            for sort_item in sort_by:
                if isinstance(sort_item, (list, tuple)) and len(sort_item) == 2:
                    column, direction = sort_item
                    if (column in config.get("allowed_sort_columns", []) and
                        direction.lower() in ["asc", "desc"]):
                        sanitized_sort.append((column, direction.lower()))
            sanitized["sort_by"] = sanitized_sort
        else:
            sanitized["sort_by"] = None
        
        # Sanitize filters
        filters = params.get("filters", {})
        if filters and config.get("enable_filtering", True):
            max_conditions = config.get("max_filter_conditions", 10)
            if len(filters) <= max_conditions:
                sanitized["filters"] = filters
            else:
                sanitized["filters"] = dict(list(filters.items())[:max_conditions])
        else:
            sanitized["filters"] = None
        
        # Sanitize search
        search = params.get("search")
        if search and config.get("enable_search", True):
            sanitized["search"] = str(search)[:100]  # Limit search term length
        else:
            sanitized["search"] = None
        
        return sanitized
    
    @staticmethod
    def handle_pagination_error(error, default_response=None):
        """
        Handle pagination errors gracefully
        
        Args:
            error: Exception that occurred
            default_response: Default response to return
            
        Returns:
            Error response dictionary
        """
        error_response = {
            "success": False,
            "error": {
                "type": type(error).__name__,
                "message": str(error)
            },
            "data": default_response or []
        }
        
        # Log error (in production, use proper logging)
        print(f"Pagination error: {error}")
        
        return error_response

class PaginationAPIEndpoint:
    """
    Example implementation of paginated API endpoint
    """
    
    def __init__(self, df, config=None):
        """
        Initialize API endpoint
        
        Args:
            df: Source DataFrame
            config: Pagination configuration
        """
        self.df = df
        self.config = config or ProductionPaginationUtils.create_pagination_config()
        self.engine = AdvancedPaginationEngine(df)
        self.formatter = PaginationResponseFormatter()
    
    def get_paginated_results(self, request_params):
        """
        Process pagination request and return formatted response
        
        Args:
            request_params: Dictionary of request parameters
            
        Returns:
            Formatted API response
        """
        try:
            # Sanitize parameters
            params = ProductionPaginationUtils.sanitize_pagination_params(
                request_params, 
                self.config
            )
            
            # Execute pagination
            result = self.engine.paginate(
                page=params["page"],
                page_size=params["page_size"],
                filters=params["filters"],
                sort_by=params["sort_by"],
                search=params.get("search"),
                pagination_type=self.config["default_pagination_type"]
            )
            
            # Format response based on type
            response_format = request_params.get("format", "offset")
            
            if response_format == "cursor":
                formatted = self.formatter.format_cursor_response(
                    result.get("data"),
                    result.get("next_cursor"),
                    result.get("previous_cursor"),
                    result.get("page_size", 0)
                )
            elif response_format == "hateoas":
                formatted = self.formatter.format_hateoas_response(
                    result.get("data"),
                    params["page"],
                    params["page_size"],
                    result.get("total_count", 0)
                )
            else:
                formatted = self.formatter.format_offset_response(
                    result.get("data"),
                    params["page"],
                    params["page_size"],
                    result.get("total_count", 0)
                )
            
            # Add success flag
            formatted["success"] = True
            
            return formatted
            
        except Exception as e:
            return ProductionPaginationUtils.handle_pagination_error(e)

def test_pagination_patterns():
    """
    Comprehensive test suite for pagination patterns
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("RUNNING PAGINATION TESTS")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Create test data
    df = create_sample_data()
    
    test_results = {
        "passed": 0,
        "failed": 0,
        "tests": []
    }
    
    def run_test(test_name, test_func):
        """Helper to run individual test"""
        try:
            test_func()
            test_results["passed"] += 1
            test_results["tests"].append({"name": test_name, "status": "PASSED"})
            print(f"✓ {test_name}")
        except Exception as e:
            test_results["failed"] += 1
            test_results["tests"].append({
                "name": test_name, 
                "status": "FAILED", 
                "error": str(e)
            })
            print(f"✗ {test_name}: {e}")
    
    # Test 1: Offset pagination basic functionality
    def test_offset_basic():
        pager = OffsetBasedPagination(df, page_size=10)
        page = pager.get_page(1)
        assert page["page_size"] == 10, "Page size mismatch"
        assert page["page"] == 1, "Page number mismatch"
    
    run_test("Offset Pagination - Basic", test_offset_basic)
    
    # Test 2: Cursor pagination consistency
    def test_cursor_consistency():
        pager = CursorBasedPagination(df, page_size=10)
        page1 = pager.get_page()
        page2 = pager.get_page(cursor=page1["next_cursor"])
        
        # Ensure no overlap
        ids1 = [row["id"] for row in page1["data"].collect()]
        ids2 = [row["id"] for row in page2["data"].collect()]
        assert len(set(ids1) & set(ids2)) == 0, "Pages overlap"
    
    run_test("Cursor Pagination - Consistency", test_cursor_consistency)
    
    # Test 3: Keyset pagination performance
    def test_keyset_performance():
        pager = KeysetPagination(df, page_size=10)
        import time
        
        start = time.time()
        for i in range(5):
            pager.get_page()
        elapsed = time.time() - start
        
        assert elapsed < 5.0, f"Performance issue: {elapsed}s for 5 pages"
    
    run_test("Keyset Pagination - Performance", test_keyset_performance)
    
    # Test 4: Time-based pagination ordering
    def test_time_ordering():
        pager = TimeBasedPagination(df, page_size=10)
        page = pager.get_page(direction="forward")
        
        timestamps = [row["created_at"] for row in page["data"].collect()]
        assert timestamps == sorted(timestamps), "Timestamps not ordered"
    
    run_test("Time Pagination - Ordering", test_time_ordering)
    
    # Test 5: Token validation
    def test_token_validation():
        pager = TokenBasedPagination(df, page_size=10)
        page1 = pager.get_page()
        
        if page1["next_token"]:
            # Valid token should work
            page2 = pager.get_page(token=page1["next_token"])
            assert page2 is not None, "Valid token failed"
            
            # Invalid token should fail
            try:
                pager.get_page(token="invalid_token")
                assert False, "Invalid token should raise error"
            except ValueError:
                pass  # Expected
    
    run_test("Token Pagination - Validation", test_token_validation)
    
    # Test 6: Empty result handling
    def test_empty_results():
        empty_df = df.filter(col("id") < 0)  # No results
        pager = OffsetBasedPagination(empty_df, page_size=10)
        page = pager.get_page(1)
        assert page["page_size"] == 0, "Should have 0 results"
        assert page["total_pages"] == 0, "Should have 0 pages"
    
    run_test("Empty Results Handling", test_empty_results)
    
    # Test 7: Large offset handling
    def test_large_offset():
        pager = OffsetBasedPagination(df, page_size=10)
        try:
            page = pager.get_page(1000)  # Beyond available pages
            assert False, "Should raise error for invalid page"
        except ValueError:
            pass  # Expected
    
    run_test("Large Offset Handling", test_large_offset)
    
    # Test 8: Filter integration
    def test_filters():
        engine = AdvancedPaginationEngine(df)
        result = engine.paginate(
            page=1,
            page_size=10,
            filters={"user_id": "user_10"}
        )
        
        for row in result["data"].collect():
            assert row["user_id"] == "user_10", "Filter not applied"
    
    run_test("Filter Integration", test_filters)
    
    # Test 9: Sort integration
    def test_sorting():
        engine = AdvancedPaginationEngine(df)
        result = engine.paginate(
            page=1,
            page_size=10,
            sort_by=[("id", "desc")]
        )
        
        ids = [row["id"] for row in result["data"].collect()]
        assert ids == sorted(ids, reverse=True), "Sort not applied"
    
    run_test("Sort Integration", test_sorting)
    
    # Test 10: Parameter sanitization
    def test_sanitization():
        config = ProductionPaginationUtils.create_pagination_config()
        params = {
            "page": "invalid",
            "page_size": 10000,  # Too large
        }
        sanitized = ProductionPaginationUtils.sanitize_pagination_params(params, config)
        
        assert sanitized["page"] == 1, "Invalid page not sanitized"
        assert sanitized["page_size"] <= config["max_page_size"], "Page size not limited"
    
    run_test("Parameter Sanitization", test_sanitization)
    
    # Print test summary
    print("\n" + "-" * 80)
    print(f"Tests Passed: {test_results['passed']}")
    print(f"Tests Failed: {test_results['failed']}")
    print(f"Total Tests: {test_results['passed'] + test_results['failed']}")

        for test in test_results['tests']:
            if test['status'] == 'FAILED':
                print(f"  - {test['name']}: {test.get('error', 'Unknown error')}")

# Cursor-Based Pagination Example
from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import col
import base64
import json

spark = SparkSession.builder.appName("CursorPagination").getOrCreate()

# Load your data
df = spark.read.parquet("your_data.parquet")

def get_page(df, cursor=None, page_size=20):
    ordered_df = df.orderBy("id")
    
    if cursor:
        cursor_value = json.loads(base64.b64decode(cursor))["value"]
        filtered_df = ordered_df.filter(col("id") > cursor_value)
    else:
        filtered_df = ordered_df
    
    results = filtered_df.limit(page_size + 1).collect()
    has_more = len(results) > page_size
    page_results = results[:page_size]
    
    next_cursor = None
    if has_more:
        next_cursor = base64.b64encode(
            json.dumps({"value": page_results[-1]["id"]}).encode()
        ).decode()
    
    return page_results, next_cursor

# Usage
page1, cursor1 = get_page(df)
page2, cursor2 = get_page(df, cursor=cursor1)
""",
        
        "keyset_example.py": """
# Keyset Pagination Example
from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import col

spark = SparkSession.builder.appName("KeysetPagination").getOrCreate()

# Load your data
df = spark.read.parquet("your_data.parquet")

def get_page(df, last_id=None, page_size=20):
    ordered_df = df.orderBy(col("id").asc())
    
    if last_id:
        filtered_df = ordered_df.filter(col("id") > last_id)
    else:
        filtered_df = ordered_df
    
    results = filtered_df.limit(page_size + 1).collect()
    has_more = len(results) > page_size
    page_results = results[:page_size]
    
    next_key = page_results[-1]["id"] if page_results and has_more else None
    
    return page_results, next_key

# Usage
page1, key1 = get_page(df)
page2, key2 = get_page(df, last_id=key1)
page3, key3 = get_page(df, last_id=key2)
""",
        
        "time_based_example.py": """
# Time-Based Pagination Example
from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import col
from datetime import datetime

spark = SparkSession.builder.appName("TimePagination").getOrCreate()

# Load your data
df = spark.read.parquet("your_data.parquet")

def get_time_page(df, last_timestamp=None, last_id=None, page_size=20):
    ordered_df = df.orderBy(
        col("created_at").desc(),
        col("id").desc()
    )
    
    if last_timestamp:
        filtered_df = ordered_df.filter(
            (col("created_at") < last_timestamp) |
            ((col("created_at") == last_timestamp) & (col("id") < last_id))
        )
    else:
        filtered_df = ordered_df
    
    results = filtered_df.limit(page_size + 1).collect()
    has_more = len(results) > page_size
    page_results = results[:page_size]
    
    next_timestamp = None
    next_id = None
    if page_results and has_more:
        next_timestamp = page_results[-1]["created_at"]
        next_id = page_results[-1]["id"]
    
    return page_results, next_timestamp, next_id

# Usage - Get most recent items
page1, ts1, id1 = get_time_page(df)
page2, ts2, id2 = get_time_page(df, last_timestamp=ts1, last_id=id1)
""",
        
        "token_example.py": """
# Token-Based Pagination Example
from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import col
import base64
import json
import hashlib

spark = SparkSession.builder.appName("TokenPagination").getOrCreate()

# Load your data
df = spark.read.parquet("your_data.parquet")

def generate_token(last_values, secret_key="your-secret"):
    token_data = {
        "last_values": last_values,
        "timestamp": datetime.now().isoformat()
    }
    json_str = json.dumps(token_data, default=str)
    
    # Add HMAC signature in production
    signature = hashlib.sha256((json_str + secret_key).encode()).hexdigest()
    
    token_with_sig = json.dumps({
        "data": json_str,
        "signature": signature
    })
    
    return base64.b64encode(token_with_sig.encode()).decode()

def get_page(df, token=None, page_size=20):
    if token:
        decoded = base64.b64decode(token).decode()
        token_obj = json.loads(decoded)
        token_data = json.loads(token_obj["data"])
        last_id = token_data["last_values"]["id"]
        
        filtered_df = df.filter(col("id") > last_id)
    else:
        filtered_df = df
    
    ordered_df = filtered_df.orderBy("id")
    results = ordered_df.limit(page_size + 1).collect()
    
    has_more = len(results) > page_size
    page_results = results[:page_size]
    
    next_token = None
    if page_results and has_more:
        next_token = generate_token({"id": page_results[-1]["id"]})
    
    return page_results, next_token

# Usage
page1, token1 = get_page(df)
page2, token2 = get_page(df, token=token1)
"""

def comprehensive_performance_benchmark():
    """
    Run comprehensive performance benchmarks across all pagination patterns
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("COMPREHENSIVE PERFORMANCE BENCHMARK")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Create larger dataset for meaningful benchmarks
    print("\n[Benchmark] Creating large dataset (10,000 records)...")
    large_data = [
        (i, 
         f"user_{i % 100}", 
         f"order_{i:06d}", 
         100.0 + (i * 10.5), 
         datetime(2024, 1, 1) + timedelta(hours=i))
        for i in range(1, 10001)
    ]
    
    schema = StructType([
        StructField("id", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("user_id", StringType(), False),
        StructField("order_number", StringType(), False),
        StructField("amount", StringType(), False),
        StructField("created_at", TimestampType(), False)
    ])
    
    large_df = spark.createDataFrame(large_data, schema)
    large_df.cache()
    
    print(f"✓ Dataset created with {large_df.count()} records")
    
    # Benchmark configuration
    page_size = 50
    num_iterations = 20
    
    benchmark_results = {}
    
    # ========================================================================
    # Benchmark 1: Offset-Based Pagination
    # ========================================================================
    print("\n[Benchmark 1] Testing Offset-Based Pagination...")
    offset_pager = OffsetBasedPagination(large_df, page_size=page_size)
    
    offset_times = []
    import time
    
    for i in range(1, num_iterations + 1):
        start = time.time()
        page = offset_pager.get_page(i)
        _ = page['data'].count()  # Force evaluation
        elapsed = time.time() - start
        offset_times.append(elapsed)
    
    benchmark_results['offset'] = {
        'avg_time': sum(offset_times) / len(offset_times),
        'min_time': min(offset_times),
        'max_time': max(offset_times),
        'total_time': sum(offset_times),
        'times': offset_times
    }
    
    print(f"  Average: {benchmark_results['offset']['avg_time']:.4f}s")
    print(f"  Min: {benchmark_results['offset']['min_time']:.4f}s")
    print(f"  Max: {benchmark_results['offset']['max_time']:.4f}s")
    
    # ========================================================================
    # Benchmark 2: Cursor-Based Pagination
    # ========================================================================
    print("\n[Benchmark 2] Testing Cursor-Based Pagination...")
    cursor_pager = CursorBasedPagination(large_df, page_size=page_size)
    
    cursor_times = []
    cursor = None
    
    for i in range(num_iterations):
        start = time.time()
        page = cursor_pager.get_page(cursor=cursor)
        if page['data']:
            _ = page['data'].count()  # Force evaluation
        elapsed = time.time() - start
        cursor_times.append(elapsed)
        cursor = page['next_cursor']
        if not cursor:
            break
    
    benchmark_results['cursor'] = {
        'avg_time': sum(cursor_times) / len(cursor_times),
        'min_time': min(cursor_times),
        'max_time': max(cursor_times),
        'total_time': sum(cursor_times),
        'times': cursor_times
    }
    
    print(f"  Average: {benchmark_results['cursor']['avg_time']:.4f}s")
    print(f"  Min: {benchmark_results['cursor']['min_time']:.4f}s")
    print(f"  Max: {benchmark_results['cursor']['max_time']:.4f}s")
    
    # ========================================================================
    # Benchmark 3: Keyset Pagination
    # ========================================================================
    print("\n[Benchmark 3] Testing Keyset Pagination...")
    keyset_pager = KeysetPagination(large_df, page_size=page_size)
    
    keyset_times = []
    last_key = None
    
    for i in range(num_iterations):
        start = time.time()
        page = keyset_pager.get_page(last_key=last_key)
        if page['data']:
            _ = page['data'].count()  # Force evaluation
        elapsed = time.time() - start
        keyset_times.append(elapsed)
        last_key = page['next_key']
        if not last_key:
            break
    
    benchmark_results['keyset'] = {
        'avg_time': sum(keyset_times) / len(keyset_times),
        'min_time': min(keyset_times),
        'max_time': max(keyset_times),
        'total_time': sum(keyset_times),
        'times': keyset_times
    }

    print(f"  Min: {benchmark_results['keyset']['min_time']:.4f}s")
    print(f"  Max: {benchmark_results['keyset']['max_time']:.4f}s")
    
    # ========================================================================
    # Benchmark 4: Time-Based Pagination
    # ========================================================================
    print("\n[Benchmark 4] Testing Time-Based Pagination...")
    time_pager = TimeBasedPagination(large_df, page_size=page_size)

    last_id = None
    
    for i in range(num_iterations):

    print(f"  Min: {benchmark_results['time']['min_time']:.4f}s")

        page = token_pager.get_page(token=token)
        if page['data']:
            _ = page['data'].count()  # Force evaluation
        elapsed = time.time() - start
        token_times.append(elapsed)
        token = page['next_token']
        if not token:
            break
    
    benchmark_results['token'] = {
        'avg_time': sum(token_times) / len(token_times),
        'min_time': min(token_times),
        'max_time': max(token_times),
        'total_time': sum(token_times),
        'times': token_times
    }
    
    print(f"  Average: {benchmark_results['token']['avg_time']:.4f}s")
    print(f"  Min: {benchmark_results['token']['min_time']:.4f}s")
    print(f"  Max: {benchmark_results['token']['max_time']:.4f}s")
    
    # ========================================================================
    # Generate Benchmark Report
    # ========================================================================
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("BENCHMARK SUMMARY")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Sort by average time
    sorted_results = sorted(
        benchmark_results.items(),
        key=lambda x: x[1]['avg_time']
    )
    
    print("\nRanking by Average Performance (fastest to slowest):")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    for rank, (pattern, metrics) in enumerate(sorted_results, 1):
        print(f"\n{rank}. {pattern.upper()} Pagination")
        print(f"   Average Time: {metrics['avg_time']:.4f}s")
        print(f"   Min Time:     {metrics['min_time']:.4f}s")
        print(f"   Max Time:     {metrics['max_time']:.4f}s")
        print(f"   Total Time:   {metrics['total_time']:.4f}s")
        print(f"   Iterations:   {len(metrics['times'])}")
    
    # Performance comparison chart
    print("\n" + "-" * 80)
    print("Performance Comparison (relative to fastest):")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    fastest_time = sorted_results[0][1]['avg_time']
    
    for pattern, metrics in sorted_results:
        relative_perf = (metrics['avg_time'] / fastest_time) * 100
        bar_length = int(relative_perf / 5)
        bar = "█" * bar_length
        print(f"{pattern:12s} | {bar} {relative_perf:.1f}%")
    
    # Cleanup
    large_df.unpersist()
    
    return benchmark_results

def scalability_analysis():
    """
    Analyze how each pagination pattern scales with dataset size
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("SCALABILITY ANALYSIS")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    dataset_sizes = [100, 500, 1000, 5000, 10000]
    page_size = 50
    
    scalability_results = {
        'offset': [],
        'keyset': [],
        'cursor': []
    }
    
    for size in dataset_sizes:
        print(f"\n[Scalability] Testing with {size} records...")
        
        # Create dataset
        data = [
            (i, f"user_{i % 100}", f"order_{i:06d}", 
             100.0 + (i * 10.5), datetime(2024, 1, 1) + timedelta(hours=i))
            for i in range(1, size + 1)
        ]
        
        schema = StructType([
            StructField("id", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("user_id", StringType(), False),
            StructField("order_number", StringType(), False),
            StructField("amount", StringType(), False),
            StructField("created_at", TimestampType(), False)
        ])
        
        test_df = spark.createDataFrame(data, schema)
        test_df.cache()
        
        import time
        
        # Test offset at middle of dataset
        middle_page = size // (page_size * 2)
        offset_pager = OffsetBasedPagination(test_df, page_size=page_size)
        start = time.time()
        page = offset_pager.get_page(middle_page)
        _ = page['data'].count()
        offset_time = time.time() - start
        scalability_results['offset'].append((size, offset_time))
        
        # Test keyset
        keyset_pager = KeysetPagination(test_df, page_size=page_size)
        start = time.time()
        page = keyset_pager.get_page()
        _ = page['data'].count()
        keyset_time = time.time() - start
        scalability_results['keyset'].append((size, keyset_time))
        
        # Test cursor
        cursor_pager = CursorBasedPagination(test_df, page_size=page_size)
        start = time.time()
        page = cursor_pager.get_page()
        _ = page['data'].count()
        cursor_time = time.time() - start
        scalability_results['cursor'].append((size, cursor_time))
        
        test_df.unpersist()
        
        print(f"  Offset:  {offset_time:.4f}s")
        print(f"  Keyset:  {keyset_time:.4f}s")
        print(f"  Cursor:  {cursor_time:.4f}s")
    
    # Print scalability report
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("SCALABILITY REPORT")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    print("\nDataset Size vs. Performance:")
    print("-" * 80)
    print(f"{'Size':>10s} | {'Offset':>10s} | {'Keyset':>10s} | {'Cursor':>10s}")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    for i, size in enumerate(dataset_sizes):
        print(f"{size:>10d} | "
              f"{scalability_results['offset'][i][1]:>9.4f}s | "
              f"{scalability_results['keyset'][i][1]:>9.4f}s | "
              f"{scalability_results['cursor'][i][1]:>9.4f}s")
    
    print("\nScalability Factor (time ratio from smallest to largest dataset):")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    for pattern in ['offset', 'keyset', 'cursor']:
        first_time = scalability_results[pattern][0][1]
        last_time = scalability_results[pattern][-1][1]
        factor = last_time / first_time if first_time > 0 else 0
        print(f"{pattern.capitalize():12s}: {factor:.2f}x slower")
    
    return scalability_results

def concurrency_test():
    """
    Test pagination patterns under concurrent access
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("CONCURRENCY TEST")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor, as_completed
    import time
    
    # Create test dataset
    data = [
        (i, f"user_{i % 100}", f"order_{i:06d}", 
         100.0 + (i * 10.5), datetime(2024, 1, 1) + timedelta(hours=i))
        for i in range(1, 5001)
    ]
    
    schema = StructType([
        StructField("id", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("user_id", StringType(), False),
        StructField("order_number", StringType(), False),
        StructField("amount", StringType(), False),
        StructField("created_at", TimestampType(), False)
    ])
    
    test_df = spark.createDataFrame(data, schema)
    test_df.cache()
    
    num_threads = 10
    requests_per_thread = 5
    
    def worker_offset(thread_id):
        """Worker function for offset pagination"""
        pager = OffsetBasedPagination(test_df, page_size=50)
        results = []
        for i in range(requests_per_thread):
            page_num = (thread_id * requests_per_thread) + i + 1
            start = time.time()
            try:
                page = pager.get_page(page_num)
                elapsed = time.time() - start
                results.append(('success', elapsed))
            except Exception as e:
                elapsed = time.time() - start
                results.append(('error', elapsed))
        return results
    
    def worker_keyset(thread_id):
        """Worker function for keyset pagination"""
        pager = KeysetPagination(test_df, page_size=50)
        results = []
        last_key = thread_id * 250  # Start from different positions
        for i in range(requests_per_thread):
            start = time.time()
            try:
                page = pager.get_page(last_key=last_key)
                elapsed = time.time() - start
                results.append(('success', elapsed))
                last_key = page['next_key']
                if not last_key:
                    break
            except Exception as e:
                elapsed = time.time() - start
                results.append(('error', elapsed))
        return results
    
    # Test offset pagination concurrency
    print("\n[Concurrency] Testing Offset Pagination with {} threads...".format(num_threads))
    start_time = time.time()
    
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=num_threads) as executor:
        futures = [executor.submit(worker_offset, i) for i in range(num_threads)]
        offset_results = []
        for future in as_completed(futures):
            offset_results.extend(future.result())
    
    offset_duration = time.time() - start_time
    offset_success = sum(1 for r in offset_results if r[0] == 'success')
    offset_avg_time = sum(r[1] for r in offset_results) / len(offset_results)
    
    print(f"  Duration: {offset_duration:.2f}s")
    print(f"  Successful requests: {offset_success}/{len(offset_results)}")
    print(f"  Average request time: {offset_avg_time:.4f}s")
    
    # Test keyset pagination concurrency
    print("\n[Concurrency] Testing Keyset Pagination with {} threads...".format(num_threads))
    start_time = time.time()
    
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=num_threads) as executor:
        futures = [executor.submit(worker_keyset, i) for i in range(num_threads)]
        keyset_results = []
        for future in as_completed(futures):
            keyset_results.extend(future.result())
    
    keyset_duration = time.time() - start_time
    keyset_success = sum(1 for r in keyset_results if r[0] == 'success')
    keyset_avg_time = sum(r[1] for r in keyset_results) / len(keyset_results)
    
    print(f"  Duration: {keyset_duration:.2f}s")
    print(f"  Successful requests: {keyset_success}/{len(keyset_results)}")
    print(f"  Average request time: {keyset_avg_time:.4f}s")
    
    # Summary
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("CONCURRENCY TEST SUMMARY")
    print("=" * 80)
    print(f"\nOffset Pagination:")
    print(f"  Throughput: {len(offset_results)/offset_duration:.2f} req/s")
    print(f"  Success rate: {offset_success/len(offset_results)*100:.1f}%")
    
    print(f"\nKeyset Pagination:")
    print(f"  Throughput: {len(keyset_results)/keyset_duration:.2f} req/s")
    print(f"  Success rate: {keyset_success/len(keyset_results)*100:.1f}%")
    
    test_df.unpersist()
    
    return {
        'offset': {
            'duration': offset_duration,
            'success_rate': offset_success/len(offset_results),
            'avg_time': offset_avg_time
        },
        'keyset': {
            'duration': keyset_duration,
            'success_rate': keyset_success/len(keyset_results),
            'avg_time': keyset_avg_time
        }
    }

def data_consistency_test():
    """
    Test data consistency across pagination patterns
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("DATA CONSISTENCY TEST")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Create test dataset
    data = [
        (i, f"user_{i % 100}", f"order_{i:06d}", 
         100.0 + (i * 10.5), datetime(2024, 1, 1) + timedelta(hours=i))
        for i in range(1, 1001)
    ]
    
    schema = StructType([
        StructField("id", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("user_id", StringType(), False),
        StructField("order_number", StringType(), False),
        StructField("amount", StringType(), False),
        StructField("created_at", TimestampType(), False)
    ])
    
    test_df = spark.createDataFrame(data, schema)
    
    page_size = 50
    total_records = test_df.count()
    
    print(f"\nDataset: {total_records} records, page size: {page_size}")
    
    # Test 1: Check for duplicates across pages
    print("\n[Test 1] Checking for duplicate records across pages...")
    
    def check_duplicates(pager_class, **kwargs):
        """Check if any records appear in multiple pages"""
        pager = pager_class(test_df, page_size=page_size, **kwargs)
        all_ids = set()
        duplicates = []
        page_num = 1
        
        if pager_class == OffsetBasedPagination:
            total_pages = (total_records + page_size - 1) // page_size
            for i in range(1, total_pages + 1):
                page = pager.get_page(i)
                page_ids = {row['id'] for row in page['data'].collect()}
                
                # Check for duplicates
                overlap = all_ids & page_ids
                if overlap:
                    duplicates.extend(overlap)
                
                all_ids.update(page_ids)
        else:
            # For cursor/keyset pagination
            cursor_or_key = None
            while True:
                if pager_class == CursorBasedPagination:
                    page = pager.get_page(cursor=cursor_or_key)
                    cursor_or_key = page.get('next_cursor')
                elif pager_class == KeysetPagination:
                    page = pager.get_page(last_key=cursor_or_key)
                    cursor_or_key = page.get('next_key')
                
                if not page['data'] or page['page_size'] == 0:
                    break
                
                page_ids = {row['id'] for row in page['data'].collect()}
                
                # Check for duplicates
                overlap = all_ids & page_ids
                if overlap:
                    duplicates.extend(overlap)
                
                all_ids.update(page_ids)
                
                if not cursor_or_key:
                    break
        
        return len(duplicates), len(all_ids)
    
    # Test offset pagination
    offset_dups, offset_total = check_duplicates(OffsetBasedPagination)
    print(f"  Offset: {offset_dups} duplicates, {offset_total} unique records")
    
    # Test cursor pagination
    cursor_dups, cursor_total = check_duplicates(CursorBasedPagination)
    print(f"  Cursor: {cursor_dups} duplicates, {cursor_total} unique records")
    
    # Test keyset pagination
    keyset_dups, keyset_total = check_duplicates(KeysetPagination)
    print(f"  Keyset: {keyset_dups} duplicates, {keyset_total} unique records")
    
    # Test 2: Check for missing records
    print("\n[Test 2] Checking for missing records...")
    
    print(f"  Offset: {total_records - offset_total} missing records")
    print(f"  Cursor: {total_records - cursor_total} missing records")
    print(f"  Keyset: {total_records - keyset_total} missing records")
    
    # Test 3: Order consistency
    print("\n[Test 3] Checking order consistency...")
    
    def check_order(pager_class, **kwargs):
        """Check if records are in correct order"""
        pager = pager_class(test_df, page_size=page_size, **kwargs)
        all_ids = []
        
        if pager_class == OffsetBasedPagination:
            total_pages = (total_records + page_size - 1) // page_size
            for i in range(1, min(total_pages + 1, 6)):  # Check first 5 pages
                page = pager.get_page(i)
                page_ids = [row['id'] for row in page['data'].collect()]
                all_ids.extend(page_ids)
        else:
            cursor_or_key = None
            for _ in range(5):  # Check first 5 pages
                if pager_class == CursorBasedPagination:
                    page = pager.get_page(cursor=cursor_or_key)
                    cursor_or_key = page.get('next_cursor')
                elif pager_class == KeysetPagination:
                    page = pager.get_page(last_key=cursor_or_key)
                    cursor_or_key = page.get('next_key')
                
                if not page['data'] or page['page_size'] == 0:
                    break
                
                page_ids = [row['id'] for row in page['data'].collect()]
                all_ids.extend(page_ids)
                
                if not cursor_or_key:
                    break
        
        # Check if sorted
        is_sorted = all_ids == sorted(all_ids)
        return is_sorted
    
    offset_ordered = check_order(OffsetBasedPagination)
    cursor_ordered = check_order(CursorBasedPagination)
    keyset_ordered = check_order(KeysetPagination)
    
    print(f"  Offset: {'✓ Ordered' if offset_ordered else '✗ Not ordered'}")
    print(f"
```python
    print(f"  Cursor: {'✓ Ordered' if cursor_ordered else '✗ Not ordered'}")
    print(f"  Keyset: {'✓ Ordered' if keyset_ordered else '✗ Not ordered'}")
    
    # Summary
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("DATA CONSISTENCY SUMMARY")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    consistency_score = {
        'offset': {
            'no_duplicates': offset_dups == 0,
            'no_missing': offset_total == total_records,
            'ordered': offset_ordered,
            'score': sum([offset_dups == 0, offset_total == total_records, offset_ordered])
        },
        'cursor': {
            'no_duplicates': cursor_dups == 0,
            'no_missing': cursor_total == total_records,
            'ordered': cursor_ordered,
            'score': sum([cursor_dups == 0, cursor_total == total_records, cursor_ordered])
        },
        'keyset': {
            'no_duplicates': keyset_dups == 0,
            'no_missing': keyset_total == total_records,
            'ordered': keyset_ordered,
            'score': sum([keyset_dups == 0, keyset_total == total_records, keyset_ordered])
        }
    }
    
    for pattern, metrics in consistency_score.items():
        print(f"\n{pattern.upper()} Pagination:")
        print(f"  No duplicates: {'✓' if metrics['no_duplicates'] else '✗'}")
        print(f"  No missing records: {'✓' if metrics['no_missing'] else '✗'}")
        print(f"  Correct order: {'✓' if metrics['ordered'] else '✗'}")
        print(f"  Consistency score: {metrics['score']}/3")
    
    return consistency_score

def edge_cases_test():
    """
    Test edge cases and error handling
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("EDGE CASES TESTING")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Create test datasets
    normal_data = [
        (i, f"user_{i}", f"order_{i:06d}", 
         100.0 + i, datetime(2024, 1, 1) + timedelta(hours=i))
        for i in range(1, 101)
    ]
    
    schema = StructType([
        StructField("id", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("user_id", StringType(), False),
        StructField("order_number", StringType(), False),
        StructField("amount", StringType(), False),
        StructField("created_at", TimestampType(), False)
    ])
    
    normal_df = spark.createDataFrame(normal_data, schema)
    empty_df = spark.createDataFrame([], schema)
    
    edge_case_results = []
    
    # Edge Case 1: Empty dataset
    print("\n[Edge Case 1] Empty dataset...")
    try:
        pager = OffsetBasedPagination(empty_df, page_size=10)
        page = pager.get_page(1)
        result = "✓ Handled correctly" if page['page_size'] == 0 else "✗ Incorrect handling"
        edge_case_results.append(("Empty dataset - Offset", result))
        print(f"  Offset: {result}")
    except Exception as e:
        edge_case_results.append(("Empty dataset - Offset", f"✗ Error: {e}"))
        print(f"  Offset: ✗ Error: {e}")
    
    try:
        pager = KeysetPagination(empty_df, page_size=10)
        page = pager.get_page()
        result = "✓ Handled correctly" if page['data'] is None or page['page_size'] == 0 else "✗ Incorrect handling"
        edge_case_results.append(("Empty dataset - Keyset", result))
        print(f"  Keyset: {result}")
    except Exception as e:
        edge_case_results.append(("Empty dataset - Keyset", f"✗ Error: {e}"))
        print(f"  Keyset: ✗ Error: {e}")
    
    # Edge Case 2: Single record
    print("\n[Edge Case 2] Single record dataset...")
    single_df = spark.createDataFrame(normal_data[:1], schema)
    
    try:
        pager = OffsetBasedPagination(single_df, page_size=10)
        page = pager.get_page(1)
        result = "✓ Handled correctly" if page['page_size'] == 1 else "✗ Incorrect handling"
        edge_case_results.append(("Single record - Offset", result))
        print(f"  Offset: {result}")
    except Exception as e:
        edge_case_results.append(("Single record - Offset", f"✗ Error: {e}"))
        print(f"  Offset: ✗ Error: {e}")
    
    # Edge Case 3: Page size larger than dataset
    print("\n[Edge Case 3] Page size larger than dataset...")
    try:
        pager = OffsetBasedPagination(normal_df, page_size=1000)
        page = pager.get_page(1)
        result = "✓ Handled correctly" if page['page_size'] == 100 else "✗ Incorrect handling"
        edge_case_results.append(("Large page size", result))
        print(f"  Result: {result} (returned {page['page_size']} records)")
    except Exception as e:
        edge_case_results.append(("Large page size", f"✗ Error: {e}"))
        print(f"  Result: ✗ Error: {e}")
    
    # Edge Case 4: Invalid page number
    print("\n[Edge Case 4] Invalid page number...")
    try:
        pager = OffsetBasedPagination(normal_df, page_size=10)
        page = pager.get_page(1000)
        edge_case_results.append(("Invalid page number", "✗ Should have raised error"))
        print(f"  Result: ✗ Should have raised error")
    except ValueError:
        edge_case_results.append(("Invalid page number", "✓ Correctly raised ValueError"))
        print(f"  Result: ✓ Correctly raised ValueError")
    except Exception as e:
        edge_case_results.append(("Invalid page number", f"✗ Unexpected error: {e}"))
        print(f"  Result: ✗ Unexpected error: {e}")
    
    # Edge Case 5: Negative page number
    print("\n[Edge Case 5] Negative page number...")
    try:
        pager = OffsetBasedPagination(normal_df, page_size=10)
        page = pager.get_page(-1)
        edge_case_results.append(("Negative page number", "✗ Should have raised error"))
        print(f"  Result: ✗ Should have raised error")
    except ValueError:
        edge_case_results.append(("Negative page number", "✓ Correctly raised ValueError"))
        print(f"  Result: ✓ Correctly raised ValueError")
    except Exception as e:
        edge_case_results.append(("Negative page number", f"✗ Unexpected error: {e}"))
        print(f"  Result: ✗ Unexpected error: {e}")
    
    # Edge Case 6: Invalid cursor
    print("\n[Edge Case 6] Invalid cursor...")
    try:
        pager = CursorBasedPagination(normal_df, page_size=10)
        page = pager.get_page(cursor="invalid_cursor_string")
        edge_case_results.append(("Invalid cursor", "✗ Should have handled error"))
        print(f"  Result: ✗ Should have handled error")
    except Exception:
        edge_case_results.append(("Invalid cursor", "✓ Correctly handled invalid cursor"))
        print(f"  Result: ✓ Correctly handled invalid cursor")
    
    # Edge Case 7: Null values in sort column
    print("\n[Edge Case 7] Null values in sort column...")
    null_data = normal_data[:10]
    # Note: Can't add None to IntegerType(False), so we skip this test
    print(f"  Result: ⊘ Skipped (schema doesn't allow nulls)")
    edge_case_results.append(("Null values", "⊘ Skipped"))
    
    # Edge Case 8: Duplicate values in sort column
    print("\n[Edge Case 8] Duplicate values in sort column...")
    dup_data = [(1, f"user_{i}", f"order_{i:06d}", 
                 100.0, datetime(2024, 1, 1)) for i in range(1, 21)]
    dup_df = spark.createDataFrame(dup_data, schema)
    
    try:
        pager = KeysetPagination(dup_df, page_size=5)
        page1 = pager.get_page()
        page2 = pager.get_page(last_key=page1['next_key']) if page1['next_key'] else None
        
        if page2:
            ids1 = {row['id'] for row in page1['data'].collect()}
            ids2 = {row['id'] for row in page2['data'].collect()}
            overlap = ids1 & ids2
            result = "✓ Handled correctly" if len(overlap) == 0 else "✗ Has duplicates"
        else:
            result = "✓ Handled correctly"
        
        edge_case_results.append(("Duplicate sort values", result))
        print(f"  Result: {result}")
    except Exception as e:
        edge_case_results.append(("Duplicate sort values", f"✗ Error: {e}"))
        print(f"  Result: ✗ Error: {e}")
    
    # Edge Case 9: Very small page size (1)
    print("\n[Edge Case 9] Very small page size (1)...")
    try:
        pager = OffsetBasedPagination(normal_df, page_size=1)
        page = pager.get_page(1)
        result = "✓ Handled correctly" if page['page_size'] == 1 else "✗ Incorrect handling"
        edge_case_results.append(("Page size = 1", result))
        print(f"  Result: {result}")
    except Exception as e:
        edge_case_results.append(("Page size = 1", f"✗ Error: {e}"))
        print(f"  Result: ✗ Error: {e}")
    
    # Edge Case 10: Last page with partial results
    print("\n[Edge Case 10] Last page with partial results...")
    try:
        pager = OffsetBasedPagination(normal_df, page_size=15)
        total_pages = pager.total_pages
        last_page = pager.get_page(total_pages)
        expected_size = 100 % 15 if 100 % 15 != 0 else 15
        result = "✓ Handled correctly" if last_page['page_size'] == expected_size else "✗ Incorrect handling"
        edge_case_results.append(("Partial last page", result))
        print(f"  Result: {result} (expected {expected_size}, got {last_page['page_size']})")
    except Exception as e:
        edge_case_results.append(("Partial last page", f"✗ Error: {e}"))
        print(f"  Result: ✗ Error: {e}")
    
    # Summary
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("EDGE CASES SUMMARY")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    passed = sum(1 for _, result in edge_case_results if result.startswith("✓"))
    failed = sum(1 for _, result in edge_case_results if result.startswith("✗"))
    skipped = sum(1 for _, result in edge_case_results if result.startswith("⊘"))
    
    print(f"\nTotal tests: {len(edge_case_results)}")
    print(f"Passed: {passed}")
    print(f"Failed: {failed}")
    print(f"Skipped: {skipped}")
    
    if failed > 0:
        print("\nFailed tests:")
        for case, result in edge_case_results:
            if result.startswith("✗"):
                print(f"  - {case}: {result}")
    
    return edge_case_results

1. INTRODUCTION
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

This library provides five different pagination patterns for PySpark:

• Offset-Based Pagination (LIMIT/OFFSET)
• Cursor-Based Pagination (Position Markers)
• Keyset Pagination (Seek Method)
• Time-Based Pagination (Temporal)
• Token-Based Pagination (Stateless)

Each pattern has different trade-offs in terms of performance, consistency,
and complexity. Choose based on your specific requirements.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
2. PATTERN DESCRIPTIONS
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

2.1 OFFSET-BASED PAGINATION
────────────────────────────

Description:
  Traditional pagination using LIMIT and OFFSET clauses.

Pros:
  ✓ Simple to implement
  ✓ Allows jumping to any page
  ✓ Familiar to users (page numbers)
  ✓ Easy to understand

Cons:
  ✗ Performance degrades with large offsets
  ✗ Inconsistent results if data changes
  ✗ Can skip or duplicate records
  ✗ Database must scan all skipped rows

Use When:
  • Dataset is small (<10,000 records)
  • Need page numbers in UI
  • Data doesn't change frequently
  • Simplicity is priority

Avoid When:
  • Dataset is large
  • Real-time data
  • Performance is critical

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

2.2 CURSOR-BASED PAGINATION
────────────────────────────

Description:
  Uses encoded position markers to track pagination state.

Pros:
  ✓ Consistent results even if data changes
  ✓ Better performance than offset
  ✓ No skipped or duplicated records
  ✓ Good for infinite scroll

Cons:
  ✗ Cannot jump to arbitrary pages
  ✗ Cursor becomes invalid if record deleted
  ✗ More complex than offset
  ✗ Cursor strings can be large

Use When:
  • Implementing infinite scroll
  • Data changes frequently
  • Need consistent results
  • Sequential access pattern

Avoid When:
  • Need random page access
  • Simple use case
  • Cursor size is concern

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

2.3 KEYSET PAGINATION
──────────────────────

Description:
  Uses WHERE clause filtering based on last seen key value.

Pros:
  ✓ Excellent performance even with large datasets
  ✓ Consistent results
  ✓ Efficient index usage
  ✓ Scales well

Cons:
  ✗ Requires unique, sequential key
  ✗ Cannot jump to arbitrary pages
  ✗ Complex with multiple sort columns
  ✗ Doesn't work well with non-unique keys

Use When:
  • Large datasets (>100,000 records)
  • Performance is critical
  • Have unique sequential key
  • Sequential access pattern

Avoid When:
  • Need random page access
  • No unique key available
  • Complex multi-column sorting

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

2.4 TIME-BASED PAGINATION
──────────────────────────

Description:
  Paginates based on timestamp values with tie-breaker.

Pros:
  ✓ Natural for time-series data
  ✓ Efficient for recent data queries
  ✓ Works well with time-partitioning
  ✓ Good for activity feeds

Cons:
  ✗ Requires timestamp column
  ✗ Issues with same timestamp
  ✗ Needs tie-breaker column
  ✗ Only works for temporal data

Use When:
  • Time-series data
  • Activity feeds
  • Chronological ordering
  • Recent data queries

Avoid When:
  • Data not time-ordered
  • Need non-temporal sorting
  • No timestamp column

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

2.5 TOKEN-BASED PAGINATION
───────────────────────────

Description:
  Uses encrypted/signed tokens containing pagination state.

Pros:
  ✓ Secure (tokens can be encrypted)
  ✓ Flexible (encode multiple parameters)
  ✓ Stateless (all state in token)
  ✓ Good for APIs

Cons:
  ✗ Token size can be large
  ✗ Requires token generation logic
  ✗ More complex to implement
  ✗ Token validation overhead

Use When:
  • Public APIs
  • Need security
  • Complex state required
  • Rate limiting needed

Avoid When:
  • Simplicity preferred
  • Token size is concern
  • Internal use only

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
3. USAGE EXAMPLES
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

3.1 OFFSET-BASED PAGINATION
────────────────────────────

from pagination_patterns import OffsetBasedPagination

# Initialize
pager = OffsetBasedPagination(df, page_size=20)

# Get specific page
page = pager.get_page(1)

# Access data
data = page['data']
total_pages = page['total_pages']
has_next = page['has_next']

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

3.2 CURSOR-BASED PAGINATION
────────────────────────────

from pagination_patterns import CursorBasedPagination

# Initialize
pager = CursorBasedPagination(df, page_size=20)

# Get first page
page1 = pager.get_page()

# Get next page using cursor
page2 = pager.get_page(cursor=page1['next_cursor'])

# Navigate backward
page1_again = pager.get_page(
    cursor=page2['previous_cursor'],
    direction='previous'
)

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

3.3 KEYSET PAGINATION
──────────────────────

from pagination_patterns import KeysetPagination

# Initialize
pager = KeysetPagination(df, page_size=20, key_column='id')

# Get first page
page1 = pager.get_page()

# Get next page using last key
page2 = pager.get_page(last_key=page1['next_key'])

# Composite key pagination
page = pager.get_page_with_composite_key(
    sort_columns=[('created_at', 'desc'), ('id', 'desc')]
)

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

3.4 TIME-BASED PAGINATION
──────────────────────────

from pagination_patterns import TimeBasedPagination
from datetime import datetime

# Initialize
pager = TimeBasedPagination(df, page_size=20)

# Get recent items (newest first)
page = pager.get_page(direction='backward')

# Get older items
older = pager.get_page(
    last_timestamp=page['next_timestamp'],
    last_id=page['next_id'],
    direction='backward'
)

# Get time window
window = pager.get_time_window(
    start_time=datetime(2024, 1, 1),
    end_time=datetime(2024, 1, 31)
)

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

3.5 TOKEN-BASED PAGINATION
───────────────────────────

from pagination_patterns import TokenBasedPagination

# Initialize
pager = TokenBasedPagination(df, page_size=20)

# Get first page
page1 = pager.get_page()

# Get next page using token
page2 = pager.get_page(token=page1['next_token'])

# With filters
filtered = pager.get_page_with_filters(
    filters={'amount': {'>=': 100, '<=': 500}}
)

4. PERFORMANCE CHARACTERISTICS
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Pattern          | Small Data | Large Data | Random Access | Sequential
─────────────────┼────────────┼────────────┼───────────────┼────────────
Offset           | Excellent  | Poor       | Yes           | Yes
Cursor           | Good       | Good       | No            | Yes
Keyset           | Good       | Excellent  | No            | Yes
Time-Based       | Good       | Good       | No            | Yes
Token            | Good       | Good       | Limited       | Yes

Memory Usage:    Offset < Keyset < Cursor < Time < Token
Complexity:      Offset < Keyset < Time < Cursor < Token
Consistency:     Keyset = Cursor = Time > Token > Offset

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
