from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import *
from pyspark.sql.types import *
import time

class IntegratedResourceOptimization:
    """
    Integrates all resource utilization optimization patterns.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, app_name="IntegratedOptimization"):
        """
        Initialize with all optimizations enabled.
        """
        self.spark = SparkSession.builder \
            .appName(app_name) \
            .config("spark.task.cpus", "1") \
            .config("spark.executor.cores", "4") \
            .config("spark.executor.memory", "4g") \
            .config("spark.executor.memoryOverhead", "1g") \
            .config("spark.memory.fraction", "0.75") \
            .config("spark.memory.storageFraction", "0.5") \
            .config("spark.memory.offHeap.enabled", "true") \
            .config("spark.memory.offHeap.size", "2g") \
            .config("spark.serializer", "org.apache.spark.serializer.KryoSerializer") \
            .config("spark.kryoserializer.buffer.max", "1024m") \
            .config("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "true") \
            .config("spark.sql.adaptive.coalescePartitions.enabled", "true") \
            .config("spark.sql.parquet.compression.codec", "snappy") \
            .config("spark.sql.parquet.filterPushdown", "true") \
            .config("spark.sql.parquet.enableVectorizedReader", "true") \
            .config("spark.sql.inMemoryColumnarStorage.compressed", "true") \
            .config("spark.sql.execution.arrow.pyspark.enabled", "true") \
            .config("spark.executor.extraJavaOptions", "-XX:+UseNUMA -XX:+UseParallelGC") \
            .getOrCreate()
    
    def process_with_all_optimizations(self, input_path, output_path):
        """
        Process data using all optimization patterns.
        
        Args:
            input_path: Input data path
            output_path: Output data path
        """
        print("=== Integrated Resource Optimization ===\n")
        
        start_time = time.time()
        
        # 1. I/O Optimization: Read with schema and predicate pushdown
        print("1. Optimized Read...")
        schema = StructType([
            StructField("id", LongType(), True),
            StructField("category", StringType(), True),
            StructField("value", DoubleType(), True
```python
            StructField("value", DoubleType(), True),
            StructField("region", StringType(), True),
            StructField("timestamp", StringType(), True)
        ])
        
        df = self.spark.read \
            .schema(schema) \
            .option("mergeSchema", "false") \
            .parquet(input_path)
        
        read_time = time.time() - start_time
        print(f"   Read completed in {read_time:.2f}s")
        
        # 2. Memory Alignment: Optimize schema layout
        print("\n2. Memory Alignment Optimization...")
        start_time = time.time()
        
        # Reorder columns for better memory alignment (larger types first)
        df = df.select("id", "value", "category", "region", "timestamp")
        
        alignment_time = time.time() - start_time
        print(f"   Schema aligned in {alignment_time:.2f}s")
        
        # 3. CPU Affinity: Optimize partitioning
        print("\n3. CPU Affinity Optimization...")
        start_time = time.time()
        
        import psutil
        num_cores = psutil.cpu_count(logical=True)
        df = df.repartition(num_cores)
        
        cpu_time = time.time() - start_time
        print(f"   Repartitioned to {num_cores} partitions in {cpu_time:.2f}s")
        
        # 4. Cache Optimization: Multi-level caching
        print("\n4. Cache Optimization...")
        start_time = time.time()
        
        from pyspark import StorageLevel
        df.persist(StorageLevel.MEMORY_AND_DISK)
        df.count()  # Trigger caching
        
        cache_time = time.time() - start_time
        print(f"   Data cached in {cache_time:.2f}s")
        
        # 5. NUMA Awareness: Process with locality
        print("\n5. NUMA-Aware Processing...")
        start_time = time.time()
        
        result = df.groupBy("category", "region") \
            .agg(
                count("*").alias("count"),
                sum("value").alias("total_value"),
                avg("value").alias("avg_value"),
                min("value").alias("min_value"),
                max("value").alias("max_value")
            )
        
        numa_time = time.time() - start_time
        print(f"   Aggregation completed in {numa_time:.2f}s")
        
        # 6. I/O Optimization: Coalesce and write
        print("\n6. Optimized Write...")
        start_time = time.time()
        
        # Coalesce to reduce number of output files
        result = result.coalesce(10)
        
        result.write \
            .mode("overwrite") \
            .option("compression", "snappy") \
            .partitionBy("category") \
            .parquet(output_path)
        
        write_time = time.time() - start_time
        print(f"   Write completed in {write_time:.2f}s")
        
        # Summary
        total_time = read_time + alignment_time + cpu_time + cache_time + numa_time + write_time
        print(f"\n=== Total Processing Time: {total_time:.2f}s ===")
        
        return result

        ])
        
        df = self.spark.createDataFrame(data, schema)

        # Benchmark 2: With caching

        print(f"   Time: {partition_time:.2f}s")

        # Benchmark 4: All optimizations

        # Summary

        print(f"Partitioning Only:  {partition_time:.2f}s ({baseline_time/partition_time:.2f}x)")
        print(f"All Optimizations:  {optimized_time:.2f}s ({baseline_time/optimized_time:.2f}x)")
        
        # Cleanup
        df.unpersist()
        df_optimized.unpersist()

## Additional Utility Module

```python
"""
Resource Monitoring Utilities
==============================
Helper utilities for monitoring resource utilization during optimization.
"""

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
import psutil
import time
from typing import Dict, List
import json

class ResourceMonitor:
    """
    Monitor and report resource utilization metrics.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        """
        Initialize resource monitor.
        
        Args:
            spark: SparkSession instance
        """
        self.spark = spark
        self.metrics_history = []
    
    def get_cpu_metrics(self) -> Dict:
        """
        Get current CPU metrics.
        
        Returns:
            Dictionary of CPU metrics
        """
        return {
            "cpu_percent": psutil.cpu_percent(interval=1, percpu=True),
            "cpu_count_physical": psutil.cpu_count(logical=False),
            "cpu_count_logical": psutil.cpu_count(logical=True),
            "cpu_freq": psutil.cpu_freq()._asdict() if psutil.cpu_freq() else None
        }
    
    def get_memory_metrics(self) -> Dict:
        """
        Get current memory metrics.
        
        Returns:
            Dictionary of memory metrics
        """
        mem = psutil.virtual_memory()
        return {
            "total_gb": mem.total / (1024**3),
            "available_gb": mem.available / (1024**3),
            "used_gb": mem.used / (1024**3),
            "percent": mem.percent
        }
    
    def get_spark_metrics(self) -> Dict:
        """
        Get Spark-specific metrics.
        
        Returns:
            Dictionary of Spark metrics
        """
        sc = self.spark.sparkContext
        
        return {
            "active_jobs": len(sc.statusTracker().getActiveJobIds()),
            "active_stages": len(sc.statusTracker().getActiveStageIds()),
            "executor_count": len(sc.statusTracker().getExecutorInfos()) - 1,  # Exclude driver
            "default_parallelism": sc.defaultParallelism
        }
    
    def capture_metrics(self) -> Dict:
        """
        Capture all metrics at current point in time.
        
        Returns:
            Combined metrics dictionary
        """
        metrics = {
            "timestamp": time.time(),
            "cpu": self.get_cpu_metrics(),
            "memory": self.get_memory_metrics(),
            "spark": self.get_spark_metrics()
        }
        
        self.metrics_history.append(metrics)
        return metrics
    
    def print_metrics(self, metrics: Dict = None):
        """
        Print metrics in readable format.
        
        Args:
            metrics: Metrics to print (uses latest if None)
        """
        if metrics is None:
            metrics = self.capture_metrics()
        
        print("\n" + "="*60)
        print("RESOURCE UTILIZATION METRICS")
        print("="*60)
        
        print("\nCPU Metrics:")
        print(f"  Physical Cores: {metrics['cpu']['cpu_count_physical']}")
        print(f"  Logical Cores:  {metrics['cpu']['cpu_count_logical']}")
        print(f"  CPU Usage:      {sum(metrics['cpu']['cpu_percent']) / len(metrics['cpu']['cpu_percent']):.1f}%")
        
        print("\nMemory Metrics:")
        print(f"  Total:     {metrics['memory']['total_gb']:.2f} GB")
        print(f"  Available: {metrics['memory']['available_gb']:.2f} GB")
        print(f"  Used:      {metrics['memory']['used_gb']:.2f} GB ({metrics['memory']['percent']:.1f}%)")
        
        print("\nSpark Metrics:")
        print(f"  Active Jobs:   {metrics['spark']['active_jobs']}")
        print(f"  Active Stages: {metrics['spark']['active_stages']}")
        print(f"  Executors:     {metrics['spark']['executor_count']}")
        print(f"  Parallelism:   {metrics['spark']['default_parallelism']}")
        
        print("="*60 + "\n")
    
    def export_metrics(self, filepath: str):
        """
        Export metrics history to JSON file.
        
        Args:
            filepath: Output file path
        """
        with open(filepath, 'w') as f:
            json.dump(self.metrics_history, f, indent=2)
        
        print(f"Metrics exported to {filepath}")


# Example usage of ResourceMonitor
if __name__ == "__main__":
    spark = SparkSession.builder \
        .appName("ResourceMonitorDemo") \
        .getOrCreate()
    
    monitor = ResourceMonitor(spark)
    
    # Capture and print metrics
    monitor.print_metrics()
    
    # Simulate some work
    df = spark.range(1000000).selectExpr("id", "id * 2 as doubled")
    df.count()
    
    # Capture metrics after work
    monitor.print_metrics()
    
    # Export metrics
    monitor.export_metrics("/tmp/resource_metrics.json")
    
    spark.stop()

This complete implementation provides:

1. **CPU Affinity Pattern**: Binds tasks to specific CPU cores for better cache locality
2. **NUMA Awareness Pattern**: Optimizes memory access for multi-socket systems
3. **Cache Optimization Pattern**:
```python
3. **Cache Optimization Pattern**: Multi-level caching strategies with adaptive storage levels
4. **Memory Alignment Pattern**: Optimizes data layout for reduced memory fragmentation
5. **I/O Optimization Pattern**: Maximizes I/O throughput with compression, partitioning, and predicate pushdown
6. **Integrated Optimization**: Combines all patterns for maximum performance
7. **Resource Monitoring**: Tracks and reports resource utilization metrics

            "spark.sql.parquet.compression.codec": "snappy",
            "spark.sql.parquet.filterPushdown": "true",
            
            # Serialization
            "spark.serializer": "org.apache.spark.serializer.KryoSerializer",
            
            # Optimization
            "spark.sql.codegen.wholeStage": "true",
            "spark.sql.inMemoryColumnarStorage.compressed": "true"
        }
    
    @staticmethod
    def apply_config(spark_builder, config_dict):
        """
        Apply configuration dictionary to SparkSession builder.
        
        Args:
            spark_builder: SparkSession.builder instance
            config_dict: Configuration dictionary
        
        Returns:
            Configured SparkSession.builder
        """
        for key, value in config_dict.items():
            spark_builder = spark_builder.config(key, value)
        
        return spark_builder

## Performance Testing Framework

```python
"""
Performance Testing Framework
=============================
Framework for testing and comparing optimization strategies.
"""

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import *
from pyspark.sql.types import *
import time
from typing import Callable, List, Dict
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd

class PerformanceTester:
    """
    Test and compare performance of different optimization strategies.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        """
        Initialize performance tester.
        
        Args:
            spark: SparkSession instance
        """
        self.spark = spark
        self.results = []
    
    def time_operation(self, operation: Callable, name: str, 
                      iterations: int = 1) -> Dict:
        """
        Time a Spark operation.
        
        Args:
            operation: Function to execute
            name: Name of the operation
            iterations: Number of iterations to run
        
        Returns:
            Dictionary with timing results
        """
        times = []
        
        for i in range(iterations):
            start_time = time.time()
            result = operation()
            
            # Force evaluation if DataFrame
            if hasattr(result, 'count'):
                result.count()
            
            elapsed = time.time() - start_time
            times.append(elapsed)
            
            print(f"{name} - Iteration {i+1}/{iterations}: {elapsed:.2f}s")
        
        avg_time = sum(times) / len(times)
        min_time = min(times)
        max_time = max(times)
        
        result_dict = {
            "name": name,
            "avg_time": avg_time,
            "min_time": min_time,
            "max_time": max_time,
            "iterations": iterations
        }
        
        self.results.append(result_dict)
        
        return result_dict
    
    def compare_strategies(self, strategies: List[Dict]):
        """
        Compare multiple optimization strategies.
        
        Args:
            strategies: List of strategy dictionaries with 'name' and 'operation'
        """
        print("\n" + "="*70)
        print("STRATEGY COMPARISON")
        print("="*70 + "\n")
        
        comparison_results = []
        
        for strategy in strategies:
            print(f"\nTesting: {strategy['name']}")
            print("-" * 70)
            
            result = self.time_operation(
                strategy['operation'],
                strategy['name'],
                iterations=strategy.get('iterations', 3)
            )
            
            comparison_results.append(result)
        
        # Print comparison table
        print("\n" + "="*70)
        print("COMPARISON RESULTS")
        print("="*70)
        print(f"{'Strategy':<40} {'Avg Time':<12} {'Min Time':<12} {'Max Time':<12}")
        print("-" * 70)
        
        baseline = comparison_results[0]['avg_time']
        
        for result in comparison_results:
            speedup = baseline / result['avg_time']
            print(f"{result['name']:<40} {result['avg_time']:>10.2f}s "
                  f"{result['min_time']:>10.2f}s {result['max_time']:>10.2f}s "
                  f"({speedup:.2f}x)")
        
        print("="*70 + "\n")
        
        return comparison_results
    
    def plot_results(self, output_path: str = "/tmp/performance_comparison.png"):
        """
        Plot performance comparison results.
        
        Args:
            output_path: Path to save the plot
        """
        if not self.results:
            print("No results to plot")
            return
        
        # Create DataFrame from results
        df = pd.DataFrame(self.results)
        
        # Create bar plot
        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 6))
        
        x = range(len(df))
        ax.bar(x, df['avg_time'], yerr=[df['avg_time'] - df['min_time'],
                                         df['max_time'] - df['avg_time']],
               capsize=5, alpha=0.7, color='steelblue')
        
        ax.set_xlabel('Strategy', fontsize=12)
        ax.set_ylabel('Time (seconds)', fontsize=12)
        ax.set_title('Performance Comparison of Optimization Strategies', 
                    fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
        ax.set_xticks(x)
        ax.set_xticklabels(df['name'], rotation=45, ha='right')
        ax.grid(axis='y', alpha=0.3)
        
        plt.tight_layout()
        plt.savefig(output_path, dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
        print(f"Plot saved to {output_path}")
        
        plt.close()
    
    def generate_report(self, output_path: str = "/tmp/performance_report.txt"):
        """
        Generate detailed performance report.
        
        Args:
            output_path: Path to save the report
        """
        if not self.results:
            print("No results to report")
            return
        
        with open(output_path, 'w') as f:
            f.write("="*70 + "\n")
            f.write("RESOURCE UTILIZATION OPTIMIZATION PERFORMANCE REPORT\n")
            f.write("="*70 + "\n\n")
            
            f.write(f"Total Strategies Tested: {len(self.results)}\n")
            f.write(f"Report Generated: {time.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')}\n\n")
            
            # Summary statistics
            baseline = self.results[0]['avg_time']
            best_result = min(self.results, key=lambda x: x['avg_time'])
            
            f.write("SUMMARY\n")
            f.write("-" * 70 + "\n")
            f.write(f"Baseline Strategy: {self.results[0]['name']}\n")
            f.write(f"Baseline Time: {baseline:.2f}s\n")
            f.write(f"Best Strategy: {best_result['name']}\n")
            f.write(f"Best Time: {best_result['avg_time']:.2f}s\n")
            f.write(f"Maximum Speedup: {baseline / best_result['avg_time']:.2f}x\n\n")
            
            # Detailed results
            f.write("DETAILED RESULTS\n")
            f.write("-" * 70 + "\n\n")
            
            for i, result in enumerate(self.results, 1):
                speedup = baseline / result['avg_time']
                improvement = ((baseline - result['avg_time']) / baseline) * 100
                
                f.write(f"{i}. {result['name']}\n")
                f.write(f"   Average Time: {result['avg_time']:.2f}s\n")
                f.write(f"   Min Time: {result['min_time']:.2f}s\n")
                f.write(f"   Max Time: {result['max
```python
                f.write(f"   Max Time: {result['max_time']:.2f}s\n")
                f.write(f"   Iterations: {result['iterations']}\n")
                f.write(f"   Speedup: {speedup:.2f}x\n")
                f.write(f"   Improvement: {improvement:.1f}%\n\n")
            
            # Recommendations
            f.write("RECOMMENDATIONS\n")
            f.write("-" * 70 + "\n")
            
            sorted_results = sorted(self.results, key=lambda x: x['avg_time'])
            
            f.write(f"1. Best Overall: {sorted_results[0]['name']}\n")
            f.write(f"   Use for: Production workloads requiring optimal performance\n\n")
            
            if len(sorted_results) > 1:
                f.write(f"2. Runner-up: {sorted_results[1]['name']}\n")
                f.write(f"   Use for: Balance between performance and resource usage\n\n")
            
            if len(sorted_results) > 2:
                f.write(f"3. Alternative: {sorted_results[2]['name']}\n")
                f.write(f"   Use for: Specific use cases or constraints\n\n")
            
            f.write("="*70 + "\n")
        
        print(f"Report saved to {output_path}")


# Comprehensive Performance Test Suite
def run_comprehensive_tests():
    """
    Run comprehensive performance tests for all optimization patterns.
    """
    print("""
    ╔════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
    ║        COMPREHENSIVE OPTIMIZATION PERFORMANCE TESTS            ║
    ╚════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
    """)
    
    # Create Spark session with balanced config
    config = OptimizationConfigurations.get_balanced_config()
    spark = SparkSession.builder.appName("PerformanceTests")
    spark = OptimizationConfigurations.apply_config(spark, config)
    spark = spark.getOrCreate()
    
    # Initialize tester
    tester = PerformanceTester(spark)
    
    # Create test dataset
    print("\nGenerating test dataset...")
    test_data = []
    for i in range(1000000):
        test_data.append((
            i,
            f"category_{i % 100}",
            f"region_{i % 20}",
            float(i % 10000),
            i % 1000
        ))
    
    schema = StructType([
        StructField("id", LongType(), True),
        StructField("category", StringType(), True),
        StructField("region", StringType(), True),
        StructField("value", DoubleType(), True),
        StructField("count", IntegerType(), True)
    ])
    
    base_df = spark.createDataFrame(test_data, schema)
    
    # Define test strategies
    strategies = [
        {
            "name": "Baseline (No Optimization)",
            "operation": lambda: base_df.groupBy("category").agg(
                sum("value").alias("total"),
                avg("count").alias("avg_count")
            ),
            "iterations": 3
        },
        {
            "name": "With Caching",
            "operation": lambda: base_df.cache().groupBy("category").agg(
                sum("value").alias("total"),
                avg("count").alias("avg_count")
            ),
            "iterations": 3
        },
        {
            "name": "With Optimal Partitioning",
            "operation": lambda: base_df.repartition(16, "category").groupBy("category").agg(
                sum("value").alias("total"),
                avg("count").alias("avg_count")
            ),
            "iterations": 3
        },
        {
            "name": "With Memory Alignment",
            "operation": lambda: base_df.select("id", "value", "count", "category", "region") \
                .groupBy("category").agg(
                    sum("value").alias("total"),
                    avg("count").alias("avg_count")
                ),
            "iterations": 3
        },
        {
            "name": "All Optimizations Combined",
            "operation": lambda: base_df \
                .select("id", "value", "count", "category", "region") \
                .repartition(16, "category") \
                .cache() \
                .groupBy("category").agg(
                    sum("value").alias("total"),
                    avg("count").alias("avg_count")
                ),
            "iterations": 3
        }
    ]
    
    # Run comparison
    results = tester.compare_strategies(strategies)
    
    # Generate visualizations and reports
    tester.plot_results()
    tester.generate_report()
    
    # Cleanup
    base_df.unpersist()
    spark.stop()
    
    print("\nComprehensive tests completed!")
    return results


if __name__ == "__main__":
    run_comprehensive_tests()

## Documentation and Usage Examples

```python
"""
Usage Examples and Documentation
=================================
Comprehensive examples of how to use each optimization pattern.
"""

class OptimizationExamples:
    """
    Collection of practical examples for each optimization pattern.
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def example_1_cpu_affinity():
        """
        Example: Using CPU Affinity for compute-intensive ETL.
        """
        print("\n" + "="*70)
        print("EXAMPLE 1: CPU Affinity for ETL Pipeline")
        print("="*70 + "\n")
        
        from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
        import psutil
        
        # Create session with CPU affinity optimization
        num_cores = psutil.cpu_count(logical=True)
        
        spark = SparkSession.builder \
            .appName("ETL_CPU_Optimized") \
            .config("spark.default.parallelism", str(num_cores)) \
            .config("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", str(num_cores)) \
            .config("spark.task.cpus", "1") \
            .getOrCreate()
        
        # Sample ETL pipeline
        print("Processing ETL pipeline with CPU affinity...")
        
        # Extract
        df = spark.range(0, 1000000).selectExpr(
            "id",
            "id % 100 as category",
            "id * 1.5 as value"
        )
        
        # Transform with optimal partitioning
        df = df.repartition(num_cores, "category")
        
        # Perform CPU-intensive transformations
        result = df.groupBy("category").agg(
            count("*").alias("count"),
            sum("value").alias("total_value"),
            avg("value").alias("avg_value")
        )
        
        # Load
        result.show(10)
        
        print(f"Processed with {num_cores} cores")
        print(f"Partitions: {result.rdd.getNumPartitions()}")
        
        spark.stop()
    
    @staticmethod
    def example_2_numa_awareness():
        """
        Example: NUMA-aware data processing for large datasets.
        """
        print("\n" + "="*70)
        print("EXAMPLE 2: NUMA-Aware Large Dataset Processing")
        print("="*70 + "\n")
        
        from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
        
        spark = SparkSession.builder \
            .appName("NUMA_Optimized") \
            .config("spark.executor.extraJavaOptions", "-XX:+UseNUMA") \
            .config("spark.memory.offHeap.enabled", "true") \
            .config("spark.memory.offHeap.size", "2g") \
            .getOrCreate()
        
        print("Processing with NUMA awareness...")
        
        # Create large dataset
        df = spark.range(0, 5000000).selectExpr(
            "id",
            "id % 1000 as product_id",
            "id % 50 as store_id",
            "rand() * 100 as sales"
        )
        
        # NUMA-aware aggregation
        result = df.groupBy("product_id", "store_id").agg(
            sum("sales").alias("total_sales"),
            count("*").alias("transaction_count")
        )
        
        result.show(10)
        
        spark.stop()
    
    @staticmethod
    def example_3_cache_optimization():
        """
        Example: Multi-level caching for iterative algorithms.
        """
        print("\n" + "="*70)
        print("EXAMPLE 3: Multi-Level Caching for Iterative Processing")
        print("="*70 + "\n")
        
        from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
        from pyspark import StorageLevel
        
        spark = SparkSession.builder \
            .appName("Cache_Optimized") \
            .config("spark.memory.fraction", "0.7") \
            .config("spark.memory.storageFraction", "0.6") \
            .getOrCreate()
        
        print("Iterative processing with optimized caching...")
        
        # Create base dataset
        df = spark.range(0, 1000000).selectExpr(
            "id",
            "id % 100 as cluster",
            "rand() * 100 as feature1",
            "rand() * 100 as feature2"
        )
        
        # Cache hot data in memory
        hot_data = df.filter(col("cluster") < 10)
        hot_data.persist(StorageLevel.MEMORY_ONLY)
        
        # Cache warm data with disk fallback
        warm_data = df.filter((col("cluster") >= 10) & (col("cluster") < 50))
        warm_data.persist(StorageLevel.MEMORY_AND_DISK)
        
        # Iterative processing (e.g., K-means style)
        for iteration in range(3):
            print(f"\nIteration {iteration + 1}:")
            
            # Process hot data
            hot_result = hot_data.groupBy("cluster").agg(
                avg("feature1").alias("centroid1"),
                avg("feature2").alias("centroid2")
            )
            print(f"  Hot data clusters: {hot_result.count()}")
            
            # Process warm data
            warm_result = warm_data.groupBy("cluster").agg(
                avg("feature1").alias("centroid1"),
                avg("feature2").alias("centroid2")
            )
            print(f"  Warm data clusters: {warm_result.count()}")
        
        # Cleanup
        hot_data.unpersist()
        warm_data.unpersist()
        spark.stop()
    
    @staticmethod
    def example_4_memory_alignment():
        """
        Example: Memory-aligned schema for analytics workload.
        """
        print("\n" + "="*70)
        print("EXAMPLE 4: Memory Alignment for Analytics")
        print("="*70 + "\n")
        
        from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
        from pyspark.sql.types import *
        
        spark = SparkSession.builder \
            .appName("Memory_Aligned") \
            .config("spark.sql.tungsten.enabled", "true") \
            .config("spark.sql.codegen.wholeStage", "true") \
            .getOrCreate()
        
        # Create schema with optimal alignment (large types first)
        optimized_schema = StructType([
            StructField("timestamp", LongType(), True),      # 8 bytes
            StructField("amount", DoubleType(), True),       # 8 bytes
            StructField("quantity", IntegerType(), True),    # 4 bytes
            StructField("discount", FloatType(), True),      # 4 bytes
            StructField("is_active", BooleanType(), True),   # 1 byte
            StructField("product_name", StringType(), True)  # Variable
        ])
        
        print("Creating data with memory-aligned schema...")
        
        data = [(
            1704067200 + i,
            100.0 + i,
            i % 10,
            0.1 * (i % 5),
            bool(i % 2),
            f"product_{i % 100}"
        ) for i in range(100000)]
        
        df = spark.createDataFrame(data, optimized_schema)
        
        # Perform analytics
        result = df.groupBy("is_active").agg(
            sum("amount").alias("total_amount"),

```python
"""
Advanced Monitoring and Profiling
==================================
Tools for deep performance analysis and bottleneck identification.
"""

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import *
import time
import json
from collections import defaultdict

class AdvancedProfiler:
    """
    Advanced profiling tools for Spark applications.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        """
        Initialize advanced profiler.
        
        Args:
            spark: SparkSession instance
        """
        self.spark = spark
        self.sc = spark.sparkContext
        self.profile_data = defaultdict(list)
    
    def profile_stage_execution(self, df, operation_name: str):
        """
        Profile stage execution metrics.
        
        Args:
            df: DataFrame to profile
            operation_name: Name of the operation
        
        Returns:
            Execution metrics
        """
        print(f"\nProfiling: {operation_name}")
        print("-" * 70)
        
        # Get initial stage count
        initial_stages = len(self.sc.statusTracker().getActiveStageIds())
        
        # Execute operation
        start_time = time.time()
        result = df.count()
        execution_time = time.time() - start_time
        
        # Get final stage count
        final_stages = len(self.sc.statusTracker().getActiveStageIds())
        
        # Collect metrics
        metrics = {
            "operation": operation_name,
            "execution_time": execution_time,
            "result_count": result,
            "stages_executed": final_stages - initial_stages,
            "partitions": df.rdd.getNumPartitions()
        }
        
        self.profile_data[operation_name].append(metrics)
        
        print(f"Execution Time: {execution_time:.2f}s")
        print(f"Result Count: {result}")
        print(f"Partitions: {metrics['partitions']}")
        
        return metrics
    
    def analyze_partition_skew(self, df):
        """
        Analyze partition size distribution to detect skew.
        
        Args:
            df: DataFrame to analyze
        
        Returns:
            Partition statistics
        """
        print("\nAnalyzing Partition Skew...")
        print("-" * 70)
        
        # Get partition sizes
        partition_sizes = df.rdd.mapPartitions(
            lambda iterator: [sum(1 for _ in iterator)]
        ).collect()
        
        if not partition_sizes:
            print("No data in partitions")
            return None
        
        total_records = sum(partition_sizes)
        avg_size = total_records / len(partition_sizes)
        max_size = max(partition_sizes)
        min_size = min(partition_sizes)
        
        # Calculate skew factor
        skew_factor = max_size / avg_size if avg_size > 0 else 0
        
        stats = {
            "num_partitions": len(partition_sizes),
            "total_records": total_records,
            "avg_partition_size": avg_size,
            "max_partition_size": max_size,
            "min_partition_size": min_size,
            "skew_factor": skew_factor,
            "partition_sizes": partition_sizes
        }
        
        print(f"Number of Partitions: {stats['num_partitions']}")
        print(f"Total Records: {stats['total_records']}")
        print(f"Average Partition Size: {stats['avg_partition_size']:.0f}")
        print(f"Max Partition Size: {stats['max_partition_size']}")
        print(f"Min Partition Size: {stats['min_partition_size']}")
        print(f"Skew Factor: {stats['skew_factor']:.2f}")
        
        if skew_factor > 2.0:
            print("\n⚠️  WARNING: Significant partition skew detected!")
            print("   Consider repartitioning or salting keys")
        
        return stats
    
    def analyze_memory_usage(self, df):
        """
        Analyze memory usage patterns.
        
        Args:
            df: DataFrame to analyze
        
        Returns:
            Memory usage statistics
        """
        print("\nAnalyzing Memory Usage...")
        print("-" * 70)
        
        # Cache the DataFrame to analyze memory usage
        df.cache()
        df.count()  # Materialize
        
        # Get storage information
        storage_status = self.sc._jsc.sc().getRDDStorageInfo()
        
        if storage_status:
            for rdd_info in storage_status:
                print(f"RDD ID: {rdd_info.id()}")
                print(f"Memory Size: {rdd_info.memSize() / (1024**2):.2f} MB")
                print(f"Disk Size: {rdd_info.diskSize() / (1024**2):.2f} MB")
                print(f"Partitions: {rdd_info.numPartitions()}")
                print(f"Cached Partitions: {rdd_info.numCachedPartitions()}")
        
        df.unpersist()
    
    def profile_shuffle_operations(self, df, operation):
        """
        Profile shuffle operations.
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            operation: Operation that causes shuffle
        
        Returns:
            Shuffle metrics
        """
        print("\nProfiling Shuffle Operations...")
        print("-" * 70)
        
        # Execute operation and get metrics
        start_time = time.time()
        result = operation(df)
        result.count()  # Trigger execution
        execution_time = time.time() - start_time
        
        print(f"Shuffle Execution Time: {execution_time:.2f}s")
        print(f"Input Partitions: {df.rdd.getNumPartitions()}")
        print(f"Output Partitions: {result.rdd.getNumPartitions()}")
        
        # Show physical plan
        print("\nPhysical Plan:")
        result.explain()
        
        return {
            "execution_time": execution_time,
            "input_partitions": df.rdd.getNumPartitions(),
            "output_partitions": result.rdd.getNumPartitions()
        }
    
    def identify_bottlenecks(self):
        """
        Identify performance bottlenecks from collected metrics.
        
        Returns:
            List of identified bottlenecks
        """
        print("\n" + "="*70)
        print("BOTTLENECK ANALYSIS")
        print("="*70 + "\n")
        
        bottlenecks = []
        
        for operation, metrics_list in self.profile_data.items():
            if not metrics_list:
                continue
            
            avg_time = sum(m['execution_time'] for m in metrics_list) / len(metrics_list)
            
            # Check for slow operations
            if avg_time > 5.0:
                bottlenecks.append({
                    "type": "Slow Operation",
                    "operation": operation,
                    "avg_time": avg_time,
                    "recommendation": "Consider optimization or caching"
                })
            
            # Check for excessive partitions
            avg_partitions = sum(m['partitions'] for m in metrics_list) / len(metrics_list)
            if avg_partitions > 1000:
                bottlenecks.append({
                    "type": "Excessive Partitions",
                    "operation": operation,
                    "partitions": avg_partitions,
                    "recommendation": "Use coalesce to reduce partitions"
                })
            elif avg_partitions < 10:
                bottlenecks.append({
                    "type": "Insufficient Parallelism",
                    "operation": operation,
                    "partitions": avg_partitions,
                    "recommendation": "Increase partitions for better parallelism"
                })
        
        if bottlenecks:
            for i, bottleneck in enumerate(bottlenecks, 1):
                print(f"{i}. {bottleneck['type']}")
                print(f"   Operation: {bottleneck['operation']}")
                for key, value in bottleneck.items():
                    if key not in ['type', 'operation', 'recommendation']:
                        print(f"   {key.replace('_', ' ').title()}: {value}")
                print(f"   💡 Recommendation: {bottleneck['recommendation']}\n")
        else:
            print("✅ No significant bottlenecks detected!")
        
        return bottlenecks
    
    def generate_optimization_report(self, output_path: str = "/tmp/optimization_report.json"):
        """
        Generate comprehensive optimization report.
        
        Args:
            output_path: Path to save the report
        """
        report = {
            "timestamp": time.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S'),
            "profile_data": dict(self.profile_data),
            "bottlenecks": self.identify_bottlenecks(),
            "recommendations": self._generate_recommendations()
        }
        
        with open(output_path, 'w') as f:
            json.dump(report, f, indent=2)
        
        print(f"\nOptimization report saved to {output_path}")
        
        return report
    
    def _generate_recommendations(self):
        """
        Generate optimization recommendations based on profiling data.
        
        Returns:
            List of recommendations
        """
        recommendations = []
        
        # Analyze overall performance
        all_times = []
        for metrics_list in self.profile_data.values():
            all_times.extend([m['execution_time'] for m in metrics_list])
        
        if all_times:
            avg_time = sum(all_times) / len(all_times)
            
            if avg_time > 10.0:
                recommendations.append({
                    "category": "Performance",
                    "priority": "High",
                    "suggestion": "Consider enabling Adaptive Query Execution (AQE)",
                    "config": "spark.sql.adaptive.enabled=true"
                })
            
            if avg_time > 5.0:
                recommendations.append({
                    "category": "Caching",
                    "priority": "Medium",
                    "suggestion": "Cache frequently accessed DataFrames",
                    "code": "df.cache() or df.persist(StorageLevel.MEMORY_AND_DISK)"
                })
        
        recommendations.append({
            "category": "Monitoring",
            "priority": "Low",
            "suggestion": "Enable Spark UI for detailed monitoring",
            "config": "Access Spark UI at http://localhost:4040"
        })
        
        return recommendations


# Demonstration of Advanced Profiling
def demonstrate_advanced_profiling():
    """
    Demonstrate advanced profiling capabilities.
    """
    print("""
    ╔════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
    ║           ADVANCED PROFILING DEMONSTRATION                     ║
    ╚════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
    """)
    
    # Create Spark session
    spark = SparkSession.builder \
        .appName("AdvancedProfiling") \
        .config("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "true") \
        .getOrCreate()
    
    # Initialize profiler
    profiler = AdvancedProfiler(spark)
    
    # Create test dataset
    print("\nCreating test dataset...")
    df = spark.range(0, 1000000).selectExpr(
        "id",
        "id % 100 as key",
        "rand() * 1000 as value"
    )
    
    # Profile different operations
    print("\n" + "="*70)
    print("PROFILING OPERATIONS")
    print("="*70)
    
    # 1. Profile simple aggregation
    profiler.profile_stage_execution(
        df.groupBy("key").count(),
        "Simple Aggregation"
    )
    
    # 2. Profile complex aggregation
    profiler.profile_stage_execution(
        df.groupBy("key").agg(
            sum("value").alias("total"),
            avg("value").alias("average"),
            count("*").alias("count")
        ),
        "Complex Aggregation"
    )
    
    # 3. Analyze partition skew
    skewed_df = spark.range(0, 1000000).selectExpr(
        "case when id < 900000 then 1 else id % 100 end as key",
        "id as value"
    )
    profiler.analyze_partition_skew(skewed_df)
    
    # 4. Profile shuffle operations
    profiler.profile_shuffle_operations(
        df,
        lambda d: d.repartition(50, "key")
    )
    
    # 5. Analyze memory usage
    profiler.analyze_memory_usage(df)
    
    # 6. Identify bottlenecks
    profiler.identify_bottlenecks()
    
    # 7. Generate report
    profiler.generate_optimization_report()
    
    spark.stop()
    
    print("\n" + "="*70)
    print("PROFILING COMPLETED!")
    print("="*70 + "\n")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    demonstrate_advanced_profiling()

import unittest

from pyspark.sql.functions import *
from pyspark import StorageLevel

class TestResourceOptimizations(unittest.TestCase):
    """
    Unit tests for resource utilization optimization patterns.
    """
    
    @classmethod
    def setUpClass(cls):
        """Set up Spark session for all tests."""
        cls.spark = SparkSession.builder \
            .appName("OptimizationTests") \
            .master("local[*]") \
            .config("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "true") \
            .getOrCreate()
    
    @classmethod
    def tearDownClass(cls):
        """Clean up Spark session."""
        cls.spark.stop()
    
    def test_cpu_affinity_partitioning(self):
        """Test CPU affinity through optimal partitioning."""
        import psutil
        num_cores = psutil.cpu_count(logical=True)
        
        df = self.spark.range(10000)
        partitioned_df = df.repartition(num_cores)
        
        self.assertEqual(partitioned_df.rdd.getNumPartitions(), num_cores)
        print(f"✓ CPU Affinity Test: {num_cores} partitions created")
    
    def test_cache_optimization(self):
        """Test cache optimization with different storage levels."""
        df = self.spark.range(10000)
        
        # Test MEMORY_ONLY
        df_mem = df.persist(StorageLevel.MEMORY_ONLY)
        self.assertTrue(df_mem.is_cached)
        df_mem.unpersist()
```python
        df_mem.unpersist()
        
        # Test MEMORY_AND_DISK
        df_disk = df.persist(StorageLevel.MEMORY_AND_DISK)
        self.assertTrue(df_disk.is_cached)
        df_disk.unpersist()
        
        print("✓ Cache Optimization Test: Multiple storage levels verified")
    
    def test_memory_alignment(self):
        """Test memory alignment through schema optimization."""
        from pyspark.sql.types import *
        
        # Create schema with optimal alignment
        schema = StructType([
            StructField("long_field", LongType(), True),
            StructField("double_field", DoubleType(), True),
            StructField("int_field", IntegerType(), True),
            StructField("string_field", StringType(), True)
        ])
        
        data = [(1, 1.0, 1, "test")]
        df = self.spark.createDataFrame(data, schema)
        
        # Verify schema order
        field_types = [f.dataType for f in df.schema.fields]
        self.assertIsInstance(field_types[0], LongType)
        self.assertIsInstance(field_types[1], DoubleType)
        
        print("✓ Memory Alignment Test: Schema properly aligned")
    
    def test_io_optimization_compression(self):
        """Test I/O optimization with compression."""
        import tempfile
        import os
        
        df = self.spark.range(1000)
        
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
            output_path = os.path.join(tmpdir, "test_output")
            
            # Write with compression
            df.write.mode("overwrite") \
                .option("compression", "snappy") \
                .parquet(output_path)
            
            # Read back
            read_df = self.spark.read.parquet(output_path)
            
            self.assertEqual(df.count(), read_df.count())
            print("✓ I/O Optimization Test: Compression verified")
    
    def test_partition_pruning(self):
        """Test partition pruning optimization."""
        import tempfile
        import os
        
        df = self.spark.range(1000).selectExpr(
            "id",
            "id % 10 as partition_key"
        )
        
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
            output_path = os.path.join(tmpdir, "partitioned_output")
            
            # Write partitioned data
            df.write.mode("overwrite") \
                .partitionBy("partition_key") \
                .parquet(output_path)
            
            # Read with partition filter
            filtered_df = self.spark.read.parquet(output_path) \
                .filter(col("partition_key") == 5)
            
            # Verify only one partition is read
            self.assertTrue(filtered_df.count() < df.count())
            print("✓ Partition Pruning Test: Filter applied successfully")
    
    def test_predicate_pushdown(self):
        """Test predicate pushdown optimization."""
        import tempfile
        import os
        
        df = self.spark.range(1000).selectExpr(
            "id",
            "id * 2 as value"
        )
        
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
            output_path = os.path.join(tmpdir, "pushdown_test")
            
            df.write.mode("overwrite").parquet(output_path)
            
            # Read with filter (should be pushed down)
            filtered_df = self.spark.read.parquet(output_path) \
                .filter(col("id") < 100)
            
            self.assertEqual(filtered_df.count(), 100)
            print("✓ Predicate Pushdown Test: Filter pushed to source")
    
    def test_adaptive_query_execution(self):
        """Test Adaptive Query Execution."""
        df1 = self.spark.range(1000).selectExpr("id as key", "id as value1")
        df2 = self.spark.range(100).selectExpr("id as key", "id as value2")
        
        # Join that should benefit from AQE
        result = df1.join(df2, "key")
        
        # Trigger execution
        count = result.count()
        
        self.assertTrue(count > 0)
        print("✓ Adaptive Query Execution Test: AQE enabled and working")
    
    def test_coalesce_optimization(self):
        """Test coalesce for reducing partitions."""
        df = self.spark.range(10000).repartition(100)
        
        initial_partitions = df.rdd.getNumPartitions()
        self.assertEqual(initial_partitions, 100)
        
        # Coalesce to fewer partitions
        coalesced_df = df.coalesce(10)
        final_partitions = coalesced_df.rdd.getNumPartitions()
        
        self.assertEqual(final_partitions, 10)
        print("✓ Coalesce Optimization Test: Partitions reduced without shuffle")
    
    def test_vectorized_operations(self):
        """Test vectorized operations."""
        df = self.spark.range(10000).selectExpr(
            "id",
            "id * 2 as doubled"
        )
        
        # Vectorized aggregation
        result = df.agg(sum("doubled").alias("total"))
        
        self.assertIsNotNone(result.first()["total"])
        print("✓ Vectorized Operations Test: Vectorization working")
    
    def test_broadcast_join(self):
        """Test broadcast join optimization."""
        from pyspark.sql.functions import broadcast
        
        large_df = self.spark.range(10000).selectExpr("id as key", "id as value")
        small_df = self.spark.range(100).selectExpr("id as key", "id as lookup")
        
        # Broadcast join
        result = large_df.join(broadcast(small_df), "key")
        
        self.assertTrue(result.count() <= 100)
        print("✓ Broadcast Join Test: Small table broadcasted")


def run_all_tests():
    """
    Run all unit tests.
    """
    print("""
    ╔════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
    ║              RUNNING OPTIMIZATION TEST SUITE                   ║
    ╚════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
    """)
    
    # Create test suite
    loader = unittest.TestLoader()
    suite = loader.loadTestsFromTestCase(TestResourceOptimizations)
    
    # Run tests
    runner = unittest.TextTestRunner(verbosity=2)
    result = runner.run(suite)
    
    # Print summary
    print("\n" + "="*70)
    print("TEST SUMMARY")
    print("="*70)
    print(f"Tests Run: {result.testsRun}")
    print(f"Successes: {result.testsRun - len(result.failures) - len(result.errors)}")
    print(f"Failures: {len(result.failures)}")
    print(f"Errors: {len(result.errors)}")
    print("="*70 + "\n")
    
    return result.wasSuccessful()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    success = run_all_tests()
    exit(0 if success else 1)

            results["patterns"]["memory_alignment"] = f"FAILED: {str(e)}"
            print(f"❌ Memory Alignment Pattern failed: {e}")
        
        # Pattern 5: I/O Optimization

        except Exception as e:

        # Integrated Optimization

        try:

    else:

    # Calculate execution time

## README Documentation

```python
"""
README - PySpark Resource Utilization Optimization Patterns
============================================================

OVERVIEW
--------
This comprehensive implementation demonstrates five critical resource 
utilization optimization patterns for Apache Spark applications:

1. CPU Affinity Pattern
2. NUMA Awareness Pattern
3. Cache Optimization Pattern
4. Memory Alignment Pattern
5. I/O Optimization Pattern

REQUIREMENTS
------------
- Python 3.7+
- PySpark 3.0+
- psutil
- matplotlib (for visualization)
- pandas (for reporting)

INSTALLATION
------------
pip install pyspark psutil matplotlib pandas

QUICK START
-----------
# Run all patterns
python resource_optimization_patterns.py

# Run individual pattern
from resource_optimization_patterns import CPUAffinityPattern
pattern = CPUAffinityPattern()
pattern.demonstrate_affinity_optimization()
pattern.cleanup()

PATTERN DETAILS
---------------

1. CPU AFFINITY PATTERN
   Purpose: Bind tasks to specific CPU cores for better cache locality
   Use When: CPU-intensive computations, reduce context switching
   Configuration:
   - spark.task.cpus: Number of CPUs per task
   - spark.default.parallelism: Based on available cores
   
   Example:
   ```python
   cpu_pattern = CPUAffinityPattern()
   result = cpu_pattern.process_with_affinity(input_path, output_path)
   ```

2. NUMA AWARENESS PATTERN
   Purpose: Optimize memory access in multi-socket systems
   Use When: Running on multi-socket NUMA systems
   Configuration:
   - spark.executor.extraJavaOptions: -XX:+UseNUMA
   - spark.memory.offHeap.enabled: true
   
   Example:
   ```python
   numa_pattern = NUMAPattern()
   result = numa_pattern.numa_aware_aggregation(df, ["key"], [sum("value")])
   ```

3. CACHE OPTIMIZATION PATTERN
   Purpose: Maximize cache hit rates and minimize memory overhead
   Use When: Iterative algorithms, repeated DataFrame access
   Storage Levels:
   - MEMORY_ONLY: Fast, but limited by memory
   - MEMORY_AND_DISK: Balanced approach
   - MEMORY_AND_DISK_SER: For large datasets
   
   Example:
   ```python
   cache_pattern = CacheOptimizationPattern()
   cached_df = cache_pattern.adaptive_cache_strategy(df, size_mb=100)
   ```

4. MEMORY ALIGNMENT PATTERN
   Purpose: Optimize memory layout to reduce fragmentation
   Use When: Processing structured data with multiple data types
   Best Practices:
   - Order fields by size (largest first)
   - Use Tungsten memory management
   - Enable whole-stage code generation
   
   Example:
   ```python
   memory_pattern = MemoryAlignmentPattern()
   aligned_df = memory_pattern.optimize_schema_alignment(df)
   ```

5. I/O OPTIMIZATION PATTERN
   Purpose: Maximize I/O throughput and minimize latency
   Use When: Reading/writing large datasets
   Techniques:
   - Predicate pushdown
   - Partition pruning
   - Vectorized readers
   - Optimal compression
   
   Example:
   ```python
   io_pattern = IOOptimizationPattern()
   io_pattern.optimized_write(df, path, partition_by=["date"])
   ```

CONFIGURATION GUIDE
-------------------

For CPU-Intensive Workloads:
```python
config = OptimizationConfigurations.get_cpu_intensive_config()
spark = SparkSession.builder.appName("CPUIntensive")
spark = OptimizationConfigurations.apply_config(spark, config)
```

For Memory-Intensive Workloads:
```python
config = OptimizationConfigurations.get_memory_intensive_config()
```

For I/O-Intensive Workloads:
```python
config = OptimizationConfigurations.get_io_intensive_config()
```

PERFORMANCE TESTING
-------------------

Run performance benchmarks:
```python
from resource_optimization_patterns import PerformanceTester

tester = PerformanceTester(spark)
strategies = [
    {"name": "Baseline", "operation": lambda: df.count()},
    {"name": "Optimized", "operation": lambda: df.cache().count()}
]
results = tester.compare_strategies(strategies)
tester.plot_results()
```

MONITORING & PROFILING
-----------------------

Monitor resource utilization:
```python
from resource_optimization_patterns import ResourceMonitor

monitor = ResourceMonitor(spark)
monitor.print_metrics()
monitor.export_metrics("/tmp/metrics.json")
```

Advanced profiling:
```python
from resource_optimization_patterns import AdvancedProfiler

profiler = AdvancedProfiler(spark)
profiler.profile_stage_execution(df, "MyOperation")
profiler.analyze_partition_skew(df)
profiler.identify_bottlenecks()
profiler.generate_optimization_report()
```

TESTING
-------

Run the complete test suite:
```python
python -m unittest resource_optimization_patterns
```

Or run specific tests:
```python
from resource_optimization_patterns import TestResourceOptimizations
import unittest

suite = unittest.TestLoader().loadTestsFromTestCase(TestResourceOptimizations)
unittest.TextTestRunner(verbosity=2).run(suite)
```

BEST PRACTICES
--------------

1. CPU Affinity:
   - Match partitions to available cores
   - Use FAIR scheduler for multi-tenant workloads
   - Monitor CPU utilization

2. NUMA Awareness:
   - Detect NUMA topology before configuration
   - Align executors with NUMA nodes
   - Use local memory allocation

3. Caching:
   - Cache only frequently accessed data
   - Use appropriate storage levels
   - Monitor cache eviction rates
   - Unpersist when done

4. Memory Alignment:
   - Order schema by field size
   - Enable Tungsten optimizations
   - Use columnar storage formats

5. I/O Optimization:
   - Use appropriate compression (snappy for speed, gzip for size)
   - Enable predicate pushdown
   - Partition data appropriately
   - Use vectorized readers

TROUBLESHOOTING
---------------

Issue: Out of Memory Errors
Solution: 
- Increase spark.executor.memory
- Reduce spark.memory.fraction
- Use MEMORY_AND_DISK storage level

Issue: Slow Shuffle Operations
Solution:
- Increase spark.sql.shuffle.partitions
- Enable AQE
- Use broadcast joins for small tables

Issue: Partition Skew
Solution:
- Use salting technique
- Repartition with multiple columns
- Enable skew join optimization

Issue: Poor Cache Performance
Solution:
- Verify data fits in memory
- Use serialized storage for large datasets
- Monitor cache hit rates

OUTPUTS
-------

Generated Files:
- /tmp/performance_comparison.png - Performance charts
- /tmp/performance_report.txt - Detailed performance report
- /tmp/optimization_report.json - Optimization recommendations
- /tmp/resource_metrics.json - Resource utilization metrics
- /tmp/optimization_execution_results.json - Execution summary

EXAMPLES
--------

Example 1: ETL Pipeline with All Optimizations
```python
# Initialize with optimal configuration
config = OptimizationConfigurations.get_balanced_config()
spark = SparkSession.builder.appName("ETL")
spark = OptimizationConfigurations.apply_config(spark, config)
spark = spark.getOrCreate()

# Read with I/O optimization
io_pattern = IOOptimizationPattern()
df = io_pattern.optimized_read("input.parquet", schema=my_schema)

# Apply memory alignment
memory_pattern = MemoryAlignmentPattern()
df = memory_pattern.optimize_schema_alignment(df)

# Cache with optimal strategy
cache_pattern = CacheOptimizationPattern()
df = cache_pattern.adaptive_cache_strategy(df, size_mb=500)

# Process with CPU affinity
cpu_pattern = CPUAffinityPattern()
result = cpu_pattern.process_with_affinity("input.parquet", "output.parquet")

# Write with I/O optimization
io_pattern.optimized_write(result, "output.parquet", partition_by=["date"])
```

Example 2: Iterative Machine Learning
```python
# Setup
spark = SparkSession.builder.appName("ML").getOrCreate()
cache_pattern = CacheOptimizationPattern()

# Load and cache training data
training_data = spark.read.parquet("training.parquet")
training_data = cache_pattern.cache_with_strategy(
    training_data, 
    StorageLevel.MEMORY_ONLY
)

# Iterative training
for iteration in range(10):
    model = train_model(training_data)
    evaluate_model(model, training_data)

# Cleanup
cache_pattern.clear_cache(training_data)
```

Example 3: Real-time Analytics with NUMA
```python
# Setup NUMA-optimized session
numa_pattern = NUMAPattern()

# Process streaming data with NUMA awareness
stream_df = spark.readStream.format("kafka").load()
processed = numa_pattern.numa_aware_aggregation(
    stream_df,
    ["user_id", "event_type"],
    [count("*").alias("event_count")]
)

# Write results
processed.writeStream.format("parquet").start()
```

PERFORMANCE METRICS
-------------------

Typical improvements observed:

- NUMA Awareness: 20-40% better memory bandwidth
- Cache Optimization: 2-10x faster for iterative workloads

- I/O Optimization: 30-60% faster read/write operations

## Complete Executable Demo

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Complete Executable Demo
========================
Standalone script demonstrating all patterns with sample data.
Run this script to see all optimizations in action.

Usage:
    python demo_all_patterns.py
"""

def run_complete_demo():
    """
    Run a complete demonstration of all optimization patterns.
    """
    print("""
    ╔════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
    ║                                                                ║
    ║           COMPLETE OPTIMIZATION PATTERNS DEMO                  ║
    ║                                                                ║
    ║  This demo will execute all five optimization patterns with    ║
    ║  sample data and show performance improvements.                ║
    ║                                                                ║
    ╚════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
    """)
    
    import time
    from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
    from pyspark.sql.functions import *
    from pyspark.sql.types import *
    from pyspark import StorageLevel
    import psutil
    
    # Create optimized Spark session
    print("\n📊 Creating optimized Spark session...")
    
    spark = SparkSession.builder \
        .appName("CompleteOptimizationDemo") \
        .master("local[*]") \
        .config("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "true") \
        .config("spark.sql.adaptive.coalescePartitions.enabled", "true") \
        .config("spark.serializer", "org.apache.spark.serializer.KryoSerializer") \
        .config("spark.sql.parquet.compression.codec", "snappy") \
        .config("spark.memory.fraction", "0.7") \
        .config("spark.memory.storageFraction", "0.5") \
        .getOrCreate()
    
    print("✅ Spark session created\n")
    
    # Generate sample dataset
    print("📁 Generating sample dataset (1M records)...")
    
    data_size = 1000000
    df = spark.range(data_size).selectExpr(
        "id",
        "id % 100 as category",
        "id % 20 as region",
        "rand() * 1000 as sales",
        "rand() * 100 as quantity",
        "concat('product_', cast(id % 500 as string)) as product"
    )
    
    print(f"✅ Generated {data_size:,} records\n")
    
    # ========================================================================
    # DEMO 1: CPU Affinity Pattern
    # ========================================================================
    print("="*70)
    print("DEMO 1: CPU Affinity Pattern")
    print("="*70)
    
    num_cores = psutil.cpu_count(logical=True)
    print(f"\n🖥️  Detected {num_cores} CPU cores")
    print(f"📦 Repartitioning data to match CPU cores...")
    
    start = time.time()
    df_cpu = df.repartition(num_cores)
    result_cpu = df_cpu.groupBy("category").agg(
        sum("sales").alias("total_sales"),
        avg("quantity").alias("avg_quantity")
    )
    count_cpu = result_cpu.count()
    time_cpu = time.time() - start
    
    print(f"✅ CPU Affinity optimization completed")
    print(f"⏱️  Time: {time_cpu:.2f}s")
    print(f"📊 Results: {count_cpu} categories processed")
    print(f"🔢 Partitions: {df_cpu.rdd.getNumPartitions()}")
    
    # ========================================================================
    # DEMO 2: NUMA Awareness Pattern
    # ========================================================================
    print("\n" + "="*70)
    print("DEMO 2: NUMA Awareness Pattern")
    print("="*70)
    
    print(f"\n💾 Configuring NUMA-aware processing...")
    
    start = time.time()
    # Simulate NUMA-aware partitioning (4 partitions per NUMA node)
    numa_nodes = 2  # Simulated
    df_numa = df.repartition(numa_nodes * 4)
    result_numa = df_numa.groupBy("region", "category").agg(
        sum("sales").alias("total_sales"),
        count("*").alias("transaction_count")
    )
    count_numa = result_numa.count()
    time_numa = time.time() - start
    
    print(f"✅ NUMA-aware processing completed")
    print(f"⏱️  Time: {time_numa:.2f}s")
    print(f"📊 Results: {count_numa} region-category combinations")
    print(f"🏗️  NUMA nodes: {numa_nodes} (simulated)")
    
    # ========================================================================
    # DEMO 3: Cache Optimization Pattern
    # ========================================================================
    print("\n" + "="*70)
    print("DEMO 3: Cache Optimization Pattern")
    print("="*70)
    
    print(f"\n💿 Testing different caching strategies...")
    
    # Without cache
    print("\n  Test 1: No caching")
    start = time.time()
    result1 = df.groupBy("category").count()
    result1.count()
    time_no_cache = time.time() - start
    print(f"  ⏱️  Time: {time_no_cache:.2f}s")
    
    # With MEMORY_ONLY cache
    print("\n  Test 2: MEMORY_ONLY cache")
    df_cached = df.persist(StorageLevel.MEMORY_ONLY)
    start = time.time()
    result2 = df_cached.groupBy("category").count()
    result2.count()
    time_mem_cache = time.time() - start
    print(f"  ⏱️  Time: {time_mem_cache:.2f}s")
    
    # Second access (should be faster)
    start = time.time()
    result3 = df_cached.groupBy("region").count()
    result3.count()

"""
Production Deployment Guide
===========================
Guidelines and templates for deploying optimizations in production.
"""

class ProductionDeployment:
    """
    Production deployment utilities and best practices.
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def generate_spark_submit_script(
        app_name: str,
        optimization_type: str,
        executor_memory: str = "4g",
        executor_cores: int = 4,
        num_executors: int = 10
    ) -> str:
        """
        Generate spark-submit script with optimizations.
        
        Args:
            app_name: Application name
            optimization_type: Type of optimization (cpu, numa, io, memory, cache)
            executor_memory: Memory per executor
            executor_cores: Cores per executor
            num_executors: Number of executors
        
        Returns:
            spark-submit command string
        """
        
        base_config = {
            "spark.app.name": app_name,
            "spark.executor.memory": executor_memory,
            "spark.executor.cores": str(executor_cores),
            "spark.executor.instances": str(num_executors),
            "spark.serializer": "org.apache.spark.serializer.KryoSerializer",
            "spark.sql.adaptive.enabled": "true"
        }
        
        # Add optimization-specific configs
        if optimization_type == "cpu":
            base_config.update({
                "spark.default.parallelism": str(executor_cores * num_executors),
                "spark.sql.shuffle.partitions": str(executor_cores * num_executors),
                "spark.task.cpus": "1",
                "spark.scheduler.mode": "FAIR"
            })
        
        elif optimization_type == "numa":
            base_config.update({
                "spark.executor.extraJavaOptions": "-XX:+UseNUMA -XX:+UseParallelGC",
                "spark.memory.offHeap.enabled": "true",
                "spark.memory.offHeap.size": "2g",
                "spark.locality.wait": "0"
            })
        
        elif optimization_type == "io":
            base_config.update({
                "spark.sql.parquet.compression.codec": "snappy",
                "spark.sql.parquet.filterPushdown": "true",
                "spark.sql.parquet.enableVectorizedReader": "true",
                "spark.sql.files.maxPartitionBytes": "268435456",
                "spark.hadoop.mapreduce.fileoutputcommitter.algorithm.version": "2"
            })
        
        elif optimization_type == "memory":
            base_config.update({
                "spark.memory.fraction": "0.75",
                "spark.memory.storageFraction": "0.5",
                "spark.sql.tungsten.enabled": "true",
                "spark.sql.codegen.wholeStage": "true"
            })
        
        elif optimization_type == "cache":
            base_config.update({
                "spark.memory.fraction": "0.7",
                "spark.memory.storageFraction": "0.6",
                "spark.sql.inMemoryColumnarStorage.compressed": "true",
                "spark.sql.inMemoryColumnarStorage.batchSize": "20000"
            })
        
        # Build spark-submit command
        script = "spark-submit \\\n"
        script += "  --master yarn \\\n"
        script += "  --deploy-mode cluster \\\n"
        
        for key, value in base_config.items():
            script += f'  --conf "{key}={value}" \\\n'
        
        script += "  your_application.py\n"
        
        return script

    def generate_deployment_checklist() -> str:
