```python
# ============================================================================
# EXTENDED EXAMPLES AND ADVANCED PATTERNS
# ============================================================================

def global_window_pattern():
    """
    BONUS PATTERN: Global Window Pattern
    Processes all data as a single unbounded window
    Use Case: Running aggregations, global counters
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("BONUS PATTERN: GLOBAL WINDOW PATTERN")
    print("="*80)
    
    # Create streaming DataFrame
    stream_df = spark \
        .readStream \
        .format("rate") \
        .option("rowsPerSecond", 5) \
        .load() \
        .select(
            (col("value") % 10).cast("string").alias("category"),
            col("timestamp").alias("event_time"),
            (rand() * 100).alias("metric_value")
        )
    
    # Global aggregation without windowing
    # This maintains state for all time
    global_agg = stream_df \
        .groupBy("category") \
        .agg(
            count("*").alias("total_count"),
            sum("metric_value").alias("total_sum"),
            avg("metric_value").alias("avg_value"),
            min("metric_value").alias("min_value"),
            max("metric_value").alias("max_value")
        ) \
        .withColumn("last_updated", current_timestamp())
    
    # Write with update mode (only changed aggregates)
    query = global_agg \
        .writeStream \
        .outputMode("update") \
        .format("console") \
        .option("truncate", "false") \
        .queryName("global_window") \
        .start()
    
    return query


def multi_stream_join_pattern():
    """
    ADVANCED PATTERN: Multi-Stream Join with Windows
    Joins multiple streams with different windowing strategies
    Use Case: Correlating events from different sources
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("ADVANCED PATTERN: MULTI-STREAM JOIN WITH WINDOWS")
    print("="*80)
    
    # Stream 1: User clicks
    clicks_stream = spark \
        .readStream \
        .format("rate") \
        .option("rowsPerSecond", 10) \
        .load() \
        .select(
            (col("value") % 100).cast("string").alias("user_id"),
            col("timestamp").alias("click_time"),
            (col("value") % 50).cast("string").alias("page_id")
        ) \
        .withColumn("click_id", monotonically_increasing_id())
    
    # Stream 2: User purchases
    purchases_stream = spark \
        .readStream \
        .format("rate") \
        .option("rowsPerSecond", 2) \
        .load() \
        .select(
            (col("value") % 100).cast("string").alias("user_id"),
            col("timestamp").alias("purchase_time"),
            (rand() * 500).alias("amount")
        ) \
        .withColumn("purchase_id", monotonically_increasing_id())
    
    # Join streams with time constraints
    # Join clicks and purchases that occur within 10 minutes
    joined_stream = clicks_stream \
        .withWatermark("click_time", "15 minutes") \
        .join(
            purchases_stream.withWatermark("purchase_time", "15 minutes"),
            expr("""
                user_id = user_id AND
                purchase_time >= click_time AND
                purchase_time <= click_time + interval 10 minutes
            """),
            "leftOuter"
        )
    
    # Analyze conversion within windows
    conversion_analysis = joined_stream \
        .groupBy(
            window(col("click_time"), "5 minutes"),
            col("page_id")
        ) \
        .agg(
            count("click_id").alias("total_clicks"),
            count("purchase_id").alias("conversions"),
            sum("amount").alias("revenue")
        ) \
        .select(
            col("window.start").alias("window_start"),
            col("window.end").alias("window_end"),
            col("page_id"),
            col("total_clicks"),
            col("conversions"),
            round(col("revenue"), 2).alias("revenue"),
            round((col("conversions") / col("total_clicks") * 100), 2).alias("conversion_rate")
        )
    
    query = conversion_analysis \
        .writeStream \
        .outputMode("append") \
        .format("console") \
        .option("truncate", "false") \
        .queryName("multi_stream_join") \
        .start()
    
    return query


def late_data_handling_pattern():
    """
    ADVANCED PATTERN: Late Data Handling with Multiple Watermarks
    Demonstrates sophisticated late data handling strategies
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("ADVANCED PATTERN: LATE DATA HANDLING")
    print("="*80)
    
    # Create stream with intentional late data
    stream_df = spark \
        .readStream \
        .format("rate") \
        .option("rowsPerSecond", 10) \
        .load() \
        .select(
            (col("value") % 20).cast("string").alias("sensor_id"),
            # Simulate late data by subtracting random delays
            (col("timestamp").cast("long") - (rand() * 300).cast("long")).cast("timestamp").alias("event_time"),
            (rand() * 100).alias("reading")
        )
    
    # Strategy 1: Aggressive watermark (drop late data quickly)
    aggressive_watermark = stream_df \
        .withWatermark("event_time", "30 seconds") \
        .groupBy(
            window(col("event_time"), "1 minute"),
            col("sensor_id")
        ) \
        .agg(
            count("*").alias("count"),
            avg("reading").alias("avg_reading")
        ) \
        .select(
            col("window.start").alias("window_start"),
            col("window.end").alias("window_end"),
            col("sensor_id"),
            col("count"),
            round(col("avg_reading"), 2).alias("avg_reading")
        ) \
        .withColumn("watermark_strategy", lit("aggressive_30s"))
    
    # Strategy 2: Lenient watermark (accept more late data)
    lenient_watermark = stream_df \
        .withWatermark("event_time", "5 minutes") \
        .groupBy(
            window(col("event_time"), "1 minute"),
            col("sensor_id")
        ) \
        .agg(
            count("*").alias("count"),
            avg("reading").alias("avg_reading")
        ) \
        .select(
            col("window.start").alias("window_start"),
            col("window.end").alias("window_end"),
            col("sensor_id"),
            col("count"),
            round(col("avg_reading"), 2).alias("avg_reading")
        ) \
        .withColumn("watermark_strategy", lit("lenient_5m"))
    
    # Track dropped vs accepted late data
    late_data_stats = stream_df \
        .withColumn("processing_time", current_timestamp()) \
        .withColumn("latency_seconds", 
                   unix_timestamp("processing_time") - unix_timestamp("event_time")) \
        .withColumn("is_late",
            when(col("latency_seconds") > 30, "late")
            .when(col("latency_seconds") > 300, "very_late")
            .otherwise("on_time")
        ) \
        .groupBy(
            window(current_timestamp(), "1 minute"),
            col("is_late")
        ) \
        .agg(count("*").alias("record_count"))
    
    query_aggressive = aggressive_watermark \
        .writeStream \
        .outputMode("append") \
        .format("memory") \
        .queryName("aggressive_watermark") \
        .start()
    
    query_lenient = lenient_watermark \
        .writeStream \
        .outputMode("append") \
        .format("memory") \
        .queryName("lenient_watermark") \
        .start()
    
    query_stats = late_data_stats \
        .writeStream \
        .outputMode("update") \
        .format("console") \
        .option("truncate", "false") \
        .queryName("late_data_stats") \
        .start()
    
    return query_aggressive, query_lenient, query_stats


def stateful_aggregation_pattern():
    """
    ADVANCED PATTERN: Stateful Aggregation with Custom State Management
    Uses mapGroupsWithState for complex stateful operations
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("ADVANCED PATTERN: STATEFUL AGGREGATION")
    print("="*80)
    
    from pyspark.sql.streaming import GroupState, GroupStateTimeout
    
    # Define state schema
    state_schema = StructType([
        StructField("user_id", StringType()),
        StructField("total_events", IntegerType()),
        StructField("total_value", DoubleType()),
        StructField("last_event_time", TimestampType()),
        StructField("session_count", IntegerType())
    ])
    
    # Create input stream
    events_df = spark \
        .readStream \
        .format("rate") \
        .option("rowsPerSecond", 5) \
        .load() \
        .select(
            (col("value") % 10).cast("string").alias("user_id"),
            col("timestamp").alias("event_time"),
            (rand() * 100).alias("value")
        )
    
    # Note: mapGroupsWithState requires Scala/Java UDF in PySpark
    # Alternative approach using structured operations
    user_window = Window.partitionBy("user_id").orderBy("event_time")
    
    stateful_df = events_df \
        .withWatermark("event_time", "10 minutes") \
        .withColumn("prev_event_time", lag("event_time", 1).over(user_window)) \
        .withColumn("time_gap",
            when(col("prev_event_time").isNotNull(),
                 unix_timestamp("event_time") - unix_timestamp("prev_event_time"))
            .otherwise(0)
        ) \
        .withColumn("new_session", when(col("time_gap") > 300, 1).otherwise(0)) \
        .withColumn("session_num", sum("new_session").over(
            user_window.rowsBetween(Window.unboundedPreceding, Window.currentRow)
        )) \
        .groupBy("user_id", "session_num") \
        .agg(
            count("*").alias("events_in_session"),
            sum("value").alias("total_value"),
            min("event_time").alias("session_start"),
            max("event_time").alias("session_end")
        ) \
        .withColumn("session_duration",
            unix_timestamp("session_end") - unix_timestamp("session_start")
        )
    
    # Running totals across sessions
    user_totals_window = Window.partitionBy("user_id").orderBy("session_start")
    
    running_totals = stateful_df \
        .withColumn("total_events_so_far",
            sum("events_in_session").over(
                user_totals_window.rowsBetween(Window.unboundedPreceding, Window.currentRow)
            )
        ) \
        .withColumn("total_value_so_far",
            sum("total_value").over(
                user_totals_window.rowsBetween(Window.unboundedPreceding, Window.currentRow)
            )
        ) \
        .withColumn("avg_session_duration",
            avg("session_duration").over(
                user_totals_window.rowsBetween(Window.unboundedPreceding, Window.currentRow)
            )
        )
    
    query = running_totals \
        .writeStream \
        .outputMode("update") \
        .format("console") \
        .option("truncate", "false") \
        .queryName("stateful_aggregation") \
        .start()
    
    return query


def hierarchical_window_pattern():
    """
    ADVANCED PATTERN: Hierarchical Windowing
    Multiple levels of aggregation from fine to coarse granularity
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("ADVANCED PATTERN: HIERARCHICAL WINDOWING")
    print("="*80)
    
    # Base event stream
    events = spark \
        .readStream \
        .format("rate") \
        .option("rowsPerSecond", 100) \
        .load() \
        .select(
            (col("value") % 5).cast("string").alias("region"),
            (col("value") % 20).cast("string").alias("product"),
            col("timestamp").alias("event_time"),
            (rand() * 100).alias("sales_amount")
        )
    
    # Level 1: Second-level aggregation
    second_level = events \
        .withWatermark("event_time", "2 minutes") \
        .groupBy(
            window(col("event_time"), "1 second"),
            col("region"),
            col("product")
        ) \
        .agg(
            count("*").alias("txn_count"),
            sum("sales_amount").alias("sales")
        )
    
    # Level 2: Minute-level aggregation (from second-level)
    minute_level = second_level \
        .groupBy(
            window(col("window.start"), "1 minute"),
            col("region"),
            col("product")
        ) \
        .agg(
            sum("txn_count").alias("txn_count"),
            sum("sales").alias("sales"),
            avg("sales").alias("avg_sales_per_second")
        )
    
    # Level 3: Hour-level aggregation (from minute-level)
    hour_level = minute_level \
        .groupBy(
            window(col("window.start"), "1 hour"),
            col("region")
        ) \
        .agg(
            sum("txn_count").alias("total_txn"),
            sum("sales").alias("total_sales"),
            avg("sales").alias("avg_sales_per_minute"),
            countDistinct("product").alias("unique_products")
        )
    
    # Level 4: Daily aggregation (from hour-level)
    daily_level = hour_level \
        .groupBy(
            window(col("window.start"), "1 day"),
            col("region")
        ) \
        .agg(
            sum("total_txn").alias("daily_txn"),
            sum("total_sales").alias("daily_sales"),
            avg("total_sales").alias("avg_sales_per_hour"),
            max("total_sales").alias("peak_hour_sales")
        ) \
        .select(
            col("window.start").alias("day"),
            col("region"),
            col("daily_txn"),
            round(col("daily_sales"), 2).alias("daily_sales"),
            round(col("avg_sales_per_hour"), 2).alias("avg_hourly_sales"),
            round(col("peak_hour_sales"), 2).alias("peak_hour_sales")
        )
    
    # Start queries at different levels
    query_minute = minute_level \
        .select(
            col("window.start").alias("minute"),
            col("region"),
            col("product"),
            col("txn_count"),
            round(col("sales"), 2).
```python
            round(col("sales"), 2).alias("sales")
        ) \
        .writeStream \
        .outputMode("append") \
        .format("memory") \
        .queryName("minute_aggregation") \
        .start()
    
    query_hour = hour_level \
        .select(
            col("window.start").alias("hour"),
            col("region"),
            col("total_txn"),
            round(col("total_sales"), 2).alias("total_sales"),
            col("unique_products")
        ) \
        .writeStream \
        .outputMode("append") \
        .format("console") \
        .option("truncate", "false") \
        .queryName("hour_aggregation") \
        .start()
    
    query_daily = daily_level \
        .writeStream \
        .outputMode("append") \
        .format("console") \
        .option("truncate", "false") \
        .queryName("daily_aggregation") \
        .start()
    
    return query_minute, query_hour, query_daily


def percentile_window_pattern():
    """
    ADVANCED PATTERN: Percentile and Statistical Windowing
    Calculates percentiles and statistical measures over windows
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("ADVANCED PATTERN: PERCENTILE & STATISTICAL WINDOWING")
    print("="*80)
    
    # Create stream with latency data
    latency_stream = spark \
        .readStream \
        .format("rate") \
        .option("rowsPerSecond", 50) \
        .load() \
        .select(
            (col("value") % 10).cast("string").alias("service_id"),
            col("timestamp").alias("request_time"),
            # Simulate latency with some outliers
            when(rand() > 0.95, rand() * 5000)  # 5% outliers
            .otherwise(rand() * 200 + 50).alias("latency_ms")
        )
    
    # Calculate percentiles and statistics
    stats_window = latency_stream \
        .withWatermark("request_time", "5 minutes") \
        .groupBy(
            window(col("request_time"), "1 minute"),
            col("service_id")
        ) \
        .agg(
            count("*").alias("request_count"),
            avg("latency_ms").alias("mean_latency"),
            stddev("latency_ms").alias("stddev_latency"),
            min("latency_ms").alias("min_latency"),
            max("latency_ms").alias("max_latency"),
            # Approximate percentiles
            expr("percentile_approx(latency_ms, 0.50)").alias("p50_latency"),
            expr("percentile_approx(latency_ms, 0.75)").alias("p75_latency"),
            expr("percentile_approx(latency_ms, 0.90)").alias("p90_latency"),
            expr("percentile_approx(latency_ms, 0.95)").alias("p95_latency"),
            expr("percentile_approx(latency_ms, 0.99)").alias("p99_latency")
        ) \
        .select(
            col("window.start").alias("window_start"),
            col("window.end").alias("window_end"),
            col("service_id"),
            col("request_count"),
            round(col("mean_latency"), 2).alias("mean_ms"),
            round(col("stddev_latency"), 2).alias("stddev_ms"),
            round(col("min_latency"), 2).alias("min_ms"),
            round(col("max_latency"), 2).alias("max_ms"),
            round(col("p50_latency"), 2).alias("p50_ms"),
            round(col("p75_latency"), 2).alias("p75_ms"),
            round(col("p90_latency"), 2).alias("p90_ms"),
            round(col("p95_latency"), 2).alias("p95_ms"),
            round(col("p99_latency"), 2).alias("p99_ms")
        )
    
    # SLA violation detection
    sla_violations = stats_window \
        .withColumn("sla_threshold_ms", lit(100.0)) \
        .withColumn("p95_violation", col("p95_ms") > col("sla_threshold_ms")) \
        .withColumn("p99_violation", col("p99_ms") > col("sla_threshold_ms")) \
        .withColumn("mean_violation", col("mean_ms") > col("sla_threshold_ms")) \
        .withColumn("violation_severity",
            when(col("p99_violation"), "CRITICAL")
            .when(col("p95_violation"), "WARNING")
            .when(col("mean_violation"), "INFO")
            .otherwise("OK")
        ) \
        .filter(col("violation_severity") != "OK")
    
    query_stats = stats_window \
        .writeStream \
        .outputMode("append") \
        .format("console") \
        .option("truncate", "false") \
        .queryName("percentile_stats") \
        .start()
    
    query_violations = sla_violations \
        .writeStream \
        .outputMode("append") \
        .format("console") \
        .option("truncate", "false") \
        .queryName("sla_violations") \
        .start()
    
    return query_stats, query_violations


def adaptive_window_pattern():
    """
    ADVANCED PATTERN: Adaptive Window Sizing
    Dynamically adjusts window size based on data characteristics
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("ADVANCED PATTERN: ADAPTIVE WINDOW SIZING")
    print("="*80)
    
    # Create stream with varying velocity
    stream_df = spark \
        .readStream \
        .format("rate") \
        .option("rowsPerSecond", 20) \
        .load() \
        .select(
            (col("value") % 10).cast("string").alias("stream_id"),
            col("timestamp").alias("event_time"),
            (rand() * 100).alias("value")
        )
    
    # Calculate velocity (events per second) in micro-windows
    velocity_calc = stream_df \
        .withWatermark("event_time", "2 minutes") \
        .groupBy(
            window(col("event_time"), "5 seconds"),
            col("stream_id")
        ) \
        .agg(count("*").alias("event_count")) \
        .withColumn("events_per_second", col("event_count") / 5)
    
    # Classify velocity and recommend window size
    adaptive_windows = velocity_calc \
        .withColumn("velocity_class",
            when(col("events_per_second") > 50, "high")
            .when(col("events_per_second") > 20, "medium")
            .otherwise("low")
        ) \
        .withColumn("recommended_window_seconds",
            when(col("velocity_class") == "high", 10)
            .when(col("velocity_class") == "medium", 30)
            .otherwise(60)
        ) \
        .select(
            col("window.start").alias("measurement_start"),
            col("window.end").alias("measurement_end"),
            col("stream_id"),
            col("event_count"),
            round(col("events_per_second"), 2).alias("events_per_second"),
            col("velocity_class"),
            col("recommended_window_seconds")
        )
    
    # Apply different window sizes based on velocity
    # Small windows for high-velocity streams
    high_velocity = stream_df \
        .withWatermark("event_time", "1 minute") \
        .groupBy(
            window(col("event_time"), "10 seconds"),
            col("stream_id")
        ) \
        .agg(
            count("*").alias("count"),
            avg("value").alias("avg_value")
        ) \
        .withColumn("window_type", lit("adaptive_10s"))
    
    # Medium windows for medium-velocity streams
    medium_velocity = stream_df \
        .withWatermark("event_time", "2 minutes") \
        .groupBy(
            window(col("event_time"), "30 seconds"),
            col("stream_id")
        ) \
        .agg(
            count("*").alias("count"),
            avg("value").alias("avg_value")
        ) \
        .withColumn("window_type", lit("adaptive_30s"))
    
    # Large windows for low-velocity streams
    low_velocity = stream_df \
        .withWatermark("event_time", "5 minutes") \
        .groupBy(
            window(col("event_time"), "1 minute"),
            col("stream_id")
        ) \
        .agg(
            count("*").alias("count"),
            avg("value").alias("avg_value")
        ) \
        .withColumn("window_type", lit("adaptive_60s"))
    
    query_velocity = adaptive_windows \
        .writeStream \
        .outputMode("append") \
        .format("console") \
        .option("truncate", "false") \
        .queryName("velocity_monitor") \
        .start()
    
    return query_velocity


def deduplication_window_pattern():
    """
    ADVANCED PATTERN: Deduplication with Windowing
    Removes duplicates within time windows
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("ADVANCED PATTERN: DEDUPLICATION WITH WINDOWING")
    print("="*80)
    
    # Create stream with potential duplicates
    stream_with_dupes = spark \
        .readStream \
        .format("rate") \
        .option("rowsPerSecond", 10) \
        .load() \
        .select(
            (col("value") % 50).cast("string").alias("event_id"),
            (col("value") % 5).cast("string").alias("user_id"),
            col("timestamp").alias("event_time"),
            (rand() * 100).alias("amount")
        )
    
    # Method 1: Deduplication within tumbling windows
    deduped_tumbling = stream_with_dupes \
        .withWatermark("event_time", "10 minutes") \
        .dropDuplicates(["event_id", "user_id"]) \
        .groupBy(
            window(col("event_time"), "1 minute"),
            col("user_id")
        ) \
        .agg(
            count("*").alias("unique_events"),
            sum("amount").alias("total_amount")
        ) \
        .select(
            col("window.start").alias("window_start"),
            col("window.end").alias("window_end"),
            col("user_id"),
            col("unique_events"),
            round(col("total_amount"), 2).alias("total_amount")
        ) \
        .withColumn("dedup_method", lit("tumbling_window"))
    
    # Method 2: Deduplication with event time constraints
    window_spec = Window.partitionBy("event_id", "user_id") \
        .orderBy("event_time")
    
    deduped_with_timestamp = stream_with_dupes \
        .withWatermark("event_time", "10 minutes") \
        .withColumn("row_num", row_number().over(window_spec)) \
        .filter(col("row_num") == 1) \
        .drop("row_num") \
        .groupBy(
            window(col("event_time"), "1 minute"),
            col("user_id")
        ) \
        .agg(
            count("*").alias("unique_events"),
            sum("amount").alias("total_amount")
        ) \
        .select(
            col("window.start").alias("window_start"),
            col("window.end").alias("window_end"),
            col("user_id"),
            col("unique_events"),
            round(col("total_amount"), 2).alias("total_amount")
        ) \
        .withColumn("dedup_method", lit("timestamp_based"))
    
    # Track duplicate statistics
    duplicate_stats = stream_with_dupes \
        .withWatermark("event_time", "10 minutes") \
        .groupBy(
            window(col("event_time"), "1 minute"),
            col("event_id"),
            col("user_id")
        ) \
        .agg(count("*").alias("occurrence_count")) \
        .filter(col("occurrence_count") > 1) \
        .groupBy("window") \
        .agg(
            count("*").alias("duplicate_event_ids"),
            sum("occurrence_count").alias("total_duplicates")
        ) \
        .select(
            col("window.start").alias("window_start"),
            col("window.end").alias("window_end"),
            col("duplicate_event_ids"),
            col("total_duplicates")
        )
    
    query_dedup = deduped_tumbling \
        .writeStream \
        .outputMode("append") \
        .format("console") \
        .option("truncate", "false") \
        .queryName("deduplication") \
        .start()
    
    query_stats = duplicate_stats \
        .writeStream \
        .outputMode("append") \
        .format("console") \
        .option("truncate", "false") \
        .queryName("duplicate_stats") \
        .start()
    
    return query_dedup, query_stats


def alert_throttling_pattern():
    """
    ADVANCED PATTERN: Alert Throttling with Windows
    Prevents alert fatigue by throttling repeated alerts
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("ADVANCED PATTERN: ALERT THROTTLING")
    print("="*80)
    
    # Create stream with potential alerts
    events_stream = spark \
        .readStream \
        .format("rate") \
        .option("rowsPerSecond", 20) \
        .load() \
        .select(
            (col("value") % 10).cast("string").alias("server_id"),
            col("timestamp").alias("event_time"),
            (rand() * 100).alias("cpu_usage"),
            (rand() * 100).alias("memory_usage")
        )
    
    # Detect threshold violations
    violations = events_stream \
        .withColumn("alert_type",
            when(col("cpu_usage") > 90, "CPU_HIGH")
            .when(col("memory_usage") > 85, "MEMORY_HIGH")
            .otherwise(None)
        ) \
        .filter(col("alert_type").isNotNull())
    
    # Throttle alerts: Only send one alert per server per alert type per 5 minutes
    throttled_alerts = violations \
        .withWatermark("event_time", "10 minutes") \
        .groupBy(
            window(col("event_time"), "5 minutes"),
            col("server_id"),
            col("alert_type")
        ) \
        .agg(
            count("*").alias("violation_count"),
            first("event_time").alias("first_occurrence"),
            last("event_time").alias("last_occurrence"),
            max("cpu_usage").alias("max_cpu"),
            max("memory_usage").alias("max_memory")
        ) \
        .select(
            col("window.start").alias("throttle_window_start"),
            col("window.end").alias("throttle_window_end"),
            col("server_id"),
            col("alert_type"),
            col("violation_count"),
            col("
```python
            col("violation_count"),
            col("first_occurrence"),
            col("last_occurrence"),
            round(col("max_cpu"), 2).alias("max_cpu"),
            round(col("max_memory"), 2).alias("max_memory")
        ) \
        .withColumn("alert_message",
            concat(
                lit("ALERT: "),
                col("alert_type"),
                lit(" on server "),
                col("server_id"),
                lit(" occurred "),
                col("violation_count").cast("string"),
                lit(" times between "),
                col("first_occurrence").cast("string"),
                lit(" and "),
                col("last_occurrence").cast("string")
            )
        ) \
        .withColumn("severity",
            when(col("violation_count") > 10, "CRITICAL")
            .when(col("violation_count") > 5, "HIGH")
            .otherwise("MEDIUM")
        )
    
    # Alert escalation based on repeated violations
    alert_escalation = throttled_alerts \
        .withColumn("should_escalate", col("violation_count") > 10) \
        .withColumn("escalation_level",
            when(col("violation_count") > 20, 3)
            .when(col("violation_count") > 10, 2)
            .when(col("violation_count") > 5, 1)
            .otherwise(0)
        )
    
    # Summary of alerts per server
    alert_summary = throttled_alerts \
        .groupBy(
            window(col("throttle_window_start"), "15 minutes"),
            col("server_id")
        ) \
        .agg(
            count("*").alias("unique_alert_types"),
            sum("violation_count").alias("total_violations"),
            collect_list("alert_type").alias("alert_types")
        ) \
        .select(
            col("window.start").alias("summary_start"),
            col("window.end").alias("summary_end"),
            col("server_id"),
            col("unique_alert_types"),
            col("total_violations"),
            col("alert_types")
        )
    
    query_throttled = throttled_alerts \
        .writeStream \
        .outputMode("append") \
        .format("console") \
        .option("truncate", "false") \
        .queryName("throttled_alerts") \
        .start()
    
    query_summary = alert_summary \
        .writeStream \
        .outputMode("append") \
        .format("console") \
        .option("truncate", "false") \
        .queryName("alert_summary") \
        .start()
    
    return query_throttled, query_summary


def top_k_window_pattern():
    """
    ADVANCED PATTERN: Top-K Elements per Window
    Finds top-K items in each time window
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("ADVANCED PATTERN: TOP-K ELEMENTS PER WINDOW")
    print("="*80)
    
    # Create stream with product views
    product_views = spark \
        .readStream \
        .format("rate") \
        .option("rowsPerSecond", 50) \
        .load() \
        .select(
            (col("value") % 100).cast("string").alias("product_id"),
            (col("value") % 10).cast("string").alias("category"),
            col("timestamp").alias("view_time"),
            (rand() * 5).cast("int").alias("view_duration_seconds")
        )
    
    # Aggregate views per window
    view_counts = product_views \
        .withWatermark("view_time", "5 minutes") \
        .groupBy(
            window(col("view_time"), "1 minute"),
            col("category"),
            col("product_id")
        ) \
        .agg(
            count("*").alias("view_count"),
            avg("view_duration_seconds").alias("avg_duration")
        )
    
    # Top 5 products per category per window
    window_spec = Window.partitionBy("window", "category") \
        .orderBy(col("view_count").desc())
    
    top_k_products = view_counts \
        .withColumn("rank", row_number().over(window_spec)) \
        .filter(col("rank") <= 5) \
        .select(
            col("window.start").alias("window_start"),
            col("window.end").alias("window_end"),
            col("category"),
            col("rank"),
            col("product_id"),
            col("view_count"),
            round(col("avg_duration"), 2).alias("avg_duration")
        ) \
        .orderBy("window_start", "category", "rank")
    
    # Top categories by total views
    category_totals = view_counts \
        .groupBy("window", "category") \
        .agg(
            sum("view_count").alias("total_views"),
            countDistinct("product_id").alias("unique_products")
        )
    
    category_window_spec = Window.partitionBy("window") \
        .orderBy(col("total_views").desc())
    
    top_categories = category_totals \
        .withColumn("category_rank", row_number().over(category_window_spec)) \
        .filter(col("category_rank") <= 3) \
        .select(
            col("window.start").alias("window_start"),
            col("window.end").alias("window_end"),
            col("category_rank"),
            col("category"),
            col("total_views"),
            col("unique_products")
        )
    
    query_products = top_k_products \
        .writeStream \
        .outputMode("append") \
        .format("console") \
        .option("truncate", "false") \
        .queryName("top_k_products") \
        .start()
    
    query_categories = top_categories \
        .writeStream \
        .outputMode("append") \
        .format("console") \
        .option("truncate", "false") \
        .queryName("top_categories") \
        .start()
    
    return query_products, query_categories


def cohort_analysis_pattern():
    """
    ADVANCED PATTERN: Cohort Analysis with Windows
    Tracks user cohorts over time windows
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("ADVANCED PATTERN: COHORT ANALYSIS")
    print("="*80)
    
    # Create stream with user events
    user_events = spark \
        .readStream \
        .format("rate") \
        .option("rowsPerSecond", 30) \
        .load() \
        .select(
            (col("value") % 200).cast("string").alias("user_id"),
            col("timestamp").alias("event_time"),
            expr("CASE WHEN rand() > 0.7 THEN 'purchase' " +
                 "WHEN rand() > 0.4 THEN 'add_to_cart' " +
                 "ELSE 'view' END").alias("event_type"),
            (rand() * 100).alias("value")
        )
    
    # Determine user cohort (based on first event time)
    user_window = Window.partitionBy("user_id").orderBy("event_time")
    
    cohorted_events = user_events \
        .withWatermark("event_time", "1 hour") \
        .withColumn("first_event_time", first("event_time").over(user_window)) \
        .withColumn("cohort_week",
            date_format(col("first_event_time"), "yyyy-ww")
        ) \
        .withColumn("event_week",
            date_format(col("event_time"), "yyyy-ww")
        ) \
        .withColumn("weeks_since_first",
            weekofyear(col("event_time")) - weekofyear(col("first_event_time"))
        )
    
    # Cohort retention analysis
    cohort_retention = cohorted_events \
        .groupBy(
            col("cohort_week"),
            col("weeks_since_first")
        ) \
        .agg(
            countDistinct("user_id").alias("active_users"),
            count("*").alias("total_events"),
            sum(when(col("event_type") == "purchase", 1).otherwise(0)).alias("purchases")
        ) \
        .orderBy("cohort_week", "weeks_since_first")
    
    # Cohort value analysis
    cohort_value = cohorted_events \
        .filter(col("event_type") == "purchase") \
        .groupBy(
            col("cohort_week"),
            col("weeks_since_first")
        ) \
        .agg(
            countDistinct("user_id").alias("purchasing_users"),
            sum("value").alias("total_revenue"),
            avg("value").alias("avg_purchase_value")
        ) \
        .select(
            col("cohort_week"),
            col("weeks_since_first"),
            col("purchasing_users"),
            round(col("total_revenue"), 2).alias("total_revenue"),
            round(col("avg_purchase_value"), 2).alias("avg_purchase_value")
        ) \
        .orderBy("cohort_week", "weeks_since_first")
    
    # Calculate retention rate (compared to week 0)
    cohort_size_window = Window.partitionBy("cohort_week") \
        .orderBy("weeks_since_first")
    
    retention_rates = cohort_retention \
        .withColumn("cohort_size", 
            first("active_users").over(cohort_size_window)
        ) \
        .withColumn("retention_rate",
            round((col("active_users") / col("cohort_size") * 100), 2)
        ) \
        .select(
            col("cohort_week"),
            col("weeks_since_first"),
            col("active_users"),
            col("cohort_size"),
            col("retention_rate"),
            col("total_events"),
            col("purchases")
        )
    
    query_retention = retention_rates \
        .writeStream \
        .outputMode("update") \
        .format("console") \
        .option("truncate", "false") \
        .queryName("cohort_retention") \
        .start()
    
    query_value = cohort_value \
        .writeStream \
        .outputMode("update") \
        .format("console") \
        .option("truncate", "false") \
        .queryName("cohort_value") \
        .start()
    
    return query_retention, query_value


def anomaly_detection_window_pattern():
    """
    ADVANCED PATTERN: Anomaly Detection with Statistical Windows
    Detects anomalies using statistical methods over windows
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("ADVANCED PATTERN: ANOMALY DETECTION")
    print("="*80)
    
    # Create stream with metrics
    metrics_stream = spark \
        .readStream \
        .format("rate") \
        .option("rowsPerSecond", 40) \
        .load() \
        .select(
            (col("value") % 20).cast("string").alias("metric_id"),
            col("timestamp").alias("metric_time"),
            # Normal distribution with occasional anomalies
            when(rand() > 0.95, rand() * 1000)  # 5% anomalies
            .otherwise(rand() * 100 + 50).alias("metric_value")
        )
    
    # Calculate baseline statistics over sliding window
    baseline_stats = metrics_stream \
        .withWatermark("metric_time", "10 minutes") \
        .groupBy(
            window(col("metric_time"), "5 minutes", "1 minute"),
            col("metric_id")
        ) \
        .agg(
            count("*").alias("sample_count"),
            avg("metric_value").alias("mean"),
            stddev("metric_value").alias("stddev"),
            min("metric_value").alias("min_value"),
            max("metric_value").alias("max_value")
        )
    
    # Join current values with baseline to detect anomalies
    # Using Z-score method: anomaly if |value - mean| > 3 * stddev
    metrics_with_baseline = metrics_stream \
        .withWatermark("metric_time", "10 minutes") \
        .alias("current") \
        .join(
            baseline_stats.alias("baseline"),
            expr("""
                current.metric_id = baseline.metric_id AND
                current.metric_time >= baseline.window.start AND
                current.metric_time < baseline.window.end
            """),
            "left"
        )
    
    anomaly_detection = metrics_with_baseline \
        .withColumn("z_score",
            when(col("baseline.stddev") > 0,
                abs(col("current.metric_value") - col("baseline.mean")) / col("baseline.stddev")
            ).otherwise(0)
        ) \
        .withColumn("is_anomaly", col("z_score") > 3) \
        .withColumn("anomaly_severity",
            when(col("z_score") > 5, "CRITICAL")
            .when(col("z_score") > 4, "HIGH")
            .when(col("z_score") > 3, "MEDIUM")
            .otherwise("NORMAL")
        ) \
        .select(
            col("current.metric_id"),
            col("current.metric_time"),
            round(col("current.metric_value"), 2).alias("value"),
            round(col("baseline.mean"), 2).alias("baseline_mean"),
            round(col("baseline.stddev"), 2).alias("baseline_stddev"),
            round(col("z_score"), 2).alias("z_score"),
            col("is_anomaly"),
            col("anomaly_severity")
        )
    
    # Filter only anomalies
    anomalies_only = anomaly_detection \
        .filter(col("is_anomaly") == True)
    
    # Aggregate anomalies per window
    anomaly_summary = anomalies_only \
        .withWatermark("metric_time", "10 minutes") \
        .groupBy(
            window(col("metric_time"), "1 minute"),
            col("metric_id"),
            col("anomaly_severity")
        ) \
        .agg(
            count("*").alias("anomaly_count"),
            avg("z_score").alias("avg_z_score"),
            max("value").alias("max_anomalous_value")
        ) \
        .select(
            col("window.start").alias("window_start"),
            col("window.end").alias("window_end"),
            col("metric_id"),
            col("anomaly_severity"),
            col("anomaly_count"),
            round(col("avg_z_score"), 2).alias("avg_z_score"),
            round(col("max_anomalous_value"), 2).alias("max_value")
        )
    
    query_detection = anomaly_detection \
        .writeStream \
        .outputMode("append") \
        .format("memory") \
        .queryName("anomaly_detection") \
        .start()
    
    query_anomalies = anomalies_only \
        .writeStream \
        .outputMode("append") \
        .format("console") \
        .option("truncate", "false") \
        .queryName("anomalies_only") \
        .start()
    
    query_summary = anomaly_summary \

        .outputMode("append") \

        .query

# 1. CHANGE AUDIT PATTERN

"""
Purpose: Track and audit all changes to data including inserts, updates, and deletes
Use Cases: Data lineage, compliance, debugging, rollback capabilities
"""

class ChangeAuditPattern:
    """
    Implements Change Data Capture (CDC) and change tracking for audit purposes
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
        self.audit_table_name = "change_audit_log"
        
    def create_audit_schema(self) -> StructType:
        """Define schema for change audit log"""
        return StructType([
            StructField("audit_id", StringType(), False),
            StructField("table_name", StringType(), False),
            StructField("record_id", StringType(), False),
            StructField("operation_type", StringType(), False),  # INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE
            StructField("changed_by", StringType(), True),
            StructField("changed_at", TimestampType(), False),
            StructField("old_values", StringType(), True),
            StructField("new_values", StringType(), True),
            StructField("changed_columns", StringType(), True),
            StructField("change_reason", StringType(), True),
            StructField("session_id", StringType(), True),
            StructField("ip_address", StringType(), True),
            StructField("application_name", StringType(), True)
        ])
    
    def capture_changes(self, 
                       old_df: DataFrame, 
                       new_df: DataFrame,
                       key_columns: List[str],
                       table_name: str,
                       user_id: str = "system",
                       metadata: Dict = None) -> DataFrame:
        """
        Capture changes between two dataframes (old and new versions)
        
        Args:
            old_df: Previous version of data
            new_df: Current version of data
            key_columns: Columns that uniquely identify records
            table_name: Name of the table being audited
            user_id: User who made the change
            metadata: Additional metadata (session_id, ip_address, etc.)
        
        Returns:
            DataFrame containing audit records
        """
        metadata = metadata or {}
        
        # Add row hash for comparison
        old_df_with_hash = old_df.withColumn(
            "row_hash", 
            md5(concat_ws("||", *[col(c) for c in old_df.columns]))
        )
        
        new_df_with_hash = new_df.withColumn(
            "row_hash",
            md5(concat_ws("||", *[col(c) for c in new_df.columns]))
        )
        
        # Detect INSERTS (records in new but not in old)
        inserts = new_df_with_hash.join(
            old_df_with_hash.select(key_columns),
            key_columns,
            "left_anti"
        ).withColumn("operation_type", lit("INSERT"))
        
        # Detect DELETES (records in old but not in new)
        deletes = old_df_with_hash.join(
            new_df_with_hash.select(key_columns),
            key_columns,
            "left_anti"
        ).withColumn("operation_type", lit("DELETE"))
        
        # Detect UPDATES (records with same key but different hash)
        updates = old_df_with_hash.alias("old").join(
            new_df_with_hash.alias("new"),
            key_columns,
            "inner"
        ).where(col("old.row_hash") != col("new.row_hash"))
        
        # Create audit records for inserts
        insert_audits = inserts.select(
            md5(concat_ws("||", *key_columns, lit(current_timestamp()))).alias("audit_id"),
            lit(table_name).alias("table_name"),
            concat_ws("||", *key_columns).alias("record_id"),
            col("operation_type"),
            lit(user_id).alias("changed_by"),
            current_timestamp().alias("changed_at"),
            lit(None).cast(StringType()).alias("old_values"),
            to_json(struct(*[c for c in inserts.columns if c not in ["row_hash", "operation_type"]])).alias("new_values"),
            lit("ALL").alias("changed_columns"),
            lit(metadata.get("reason", "New record")).alias("change_reason"),
            lit(metadata.get("session_id")).alias("session_id"),
            lit(metadata.get("ip_address")).alias("ip_address"),
            lit(metadata.get("application_name")).alias("application_name")
        )
        
        # Create audit records for deletes
        delete_audits = deletes.select(
            md5(concat_ws("||", *key_columns, lit(current_timestamp()))).alias("audit_id"),
            lit(table_name).alias("table_name"),
            concat_ws("||", *key_columns).alias("record_id"),
            col("operation_type"),
            lit(user_id).alias("changed_by"),
            current_timestamp().alias("changed_at"),
            to_json(struct(*[c for c in deletes.columns if c not in ["row_hash", "operation_type"]])).alias("old_values"),
            lit(None).cast(StringType()).alias("new_values"),
            lit("ALL").alias("changed_columns"),
            lit(metadata.get("reason", "Record deleted")).alias("change_reason"),
            lit(metadata.get("session_id")).alias("session_id"),
            lit(metadata.get("ip_address")).alias("ip_address"),
            lit(metadata.get("application_name")).alias("application_name")
        )
        
        # Create audit records for updates with changed columns detection
        if updates.count() > 0:
            # Identify changed columns
            old_cols = [f"old.{c}" for c in old_df.columns if c not in key_columns]
            new_cols = [f"new.{c}" for c in new_df.columns if c not in key_columns]
            
            update_audits = updates.select(
                md5(concat_ws("||", *[f"old.{k}" for k in key_columns], lit(current_timestamp()))).alias("audit_id"),
                lit(table_name).alias("table_name"),
                concat_ws("||", *[f"old.{k}" for k in key_columns]).alias("record_id"),
                lit("UPDATE").alias("operation_type"),
                lit(user_id).alias("changed_by"),
                current_timestamp().alias("changed_at"),
                to_json(struct(*[col(c).alias(c.replace("old.", "")) for c in old_cols])).alias("old_values"),
                to_json(struct(*[col(c).alias(c.replace("new.", "")) for c in new_cols])).alias("new_values"),
                lit(",".join([c for c in old_df.columns if c not in key_columns])).alias("changed_columns"),
                lit(metadata.get("reason", "Record updated")).alias("change_reason"),
                lit(metadata.get("session_id")).alias("session_id"),
                lit(metadata.get("ip_address")).alias("ip_address"),
                lit(metadata.get("application_name")).alias("application_name")
            )
        else:
            update_audits = self.spark.createDataFrame([], self.create_audit_schema())
        
        # Union all audit records
        all_audits = insert_audits.union(delete_audits).union(update_audits)
        
        return all_audits
    
    def get_change_history(self, 
                          table_name: str,
                          record_id: Optional[str] = None,
                          start_date: Optional[datetime] = None,
                          end_date: Optional[datetime] = None) -> DataFrame:
        """
        Retrieve change history for a table or specific record
        """
        audit_df = self.spark.table(self.audit_table_name)
        
        # Filter by table
        result = audit_df.filter(col("table_name") == table_name)
        
        # Filter by record if specified
        if record_id:
            result = result.filter(col("record_id") == record_id)
        
        # Filter by date range
        if start_date:
            result = result.filter(col("changed_at") >= lit(start_date))
        if end_date:
            result = result.filter(col("changed_at") <= lit(end_date))
        
        return result.orderBy(col("changed_at").desc())
    
    def generate_change_summary_report(self, table_name: str, days: int = 7) -> DataFrame:
        """
        Generate summary report of changes for a table
        """
        audit_df = self.spark.table(self.audit_table_name)
        
        cutoff_date = datetime.now() - timedelta(days=days)
        
        summary = audit_df.filter(
            (col("table_name") == table_name) &
            (col("changed_at") >= lit(cutoff_date))
        ).groupBy(
            "operation_type",
            "changed_by"
        ).agg(
            count("*").alias("change_count"),
            _min("changed_at").alias("first_change"),
            _max("changed_at").alias("last_change")
        )
        
        return summary

            StructField("error_message", StringType(), True),

        ])
    
    def log_access(self,

                   access_type: str,

        """
        Log a data access event
        
        Args:
            user_id: User accessing the data

            metadata: Additional access metadata

        access_record = self.spark.createDataFrame([{

            "user_role": metadata.get("user_role"),

            "application_name": metadata.get("application_name"),

            "rows_accessed": metadata.get("rows_accessed"),
            "columns_accessed": metadata.get("columns_accessed"),
            "filter_conditions": metadata.get("filter_conditions"),
            "access_duration_ms": metadata.get("access_duration_ms"),
            "success": metadata.get("success", True),
            "error_message": metadata.get("error_message"),
            "data_classification": metadata.get("data_classification"),
            "compliance_tags": metadata.get("compliance_tags")
        }], self.create_access_log_schema())
        
        return access_record

                "access_timestamp",
                "anomaly_type",
                concat_ws(" -> ", col("previous_ip"), col("ip_address")).alias("details")
            )
        ).union(
            mass_extraction.select(
                "user_id",
                "resource_name",
                "access_timestamp",
                "anomaly_type",
                col("rows_accessed").cast(StringType()).alias("details")
            )
        )
        
        return all_anomalies
    
    def generate_access_report(self, 
                              start_date: datetime,
                              end_date: datetime,
                              group_by: str = "user") -> DataFrame:
        """
        Generate comprehensive access report
        
        Args:
            start_date: Report start date
            end_date: Report end date
            group_by: Grouping dimension (user, resource, classification)
        """
        access_log = self.spark.table(self.access_log_table)
        
        filtered_log = access_log.filter(
            (col("access_timestamp") >= lit(start_date)) &
            (col("access_timestamp") <= lit(end_date))
        )
        
        if group_by == "user":
            report = filtered_log.groupBy("user_id", "user_role").agg(
                count("*").alias("total_accesses"),
                countDistinct("resource_name").alias("unique_resources"),
                _sum(when(col("success") == False, 1).otherwise(0)).alias("failed_accesses"),
                _sum("rows_accessed").alias("total_rows_accessed"),
                avg("access_duration_ms").alias("avg_duration_ms"),
                collect_list("access_type").alias("access_types")
            )
        elif group_by == "resource":
            report = filtered_log.groupBy("resource_name", "data_classification").agg(
                count("*").alias("total_accesses"),
                countDistinct("user_id").alias("unique_users"),
                _sum("rows_accessed").alias("total_rows_accessed"),
                avg("access_duration_ms").alias("avg_duration_ms"),
                _max("access_timestamp").alias("last_accessed")
            )
        elif group_by == "classification":
            report = filtered_log.groupBy("data_classification").agg(
                count("*").alias("total_accesses"),
                countDistinct("user_id").alias("unique_users"),
                countDistinct("resource_name").alias("unique_resources"),
                _sum("rows_accessed").alias("total_rows_accessed")
            )
        else:
            report = filtered_log.groupBy("access_type").agg(
                count("*").alias("total_accesses"),
                avg("access_duration_ms").alias("avg_duration_ms")
            )
        
        return report


# ============================================================================
# 3. COMPLIANCE AUDIT PATTERN
# ============================================================================
"""
Purpose: Ensure data handling complies with regulations (GDPR, HIPAA, SOX, etc.)
Use Cases: Regulatory compliance, data governance, privacy management
"""

class ComplianceAuditPattern:
    """
    Implements compliance checking and reporting for regulatory requirements
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
        self.compliance_log_table = "compliance_audit_log"
        
    def create_compliance_schema(self) -> StructType:
        """Define schema for compliance audit log"""
        return StructType([
            StructField("compliance_id", StringType(), False),
            StructField("audit_timestamp", TimestampType(), False),
            StructField("regulation_type", StringType(), False),  # GDPR, HIPAA, SOX, PCI-DSS
            StructField("compliance_rule", StringType(), False),
            StructField("resource_name", StringType(), False),
            StructField("resource_type", StringType(), False),
            StructField("compliance_status", StringType(), False),  # COMPLIANT, NON_COMPLIANT, WARNING
            StructField("violation_details", StringType(), True),
            StructField("severity", StringType(), True),  # CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW
            StructField("affected_records", LongType(), True),
            StructField("data_subject_type", StringType(), True),  # CUSTOMER, EMPLOYEE, VENDOR
            StructField("retention_policy", StringType(), True),
            StructField("encryption_status", BooleanType(), True),
            StructField("anonymization_status", BooleanType(), True),
            StructField("consent_status", StringType(), True),
            StructField("remediation_action", StringType(), True),
            StructField("remediation_deadline", TimestampType(), True),
            StructField("responsible_party", StringType(), True),
            StructField("audit_trail_complete", BooleanType(), True)
        ])
    
    def check_gdpr_compliance(self, df: DataFrame, 
                             pii_columns: List[str],
                             table_name: str) -> DataFrame:
        """
        Check GDPR compliance requirements
        
        GDPR Requirements checked:
        - Right to be forgotten (data retention)
        - Data minimization
        - Consent tracking
        - Data encryption
        - Access controls
        """
        compliance_checks = []
        
        # Check 1: Data retention compliance
        if "created_date" in df.columns:
            retention_violation = df.filter(
                datediff(current_timestamp(), col("created_date")) > 365 * 7  # 7 years default
            ).count()
            
            if retention_violation > 0:
                compliance_checks.append({
                    "compliance_id": f"GDPR_RET_{table_name}_{datetime.now().strftime('%Y%m%d%H%M%S')}",
                    "audit_timestamp": datetime.now(),
                    "regulation_type": "GDPR",
                    "compliance_rule": "Data Retention Limit",
                    "resource_name": table_name,
                    "resource_type": "TABLE",
                    "compliance_status": "NON_COMPLIANT",
                    "violation_details": f"Found {retention_violation} records exceeding retention period",
                    "severity": "HIGH",
                    "affected_records": retention_violation,
                    "data_subject_type": "CUSTOMER",
                    "retention_policy": "7_YEARS",
                    "encryption_status": None,
                    "anonymization_status": None,
                    "consent_status": None,
                    "remediation_action": "Archive or delete records exceeding retention period",
                    "remediation_deadline": datetime.now() + timedelta(days=30),
                    "responsible_party": "Data Governance Team",
                    "audit_trail_complete": True
                })
        
        # Check 2: PII encryption
        for pii_col in pii_columns:
            if pii_col in df.columns:
                # Check if column appears to be encrypted (basic check)
                sample_values = df.select(pii_col).limit(100).collect()
                potentially_unencrypted = sum(
                    1 for row in sample_values 
                    if row[0] and len(str(row[0])) < 50  # Simple heuristic
                )
                
                if potentially_unencrypted > 50:  # More than 50% appear unencrypted
                    compliance_checks.append({
                        "compliance_id": f"GDPR_ENC_{table_name}_{pii_col}_{datetime.now().strftime('%Y%m%d%H%M%S')}",
                        "audit_timestamp": datetime.now(),
                        "regulation_type": "GDPR",
                        "compliance_rule": "PII Encryption Required",
                        "resource_name": table_name,
                        "resource_type": "COLUMN",
                        "compliance_status": "WARNING",
                        "violation_details": f"Column '{pii_col}' may contain unencrypted PII",
                        "severity": "CRITICAL",
                        "affected_records": df.count(),
                        "data_subject_type": "CUSTOMER",
                        "retention_policy": None,
                        "encryption_status": False,
                        "anonymization_status": False,
                        "consent_status": None,
                        "remediation_action": f"Encrypt column '{pii_col}' at rest and in transit",
                        "remediation_deadline": datetime.now() + timedelta(days=7),
                        "responsible_party": "Security Team",
                        "audit_trail_complete": True
                    })
        
        # Check 3: Consent tracking
        if "consent_given" in df.columns:
            no_consent = df.filter(
                (col("consent_given").isNull()) | (col("consent_given") == False)
            ).count()
            
            if no_consent > 0:
                compliance_checks.append({
                    "compliance_id": f"GDPR_CNS_{table_name}_{datetime.now().strftime('%Y%m%d%H%M%S')}",
                    "audit_timestamp": datetime.now(),
                    "regulation_type": "GDPR",
                    "compliance_rule": "Consent Required for Processing",
                    "resource_name": table_name,
                    "resource_type": "TABLE",
                    "compliance_status": "NON_COMPLIANT",
                    "violation_details": f"Found {no_consent} records without valid consent",
                    "severity": "CRITICAL",
                    "affected_records": no_consent,
                    "data_subject_type": "CUSTOMER",
                    "retention_policy": None,
                    "encryption_status": None,
                    "anonymization_status": None,
                    "consent_status": "MISSING",
                    "remediation_action": "Obtain consent or remove records",
                    "remediation_deadline": datetime.now() + timedelta(days=14),
                    "responsible_party": "Legal/Compliance Team",
                    "audit_trail_complete": True
                })
        
        # Check 4: Data minimization
        total_columns = len(df.columns)
        if total_columns > 50:  # Threshold for too many columns
            compliance_checks.append({
                "compliance_id": f"GDPR_MIN_{table_name}_{datetime.now().strftime('%Y%m%d%H%M%S')}",
                "audit_timestamp": datetime.now(),
                "regulation_type": "GDPR",
                "compliance_rule": "Data Minimization Principle",
                "resource_name": table_name,
                "resource_type": "TABLE",
                "compliance_status": "WARNING",
                "violation_details": f"Table has {total_columns} columns - review if all are necessary",
                "severity": "MEDIUM",
                "affected_records": df.count(),
                "data_subject_type": "CUSTOMER",
                "retention_policy": None,
                "encryption_status": None,
                "anonymization_status": None,
                "consent_status": None,
                "remediation_action": "Review and remove unnecessary columns",
                "remediation_deadline": datetime.now() + timedelta(days=60),
                "responsible_party": "Data Governance Team",
                "audit_trail_complete": True
            })
        
        if compliance_checks:
            return self.spark.createDataFrame(compliance_checks, self.create_compliance_schema())
        else:
            # Return compliant status
            compliant_record = [{
                "compliance_id": f"GDPR_OK_{table_name}_{datetime.now().strftime('%Y%m%d%H%M%S')}",
                "audit_timestamp": datetime.now(),
                "regulation_type": "GDPR",
                "compliance_rule": "All GDPR Checks",
                "resource_name": table_name,
                "resource_type": "TABLE",
                "compliance_status": "COMPLIANT",
                "violation_details": None,
                "severity": None,
                "affected_records": 0,
                "data_subject_type": "CUSTOMER",
                "retention_policy": "7_YEARS",
                "encryption_status": True,
                "anonymization_status": True,
                "consent_status": "VALID",
                "remediation_action": None,
                "remediation_deadline": None,
                "responsible_party": None,
                "audit_trail_complete": True
            }]
            return self.spark.createDataFrame(compliant_record, self.create_compliance_schema())
    
    def check_hipaa_compliance(self, df: DataFrame,
                              phi_columns: List[str],
                              table_name: str) -> DataFrame:
        """
        Check HIPAA compliance for Protected Health Information (PHI)
        
        HIPAA Requirements checked:
        - PHI encryption
        - Access controls
        - Audit trails
        - Data integrity
        """
        compliance_checks = []
        
        # Check 1: PHI encryption
        for phi_col in phi_columns:
            if phi_col in df.columns:
                compliance_checks.append({
                    "compliance_id": f"HIPAA_ENC_{table
```python
                    "compliance_id": f"HIPAA_ENC_{table_name}_{phi_col}_{datetime.now().strftime('%Y%m%d%H%M%S')}",
                    "audit_timestamp": datetime.now(),
                    "regulation_type": "HIPAA",
                    "compliance_rule": "PHI Encryption at Rest",
                    "resource_name": table_name,
                    "resource_type": "COLUMN",
                    "compliance_status": "COMPLIANT",
                    "violation_details": None,
                    "severity": None,
                    "affected_records": df.count(),
                    "data_subject_type": "PATIENT",
                    "retention_policy": "6_YEARS",
                    "encryption_status": True,
                    "anonymization_status": False,
                    "consent_status": "VALID",
                    "remediation_action": None,
                    "remediation_deadline": None,
                    "responsible_party": None,
                    "audit_trail_complete": True
                })
        
        # Check 2: Audit trail completeness
        required_audit_columns = ["created_by", "created_date", "modified_by", "modified_date"]
        missing_audit_cols = [col for col in required_audit_columns if col not in df.columns]
        
        if missing_audit_cols:
            compliance_checks.append({
                "compliance_id": f"HIPAA_AUD_{table_name}_{datetime.now().strftime('%Y%m%d%H%M%S')}",
                "audit_timestamp": datetime.now(),
                "regulation_type": "HIPAA",
                "compliance_rule": "Complete Audit Trail Required",
                "resource_name": table_name,
                "resource_type": "TABLE",
                "compliance_status": "NON_COMPLIANT",
                "violation_details": f"Missing audit columns: {', '.join(missing_audit_cols)}",
                "severity": "CRITICAL",
                "affected_records": df.count(),
                "data_subject_type": "PATIENT",
                "retention_policy": "6_YEARS",
                "encryption_status": None,
                "anonymization_status": None,
                "consent_status": None,
                "remediation_action": f"Add missing audit columns: {', '.join(missing_audit_cols)}",
                "remediation_deadline": datetime.now() + timedelta(days=7),
                "responsible_party": "IT Security Team",
                "audit_trail_complete": False
            })
        
        # Check 3: Data integrity - no null PHI values
        for phi_col in phi_columns:
            if phi_col in df.columns:
                null_count = df.filter(col(phi_col).isNull()).count()
                if null_count > 0:
                    compliance_checks.append({
                        "compliance_id": f"HIPAA_INT_{table_name}_{phi_col}_{datetime.now().strftime('%Y%m%d%H%M%S')}",
                        "audit_timestamp": datetime.now(),
                        "regulation_type": "HIPAA",
                        "compliance_rule": "Data Integrity - No Null PHI",
                        "resource_name": table_name,
                        "resource_type": "COLUMN",
                        "compliance_status": "WARNING",
                        "violation_details": f"Column '{phi_col}' has {null_count} null values",
                        "severity": "MEDIUM",
                        "affected_records": null_count,
                        "data_subject_type": "PATIENT",
                        "retention_policy": None,
                        "encryption_status": None,
                        "anonymization_status": None,
                        "consent_status": None,
                        "remediation_action": f"Investigate and fix null values in '{phi_col}'",
                        "remediation_deadline": datetime.now() + timedelta(days=30),
                        "responsible_party": "Data Quality Team",
                        "audit_trail_complete": True
                    })
        
        return self.spark.createDataFrame(compliance_checks, self.create_compliance_schema())
    
    def check_sox_compliance(self, df: DataFrame, table_name: str) -> DataFrame:
        """
        Check SOX (Sarbanes-Oxley) compliance for financial data
        
        SOX Requirements checked:
        - Data accuracy and completeness
        - Change tracking
        - Access controls
        - Data retention
        """
        compliance_checks = []
        
        # Check 1: Financial data completeness
        financial_columns = [col for col in df.columns if any(
            keyword in col.lower() for keyword in ['amount', 'balance', 'revenue', 'cost', 'price']
        )]
        
        for fin_col in financial_columns:
            null_count = df.filter(col(fin_col).isNull()).count()
            total_count = df.count()
            
            if null_count > 0:
                compliance_checks.append({
                    "compliance_id": f"SOX_CMP_{table_name}_{fin_col}_{datetime.now().strftime('%Y%m%d%H%M%S')}",
                    "audit_timestamp": datetime.now(),
                    "regulation_type": "SOX",
                    "compliance_rule": "Financial Data Completeness",
                    "resource_name": table_name,
                    "resource_type": "COLUMN",
                    "compliance_status": "NON_COMPLIANT",
                    "violation_details": f"Financial column '{fin_col}' has {null_count} null values ({null_count/total_count*100:.2f}%)",
                    "severity": "CRITICAL",
                    "affected_records": null_count,
                    "data_subject_type": "FINANCIAL",
                    "retention_policy": "7_YEARS",
                    "encryption_status": True,
                    "anonymization_status": False,
                    "consent_status": None,
                    "remediation_action": f"Fill or validate null values in '{fin_col}'",
                    "remediation_deadline": datetime.now() + timedelta(days=3),
                    "responsible_party": "Finance Team",
                    "audit_trail_complete": True
                })
        
        # Check 2: Change tracking
        if "modified_date" not in df.columns or "modified_by" not in df.columns:
            compliance_checks.append({
                "compliance_id": f"SOX_CHG_{table_name}_{datetime.now().strftime('%Y%m%d%H%M%S')}",
                "audit_timestamp": datetime.now(),
                "regulation_type": "SOX",
                "compliance_rule": "Change Tracking Required",
                "resource_name": table_name,
                "resource_type": "TABLE",
                "compliance_status": "NON_COMPLIANT",
                "violation_details": "Missing change tracking columns (modified_date, modified_by)",
                "severity": "CRITICAL",
                "affected_records": df.count(),
                "data_subject_type": "FINANCIAL",
                "retention_policy": "7_YEARS",
                "encryption_status": None,
                "anonymization_status": None,
                "consent_status": None,
                "remediation_action": "Implement change tracking columns",
                "remediation_deadline": datetime.now() + timedelta(days=7),
                "responsible_party": "IT Development Team",
                "audit_trail_complete": False
            })
        
        # Check 3: Data retention
        if "transaction_date" in df.columns or "created_date" in df.columns:
            date_col = "transaction_date" if "transaction_date" in df.columns else "created_date"
            old_records = df.filter(
                datediff(current_timestamp(), col(date_col)) > 365 * 7
            ).count()
            
            if old_records == 0:
                compliance_checks.append({
                    "compliance_id": f"SOX_RET_{table_name}_{datetime.now().strftime('%Y%m%d%H%M%S')}",
                    "audit_timestamp": datetime.now(),
                    "regulation_type": "SOX",
                    "compliance_rule": "7-Year Retention Requirement",
                    "resource_name": table_name,
                    "resource_type": "TABLE",
                    "compliance_status": "COMPLIANT",
                    "violation_details": None,
                    "severity": None,
                    "affected_records": 0,
                    "data_subject_type": "FINANCIAL",
                    "retention_policy": "7_YEARS",
                    "encryption_status": True,
                    "anonymization_status": False,
                    "consent_status": None,
                    "remediation_action": None,
                    "remediation_deadline": None,
                    "responsible_party": None,
                    "audit_trail_complete": True
                })
        
        if not compliance_checks:
            compliance_checks.append({
                "compliance_id": f"SOX_OK_{table_name}_{datetime.now().strftime('%Y%m%d%H%M%S')}",
                "audit_timestamp": datetime.now(),
                "regulation_type": "SOX",
                "compliance_rule": "All SOX Checks",
                "resource_name": table_name,
                "resource_type": "TABLE",
                "compliance_status": "COMPLIANT",
                "violation_details": None,
                "severity": None,
                "affected_records": 0,
                "data_subject_type": "FINANCIAL",
                "retention_policy": "7_YEARS",
                "encryption_status": True,
                "anonymization_status": False,
                "consent_status": None,
                "remediation_action": None,
                "remediation_deadline": None,
                "responsible_party": None,
                "audit_trail_complete": True
            })
        
        return self.spark.createDataFrame(compliance_checks, self.create_compliance_schema())
    
    def generate_compliance_dashboard(self, regulation_type: Optional[str] = None) -> DataFrame:
        """
        Generate compliance dashboard with summary metrics
        """
        compliance_log = self.spark.table(self.compliance_log_table)
        
        if regulation_type:
            compliance_log = compliance_log.filter(col("regulation_type") == regulation_type)
        
        dashboard = compliance_log.groupBy(
            "regulation_type",
            "compliance_status",
            "severity"
        ).agg(
            count("*").alias("violation_count"),
            countDistinct("resource_name").alias("affected_resources"),
            _sum("affected_records").alias("total_affected_records"),
            _min("remediation_deadline").alias("earliest_deadline")
        ).orderBy("severity", "violation_count")
        
        return dashboard
