class OptimizationBypassOrchestrator:
    """
    Orchestrates all optimization bypass patterns for complex scenarios
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
        self.disable_pattern = OptimizationDisablePattern(spark)
        self.selective_pattern = SelectiveOptimizationPattern(spark)
        self.override_pattern = OverrideOptimizationPattern(spark)
        self.debug_pattern = DebugOptimizationPattern(spark)
        self.manual_pattern = ManualOptimizationPattern(spark)
    
    def optimize_complex_etl_pipeline(self):
        """
        Demonstrates a complex ETL pipeline using all optimization patterns
        """
        print("=" * 80)
        print("COMPLEX ETL PIPELINE WITH OPTIMIZATION BYPASS PATTERNS")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        # Step 1: Create sample data
        print("\n[STEP 1] Creating sample datasets...")
        
        # Large fact table
        transactions = self.spark.range(5000000).select(
            col("id").alias("transaction_id"),
            (col("id") % 100000).alias("customer_id"),
            (col("id") % 1000).alias("product_id"),
            (col("id") % 50).alias("store_id"),
            (rand() * 1000).alias("amount"),
            (col("id") % 365).alias("day_of_year")
        )
        
        # Medium dimension table
        customers = self.spark.range(100000).select(
            col("id").alias("customer_id"),
            concat(lit("Customer_"), col("id")).alias("customer_name"),
            (col("id") % 10).alias("segment_id")
        )
        
        # Small dimension table
        products = self.spark.range(1000).select(
            col("id").alias("product_id"),
            concat(lit("Product_"), col("id")).alias("product_name"),
            (rand() * 100).alias("price")
        )
        
        # Step 2: Enable debug mode to monitor optimizations
        print("\n[STEP 2] Enabling debug mode...")
        self.debug_pattern.enable_debug_mode()
        
        # Step 3: Apply selective optimizations for join-heavy operations
        print("\n[STEP 3] Configuring selective optimizations for joins...")
        self.selective_pattern.configure_selective_optimizations('join')
        
        # Step 4: Manual partition optimization
        print("\n[STEP 4] Applying manual partition optimization...")
        transactions_optimized = self.manual_pattern.manual_partition_optimization(
            transactions, ["customer_id", "store_id"], num_partitions=200
        )
        
        # Step 5: Override join strategy - broadcast small table
        print("\n[STEP 5] Overriding join strategy for products...")
        transactions_with_products = self.override_pattern.force_broadcast_join(
            transactions_optimized, products, "product_id"
        )
        
        # Step 6: Manual join optimization for customers
        print("\n[STEP 6] Manual join optimization for customers...")
        full_data = self.manual_pattern.manual_join_optimization(
            transactions_with_products, customers, "customer_id"
        )
        
        # Step 7: Handle data skew
        print("\n[STEP 7] Handling data skew...")
        deskewed_data = self.manual_pattern.manual_skew_handling(
            full_data, "customer_id", skew_threshold=0.05
        )
        
        # Step 8: Apply manual caching for reuse
        print("\n[STEP 8] Applying manual caching strategy...")
        cached_data = self.manual_pattern.manual_caching_strategy(
            deskewed_data, "memory_and_disk"
        )
        
        # Step 9: Switch to aggregation optimizations
        print("\n[STEP 9] Switching to aggregation optimizations...")
        self.selective_pattern.configure_selective_optimizations('aggregation')
        
        # Step 10: Manual aggregation optimization
        print("\n[STEP 10] Performing optimized aggregation...")
        agg_exprs = [
            sum("amount").alias("total_sales"),
            avg("amount").alias("avg_transaction"),
            count("*").alias("num_transactions"),
            countDistinct("customer_id").alias("unique_customers")
        ]
        
        aggregated = self.manual_pattern.manual_aggregation_optimization(
            cached_data, ["store_id", "segment_id"], agg_exprs
        )
        
        # Step 11: Apply filters with manual pushdown
        print("\n[STEP 11] Applying optimized filters...")
        filters = [
            col("total_sales") > 10000,
            col("num_transactions") > 100
        ]
        final_result = self.manual_pattern.manual_filter_pushdown(
            aggregated, filters
        )
        
        # Step 12: Inspect and explain final plan
        print("\n[STEP 12] Inspecting final execution plan...")
        self.debug_pattern.explain_query_plans(final_result, 'extended')
        self.debug_pattern.inspect_shuffle_operations(final_result)
        
        # Step 13: Execute and measure
        print("\n[STEP 13] Executing pipeline...")
        start_time = time.time()
        result_count = final_result.count()
        execution_time = time.time() - start_time
        
        print(f"\n{'=' * 80}")
        print(f"PIPELINE EXECUTION SUMMARY")
        print(f"{'=' * 80}")
        print(f"Final result count: {result_count}")
        print(f"Total execution time: {execution_time:.2f} seconds")
        print(f"{'=' * 80}")
        
        # Cleanup
        cached_data.unpersist()
        
        return final_result
    
    def run_performance_comparison(self):
        """
        Compare performance with and without optimization bypass patterns
        """
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("PERFORMANCE COMPARISON: WITH vs WITHOUT OPTIMIZATION BYPASS")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        # Create test dataset
        test_df = self.spark.range(1000000).select(
            col("id"),
            (col("id") % 1000).alias("key"),
            (rand() * 1000).alias("value")
        )
        
        # Test query
        query = test_df.groupBy("key").agg(
            sum("value").alias("total"),
            avg("value").alias("average")
        ).filter(col("total") > 50000)
        
        # Scenario 1: Default optimizations
        print("\n[Scenario 1] Using default Spark optimizations...")
        start = time.time()
        count1 = query.count()
        time1 = time.time() - start
        print(f"Time: {time1:.3f}s, Count: {count1}")
        
        # Scenario 2: Disabled optimizations
        print("\n[Scenario 2] With optimizations disabled...")
        self.disable_pattern.disable_all_optimizations()
        start = time.time()
        count2 = query.count()
        time2 = time.time() - start
        print(f"Time: {time2:.3f}s, Count: {count2}")
        self.disable_pattern.restore_optimizations()
        
        # Scenario 3: Selective optimizations
        print("\n[Scenario 3] With selective optimizations...")
        self.selective_pattern.configure_selective_optimizations('aggregation')
        start = time.time()
        count3 = query.count()
        time3 = time.time() - start
        print(f"Time: {time3:.3f}s, Count: {count3}")
        
        # Scenario 4: Manual optimizations
        print("\n[Scenario 4] With manual optimizations...")
        optimized_df = self.manual_pattern.manual_partition_optimization(
            test_df, ["key"], num_partitions=50
        )
        optimized_query = optimized_df.groupBy("key").agg(
            sum("value").alias("total"),
            avg("value").alias("average")
        ).filter(col("total") > 50000)
        
        start = time.time()
        count4 = optimized_query.count()
        time4 = time.time() - start
        print(f"Time: {time4:.3f}s, Count: {count4}")
        
        # Summary
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("PERFORMANCE SUMMARY")
        print("=" * 80)
        print(f"Default optimizations:    {time1:.3f}s (baseline)")
        print(f"Disabled optimizations:   {time2:.3f}s ({time2/time1:.2f}x)")
        print(f"Selective optimizations:  {time3:.3f}s ({time3/time1:.2f}x)")
        print(f"Manual optimizations:     {time4:.3f}s ({time4/time1:.2f}x)")
        print("=" * 80)

    """

    print("SPARK OPTIMIZATION CONFIGURATION REPORT")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    important_configs = [
        # Adaptive Query Execution
        "spark.sql.adaptive.enabled",
        "spark.sql.adaptive.coalescePartitions.enabled",
        "spark.sql.adaptive.skewJoin.enabled",
        "spark.sql.adaptive.localShuffleReader.enabled",
        
        # Cost-Based Optimization
        "spark.sql.cbo.enabled",
        "spark.sql.cbo.joinReorder.enabled",
        "spark.sql.statistics.histogram.enabled",
        
        # Join Optimization
        "spark.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold",
        "spark.sql.join.preferSortMergeJoin",
        
        # Shuffle Optimization
        "spark.sql.shuffle.partitions",
        "spark.sql.adaptive.advisoryPartitionSizeInBytes",
        
        # Predicate Pushdown
        "spark.sql.parquet.filterPushdown",
        "spark.sql.orc.filterPushdown",
        
        # Execution
        "spark.sql.codegen.wholeStage",
        "spark.sql.codegen.factoryMode"
    ]
    
    for config in important_configs:
        try:
            value = spark.conf.get(config)
            print(f"{config:50s} = {value}")
        except:
            print(f"{config:50s} = NOT SET")
    
    print("=" * 80)


def benchmark_optimization_pattern(pattern_func, *args, **kwargs):
    """
    Decorator to benchmark optimization pattern execution
    """
    @wraps(pattern_func)
    def wrapper(*args, **kwargs):
        print(f"\n[BENCHMARK] Starting: {pattern_func.__name__}")
        start_time = time.time()
        
        result = pattern_func(*args, **kwargs)
        
        end_time = time.time()
        execution_time = end_time - start_time
        print(f"[BENCHMARK] Completed: {pattern_func.__name__}")
        print(f"[BENCHMARK] Execution time: {execution_time:.3f} seconds")
        
        return result
    
    return wrapper

class OptimizationMetricsCollector:
    """
    Collects and analyzes optimization metrics from Spark queries
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
        self.metrics = []
    
    def collect_query_metrics(self, df, query_name):
        """
        Collect detailed metrics for a query execution
        """
        print(f"\n[METRICS] Collecting metrics for: {query_name}")
        
        # Trigger execution and collect metrics
        start_time = time.time()
        df.cache()
        row_count = df.count()
        execution_time = time.time() - start_time
        
        # Get partition information
        num_partitions = df.rdd.getNumPartitions()
        
        # Estimate data size
        df_size_mb = self._estimate_size(df)
        
        # Collect shuffle metrics (simplified)
        physical_plan = df._jdf.queryExecution().executedPlan().toString()
        shuffle_count = physical_plan.count("Exchange")
        
        metrics = {
            'query_name': query_name,
            'execution_time': execution_time,
            'row_count': row_count,
            'num_partitions': num_partitions,
            'estimated_size_mb': df_size_mb,
            'shuffle_operations': shuffle_count,
            'timestamp': time.time()
        }
        
        self.metrics.append(metrics)
        
        # Display metrics
        print(f"  Execution Time: {execution_time:.3f}s")
        print(f"  Row Count: {row_count:,}")
        print(f"  Partitions: {num_partitions}")
        print(f"  Estimated Size: {df_size_mb:.2f} MB")
        print(f"  Shuffle Operations: {shuffle_count}")
        
        df.unpersist()
        return metrics
    
    def _estimate_size(self, df):
        """Estimate DataFrame size in MB"""
        try:
            num_rows = df.count()
            num_cols = len(df.columns)
            # Rough estimation: 50 bytes per field
            size_bytes = num_rows * num_cols * 50
            return size_bytes / (1024 * 1024)
        except:
            return 0.0
    
    def generate_report(self):
        """Generate a summary report of all collected metrics"""
        if not self.metrics:
            print("\n[METRICS] No metrics collected")
            return
        
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("OPTIMIZATION METRICS REPORT")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        for metric in self.metrics:
            print(f"\nQuery: {metric['query_name']}")
            print(f"  Execution Time: {metric['execution_time']:.3f}s")
            print(f"  Rows: {metric['row_count']:,}")
            print(f"  Partitions: {metric['num_partitions']}")
            print(f"  Size: {metric['estimated_size_mb']:.2f} MB")
            print(f"  Shuffles: {metric['shuffle_operations']}")
        
        # Summary statistics
        total_time = sum(m['execution_time'] for m in self.metrics)
        avg_time = total_time / len(self.metrics)
        
        print("\n" + "-" * 80)
        print(f"Total Queries: {len(self.metrics)}")
        print(f"Total Execution Time: {total_time:.3f}s")
        print(f"Average Execution Time: {avg_time:.3f}s")
        print("=" * 80)


class OptimizationConfigManager:
    """
    Manages optimization configurations with profiles and rollback capability
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
        self.config_stack = []
        self.profiles = self._define_profiles()
    
    def _define_profiles(self):
        """Define predefined optimization profiles"""
        return {
            'high_performance': {
                'spark.sql.adaptive.enabled': 'true',
                'spark.sql.adaptive.coalescePartitions.enabled': 'true',
                'spark.sql.adaptive.skewJoin.enabled': 'true',
                'spark.sql.cbo.enabled': 'true',
                'spark.sql.cbo.joinReorder.enabled': 'true',
                'spark.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold': '10485760',
                'spark.sql.shuffle.partitions': '200'
            },
            'memory_optimized': {
                'spark.sql.adaptive.enabled': 'true',
                'spark.sql.adaptive.coalescePartitions.enabled': 'true',
                'spark.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold': '5242880',
                'spark.sql.shuffle.partitions': '100',
                'spark.sql.inMemoryColumnarStorage.compressed': 'true',
                'spark.sql.inMemoryColumnarStorage.batchSize': '20000'
            },
            'debugging': {
                'spark.sql.adaptive.enabled': 'false',
                'spark.sql.cbo.enabled': 'false',
                'spark.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold': '-1',
                'spark.sql.shuffle.partitions': '10',
                'spark.sql.planChangeLog.level': 'WARN'
            },
            'minimal_shuffle': {
                'spark.sql.adaptive.enabled': 'true',
                'spark.sql.adaptive.coalescePartitions.enabled': 'true',
                'spark.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold': '52428800',  # 50MB
                'spark.sql.shuffle.partitions': '50'
            }
        }
    
    def save_current_config(self):
        """Save current configuration to stack"""
        current_config = {}
        
        # Get all optimization-related configs
        all_configs = [
            'spark.sql.adaptive.enabled',
            'spark.sql.adaptive.coalescePartitions.enabled',
            'spark.sql.adaptive.skewJoin.enabled',
            'spark.sql.cbo.enabled',
            'spark.sql.cbo.joinReorder.enabled',
            'spark.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold',
            'spark.sql.shuffle.partitions'
        ]
        
        for config_key in all_configs:
            try:
                current_config[config_key] = self.spark.conf.get(config_key)
            except:
                current_config[config_key] = None
        
        self.config_stack.append(current_config)
        print(f"[CONFIG] Saved configuration (stack depth: {len(self.config_stack)})")
    
    def restore_config(self):
        """Restore previous configuration from stack"""
        if not self.config_stack:
            print("[CONFIG] No saved configuration to restore")
            return
        
        previous_config = self.config_stack.pop()
        
        for key, value in previous_config.items():
            if value is not None:
                self.spark.conf.set(key, value)
        
        print(f"[CONFIG] Restored configuration (stack depth: {len(self.config_stack)})")
    
    def apply_profile(self, profile_name):
        """Apply a predefined optimization profile"""
        if profile_name not in self.profiles:
            print(f"[CONFIG] Unknown profile: {profile_name}")
            return
        
        print(f"[CONFIG] Applying profile: {profile_name}")
        
        # Save current config before applying profile
        self.save_current_config()
        
        # Apply profile
        profile = self.profiles[profile_name]
        for key, value in profile.items():
            self.spark.conf.set(key, value)
            print(f"  {key} = {value}")
    
    def create_custom_profile(self, profile_name, config_dict):
        """Create a custom optimization profile"""
        self.profiles[profile_name] = config_dict
        print(f"[CONFIG] Created custom profile: {profile_name}")
    
    def list_profiles(self):
        """List all available profiles"""
        print("\n[CONFIG] Available Profiles:")
        for profile_name in self.profiles.keys():
            print(f"  - {profile_name}")


class OptimizationRecommender:
    """
    Provides recommendations for optimization strategies based on data characteristics
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
    
    def analyze_and_recommend(self, df, operation_type='join'):
        """
        Analyze DataFrame and recommend optimization strategy
        
        Args:
            df: DataFrame to analyze
            operation_type: 'join', 'aggregation', 'filter', or 'general'
        """
        print(f"\n[RECOMMENDER] Analyzing DataFrame for {operation_type} operation...")
        
        # Collect statistics
        row_count = df.count()
        num_partitions = df.rdd.getNumPartitions()
        num_columns = len(df.columns)
        
        print(f"  Rows: {row_count:,}")
        print(f"  Partitions: {num_partitions}")
        print(f"  Columns: {num_columns}")
        
        recommendations = []
        
        # Size-based recommendations
        estimated_size_mb = (row_count * num_columns * 50) / (1024 * 1024)
        print(f"  Estimated Size: {estimated_size_mb:.2f} MB")
        
        if estimated_size_mb < 10:
            recommendations.append({
                'category': 'Size',
                'recommendation': 'Use broadcast join for this small dataset',
                'action': 'Apply broadcast() hint or increase autoBroadcastJoinThreshold'
            })
        elif estimated_size_mb > 1000:
            recommendations.append({
                'category': 'Size',
                'recommendation': 'Large dataset - consider partitioning strategy',
                'action': 'Repartition data and enable adaptive query execution'
            })
        
        # Partition-based recommendations
        if num_partitions < 10 and row_count > 100000:
            recommendations.append({
                'category': 'Partitioning',
                'recommendation': 'Too few partitions for dataset size',
                'action': f'Repartition to at least {row_count // 10000} partitions'
            })
        elif num_partitions > 1000:
            recommendations.append({
                'category': 'Partitioning',
                'recommendation': 'Too many partitions - overhead concern',
                'action': 'Coalesce to fewer partitions (200-400 recommended)'
            })
        
        # Operation-specific recommendations
        if operation_type == 'join':
            recommendations.extend(self._join_recommendations(df, estimated_size_mb))
        elif operation_type == 'aggregation':
            recommendations.extend(self._aggregation_recommendations(df, num_partitions))
        elif operation_type == 'filter':
            recommendations.extend(self._filter_recommendations(df))
        
        # Display recommendations
        print("\n[RECOMMENDER] Recommendations:")
        for i, rec in enumerate(recommendations, 1):
            print(f"\n  {i}. [{rec['category']}] {rec['recommendation']}")
            print(f"     Action: {rec['action']}")
        
        return recommendations
    
    def _join_recommendations(self, df, size_mb):
        """Generate join-specific recommendations"""
        recs = []
        
        if size_mb < 10:
            recs.append({
                'category': 'Join Strategy',
                'recommendation': 'Ideal for broadcast join',
                'action': 'Use broadcast() hint on this DataFrame'
            })
        else:
            recs.append({
                'category': 'Join Strategy',
                'recommendation': 'Use sort-merge join with pre-partitioning',
                'action': 'Repartition both DataFrames on join key before joining'
            })
        
        return recs
    
    def _aggregation_recommendations(self, df, num_partitions):
        """Generate aggregation-specific recommendations"""
        recs = []
        
        recs.append({
            'category': 'Aggregation',
            'recommendation': 'Enable adaptive query execution for better partition management',
            'action': 'Set spark.sql.adaptive.enabled=true and spark.sql.adaptive.coalescePartitions.enabled=true'
        })
        
        if num_partitions > 500:
            recs.append({
                'category': 'Aggregation',
                'recommendation': 'High partition count may cause many small tasks',
                'action': 'Consider two-stage aggregation or reduce shuffle partitions'
            })
        
        return recs
    
    def _filter_recommendations(self, df):
        """Generate filter-specific recommendations"""
        recs = []
        
        recs.append({
            'category': 'Filter',
            'recommendation': 'Enable predicate pushdown for columnar formats',
            'action': 'Ensure spark.sql.parquet.filterPushdown=true for Parquet files'
        })
        
        return recs

def example_real_world_scenario(spark: SparkSession):
    """
    Real-world scenario: E-commerce data processing with optimization bypass
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("REAL-WORLD SCENARIO: E-COMMERCE DATA PROCESSING")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Initialize components
    config_manager = OptimizationConfigManager(spark)
    metrics_collector = OptimizationMetricsCollector(spark)
    recommender = OptimizationRecommender(spark)
    
    # Create realistic e-commerce data
    print("\n[SCENARIO] Creating e-commerce datasets...")
    
    
```python
    # Orders table (large, fact table)
    orders = spark.range(10000000).select(
        col("id").alias("order_id"),
        (col("id") % 500000).alias("customer_id"),
        (col("id") % 10000).alias("product_id"),
        (rand() * 1000).alias("order_amount"),
        (col("id") % 365).alias("order_date"),
        (col("id") % 100).alias("store_id")
    )
    
    # Customers table (medium dimension)
    customers = spark.range(500000).select(
        col("id").alias("customer_id"),
        concat(lit("Customer_"), col("id")).alias("customer_name"),
        (col("id") % 50).alias("region_id"),
        (col("id") % 5).alias("customer_segment")
    )
    
    # Products table (small dimension)
    products = spark.range(10000).select(
        col("id").alias("product_id"),
        concat(lit("Product_"), col("id")).alias("product_name"),
        (col("id") % 20).alias("category_id"),
        (rand() * 500).alias("unit_price")
    )
    
    # Stores table (very small dimension)
    stores = spark.range(100).select(
        col("id").alias("store_id"),
        concat(lit("Store_"), col("id")).alias("store_name"),
        (col("id") % 10).alias("store_region")
    )
    
    # Use case 1: Daily sales report with broadcast optimization
    print("\n" + "-" * 80)
    print("USE CASE 1: Daily Sales Report")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    # Get recommendations
    recommender.analyze_and_recommend(products, 'join')
    recommender.analyze_and_recommend(stores, 'join')
    
    # Apply high-performance profile
    config_manager.apply_profile('high_performance')
    
    # Perform analysis with broadcast joins for small tables
    daily_sales = orders \
        .join(broadcast(products), "product_id") \
        .join(broadcast(stores), "store_id") \
        .groupBy("order_date", "category_id", "store_region") \
        .agg(
            sum("order_amount").alias("total_sales"),
            count("order_id").alias("num_orders"),
            avg("order_amount").alias("avg_order_value")
        )
    
    # Collect metrics
    metrics_collector.collect_query_metrics(daily_sales, "Daily Sales Report")
    
    # Use case 2: Customer segmentation with skew handling
    print("\n" + "-" * 80)
    print("USE CASE 2: Customer Segmentation Analysis")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    # Analyze for potential skew
    manual_optimizer = ManualOptimizationPattern(spark)
    
    # Join orders with customers (potentially skewed)
    customer_orders = manual_optimizer.manual_join_optimization(
        orders, customers, "customer_id"
    )
    
    # Handle skew in customer distribution
    deskewed_orders = manual_optimizer.manual_skew_handling(
        customer_orders, "customer_id", skew_threshold=0.05
    )
    
    # Perform segmentation analysis
    customer_segments = deskewed_orders \
        .groupBy("customer_segment", "region_id") \
        .agg(
            sum("order_amount").alias("segment_revenue"),
            countDistinct("customer_id").alias("unique_customers"),
            avg("order_amount").alias("avg_customer_value")
        )
    
    metrics_collector.collect_query_metrics(customer_segments, "Customer Segmentation")
    
    # Use case 3: Product performance with manual optimization
    print("\n" + "-" * 80)
    print("USE CASE 3: Product Performance Analysis")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    # Switch to aggregation-optimized profile
    config_manager.apply_profile('memory_optimized')
    
    # Manual partition optimization for aggregation
    orders_partitioned = manual_optimizer.manual_partition_optimization(
        orders, ["product_id"], num_partitions=200
    )
    
    # Perform product analysis
    product_performance = orders_partitioned \
        .join(broadcast(products), "product_id") \
        .groupBy("product_id", "product_name", "category_id") \
        .agg(
            sum("order_amount").alias("total_revenue"),
            count("order_id").alias("units_sold"),
            avg("order_amount").alias("avg_sale_price")
        ) \
        .filter(col("total_revenue") > 10000) \
        .orderBy(col("total_revenue").desc())
    
    # Cache for reuse
    cached_performance = manual_optimizer.manual_caching_strategy(
        product_performance, "memory_and_disk"
    )
    
    metrics_collector.collect_query_metrics(cached_performance, "Product Performance")
    
    # Use case 4: Complex multi-table join with debug
    print("\n" + "-" * 80)
    print("USE CASE 4: Comprehensive Sales Analysis (All Tables)")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    # Enable debug mode
    debug_optimizer = DebugOptimizationPattern(spark)
    debug_optimizer.enable_debug_mode()
    
    # Complex join across all tables
    comprehensive_analysis = orders \
        .join(broadcast(products), "product_id") \
        .join(broadcast(stores), "store_id") \
        .join(customers, "customer_id") \
        .groupBy("store_region", "category_id", "customer_segment") \
        .agg(
            sum("order_amount").alias("total_revenue"),
            count("order_id").alias("total_orders"),
            countDistinct("customer_id").alias("unique_customers"),
            avg("order_amount").alias("avg_order_value")
        ) \
        .filter(col("total_revenue") > 50000)
    
    # Explain and inspect
    debug_optimizer.explain_query_plans(comprehensive_analysis, 'extended')
    debug_optimizer.inspect_shuffle_operations(comprehensive_analysis)
    
    metrics_collector.collect_query_metrics(comprehensive_analysis, "Comprehensive Analysis")
    
    # Generate final report
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("SCENARIO COMPLETION")
    print("=" * 80)
    metrics_collector.generate_report()
    
    # Restore original configuration
    config_manager.restore_config()
    
    # Cleanup
    cached_performance.unpersist()


def example_troubleshooting_performance_issue(spark: SparkSession):
    """
    Example: Using optimization bypass patterns to troubleshoot performance issues
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("TROUBLESHOOTING SCENARIO: Slow Query Investigation")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Create problematic dataset (with skew)
    print("\n[STEP 1] Creating dataset with performance issues...")
    
    # Normal data
    normal_data = spark.range(5000000).select(
        col("id"),
        (col("id") % 10000).alias("key"),
        (rand() * 1000).alias("value")
    )
    
    # Skewed data (one key has 50% of records)
    skewed_data = spark.range(5000000).select(
        col("id"),
        lit(9999).alias("key"),  # All records have same key
        (rand() * 1000).alias("value")
    )
    
    # Combine datasets
    problematic_df = normal_data.union(skewed_data)
    
    # Initial query (slow due to skew)
    print("\n[STEP 2] Running initial query (with issues)...")
    slow_query = problematic_df.groupBy("key").agg(
        sum("value").alias("total"),
        count("*").alias("count")
    )
    
    # Measure baseline performance
    debug_pattern = DebugOptimizationPattern(spark)
    metrics_collector = OptimizationMetricsCollector(spark)
    
    print("\n[STEP 3] Analyzing slow query...")
    debug_pattern.explain_query_plans(slow_query, 'extended')
    debug_pattern.inspect_shuffle_operations(slow_query)
    
    baseline_metrics = metrics_collector.collect_query_metrics(slow_query, "Baseline (Slow)")
    
    # Diagnose the issue
    print("\n[STEP 4] Diagnosing issues...")
    recommender = OptimizationRecommender(spark)
    recommendations = recommender.analyze_and_recommend(problematic_df, 'aggregation')
    
    # Check for skew
    print("\n[STEP 5] Checking for data skew...")
    key_distribution = problematic_df.groupBy("key").count()
    max_key_count = key_distribution.agg({"count": "max"}).collect()[0][0]
    total_count = problematic_df.count()
    skew_ratio = max_key_count / total_count
    
    print(f"  Maximum key count: {max_key_count:,}")
    print(f"  Total count: {total_count:,}")
    print(f"  Skew ratio: {skew_ratio:.2%}")
    
    if skew_ratio > 0.1:
        print("  ⚠️  SEVERE SKEW DETECTED!")
    
    # Apply fix: Manual skew handling
    print("\n[STEP 6] Applying fix: Manual skew handling...")
    manual_pattern = ManualOptimizationPattern(spark)
    
    fixed_df = manual_pattern.manual_skew_handling(
        problematic_df, "key", skew_threshold=0.05
    )
    
    # Use salted key for aggregation
    fixed_query = fixed_df.groupBy("salted_key").agg(
        sum("value").alias("total"),
        count("*").alias("count")
    ).groupBy(
        split(col("salted_key"), "_").getItem(0).alias("key")
    ).agg(
        sum("total").alias("total"),
        sum("count").alias("count")
    )
    
    # Measure improved performance
    print("\n[STEP 7] Measuring improved performance...")
    improved_metrics = metrics_collector.collect_query_metrics(fixed_query, "Fixed (Optimized)")
    
    # Compare results
    print("\n[STEP 8] Performance comparison...")
    print(f"  Baseline time: {baseline_metrics['execution_time']:.3f}s")
    print(f"  Optimized time: {improved_metrics['execution_time']:.3f}s")
    improvement = baseline_metrics['execution_time'] / improved_metrics['execution_time']
    print(f"  Improvement: {improvement:.2f}x faster")
    
    # Generate report
    metrics_collector.generate_report()


def example_adaptive_optimization_control(spark: SparkSession):
    """
    Example: Fine-grained control over Adaptive Query Execution
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("ADAPTIVE QUERY EXECUTION CONTROL")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Create test data
    df1 = spark.range(1000000).select(
        col("id"),
        (col("id") % 1000).alias("key"),
        (rand() * 1000).alias("value")
    )
    
    df2 = spark.range(10000).select(
        col("id").alias("key"),
        concat(lit("Label_"), col("id")).alias("label")
    )
    
    test_query = df1.join(df2, "key").groupBy("label").agg(
        sum("value").alias("total"),
        count("*").alias("count")
    )
    
    metrics_collector = OptimizationMetricsCollector(spark)
    
    # Test 1: AQE fully enabled
    print("\n[TEST 1] AQE Fully Enabled")
    spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "true")
    spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.coalescePartitions.enabled", "true")
    spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.skewJoin.enabled", "true")
    spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.localShuffleReader.enabled", "true")
    
    metrics_collector.collect_query_metrics(test_query, "AQE Fully Enabled")
    
    # Test 2: AQE with only partition coalescing
    print("\n[TEST 2] AQE - Partition Coalescing Only")
    spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "true")
    spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.coalescePartitions.enabled", "true")
    spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.skewJoin.enabled", "false")
    spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.localShuffleReader.enabled", "false")
    
    metrics_collector.collect_query_metrics(test_query, "AQE Coalesce Only")
    
    # Test 3: AQE with only skew join handling
    print("\n[TEST 3] AQE - Skew Join Only")
    spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "true")
    spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.coalescePartitions.enabled", "false")
    spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.skewJoin.enabled", "true")
    spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.localShuffleReader.enabled", "false")
    
    metrics_collector.collect_query_metrics(test_query, "AQE Skew Join Only")
    
    # Test 4: AQE completely disabled
    print("\n[TEST 4] AQE Completely Disabled")
    spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "false")
    
    metrics_collector.collect_query_metrics(test_query, "AQE Disabled")
    
    # Generate comparison report
    metrics_collector.generate_report()

    """
    
    @staticmethod

        """Print comprehensive best practices guide"""
        
        practices = """
╔════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║                    OPTIMIZATION BYPASS BEST PRACTICES                      ║
╚════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝

1. WHEN TO DISABLE OPTIMIZATIONS
   ✓ Debugging query plans and understanding execution
   ✓ Reproducing production issues in development
   ✓ Testing different execution strategies
   ✗ Never disable in production without thorough testing
   ✗ Don't disable globally - use selective disabling

2. SELECTIVE OPTIMIZATION GUIDELINES
   ✓ Profile your workload characteristics first
   ✓ Use different profiles for different query types
   ✓ Monitor metrics to validate optimization choices
   ✗ Don't apply one-size-fits-all optimization
   ✗ Avoid frequent profile switching in same job

3. OVERRIDE OPTIMIZATION BEST PRACTICES
   ✓ Use broadcast hints for tables < 10MB
   ✓ Pre-partition on join keys for large-large joins
   ✓ Override only when you have data distribution knowledge
   ✗ Don't override without
```python
   ✗ Don't override without measuring impact
   ✗ Avoid forcing strategies that conflict with data size

4. DEBUG OPTIMIZATION RECOMMENDATIONS
   ✓ Enable debug mode in development/staging only
   ✓ Use explain() with different modes to understand plans
   ✓ Collect statistics before making optimization decisions
   ✓ Compare logical, optimized, and physical plans
   ✗ Don't enable verbose logging in production
   ✗ Avoid analyzing every query - focus on slow ones

5. MANUAL OPTIMIZATION PRINCIPLES
   ✓ Understand your data distribution before manual tuning
   ✓ Handle data skew explicitly for skewed datasets
   ✓ Use appropriate caching strategy based on reuse patterns
   ✓ Partition data on frequently joined/grouped columns
   ✗ Don't over-partition (causes small file problem)
   ✗ Avoid manual optimization without benchmarking

6. GENERAL GUIDELINES
   ✓ Always measure before and after optimization changes
   ✓ Document why specific optimizations were applied
   ✓ Use configuration management for reproducibility
   ✓ Test optimizations with production-like data volumes
   ✗ Don't assume optimizations work the same across versions
   ✗ Avoid premature optimization - profile first

7. PERFORMANCE MONITORING
   ✓ Track execution time, shuffle size, and task duration
   ✓ Monitor partition distribution and skew metrics
   ✓ Use Spark UI to identify bottlenecks
   ✓ Set up alerts for performance degradation
   ✗ Don't ignore warning signs (stragglers, spills)
   ✗ Avoid optimization without baseline metrics

8. COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
   ✗ Broadcasting tables larger than executor memory
   ✗ Creating too many small partitions (overhead)
   ✗ Disabling AQE without understanding implications
   ✗ Ignoring data skew in aggregations and joins
   ✗ Not considering shuffle cost in optimization
   ✗ Over-caching DataFrames that aren't reused

9. WHEN TO USE EACH PATTERN
   
   DISABLE PATTERN:
   - Debugging complex query plans
   - Isolating optimizer-related bugs
   - Educational purposes
   
   SELECTIVE PATTERN:
   - Different workload types in same job
   - Migrating between Spark versions
   - A/B testing optimization strategies
   
   OVERRIDE PATTERN:
   - Known data distribution patterns
   - Specific join strategy requirements
   - Broadcast eligibility edge cases
   
   DEBUG PATTERN:
   - Performance troubleshooting
   - Understanding optimizer decisions
   - Validating optimization assumptions
   
   MANUAL PATTERN:
   - Data skew handling
   - Custom partitioning requirements
   - Fine-grained performance tuning

10. OPTIMIZATION CHECKLIST
    □ Profile current performance baseline
    □ Identify bottlenecks (CPU, I/O, shuffle, skew)
    □ Choose appropriate optimization pattern
    □ Test with representative data
    □ Measure improvement
    □ Document changes and rationale
    □ Monitor in production
    □ Iterate based on metrics

╚════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
        """
        
        print(practices)

        decision_tree = """

    │
    ├─ TOO MANY PARTITIONS
    │   ├─ After shuffle? → Use coalesce() (Manual Pattern)
    │   ├─ Initial data? → Reduce shuffle partitions (Selective Pattern)
    │   └─ Enable adaptive coalescing → AQE (Selective Pattern)
    │
    ├─ TOO FEW PARTITIONS
    │   ├─ Large dataset? → Repartition by key (Manual Pattern)
    │   ├─ Uneven distribution? → Increase shuffle partitions (Selective Pattern)
    │   └─ Check parallelism → Adjust executor cores
    │
    ├─ MEMORY ISSUES
    │   ├─ Broadcast too large? → Disable broadcast (Override Pattern)
    │   ├─ Excessive caching? → Unpersist unused DataFrames (Manual Pattern)
    │   └─ Spilling to disk? → Increase executor memory or reduce partitions
    │
    ├─ OPTIMIZER BUGS
    │   ├─ Incorrect plan? → Disable specific rules (Selective Pattern)
    │   ├─ Need debugging? → Enable debug mode (Debug Pattern)
    │   └─ Temporary workaround? → Disable optimization (Disable Pattern)
    │
    └─ UNKNOWN
        └─ Start with Debug Pattern to understand execution plan

╚════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
        """
        
        print(decision_tree)

class OptimizationValidator:
    """
    Validates optimization improvements and detects regressions
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
        self.baseline_metrics = {}
    
    def set_baseline(self, query_name, df):
        """Set baseline performance for a query"""
        print(f"\n[VALIDATOR] Setting baseline for: {query_name}")
        
        start_time = time.time()
        df.cache()
        count = df.count()
        execution_time = time.time() - start_time
        df.unpersist()
        
        self.baseline_metrics[query_name] = {
            'execution_time': execution_time,
            'count': count,
            'timestamp': time.time()
        }
        
        print(f"  Baseline time: {execution_time:.3f}s")
        print(f"  Record count: {count:,}")
    
    def validate_optimization(self, query_name, df, 
                             min_improvement=1.0, 
                             max_regression=0.9):
        """
        Validate that optimization meets improvement criteria
        
        Args:
            query_name: Name of the query
            df: Optimized DataFrame
            min_improvement: Minimum speedup required (1.0 = no regression)
            max_regression: Maximum allowed slowdown (0.9 = 10% slower)
        """
        if query_name not in self.baseline_metrics:
            print(f"[VALIDATOR] No baseline for {query_name}")
            return False
        
        print(f"\n[VALIDATOR] Validating optimization for: {query_name}")
        
        # Measure optimized performance
        start_time = time.time()
        df.cache()
        count = df.count()
        execution_time = time.time() - start_time
        df.unpersist()
        
        baseline = self.baseline_metrics[query_name]
        speedup = baseline['execution_time'] / execution_time
        
        print(f"  Baseline time: {baseline['execution_time']:.3f}s")
        print(f"  Optimized time: {execution_time:.3f}s")
        print(f"  Speedup: {speedup:.2f}x")
        
        # Validate correctness
        if count != baseline['count']:
            print(f"  ❌ VALIDATION FAILED: Count mismatch!")
            print(f"     Expected: {baseline['count']:,}, Got: {count:,}")
            return False
        
        # Validate performance
        if speedup < max_regression:
            print(f"  ❌ VALIDATION FAILED: Performance regression!")
            print(f"     Speedup {speedup:.2f}x < threshold {max_regression:.2f}x")
            return False
        elif speedup < min_improvement:
            print(f"  ⚠️  WARNING: Improvement below target")
            print(f"     Speedup {speedup:.2f}x < target {min_improvement:.2f}x")
            return True
        else:
            print(f"  ✅ VALIDATION PASSED: {speedup:.2f}x improvement")
            return True
    
    def compare_strategies(self, query_name, strategies_dict):
        """
        Compare multiple optimization strategies
        
        Args:
            query_name: Name of the query
            strategies_dict: Dict of {strategy_name: dataframe}
        """
        print(f"\n[VALIDATOR] Comparing strategies for: {query_name}")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        results = []
        
        for strategy_name, df in strategies_dict.items():
            print(f"\nTesting strategy: {strategy_name}")
            
            start_time = time.time()
            df.cache()
            count = df.count()
            execution_time = time.time() - start_time
            df.unpersist()
            
            results.append({
                'strategy': strategy_name,
                'time': execution_time,
                'count': count
            })
            
            print(f"  Time: {execution_time:.3f}s")
            print(f"  Count: {count:,}")
        
        # Find best strategy
        best_strategy = min(results, key=lambda x: x['time'])
        
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("COMPARISON RESULTS")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        for result in sorted(results, key=lambda x: x['time']):
            speedup = best_strategy['time'] / result['time']
            marker = "🏆" if result == best_strategy else "  "
            print(f"{marker} {result['strategy']:30s} {result['time']:8.3f}s  ({speedup:.2f}x)")
        
        print("=" * 80)
        
        return best_strategy

def parse_arguments():
    """Parse command-line arguments for running specific patterns"""
    import argparse
    
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description='PySpark Query Optimization Bypass Patterns',
        formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter,
        epilog="""
Examples:
  # Run all patterns
  python script.py --all
  
  # Run specific pattern
  python script.py --pattern disable
  
  # Run real-world scenario
  python script.py --scenario ecommerce
  
  # Run complete workflow
  python script.py --workflow
  
  # Run performance comparison
  python script.py --compare
        """
    )
    
    parser.add_argument(
        '--all',
        action='store_true',
        help='Run all optimization patterns'
    )
    
    parser.add_argument(
        '--pattern',
        choices=['disable', 'selective', 'override', 'debug', 'manual'],
        help='Run specific optimization pattern'
    )
    
    parser.add_argument(
        '--scenario',
        choices=['ecommerce', 'troubleshooting', 'adaptive'],
        help='Run specific real-world scenario'
    )
    
    parser.add_argument(
        '--workflow',
        action='store_true',
        help='Run complete optimization workflow'
    )
    
    parser.add_argument(
        '--compare',
        action='store_true',
        help='Run performance comparison'
    )
    
    parser.add_argument(
        '--best-practices',
        action='store_true',
        help='Display best practices guide'
    )
    
    return parser.parse_args()


def run_specific_pattern(spark, pattern_name):
    """Run a specific optimization pattern"""
    patterns = {
        'disable': OptimizationDisablePattern,
        'selective': SelectiveOptimizationPattern,
        'override': OverrideOptimizationPattern,
        'debug': DebugOptimizationPattern,
        'manual': ManualOptimizationPattern
    }
    
    if pattern_name in patterns:
        print(f"\n{'=' * 80}")
        print(f"Running Pattern: {pattern_name.upper()}")
        print('=' * 80)
        
        pattern_instance = patterns[pattern_name](spark)
        pattern_instance.example_usage()
    else:
        print(f"Unknown pattern: {pattern_name}")


def run_scenario(spark, scenario_name):
    """Run a specific real-world scenario"""
    scenarios = {
        'ecommerce': example_real_world_scenario,
        'troubleshooting': example_troubleshooting_performance_issue,
        'adaptive': example_adaptive_optimization_control
    }
    
    if scenario_name in scenarios:
        scenarios[scenario_name](spark)
    else:
        print(f"Unknown scenario: {scenario_name}")

class NotebookHelper:
    """
    Helper class for running patterns in Jupyter notebooks
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
        self.patterns = {
            'disable': OptimizationDisablePattern(spark),
            'selective': SelectiveOptimizationPattern(spark),
            'override': OverrideOptimizationPattern(spark),
            'debug': DebugOptimizationPattern(spark),
            'manual': ManualOptimizationPattern(spark)
        }
        self.orchestrator = OptimizationBypassOrchestrator(spark)
    
    def demo_pattern(self, pattern_name):
        """
        Run a pattern demonstration in notebook
        
        Usage:
            helper = NotebookHelper(spark)
            helper.demo_pattern('broadcast')
        """
        if pattern_name in self.patterns:
            self.patterns[pattern_name].example_usage()
        else:
            print(f"Available patterns: {list(self.patterns.keys())}")
    
    def quick_optimize(self, df, operation_type='join'):
        """
        Quick optimization helper for notebooks
        
        Args:
            df: DataFrame to optimize
            operation_type: 'join', 'aggregation', or 'filter'
        
        Returns:
            Optimized DataFrame
        """
        print(f"Quick optimization for {operation_type}...")
        
        if operation_type == 'join':
            # Estimate size and recommend strategy
            row_count = df.count()
            if row_count < 100000:
                print("→ Recommending broadcast join")
                return broadcast(df)
            else:
                print("→ Recommending pre-partitioning")
                return df.repartition(200)
        
        elif operation_type == 'aggregation':
            print("→ Applying aggregation optimizations")
            self.patterns['selective'].configure_selective_optimizations('aggregation')
            return df
        
        elif operation_type == 'filter':
            print("→ Applying filter optimizations")
            self.patterns['selective'].configure_selective_optimizations('filter')
            return df
        
        return df
    
    def explain_detailed(self, df):
        """
        Detailed explanation helper for notebooks
        """
        self.patterns['debug'].explain_query_plans(df, 'extended')
        self.patterns['debug'].inspect_shuffle_operations(df)
    
    def benchmark_query(self, df, query_name="Query"):
        """
        Quick benchmark helper for notebooks
        """
        collector = OptimizationMetricsCollector(self.spark)
        return collector.collect_query_metrics(df, query_name)

def generate_documentation():
    """
    Generate comprehensive documentation for all patterns
    """
    doc = """
# PySpark Query Optimization Bypass Patterns

## Table of Contents
1. [Pattern 1: Optimization Disable Pattern](#pattern-1)
2. [Pattern 2: Selective Optimization Pattern](#pattern-2)
3. [Pattern 3: Override Optimization Pattern](#pattern-3)
4. [Pattern 4: Debug Optimization Pattern](#pattern-4)
5. [Pattern 5: Manual Optimization Pattern](#pattern-5)
6. [Best Practices](#best-practices)
7. [Real-World Examples](#examples)

---

## Pattern 1: Optimization Disable Pattern

### Purpose
Completely disable Spark's query optimizer for specific operations.

### Use Cases
- Debugging query plans
- Understanding optimizer behavior
- Reproducing production issues
- Testing alternative execution strategies

### Example
```python
from pyspark.sql import SparkSession

spark = SparkSession.builder.appName("DisablePattern").getOrCreate()
disable_pattern = OptimizationDisablePattern(spark)

# Disable all optimizations
disable_pattern.disable_all_optimizations()

# Run your query
result = df.join(df2, "key").filter(col("value") > 100)

# Restore optimizations
disable_pattern.restore_optimizations()
```

### Key Configurations
- `spark.sql.optimizer.excludedRules`: Exclude specific optimizer rules
- `spark.sql.cbo.enabled`: Disable cost-based optimization
- `spark.sql.adaptive.enabled`: Disable adaptive query execution

---

## Pattern 2: Selective Optimization Pattern

### Purpose
Selectively enable/disable specific optimizations for different query types.

### Use Cases
- Different workload types in same job
- Fine-tuned optimization per operation
- A/B testing optimization strategies

### Example
```python
selective_pattern = SelectiveOptimizationPattern(spark)

# For aggregation-heavy queries
selective_pattern.configure_selective_optimizations('aggregation')
result = df.groupBy("key").agg(sum("value"))

# For join-heavy queries
selective_pattern.configure_selective_optimizations('join')
result = df1.join(df2, "key")
```

### Available Profiles
- `aggregation`: Optimized for groupBy operations
- `join`: Optimized for join operations
- `filter`: Optimized for filter operations
- `custom`: User-defined optimization profile

---

## Pattern 3: Override Optimization Pattern

### Purpose
Override optimizer decisions with explicit hints and directives.

### Use Cases
- Known data distribution patterns
- Specific join strategy requirements
- Manual control over execution strategy

### Example
```python
override_pattern = OverrideOptimizationPattern(spark)

# Force broadcast join
result = override_pattern.force_broadcast_join(large_df, small_df, "key")

# Force specific join strategy
result = override_pattern.override_join_strategy(
    df1, df2, "key", strategy='SHUFFLE_HASH'
)

# Force repartitioning
result = override_pattern.force_repartition(df, 100, "partition_key")
```

### Join Strategies
- `BROADCAST`: Broadcast hash join
- `MERGE`: Sort-merge join
- `SHUFFLE_HASH`: Shuffle hash join
- `SHUFFLE_REPLICATE_NL`: Shuffle replicate nested loop join

---

## Pattern 4: Debug Optimization Pattern

### Purpose
Enable detailed logging and inspection of optimization decisions.

### Use Cases
- Performance troubleshooting
- Understanding optimizer behavior
- Validating optimization assumptions

### Example
```python
debug_pattern = DebugOptimizationPattern(spark)

# Enable debug mode
debug_pattern.enable_debug_mode()

# Explain query plans
debug_pattern.explain_query_plans(df, mode='extended')

# Inspect shuffle operations
debug_pattern.inspect_shuffle_operations(df)

# Compare execution plans
debug_pattern.compare_execution_plans(df, "My Query")
```

### Explain Modes
- `simple`: Basic physical plan
- `extended`: Logical, optimized, and physical plans
- `codegen`: Generated code
- `cost`: Cost-based statistics
- `formatted`: Formatted output

---

## Pattern 5: Manual Optimization Pattern

### Purpose
Manually optimize queries by controlling execution strategy.

### Use Cases
- Data skew handling
- Custom partitioning requirements
- Fine-grained performance tuning

### Example
```python
manual_pattern = ManualOptimizationPattern(spark)

# Handle data skew
deskewed_df = manual_pattern.manual_skew_handling(df, "skewed_column")

# Optimize partitioning
optimized_df = manual_pattern.manual_partition_optimization(
    df, ["partition_col"], num_partitions=200
)

# Optimize join
result = manual_pattern.manual_join_optimization(large_df, small_df, "key")

# Apply caching strategy
cached_df = manual_pattern.manual_caching_strategy(df, "memory_and_disk")
```

### Caching Strategies
- `memory`: MEMORY_ONLY
- `memory_and_disk`: MEMORY_AND_DISK
- `disk`: DISK_ONLY
- `memory_ser`: MEMORY_ONLY_SER

---

## Best Practices

### When to Use Each Pattern

1. **Disable Pattern**
   - ✅ Debugging and development
   - ✅ Understanding query execution
   - ❌ Production use (without testing)

2. **Selective Pattern**
   - ✅ Mixed workload types
   - ✅ Performance tuning
   - ✅ Version migrations

3. **Override Pattern**
   - ✅ Known data characteristics
   - ✅ Specific requirements
   - ❌ Without data knowledge

4. **Debug Pattern**
   - ✅ Performance issues
   - ✅ Development/staging
   - ❌ Production (verbose logging)

5. **Manual Pattern**
   - ✅ Data skew
   - ✅ Custom requirements
   - ✅ After profiling

### Performance Checklist

- [ ] Profile baseline performance
- [ ] Identify bottlenecks
- [ ] Choose appropriate pattern
- [ ] Test with representative data
- [ ] Measure improvement
- [ ] Document changes
- [ ] Monitor in production

class ProductionOptimizationManager:
    """
    Production-ready optimization manager with monitoring and alerting
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession, config_path=None):
        self.spark = spark
        self.config_path = config_path
        self.execution_history = []
        self.alert_thresholds = {
            'execution_time_multiplier': 2.0,  # Alert if 2x slower than baseline
            'shuffle_size_mb': 10000,  # Alert if shuffle > 10GB
            'partition_skew_ratio': 10.0  # Alert if max/avg partition > 10x
        }
    
    def load_configuration(self):
        """Load optimization configuration from file"""
        if self.config_path:
            try:
                import json
                with open(self.config_path, 'r') as f:
                    config = json.load(f)
                
                for key, value in config.items():
                    self.spark.conf.set(key, str(value))
                    print(f"Loaded config: {key} = {value}")
                
                return True
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"Error loading configuration: {e}")
                return False
        return False
    
    def save_configuration(self, output_path):
        """Save current optimization configuration to file"""
        import json
        
        config_keys = [
            "spark.sql.adaptive.enabled",
            "spark.sql.adaptive.coalescePartitions.enabled",
            "spark.sql.adaptive.skewJoin.enabled",
            "spark.sql.cbo.enabled",
            "spark.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold",
            "spark.sql.shuffle.partitions"
        ]
        
        config = {}
        for key in config_keys:
            try:
                config[key] = self.spark.conf.get(key)
            except:
                pass
        
        with open(output_path, 'w') as f:
            json.dump(config, f, indent=2)
        
        print(f"Configuration saved to {output_path}")
    
    def monitor_execution(self, df, query_name, baseline_time=None):
        """
        Monitor query execution and alert on anomalies
        """
        print(f"\n[MONITOR] Executing: {query_name}")
        
        start_time = time.time()
        
        # Execute query
        df.cache()
        count = df.count()
        
        execution_time = time.time() - start_time
        
        # Collect metrics
        num_partitions = df.rdd.getNumPartitions()
        physical_plan = df._jdf.queryExecution().executedPlan().toString()
        shuffle_count = physical_plan.count("Exchange")
        
        metrics = {
            'query_name': query_name,
            'timestamp': time.time(),
            'execution_time': execution_time,
            'count': count,
            'num_partitions': num_partitions,
            'shuffle_count': shuffle_count
        }
        
        self.execution_history.append(metrics)
        
        # Check alerts
        alerts = []
        
        if baseline_time and execution_time > baseline_time * self.alert_thresholds['execution_time_multiplier']:
            alerts.append(f"⚠️  SLOW EXECUTION: {execution_time:.2f}s (baseline: {baseline_time:.2f}s)")
        
        if shuffle_count > 10:
            alerts.append(f"⚠️  HIGH SHUFFLE COUNT: {shuffle_count} exchanges")
        
        # Display results
        print(f"  Execution time: {execution_time:.3f}s")
        print(f"  Record count: {count:,}")
        print(f"  Partitions: {num_partitions}")
        print(f"  Shuffles: {shuffle_count}")
        
        if alerts:
            print("\n  ALERTS:")
            for alert in alerts:
                print(f"  {alert}")
        
        df.unpersist()
        
        return metrics
    
    def generate_monitoring_report(self, output_path=None):
        """Generate monitoring report from execution history"""
        if not self.execution_history:
            print("No execution history available")
            return
        
        report = []
        report.append("=" * 80)
        report.append("OPTIMIZATION MONITORING REPORT")
        report.append("=" * 80)
        report.append(f"Total Queries Executed: {len(self.execution_history)}")
        report.append("")
        
        # Summary statistics
        total_time = sum(m['execution_time'] for m in self.execution_history)
        avg_time = total_time / len(self.execution_history)
        max_time = max(m['execution_time'] for m in self.execution_history)
        min_time = min(m['execution_time'] for m in self.execution_history)
        
        report.append(f"Total Execution Time: {total_time:.2f}s")
        report.append(f"Average Execution Time: {avg_time:.2f}s")
        report.append(f"Max Execution Time: {max_time:.2f}s")
        report.append(f"Min Execution Time: {min_time:.2f}s")
        report.append("")
        
        # Per-query details
        report.append("Query Details:")
        report.append("-" * 80)
        
        for metrics in self.execution_history:
            report.append(f"\nQuery: {metrics['query_name']}")
            report.append(f"  Time: {metrics['execution_time']:.3f}s")
            report.append(f"  Count: {metrics['count']:,}")
            report.append(f"  Partitions: {metrics['num_partitions']}")
            report.append(f"  Shuffles: {metrics['shuffle_count']}")
        
        report.append("=" * 80)
        
        # Print report
        report_text = "\n".join(report)
        print(report_text)
        
        # Save to file if requested
        if output_path:
            with open(output_path, 'w') as f:
                f.write(report_text)
            print(f"\nReport saved to {output_path}")
        
        return report_text

class OptimizationPatternTests:
    """
    Test suite for optimization patterns
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
        self.test_results = []
    
    def run_all_tests(self):
        """Run all tests"""
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("RUNNING OPTIMIZATION PATTERN TESTS")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        tests = [
            self.test_disable_pattern,
            self.test_selective_pattern,
            self.test_override_pattern,
            self.test_debug_pattern,
            self.test_manual_pattern
        ]
        
        for test in tests:
            try:
                print(f"\n[TEST] {test.__name__}")
                test()
                self.test_results.append((test.__name__, "PASSED", None))
                print(f"✅ {test.__name__} PASSED")
            except Exception as e:
                self.test_results.append((test.__name__, "FAILED", str(e)))
                print(f"❌ {test.__name__} FAILED: {e}")
        
        # Print summary
        self.print_test_summary()
    
    def test_disable_pattern(self):
        """Test optimization disable pattern"""
        pattern = OptimizationDisablePattern(self.spark)
        
        # Test disable
        pattern.disable_all_optimizations()
        assert self.spark.conf.get("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled") == "false"
        
        # Test restore
        pattern.restore_optimizations()
        
    def test_selective_pattern(self):
        """Test selective optimization pattern"""
        pattern = SelectiveOptimizationPattern(self.spark)
        
        # Test profile application
        pattern.configure_selective_optimizations('aggregation')
        assert self.spark.conf.get("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled") == "true"
        
    def test_override_pattern(self):
        """Test override optimization pattern"""
        pattern = OverrideOptimizationPattern(self.spark)
        
        df1 = self.spark.range(100)
        df2 = self.spark.range(10)
        
        # Test broadcast join
        result = pattern.force_broadcast_join(df1, df2, "id")
        assert result is not None
        
    def test_debug_pattern(self):
        """Test debug optimization pattern"""
        pattern = DebugOptimizationPattern(self.spark)
        
        # Test debug mode enable
        pattern.enable_debug_mode()
        
        df = self.spark.range(100)
        pattern.explain_query_plans(df, 'simple')
        
    def test_manual_pattern(self):
        """Test manual optimization pattern"""
        pattern = ManualOptimizationPattern(self.spark)
        
        df = self.spark.range(1000).withColumn("key", col("id") % 10)
        
        # Test partition optimization
        result = pattern.manual_partition_optimization(df, ["key"], 10)
        assert result.rdd.getNumPartitions() == 10
        
    def print_test_summary(self):
        """Print test summary"""
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("TEST SUMMARY")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        passed = sum(1 for _, status, _ in self.test_results if status == "PASSED")
        failed = sum(1 for _, status, _ in self.test_results if status == "FAILED")
        
        print(f"Total Tests: {len(self.test_results)}")
        print(f"Passed: {passed}")
        print(f"Failed: {failed}")
        print("")
        
        if failed > 0:
            print("Failed Tests:")
            for name, status, error in self.test_results:
                if status == "FAILED":
                    print(f"  ❌ {name}: {error}")
        
        print("=" * 80)

def comprehensive_production_example():
    """
    Comprehensive example for production use
    """
    print("\n" + "╔" + "=" * 78 + "╗")
    print("║" + " " * 20 + "PRODUCTION OPTIMIZATION EXAMPLE" + " " * 26 + "║")
    print("╚" + "=" * 78 + "╝")
    
    # Initialize Spark with production settings
    spark = SparkSession.builder \
        .appName("Production Optimization") \
        .config("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "true") \
        .config("spark.sql.adaptive.coalescePartitions.enabled", "true") \
        .config("spark.sql.adaptive.skewJoin.enabled", "true") \
        .config("spark.sql.cbo.enabled", "true") \
        .config("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "200") \
        .config("spark.serializer", "org.apache.spark.serializer.KryoSerializer") \
        .getOrCreate()
    
    try:
        # Initialize production manager
        prod_manager = ProductionOptimizationManager(spark)
        
        # Create sample production workload
        print("\n[PRODUCTION] Creating sample workload...")
        
        transactions = spark.range(10000000).select(
            col("id").alias("txn_id"),
            (col("id") % 100000).alias("customer_id"),
            (col("id") % 5000).alias("product_id"),
            (rand() * 1000).alias("amount"),
            (col("id") % 365).alias("day")
        )
        
        customers = spark.range(100000).select(
            col("id").alias("customer_id"),
            concat(lit("Customer_"), col("id")).alias("name")
        )
        
        products = spark.range(5000).select(
            col("id").alias("product_id"),
            concat(lit("Product_"), col("id")).alias("product_name")
        )
        
        # Query 1: Daily revenue
        print("\n[QUERY 1] Daily Revenue Report")
        daily_revenue = transactions \
            .join(broadcast(products), "product_id") \
            .groupBy("day", "product_name") \
            .agg(sum("amount").alias("revenue"))
        
        prod_manager.monitor_execution(daily_revenue, "Daily Revenue")
        
        # Query 2: Customer analytics
        print("\n[QUERY 2] Customer Analytics")
        customer_analytics = transactions \
            .join(customers, "customer_id") \
            .groupBy("customer_id", "name") \
            .agg(
                sum("amount").alias("total_spent"),
                count("*").alias("num_transactions")
            )
        
        prod_manager.monitor_execution(customer_analytics, "Customer Analytics")
        
        # Generate report
        print("\n[PRODUCTION] Generating monitoring report...")
        prod_manager.generate_monitoring_report("optimization_report.txt")
        
        # Save configuration
        prod_manager.save_configuration("production_config.json")
        
        print("\n✅ Production example completed successfully")
        
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"\n❌ Error in production example: {e}")
        import traceback
        traceback.print_exc()
    
    finally:
        spark.stop()
