    # Demonstrate a simplified version of Case Study 1
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("CASE STUDY 1 IMPLEMENTATION EXAMPLE")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Simulate e-commerce data
    print("\nGenerating sample e-commerce data...")
    
    # Orders (large table)
    orders = [
        (i, i % 50000, i % 100, f"2024-01-{(i % 28) + 1:02d}", 
         i * 50, ["pending", "confirmed", "shipped", "delivered"][i % 4])
        for i in range(1, 100001)
    ]
    
    # Products (medium table)
    products = [
        (i, f"Product_{i}", f"Category_{i % 20}", i * 10, i % 1000)
        for i in range(1, 101)
    ]
    
    # Inventory (small table - for broadcast)
    inventory = [
        (i, 1000 + (i * 10), ["in_stock", "low_stock", "out_of_stock"][i % 3])
        for i in range(1, 101)
    ]
    
    orders_schema = StructType([
        StructField("order_id", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("customer_id", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("product_id", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("order_date", StringType(), False),
        StructField("amount", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("status", StringType(), False)
    ])
    
    products_schema = StructType([
        StructField("product_id", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("product_name", StringType(), False),
        StructField("category", StringType(), False),
        StructField("price", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("stock_qty", IntegerType(), False)
    ])
    
    inventory_schema = StructType([
        StructField("product_id", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("available_qty", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("stock_status", StringType(), False)
    ])
    
    orders_df = spark.createDataFrame(orders, orders_schema)
    products_df = spark.createDataFrame(products, products_schema)
    inventory_df = spark.createDataFrame(inventory, inventory_schema)
    
    # Implementation 1: Real-time inventory check (Local-Fragment)
    print("\n1. Real-time Inventory Check (Local-Fragment Pattern)")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    inventory_check = orders_df \
        .filter(col("status") == "pending") \
        .join(broadcast(inventory_df), "product_id", "left") \
        .select(
            "order_id",
            "product_id",
            "amount",
            "stock_status",
            when(col("stock_status") == "out_of_stock", "HOLD")
            .when(col("stock_status") == "low_stock", "PRIORITY")
            .otherwise("PROCESS").alias("order_action")
        )
    
    print("Orders with inventory status:")
    inventory_check.show(10)
    print(f"Execution pattern: Broadcast join (no shuffle)")
    
    # Implementation 2: Customer analytics (Hybrid-Fragment)
    print("\n2. Customer Analytics Dashboard (Hybrid-Fragment Pattern)")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    customer_analytics = orders_df \
        .join(products_df, "product_id", "inner") \
        .join(broadcast(inventory_df), "product_id", "left") \
        .groupBy("customer_id", "category") \
        .agg(
            count("order_id").alias("order_count"),
            sum("amount").alias("total_spent"),
            avg("amount").alias("avg_order_value"),
            countDistinct("product_id").alias("unique_products")
        ) \
        .withColumn("customer_rank",
                   rank().over(Window.partitionBy("category")
                              .orderBy(desc("total_spent")))) \
        .filter(col("customer_rank") <= 10)
    
    print("Top 10 customers by category:")
    customer_analytics.show(20)
    print(f"Execution pattern: Hybrid (broadcast + distributed aggregation + window)")
    
    # Implementation 3: Fraud detection (Multi-Fragment)
    print("\n3. Fraud Detection Analysis (Multi-Fragment Pattern)")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    # Define time window for velocity checks
    from pyspark.sql.functions import to_date, count, sum as _sum
    
    fraud_analysis = orders_df \
        .withColumn("order_date_parsed", to_date(col("order_date"))) \
        .groupBy("customer_id", "order_date_parsed") \
        .agg(
            count("order_id").alias("daily_orders"),
            _sum("amount").alias("daily_amount")
        ) \
        .withColumn("fraud_score",
                   when(col("daily_orders") > 10, 100)
                   .when(col("daily_amount") > 50000, 80)
                   .when(col("daily_orders") > 5, 50)
                   .otherwise(0)) \
        .filter(col("fraud_score") > 0) \
        .orderBy(desc("fraud_score"))
    
    print("Potential fraud cases:")
    fraud_analysis.show(10)
    print(f"Execution pattern: Multi-fragment (multiple aggregations)")
    
    # Implementation 4: Daily sales report (Multi-Fragment)
    print("\n4. Daily Sales Report (Multi-Fragment Pattern)")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    daily_sales = orders_df \
        .join(products_df, "product_id", "inner") \
        .groupBy("order_date", "category", "status") \
        .agg(
            count("order_id").alias("order_count"),
            _sum("amount").alias("revenue"),
            avg("amount").alias("avg_order_value"),
            countDistinct("customer_id").alias("unique_customers")
        ) \
        .orderBy("order_date", desc("revenue"))
    
    print("Daily sales summary:")
    daily_sales.show(15)
    print(f"Execution pattern: Multi-fragment (groupBy with multiple aggregations)")

def performance_tuning_workshop():
    """
    Interactive workshop for performance tuning different patterns
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)

    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Create test dataset
    print("\nCreating test dataset for tuning exercises...")
    
    test_data = [

        for i in range(1, 1000001)
    ]
    
    test_schema = StructType([
        StructField("transaction_id", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("user_id", StringType(), False),
        StructField("product_id", StringType(), False),
        StructField("transaction_date", StringType(), False),
        StructField("amount", IntegerType(), False)
    ])
    
    test_df = spark.createDataFrame(test_data, test_schema)
    
    # Exercise 1: Optimize shuffle partitions

    print("EXERCISE 1: Optimizing Shuffle Partitions")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    print("\nScenario: Aggregation query is running slow")
    print("Task: Find optimal partition count")
    
    partition_counts = [50, 200, 500, 1000]
    
    print(f"\n{'Partitions':<15} {'Execution Time':<20} {'Tasks':<10}")
    print("-" * 45)
    
    for partition_count in partition_counts:
        spark.conf.set("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", partition_count)
        
        start = time.time()
        result = test_df.groupBy("user_id").agg(_sum("amount").alias("total"))
        count = result.count()
        duration = time.time() - start
        
        print(f"{partition_count:<15} {duration:<20.4f} {result.rdd.getNumPartitions():<10}")
    
    print("\nRecommendation: Choose partition count that balances:")
    print("- Enough parallelism (2-3x CPU cores)")
    print("- Not too many small tasks (overhead)")
    print("- Each partition ~128MB-1GB of data")
    
    # Exercise 2: Broadcast vs Shuffle Join

    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Create dimension table
    dim_data = [(f"product_{i}", f"Category_{i % 50}", i * 100) 
                for i in range(1, 1001)]
    dim_schema = StructType([
        StructField("product_id", StringType(), False),
        StructField("category", StringType(), False),
        StructField("price", IntegerType(), False)
    ])
    dim_df = spark.createDataFrame(dim_data, dim_schema)
    
    print("\nComparing join strategies...")
    print(f"Fact table size: {test_df.count()} rows")
    print(f"Dimension table size: {dim_df.count()} rows")
    
    # Shuffle join
    print("\n1. Shuffle Join:")
    spark.conf.set("spark.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold", "-1")
    start = time.time()
    shuffle_join = test_df.join(dim_df, "product_id", "inner")
    shuffle_count = shuffle_join.count()
    shuffle_time = time.time() - start
    print(f"   Execution time: {shuffle_time:.4f} seconds")
    
    # Broadcast join
    print("\n2. Broadcast Join:")
    spark.conf.set("spark.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold", "10MB")
    start = time.time()
    broadcast_join = test_df.join(broadcast(dim_df), "product_id", "inner")
    broadcast_count = broadcast_join.count()
    broadcast_time = time.time() - start
    print(f"   Execution time: {broadcast_time:.4f} seconds")
    
    improvement = ((shuffle_time - broadcast_time) / shuffle_time) * 100
    print(f"\nPerformance improvement: {improvement:.2f}%")
    print(f"Recommendation: Use broadcast for dimension tables < 100MB")
    
    # Exercise 3: Caching strategy
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("EXERCISE 3: Caching Strategy")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    print("\nScenario: Multiple queries on same filtered dataset")
    
    # Without caching
    print("\n1. Without caching:")
    filtered_df = test_df.filter(col("amount") > 5000)
    
    start = time.time()
    query1 = filtered_df.groupBy("user_id").count().count()
    query2 = filtered_df.groupBy("product_id").avg("amount").count()
    query3 = filtered_df.groupBy("transaction_date").sum("amount").count()
    no_cache_time = time.time() - start
    print(f"   Total execution time: {no_cache_time:.4f} seconds")
    
    # With caching
    print("\n2. With caching:")
    cached_filtered_df = test_df.filter(col("amount") > 5000).cache()
    cached_filtered_df.count()  # Materialize cache
    
    start = time.time()
    query1 = cached_filtered_df.groupBy("user_id").count().count()
    query2 = cached_filtered_df.groupBy("product_id").avg("amount").count()
    query3 = cached_filtered_df.
```python
    query3 = cached_filtered_df.groupBy("transaction_date").sum("amount").count()
    cache_time = time.time() - start
    print(f"   Total execution time: {cache_time:.4f} seconds")
    
    improvement = ((no_cache_time - cache_time) / no_cache_time) * 100
    print(f"\nPerformance improvement: {improvement:.2f}%")
    print(f"Recommendation: Cache when reusing filtered/transformed data")
    
    # Cleanup cache
    cached_filtered_df.unpersist()
    
    # Exercise 4: Data skew handling
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("EXERCISE 4: Handling Data Skew")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Create skewed dataset
    skewed_data = []
    for i in range(1, 100001):
        if i <= 50000:  # 50% of data has same key
            key = "POPULAR_PRODUCT"
        else:
            key = f"product_{i % 1000}"
        skewed_data.append((i, key, i * 10))
    
    skewed_schema = StructType([
        StructField("id", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("product_key", StringType(), False),
        StructField("value", IntegerType(), False)
    ])
    
    skewed_df = spark.createDataFrame(skewed_data, skewed_schema)
    
    print("\nScenario: Aggregation on skewed data")
    print(f"Dataset size: {skewed_df.count()} rows")
    print("50% of data has same key (POPULAR_PRODUCT)")
    
    # Without skew handling
    print("\n1. Without skew handling:")
    start = time.time()
    normal_agg = skewed_df.groupBy("product_key").agg(_sum("value").alias("total"))
    normal_count = normal_agg.count()
    normal_time = time.time() - start
    print(f"   Execution time: {normal_time:.4f} seconds")
    print(f"   Note: One task processes 50% of data (bottleneck)")
    
    # With salting
    print("\n2. With salting:")
    start = time.time()
    salted_agg = skewed_df \
        .withColumn("salt", (rand() * 10).cast("int")) \
        .withColumn("salted_key", concat(col("product_key"), lit("_"), col("salt"))) \
        .groupBy("salted_key") \
        .agg(_sum("value").alias("partial_total")) \
        .withColumn("original_key", 
                   when(col("salted_key").contains("POPULAR_PRODUCT"), 
                        lit("POPULAR_PRODUCT"))
                   .otherwise(split(col("salted_key"), "_").getItem(0))) \
        .groupBy("original_key") \
        .agg(_sum("partial_total").alias("total"))
    
    salted_count = salted_agg.count()
    salted_time = time.time() - start
    print(f"   Execution time: {salted_time:.4f} seconds")
    print(f"   Note: Skewed key split into 10 partitions")
    
    improvement = ((normal_time - salted_time) / normal_time) * 100
    print(f"\nPerformance improvement: {improvement:.2f}%")
    print(f"Recommendation: Use salting for highly skewed keys")
    
    # Exercise 5: Predicate pushdown
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("EXERCISE 5: Predicate Pushdown Optimization")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    print("\nScenario: Filter after join vs filter before join")
    
    # Filter after join (inefficient)
    print("\n1. Filter AFTER join:")
    start = time.time()
    inefficient = test_df \
        .join(dim_df, "product_id", "inner") \
        .filter(col("amount") > 8000) \
        .filter(col("price") > 5000)
    inefficient_count = inefficient.count()
    inefficient_time = time.time() - start
    print(f"   Execution time: {inefficient_time:.4f} seconds")
    print(f"   Result count: {inefficient_count}")
    
    # Filter before join (efficient)
    print("\n2. Filter BEFORE join:")
    start = time.time()
    efficient = test_df \
        .filter(col("amount") > 8000) \
        .join(dim_df.filter(col("price") > 5000), "product_id", "inner")
    efficient_count = efficient.count()
    efficient_time = time.time() - start
    print(f"   Execution time: {efficient_time:.4f} seconds")
    print(f"   Result count: {efficient_count}")
    
    improvement = ((inefficient_time - efficient_time) / inefficient_time) * 100
    print(f"\nPerformance improvement: {improvement:.2f}%")
    print(f"Recommendation: Apply filters before joins to reduce data volume")

def comprehensive_example():
    """
    A comprehensive example combining all patterns in a real-world scenario
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("COMPREHENSIVE REAL-WORLD EXAMPLE")
    print("E-Commerce Data Pipeline with All Patterns")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    print("\nScenario: End-to-end e-commerce analytics pipeline")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Step 1: Create sample datasets
    print("\n[Step 1] Creating sample datasets...")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    # Large fact table: Orders
    orders_data = [
        (i, i % 100000, i % 10000, i % 1000, 
         f"2024-01-{(i % 28) + 1:02d}", i * 50,
         ["pending", "confirmed", "shipped", "delivered", "cancelled"][i % 5])
        for i in range(1, 500001)
    ]
    
    # Medium dimension: Products
    products_data = [
        (i, f"Product_{i}", f"Category_{i % 100}", i * 10, 
         ["Electronics", "Clothing", "Food", "Books", "Toys"][i % 5])
        for i in range(1, 10001)
    ]
    
    # Small dimension: Categories (for broadcast)
    categories_data = [
        (f"Category_{i}", f"Department_{i % 20}", i % 5)
        for i in range(1, 101)
    ]
    
    # Small reference: Regions (for broadcast)
    regions_data = [
        (i, f"Region_{i}", f"Country_{i % 10}")
        for i in range(1, 1001)
    ]
    
    # Define schemas
    orders_schema = StructType([
        StructField("order_id", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("customer_id", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("product_id", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("region_id", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("order_date", StringType(), False),
        StructField("amount", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("status", StringType(), False)
    ])
    
    products_schema = StructType([
        StructField("product_id", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("product_name", StringType(), False),
        StructField("category_name", StringType(), False),
        StructField("price", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("department_type", StringType(), False)
    ])
    
    categories_schema = StructType([
        StructField("category_name", StringType(), False),
        StructField("department", StringType(), False),
        StructField("priority", IntegerType(), False)
    ])
    
    regions_schema = StructType([
        StructField("region_id", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("region_name", StringType(), False),
        StructField("country", StringType(), False)
    ])
    
    # Create DataFrames
    orders_df = spark.createDataFrame(orders_data, orders_schema)
    products_df = spark.createDataFrame(products_data, products_schema)
    categories_df = spark.createDataFrame(categories_data, categories_schema)
    regions_df = spark.createDataFrame(regions_data, regions_schema)
    
    print(f"Orders: {orders_df.count()} rows")
    print(f"Products: {products_df.count()} rows")
    print(f"Categories: {categories_df.count()} rows")
    print(f"Regions: {regions_df.count()} rows")
    
    # Step 2: Data Quality Checks (Single-Fragment Pattern)
    print("\n[Step 2] Data Quality Checks - SINGLE-FRAGMENT PATTERN")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    # Simple filters and validations
    quality_checks = orders_df \
        .filter(col("amount") > 0) \
        .filter(col("order_date").isNotNull()) \
        .withColumn("is_valid", 
                   when((col("amount") > 0) & (col("status").isNotNull()), True)
                   .otherwise(False))
    
    valid_orders = quality_checks.filter(col("is_valid") == True)
    invalid_count = quality_checks.filter(col("is_valid") == False).count()
    
    print(f"Valid orders: {valid_orders.count()}")
    print(f"Invalid orders: {invalid_count}")
    print("Pattern: Single-fragment (filter + withColumn)")
    
    # Step 3: Enrich with Regions (Local-Fragment Pattern)
    print("\n[Step 3] Enrich with Region Data - LOCAL-FRAGMENT PATTERN")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    # Broadcast small dimension table
    enriched_orders = valid_orders \
        .join(broadcast(regions_df), "region_id", "left")
    
    print(f"Enriched orders: {enriched_orders.count()}")
    print("Pattern: Local-fragment (broadcast join)")
    enriched_orders.select("order_id", "region_name", "country", "amount").show(5)
    
    # Step 4: Join with Products (Distributed-Fragment Pattern)
    print("\n[Step 4] Join with Product Data - DISTRIBUTED-FRAGMENT PATTERN")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    # Large table join - repartition for optimization
    orders_with_products = enriched_orders \
        .repartition("product_id") \
        .join(products_df.repartition("product_id"), "product_id", "inner")
    
    print(f"Orders with products: {orders_with_products.count()}")
    print("Pattern: Distributed-fragment (repartitioned join)")
    orders_with_products.select("order_id", "product_name", "category_name", "amount").show(5)
    
    # Step 5: Add Category Metadata (Local-Fragment Pattern)
    print("\n[Step 5] Add Category Metadata - LOCAL-FRAGMENT PATTERN")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    # Broadcast category lookup
    full_enriched = orders_with_products \
        .join(broadcast(categories_df), "category_name", "left")
    
    print(f"Fully enriched orders: {full_enriched.count()}")
    print("Pattern: Local-fragment (broadcast join)")
    
    # Step 6: Calculate Metrics (Multi-Fragment Pattern)
    print("\n[Step 6] Calculate Business Metrics - MULTI-FRAGMENT PATTERN")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    # Multiple aggregations with groupBy
    daily_metrics = full_enriched \
        .groupBy("order_date", "department", "country") \
        .agg(
            count("order_id").alias("total_orders"),
            _sum("amount").alias("total_revenue"),
            avg("amount").alias("avg_order_value"),
            countDistinct("customer_id").alias("unique_customers"),
            countDistinct("product_id").alias("unique_products")
        ) \
        .orderBy("order_date", desc("total_revenue"))
    
    print("Daily business metrics:")
    daily_metrics.show(10)
    print("Pattern: Multi-fragment (groupBy + aggregations + orderBy)")
    
    # Step 7: Customer Segmentation (Hybrid-Fragment Pattern)
    print("\n[Step 7] Customer Segmentation - HYBRID-FRAGMENT PATTERN")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    # Complex analysis with window functions
    customer_analysis = full_enriched \
        .filter(col("status") == "delivered") \
        .groupBy("customer_id", "department") \
        .agg(
            count("order_id").alias("order_count"),
            _sum("amount").alias("total_spent"),
            avg("amount").alias("avg_spent")
        ) \
        .withColumn("customer_rank",
                   rank().over(Window.partitionBy("department")
                              .orderBy(desc("total_spent")))) \
        .withColumn("customer_segment",
                   when(col("total_spent") > 50000, "VIP")
                   .when(col("total_spent") > 20000, "Premium")
                   .when(col("total_spent") > 5000, "Regular")
                   .otherwise("New")) \
        .filter(col("customer_rank") <= 100)
    
    print("Top 100 customers by department:")
    customer_analysis.show(15)
    print("Pattern: Hybrid-fragment (aggregation + window + broadcast)")
    
    # Step 8: Product Performance Analysis (Multi-Fragment Pattern)
    print("\n[Step 8] Product Performance Analysis - MULTI-FRAGMENT PATTERN")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    product_performance = full_enriched \
        .filter(col("status").isin(["delivered", "shipped"])) \
        .groupBy("product_id", "product_name", "category_name", "department") \
        .agg(
            count("order_id").alias("sales_count"),
            _sum("amount").alias("revenue"),
            avg("amount").alias("avg_price")
        ) \
        .withColumn("revenue_rank",
                   rank().over(Window.
```python
                   rank().over(Window.partitionBy("department")
                              .orderBy(desc("revenue")))) \
        .filter(col("revenue_rank") <= 10) \
        .orderBy("department", "revenue_rank")
    
    print("Top 10 products by department:")
    product_performance.show(20)
    print("Pattern: Multi-fragment (aggregation + window function)")
    
    # Step 9: Cache for Multiple Analyses
    print("\n[Step 9] Caching Strategy for Reuse")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    # Cache the enriched dataset for multiple downstream queries
    full_enriched.cache()
    full_enriched.count()  # Materialize cache
    
    print("Cached enriched dataset for reuse")
    print(f"Storage level: {full_enriched.storageLevel}")
    
    # Step 10: Generate Final Reports
    print("\n[Step 10] Generate Final Reports - HYBRID-FRAGMENT PATTERN")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    # Report 1: Regional Performance
    regional_report = full_enriched \
        .groupBy("country", "region_name", "department") \
        .agg(
            count("order_id").alias("orders"),
            _sum("amount").alias("revenue"),
            countDistinct("customer_id").alias("customers")
        ) \
        .withColumn("revenue_per_customer",
                   (col("revenue") / col("customers")).cast("decimal(10,2)")) \
        .orderBy(desc("revenue"))
    
    print("\nRegional Performance Report:")
    regional_report.show(15)
    
    # Report 2: Category Trends
    category_trends = full_enriched \
        .groupBy("department", "category_name", "order_date") \
        .agg(
            count("order_id").alias("daily_orders"),
            _sum("amount").alias("daily_revenue")
        ) \
        .withColumn("moving_avg_revenue",
                   avg("daily_revenue").over(
                       Window.partitionBy("department", "category_name")
                             .orderBy("order_date")
                             .rowsBetween(-6, 0))) \
        .orderBy("department", "category_name", "order_date")
    
    print("\nCategory Trends with 7-day Moving Average:")
    category_trends.show(15)
    
    # Report 3: Customer Lifetime Value
    customer_ltv = full_enriched \
        .groupBy("customer_id") \
        .agg(
            count("order_id").alias("total_orders"),
            _sum("amount").alias("lifetime_value"),
            min("order_date").alias("first_order"),
            max("order_date").alias("last_order"),
            countDistinct("product_id").alias("unique_products_purchased")
        ) \
        .withColumn("avg_order_value",
                   (col("lifetime_value") / col("total_orders")).cast("decimal(10,2)")) \
        .orderBy(desc("lifetime_value")) \
        .limit(50)
    
    print("\nTop 50 Customers by Lifetime Value:")
    customer_ltv.show(20)
    
    # Step 11: Performance Summary
    print("\n[Step 11] Performance Summary")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    print("\nPattern Usage Summary:")
    print("├─ Single-Fragment: Data quality checks")
    print("├─ Local-Fragment: 2 broadcast joins (regions, categories)")
    print("├─ Distributed-Fragment: 1 large table join (products)")
    print("├─ Multi-Fragment: 3 aggregation queries")
    print("└─ Hybrid-Fragment: 2 complex analytical queries")
    
    print("\nOptimization Techniques Applied:")
    print("✓ Broadcast joins for small dimensions")
    print("✓ Repartitioning before large joins")
    print("✓ Caching for reused datasets")
    print("✓ Window functions for rankings")
    print("✓ Predicate pushdown with filters")
    print("✓ Column pruning in selections")
    
    # Cleanup
    full_enriched.unpersist()
    
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("COMPREHENSIVE EXAMPLE COMPLETED")
    print("=" * 80)

## 🎯 **USAGE EXAMPLES**

### **Example 1: Quick Pattern Selection**

```python
from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import *

spark = SparkSession.builder.appName("QuickExample").getOrCreate()

# Your data
large_df = spark.read.parquet("large_dataset.parquet")
small_df = spark.read.parquet("small_lookup.parquet")

# Pattern Selection Guide:

# 1. SINGLE-FRAGMENT: Simple filter
result = large_df.filter(col("amount") > 1000)

# 2. MULTI-FRAGMENT: Aggregation
result = large_df.groupBy("category").agg(sum("amount"))

# 3. DISTRIBUTED-FRAGMENT: Large join
result = large_df.join(another_large_df, "key")

# 4. LOCAL-FRAGMENT: Small lookup
result = large_df.join(broadcast(small_df), "key")

# 5. HYBRID-FRAGMENT: Complex query
result = large_df \
    .join(another_large_df, "key1") \
    .join(broadcast(small_df), "key2") \
    .groupBy("category").agg(sum("amount"))
```

## 📊 **PATTERN COMPARISON TABLE**

| Pattern | Stages | Shuffles | Network I/O | Best For | Avoid When |
|---------|--------|----------|-------------|----------|------------|
| **Single-Fragment** | 1 | 0 | Minimal | Filters, maps, simple transforms | Need aggregation/join |
| **Multi-Fragment** | 2+ | 1+ | Moderate | GroupBy, orderBy, window functions | Very small data |
| **Distributed-Fragment** | Multiple | Multiple | High | Large joins, big data processing | Small datasets |
| **Local-Fragment** | 1-2 | 0 | Low (broadcast) | Dimension table joins | Large dimension tables |
| **Hybrid-Fragment** | Multiple | Selective | Optimized | Complex analytics, mixed operations | Simple queries |

## 🔧 **TROUBLESHOOTING GUIDE**

### **Problem: Query is slow**
```python
# Diagnosis
df.explain(mode="cost")  # Check plan
# Look for: multiple shuffles, large partition counts

# Solutions
1. Enable AQE: spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "true")
2. Tune partitions: spark.conf.set("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "500")
3. Cache reused data: df.cache()
4. Broadcast small tables: broadcast(small_df)
```

### **Problem: Out of Memory**
```python
# Diagnosis
# Check Spark UI → Executors → Memory usage

# Solutions
1. Increase memory: --executor-memory 32g
2. Reduce partition size: df.repartition(1000)
3. Disable broadcast: spark.conf.set("spark.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold", "-1")
4. Use disk spilling: spark.conf.set("spark.memory.fraction", "0.6")
```

### **Problem: Data Skew**
```python
# Diagnosis
# Check Spark UI → Stages → Task duration variance

# Solution: Salting
from pyspark.sql.functions import rand, concat, lit

# Add salt
salted_df = df.withColumn("salt", (rand() * 10).cast("int")) \
              .withColumn("salted_key", concat(col("key"), lit("_"), col("salt")))

# Aggregate with salt
result = salted_df \
    .groupBy("salted_key").agg(sum("value").alias("partial")) \
    .withColumn("original_key", split(col("salted_key"), "_")[0]) \
    .groupBy("original_key").agg(sum("partial").alias("total"))
```

## 📝 **ADDITIONAL UTILITIES**

```python
# ============================================================================
# UTILITY FUNCTIONS
# ============================================================================

def get_partition_info(df):
    """Get detailed partition information"""
    print(f"Number of partitions: {df.rdd.getNumPartitions()}")
    
    # Get partition sizes
    partition_sizes = df.rdd.glom().map(len).collect()
    print(f"Partition sizes: {partition_sizes}")
    print(f"Min size: {min(partition_sizes)}")
    print(f"Max size: {max(partition_sizes)}")
    print(f"Avg size: {sum(partition_sizes) / len(partition_sizes):.2f}")
    
    # Check for skew
    skew_ratio = max(partition_sizes) / (sum(partition_sizes) / len(partition_sizes))
    print(f"Skew ratio: {skew_ratio:.2f}")
    if skew_ratio > 3:
        print("⚠️  WARNING: Significant data skew detected!")


def compare_plans(df1, df2, name1="Plan 1", name2="Plan 2"):
    """Compare execution plans of two DataFrames"""
    print(f"\n{'=' * 80}")
    print(f"COMPARING: {name1} vs {name2}")
    print(f"{'=' * 80}")
    
    print(f"\n{name1}:")
    df1.explain(mode="formatted")
    
    print(f"\n{name2}:")
    df2.explain(mode="formatted")
    
    # Count operations
    plan1 = df1._jdf.queryExecution().executedPlan().toString()
    plan2 = df2._jdf.queryExecution().executedPlan().toString()
    
    print(f"\n{'=' * 80}")
    print("OPERATION COUNTS:")
    print(f"{'=' * 80}")
    print(f"{'Operation':<30} {name1:<15} {name2:<15}")
    print("-" * 60)
    print(f"{'Exchange (Shuffle)':<30} {plan1.count('Exchange'):<15} {plan2.count('Exchange'):<15}")
    print(f"{'BroadcastHashJoin':<30} {plan1.count('BroadcastHashJoin'):<15} {plan2.count('BroadcastHashJoin'):<15}")
    print(f"{'SortMergeJoin':<30} {plan1.count('SortMergeJoin'):<15} {plan2.count('SortMergeJoin'):<15}")
    print(f"{'HashAggregate':<30} {plan1.count('HashAggregate'):<15} {plan2.count('HashAggregate'):<15}")


def optimize_dataframe(df, operation_type="general"):
    """
    Automatically optimize DataFrame based on operation type
    
    Args:
        df: Input DataFrame
        operation_type: "filter", "join", "aggregate", "general"
    
    Returns:
        Optimized DataFrame
    """
    if operation_type == "filter":
        # For filter operations: ensure good partitioning
        return df.repartition(spark.sparkContext.defaultParallelism)
    
    elif operation_type == "join":
        # For joins: repartition on join key
        print("Note: Repartition on join key for best performance")
        return df
    
    elif operation_type == "aggregate":
        # For aggregations: optimal partition count
        optimal_partitions = max(200, spark.sparkContext.defaultParallelism * 2)
        spark.conf.set("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", optimal_partitions)
        return df
    
    else:
        # General optimization
        spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "true")
        return df


def profile_query(df, query_name="Query"):
    """
    Profile a query and provide optimization recommendations
    """
    import time
    
    print(f"\n{'=' * 80}")
    print(f"PROFILING: {query_name}")
    print(f"{'=' * 80}")
    
    # Execute and time
    start = time.time()
    count = df.count()
    duration = time.time() - start
    
    # Get metrics
    num_partitions = df.rdd.getNumPartitions()
    plan = df._jdf.queryExecution().executedPlan().toString()
    
    # Analyze
    has_broadcast = "BroadcastHashJoin" in plan
    num_shuffles = plan.count("Exchange")
    has_sort = "Sort" in plan
    
    # Report
    print(f"\nExecution Metrics:")
    print(f"  Duration: {duration:.4f} seconds")
    print(f"  Row count: {count:,}")
    print(f"  Partitions: {num_partitions}")
    print(f"  Shuffles: {num_shuffles}")
    print(f"  Has broadcast: {has_broadcast}")
    print(f"  Has sort: {has_sort}")
    
    # Recommendations
    print(f"\nRecommendations:")
    if num_shuffles > 3:
        print("  ⚠️  High shuffle count - consider combining operations")
    if num_partitions < 10:
        print("  ⚠️  Low partition count - consider repartitioning")
    if num_partitions > 2000:
        print("  ⚠️  High partition count - consider coalescing")
    if not has_broadcast and num_shuffles > 0:
        print("  💡 Consider broadcast joins for small tables")
    if duration > 60:
        print("  ⏱️  Long execution time - review optimization opportunities")
    
    return {
        'duration': duration,
        'count': count,
        'partitions': num_partitions,
        'shuffles': num_shuffles,
        'has_broadcast': has_broadcast
    }


# Example usage of utilities
if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Create sample data
    sample_df = spark.range(0, 1000000).withColumn("value", col("id") * 2)
    
    # Get partition info
    get_partition_info(sample_df)
    
    # Profile a query
    aggregated = sample_df.groupBy((col("id") % 100).alias("group")).agg(sum("value"))
    profile_query(aggregated, "Sample Aggregation")
    
    # Compare plans
    plan1 = sample_df.filter(col("id") > 500000)
    plan2 = sample_df.filter(col("id") > 500000).coalesce(10)
    compare_plans(plan1, plan2, "Without Coalesce", "With Coalesce")

```

### **Pattern Selection Matrix:**

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    WHEN TO USE EACH PATTERN                     │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                 │
│  Data Size    Operation Type    Recommended Pattern            │
│  ─────────    ──────────────    ───────────────────            │
│                                                                 │
│  Any          Filter/Select     → Single-Fragment              │
│  Any          Map/FlatMap       → Single-Fragment              │
│                                                                 │
│  Medium+      GroupBy           → Multi-Fragment               │
│  Medium+      OrderBy           → Multi-Fragment               │
│  Medium+      Window Functions  → Multi-Fragment               │
│                                                                 │
│  Large        Join (Large)      → Distributed-Fragment         │
│  Large        Distributed Agg   → Distributed-Fragment         │
│                                                                 │
│  Small        Join (Dimension)  → Local-Fragment (Broadcast)   │
│  Any          Lookup Table      → Local-Fragment (Broadcast)   │
│                                                                 │
│  Mixed        Complex Query     → Hybrid-Fragment              │
│  Mixed        Multi-Stage ETL   → Hybrid-Fragment              │
│                                                                 │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### **Performance Tuning Priority:**

```
Priority 1 (Highest Impact):
───────────────────────────
1. Enable Adaptive Query Execution
2. Optimize partition counts
3. Use broadcast for small tables
4. Handle data skew

Priority 2 (Medium Impact):
──────────────────────────
5. Cache reused DataFrames
6. Apply predicate pushdown
7. Use column pruning
8. Repartition on join keys

Priority 3 (Fine-Tuning):
────────────────────────
9. Tune memory settings
10. Adjust parallelism
11. Use bucketing
12. Enable CBO statistics
```

```python
# ============================================================================
# PRO TIPS FOR PRODUCTION
# ============================================================================

# TIP 1: Always explain your queries
def explain_query(df, name="Query"):
    """Always check execution plan before running in production"""
    print(f"\n=== {name} Execution Plan ===")
    df.explain(mode="formatted")
    
    # Check for red flags
    plan = df._jdf.queryExecution().executedPlan().toString()
    warnings = []
    
    if plan.count("Exchange") > 5:
        warnings.append("⚠️  Too many shuffles detected")
    if "CartesianProduct" in plan:
        warnings.append("🚨 CRITICAL: Cartesian product detected!")
    if plan.count("Sort") > 2:
        warnings.append("⚠️  Multiple sorts - consider optimization")
    
    if warnings:
        print("\nWARNINGS:")
        for w in warnings:
            print(f"  {w}")
    else:
        print("\n✅ No major issues detected")


# TIP 2: Monitor resource usage
def monitor_execution(df, action_func):
    """Monitor resource usage during execution"""
    import time
    import psutil
    
    # Get initial state
    initial_memory = psutil.virtual_memory().percent
    
    # Execute
    start = time.time()
    result = action_func(df)
    duration = time.time() - start
    
    # Get final state
    final_memory = psutil.virtual_memory().percent
    
    print(f"\nExecution Metrics:")
    print(f"  Duration: {duration:.2f}s")
    print(f"  Memory change: {final_memory - initial_memory:.2f}%")
    print(f"  Result: {result}")
    
    return result


# TIP 3: Use checkpoints for long pipelines
def checkpoint_pipeline(df, checkpoint_dir="/tmp/checkpoints"):
    """Checkpoint DataFrames in long pipelines"""
    spark.sparkContext.setCheckpointDir(checkpoint_dir)
    return df.checkpoint()


# TIP 4: Validate data quality
def validate_data(df, checks):
    """
    Validate data quality before processing
    
    Args:
        df: Input DataFrame
        checks: Dict of validation rules
    
    Example:
        checks = {
            'not_null': ['id', 'amount'],
            'positive': ['amount', 'quantity'],
            'valid_range': {'age': (0, 120)}
        }
    """
    issues = []
    
    # Check nulls
    if 'not_null' in checks:
        for col_name in checks['not_null']:
            null_count = df.filter(col(col_name).isNull()).count()
            if null_count > 0:
                issues.append(f"Found {null_count} nulls in {col_name}")
    
    # Check positive values
    if 'positive' in checks:
        for col_name in checks['positive']:
            neg_count = df.filter(col(col_name) <= 0).count()
            if neg_count > 0:
                issues.append(f"Found {neg_count} non-positive values in {col_name}")
    
    # Check ranges
    if 'valid_range' in checks:
        for col_name, (min_val, max_val) in checks['valid_range'].items():
            invalid = df.filter(
                (col(col_name) < min_val) | (col(col_name) > max_val)
            ).count()
            if invalid > 0:
                issues.append(f"Found {invalid} out-of-range values in {col_name}")
    
    # Report
    if issues:
        print("❌ DATA QUALITY ISSUES:")
        for issue in issues:
            print(f"  • {issue}")
        return False
    else:
        print("✅ All data quality checks passed")
        return True


# TIP 5: Create reusable optimization configurations
class SparkOptimizer:
    """Reusable Spark optimization configurations"""
    
    @staticmethod
    def configure_for_streaming():
        """Optimize for streaming workloads"""
        spark.conf.set("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "100")
        spark.conf.set("spark.streaming.backpressure.enabled", "true")
        spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "false")  # Not for streaming
        print("✅ Configured for streaming workloads")
    
    @staticmethod
    def configure_for_batch():
        """Optimize for batch workloads"""
        spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "true")
        spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.coalescePartitions.enabled", "true")
        spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.skewJoin.enabled", "true")
        spark.conf.set("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "1000")
        print("✅ Configured for batch workloads")
    
    @staticmethod
    def configure_for_interactive():
        """Optimize for interactive queries"""
        spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "true")
        spark.conf.set("spark.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold", "100MB")
        spark.conf.set("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "200")
        spark.conf.set("spark.sql.cbo.enabled", "true")
        print("✅ Configured for interactive queries")
    
    @staticmethod
    def configure_for_ml():
        """Optimize for machine learning workloads"""
        spark.conf.set("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "500")
        spark.conf.set("spark.executor.memory", "32g")
        spark.conf.set("spark.memory.fraction", "0.8")
        spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "true")
        print("✅ Configured for ML workloads")


# TIP 6: Create execution reports
def generate_execution_report(df, query_name, output_path=None):
    """Generate detailed execution report"""
    import json
    from datetime import datetime
    
    report = {
        'query_name': query_name,
        'timestamp': datetime.now().isoformat(),
        'partitions': df.rdd.getNumPartitions(),
        'schema': [f.name for f in df.schema.fields],
        'optimizations': []
    }
    
    # Analyze plan
    plan = df._jdf.queryExecution().executedPlan().toString()
    
    if "BroadcastHashJoin" in plan:
        report['optimizations'].append("Broadcast join detected")
    if "Exchange" in plan:
        report['optimizations'].append(f"{plan.count('Exchange')} shuffle operations")
    if "AdaptiveSparkPlan" in plan:
        report['optimizations'].append("Adaptive execution enabled")
    
    # Print report
    print(f"\n{'=' * 80}")
    print(f"EXECUTION REPORT: {query_name}")
    print(f"{'=' * 80}")
    print(json.dumps(report, indent=2))
    
    # Save if path provided
    if output_path:
        with open(output_path, 'w') as f:
            json.dumps(report, f, indent=2)
        print(f"\n✅ Report saved to {output_path}")
    
    return report


# Example usage of pro tips
if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Create sample data
    sample_df = spark.range(0, 1000000).withColumn("value", col("id") * 2)
    
    # Use pro tips
    explain_query(sample_df.filter(col("id") > 500000), "Sample Filter")
    
    # Validate data
    validate_data(sample_df, {
        'not_null': ['id', 'value'],
        'positive': ['id', 'value']
    })
    
    # Configure optimizer
    optimizer = SparkOptimizer()
    optimizer.configure_for_batch()
    
    # Generate report
    generate_execution_report(sample_df, "Sample Query")

```python
# ============================================================================
# APPENDIX A: CUSTOM QUERY OPTIMIZATION RULES
# ============================================================================

from pyspark.sql.catalyst.plans.logical import LogicalPlan
from pyspark.sql.catalyst.rules import Rule

class CustomOptimizationRules:
    """
    Advanced: Custom optimization rules for specific use cases
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def optimize_repeated_filters(df):
        """
        Combine multiple filter conditions into a single filter
        """
        # Instead of:
        # df.filter(cond1).filter(cond2).filter(cond3)
        
        # Use:
        # df.filter(cond1 & cond2 & cond3)
        
        print("Optimization: Combining multiple filters")
        return df
    
    @staticmethod
    def optimize_select_chains(df, columns):
        """
        Optimize multiple select operations
        """
        # Instead of:
        # df.select(col1).select(col2).select(col3)
        
        # Use:
        # df.select(col1, col2, col3)
        
        print("Optimization: Combining select operations")
        return df.select(*columns)
    
    @staticmethod
    def optimize_join_order(dfs, join_keys):
        """
        Optimize join order based on table sizes
        Start with smallest table
        """
        # Sort DataFrames by size (smallest first)
        df_sizes = [(df, df.count()) for df in dfs]
        df_sizes.sort(key=lambda x: x[1])
        
        print("Optimization: Ordering joins by table size")
        
        # Join smallest to largest
        result = df_sizes[0][0]
        for df, size in df_sizes[1:]:
            result = result.join(df, join_keys, "inner")
        
        return result


# ============================================================================
# APPENDIX B: PARTITION STRATEGIES
# ============================================================================

class PartitionStrategies:
    """
    Advanced partitioning strategies for different scenarios
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def hash_partition(df, key_cols, num_partitions):
        """
        Hash-based partitioning for even distribution
        """
        return df.repartition(num_partitions, *key_cols)
    
    @staticmethod
    def range_partition(df, order_col, num_partitions):
        """
        Range-based partitioning for sorted data
        """
        return df.repartitionByRange(num_partitions, order_col)
    
    @staticmethod
    def adaptive_partition(df, target_size_mb=128):
        """
        Automatically determine partition count based on data size
        """
        # Estimate data size
        sample_size = df.sample(0.01).count()
        estimated_total = sample_size * 100
        
        # Calculate partitions (target 128MB per partition)
        # Assuming ~1KB per row average
        estimated_size_mb = (estimated_total * 1024) / (1024 * 1024)
        optimal_partitions = max(1, int(estimated_size_mb / target_size_mb))
        
        print(f"Adaptive partitioning: {optimal_partitions} partitions")
        return df.repartition(optimal_partitions)
    
    @staticmethod
    def skew_aware_partition(df, key_col, skew_threshold=0.3):
        """
        Partition with skew awareness
        """
        from pyspark.sql.functions import count as sql_count
        
        # Identify skewed keys
        key_distribution = df.groupBy(key_col).agg(sql_count("*").alias("count"))
        total_count = df.count()
        
        skewed_keys = key_distribution.filter(
            col("count") / total_count > skew_threshold
        ).select(key_col).collect()
        
        if skewed_keys:
            print(f"Found {len(skewed_keys)} skewed keys")
            # Apply salting to skewed keys
            from pyspark.sql.functions import when, rand
            
            skewed_values = [row[key_col] for row in skewed_keys]
            
            return df.withColumn(
                "partition_key",
                when(col(key_col).isin(skewed_values),
                     concat(col(key_col), lit("_"), (rand() * 10).cast("int")))
                .otherwise(col(key_col))
            )
        else:
            print("No significant skew detected")
            return df


# ============================================================================
# APPENDIX C: ADVANCED JOIN STRATEGIES
# ============================================================================

class AdvancedJoinStrategies:
    """
    Advanced join strategies for complex scenarios
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def bucket_join(df1, df2, join_key, num_buckets=50, table_name1="table1", table_name2="table2"):
        """
        Bucket-based join for repeated joins on same key
        Eliminates shuffle if both tables are bucketed on join key
        """
        # Write bucketed tables
        df1.write \
            .bucketBy(num_buckets, join_key) \
            .sortBy(join_key) \
            .mode("overwrite") \
            .saveAsTable(table_name1)
        
        df2.write \
            .bucketBy(num_buckets, join_key) \
            .sortBy(join_key) \
            .mode("overwrite") \
            .saveAsTable(table_name2)
        
        # Read and join (no shuffle!)
        bucketed_df1 = spark.table(table_name1)
        bucketed_df2 = spark.table(table_name2)
        
        print(f"Bucket join: {num_buckets} buckets, no shuffle required")
        return bucketed_df1.join(bucketed_df2, join_key)
    
    @staticmethod
    def broadcast_hash_join(large_df, small_df, join_key):
        """
        Explicit broadcast hash join
        """
        print("Using broadcast hash join strategy")
        return large_df.join(broadcast(small_df), join_key, "inner")
    
    @staticmethod
    def sort_merge_join(df1, df2, join_key):
        """
        Sort-merge join for large tables
        """
        print("Using sort-merge join strategy")
        
        # Disable broadcast to force sort-merge
        spark.conf.set("spark.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold", "-1")
        
        # Repartition on join key for better performance
        df1_repart = df1.repartition(join_key)
        df2_repart = df2.repartition(join_key)
        
        result = df1_repart.join(df2_repart, join_key, "inner")
        
        # Reset config
        spark.conf.set("spark.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold", "10485760")
        
        return result
    
    @staticmethod
    def skew_join(df1, df2, join_key, skewed_keys):
        """
        Handle skewed joins using iterative broadcast
        """
        from pyspark.sql.functions import broadcast
        
        print(f"Skew join: handling {len(skewed_keys)} skewed keys")
        
        # Split into skewed and non-skewed
        df1_skewed = df1.filter(col(join_key).isin(skewed_keys))
        df1_normal = df1.filter(~col(join_key).isin(skewed_keys))
        
        df2_skewed = df2.filter(col(join_key).isin(skewed_keys))
        df2_normal = df2.filter(~col(join_key).isin(skewed_keys))
        
        # Normal join for non-skewed data
        normal_result = df1_normal.join(df2_normal, join_key, "inner")
        
        # Broadcast join for skewed data
        skewed_result = df1_skewed.join(broadcast(df2_skewed), join_key, "inner")
        
        # Union results
        return normal_result.union(skewed_result)


# ============================================================================
# APPENDIX D: MEMORY MANAGEMENT STRATEGIES
# ============================================================================

class MemoryManagementStrategies:
    """
    Advanced memory management for large-scale processing
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def configure_memory_for_workload(workload_type):
        """
        Configure memory based on workload type
        """
        configs = {
            'shuffle_heavy': {
                'spark.memory.fraction': '0.5',
                'spark.memory.storageFraction': '0.3',
                'spark.shuffle.memoryFraction': '0.6'
            },
            'cache_heavy': {
                'spark.memory.fraction': '0.6',
                'spark.memory.storageFraction': '0.6',
                'spark.shuffle.memoryFraction': '0.3'
            },
            'balanced': {
                'spark.memory.fraction': '0.6',
                'spark.memory.storageFraction': '0.5',
                'spark.shuffle.memoryFraction': '0.4'
            }
        }
        
        if workload_type in configs:
            for key, value in configs[workload_type].items():
                spark.conf.set(key, value)
            print(f"✅ Configured memory for {workload_type} workload")
        else:
            print(f"❌ Unknown workload type: {workload_type}")
    
    @staticmethod
    def enable_off_heap_memory(size_gb=10):
        """
        Enable off-heap memory for large datasets
        """
        spark.conf.set("spark.memory.offHeap.enabled", "true")
        spark.conf.set("spark.memory.offHeap.size", f"{size_gb}g")
        print(f"✅ Enabled {size_gb}GB off-heap memory")
    
    @staticmethod
    def configure_spill_settings():
        """
        Configure disk spilling for memory-intensive operations
        """
        spark.conf.set("spark.shuffle.spill.compress", "true")
        spark.conf.set("spark.shuffle.compress", "true")
        spark.conf.set("spark.io.compression.codec", "snappy")
        print("✅ Configured spill settings")
    
    @staticmethod
    def monitor_memory_usage(df, operation_name="Operation"):
        """
        Monitor memory usage during operation
        """
        import gc
        import psutil
        
        # Force garbage collection
        gc.collect()
        
        # Get memory before
        process = psutil.Process()
        mem_before = process.memory_info().rss / 1024 / 1024  # MB
        
        # Execute operation
        df.cache()
        count = df.count()
        
        # Get memory after
        mem_after = process.memory_info().rss / 1024 / 1024  # MB
        
        print(f"\n{operation_name} Memory Usage:")
        print(f"  Before: {mem_before:.2f} MB")
        print(f"  After: {mem_after:.2f} MB")
        print(f"  Delta: {mem_after - mem_before:.2f} MB")
        print(f"  Rows: {count:,}")
        
        return mem_after - mem_before


# ============================================================================
# APPENDIX E: QUERY COST ESTIMATION
# ============================================================================

class QueryCostEstimator:
    """
    Estimate query cost before execution
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def estimate_shuffle_cost(df, group_keys):
        """
        Estimate cost of shuffle operation
        """
        # Sample to estimate
        sample_df = df.sample(0.01)
        sample_count = sample_df.count()
        estimated_total = sample_count * 100
        
        # Estimate groups
        sample_groups = sample_df.select(*group_keys).distinct().count()
        estimated_groups = sample_groups * 100
        
        # Calculate shuffle cost
        shuffle_ratio = estimated_groups / estimated_total if estimated_total > 0 else 0
        
        print(f"\nShuffle Cost Estimation:")
        print(f"  Estimated rows: {estimated_total:,}")
        print(f"  Estimated groups: {estimated_groups:,}")
        print(f"  Shuffle ratio: {shuffle_ratio:.2%}")
        
        if shuffle_ratio > 0.5:
            print("  ⚠️  HIGH shuffle cost - consider optimization")
        elif shuffle_ratio > 0.2:
            print("  ⚡ MODERATE shuffle cost")
        else:
            print("  ✅ LOW shuffle cost")
        
        return shuffle_ratio
    
    @staticmethod
    def estimate_join_cost(df1, df2, join_key):
        """
        Estimate cost of join operation
        """
        # Get sizes
        count1 = df1.count()
        count2 = df2.count()
        
        # Estimate join cardinality
        distinct1 = df1.select(join_key).distinct().count()
        distinct2 = df2.select(join_key).distinct().count()
        
        # Estimate output size
        avg_fanout1 = count1 / distinct1 if distinct1 > 0 else 1
        avg_fanout2 = count2 / distinct2 if distinct2 > 0 else 1
        estimated_output = min(distinct1, distinct2) * avg_fanout1 * avg_fanout2
        
        print(f"\nJoin Cost Estimation:")
        print(f"  Left table: {count1:,} rows, {distinct1:,} distinct keys")
        print(f"  Right table: {count2:,} rows, {distinct2:,} distinct keys")
        print(f"  Estimated output: {estimated_output:,} rows")
        print(f"  Selectivity: {estimated_output / (count1 * count2):.2%}")
        
        # Recommend strategy
        if count2 < 100000:
            print("  💡 Recommendation: Broadcast join")
        elif distinct1 == distinct2:
            print("  💡 Recommendation: Bucket join")
        else:
            print("  💡 Recommendation: Sort-merge join")
        
        return estimated_output
    
    @staticmethod
    def estimate_query_complexity(df):
        """
        Estimate overall query complexity
        """
        plan = df._jdf.queryExecution().executedPlan().toString()
        
        complexity_score = 0
        
        # Count operations
        num_shuffles = plan.count("Exchange")
        num_joins = plan.count("Join")
        num_aggregates = plan.count("Aggregate")
        num_sorts = plan.count("Sort")
        
        # Calculate score
        complexity_score += num_shuffles * 10
        complexity_score += num_joins * 5
        complexity_score += num_aggregates * 3
        complexity_score += num_sorts * 2
        
        print(f"\nQuery Complexity Analysis:")
        print(f"  Shuffles: {num_shuffles}")
        print(f"  Joins: {num_joins}")
        print(f"  Aggregates: {num_aggregates}")
        print(f"  Sorts: {num_sorts}")
        print(f"  Complexity Score: {complexity_score}")
